The consequence is stated rather than hidden: `@capacitor/cli` declares `engines.node >= 22` and **hard-fails** below it, so `native/android/` was generated under a hermetically fetched Node 22 (`npx node@22`), and CI pins Node 22. **JDK 21**, matching the template's `capacitor.build.gradle`. **`native/android/` is committed** — it carries the application id, the (e) hardening and the Gradle pins, none of which survives regeneration. **Debug signing only**; no release keystore exists in the repository or in CI, and key custody is a later explicit decision. **`native/` is a new top-level subtree** rather than `app/native/`: under `app/` it would enter the Docker build context and land inside the "every shipped `app/` file is excluded" reasoning `.pre-commit-config.yaml` documents, making correctness depend on `.dockerignore` — a file the ship-list guard explicitly does not consult.

  o. **The GA4 egress is inherited unchanged into the Android channel, and it is given a permanent address rather than being called a later-packet question.** `app/index.html` loads `googletagmanager.com` and emits through `trackEvent`; the APK carries the same bytes and therefore the same behaviour. Payloads are already §4-safe and cleared under `GA-DL-001`, so this is not new *data* — but it is the same egress over a **new distribution channel**, so it was raised in the plan's Escalations. Removing or gating it was rejected: it is a product change this packet forbids, and it would fork the two channels' bytes and destroy the byte-identity guarantee (d) rests on. **The standing decision, stated so it cannot be read as settled:** whether the native channel should carry web analytics **at all** is an owner decision under the escalation list (public exposure + egress, PDR-027 §2), and its **deadline is before any APK is distributed to anyone outside the author's family** — not before this packet, and not at the end of this milestone. It is open until that decision is made.

- **Rationale.** L1's whole ladder — schema, journal, write path, export — is unreachable until the app has a native container to hold a native store, so P1 buys exactly one thing and buys it cleanly: a container that changes nothing. That constraint is what makes byte-identity the right acceptance criterion rather than a nicety; "the Android build behaves identically" is either a property a test can check or a sentence somebody wrote. The two invariants are chosen by the same test: each states the fail-closed default it actually enforces, and each names in its Scope what it knowingly does not cover — which is how (i) stays visible instead of becoming the thing everyone assumed someone else had handled. The two corrections are one defect in two costumes: a claim with a false provenance. `MUST_MATCH` was described as a deliberate choice by configs that declare nothing, and the `ALLOW_LOOSE` replacement arrived as an unverified note that would have read as an observation. Correcting the first while committing the second would have been the more expensive mistake, because it would have looked like diligence.

- **No dedicated ADR by design at the repo layer.** The architecture is decided upstream — **ADR-043** §1 (platform is Capacitor; native storage is the source of truth; WebView storage forbidden for persistent data), §3 (Android-first, direct APK) and §5 (origin storage is not inherited, so migration needs an explicit bridge — P3, not here); **PDR-026** §2 (the L1..L7 ladder); **ADR-037** (buildless hybrid parity and the parity-suite precedent this packet extends rather than replaces); **ADR-030** §2 (invariants compiled into structural checks); **ADR-024** (versioning by filename — untouched: no published asset changes); **ADR-020** (the promotion gate — untouched); **PDR-019** (dark build — direct APK is compatible, and nothing here makes the app publicly reachable). This entry records what the repo did with those, not a new architectural decision.

- **Alternatives considered.**
  1. **Point `webDir` at `app/`.** Rejected — it packages `node_modules/`, `tests/` and the baselines into the APK. See (a).
  2. **Hand-maintain the APK's file list in `capacitor.config.json`.** Rejected — a second ship list is a second thing to forget on every extraction packet, and it fails silently in both directions. See (a).
  3. **Write a second `COPY` parser for the stager.** Rejected — see (b).
  4. **Record the full ADR-043 §1 inversion as an enforced invariant now.** Rejected — the native store is L1-P2 and family data is still in `localStorage`; claiming it would be exactly the wish-list drift `AGENTS.md` §10 exists to prevent. See (c).
  5. **Strip comments before scanning for storage access.** Rejected — it fails open on any line carrying a `https://` literal. See (c).
  6. **Let the native spec stage the web root itself.** Rejected — it makes its own assertion tautological. See (d).
  7. **Leave Android Auto Backup at the template default.** Rejected, and escalated first with both branches written out. See (e).
  8. **Give the `native` project its own baseline set.** Rejected — tautological given byte-identity, and it doubles the re-blessing cost. See (g).
  9. **Disable service-worker registration in the native build.** Rejected twice over: it is a product change this packet forbids, and it would fork the two channels' bytes. See (i).
  10. **Pin Capacitor 6.x** so the dev box's Node 18 could run the CLI. Rejected — see (n).
  11. **Generate `native/android/` in CI instead of committing it.** Rejected — the (e) hardening and the application id do not survive regeneration, and the invariant that pins them would have nothing to read.
  12. **State the `ALLOW_LOOSE` claim as an owner-supplied fact.** Rejected on owner correction — see (k).
  13. **Switch the three configs to an explicit `MUST_MATCH` while in the files.** Rejected — the delivery channel is the only one and a mismatch would break it. Recorded as open debt. See (j).
  14. **Correct only the two `cloudbuild.yaml` files the handoff named**, leaving `api/cloudbuild.staging.yaml`. Rejected — it is the identical claim in the identical class of file; a partial correction manufactures a new inconsistency. Flagged in the plan as a deliberate widening of a literal instruction.
  15. **Reconcile `AGENTS.md` §8's layout block and §3's intent-level entry now.** Rejected — contract edits stay out of packets and land at milestone close.

- **Supersedes.** None. **Corrects** the `MUST_MATCH` claim in `app/cloudbuild.yaml`, `api/cloudbuild.yaml`, `api/cloudbuild.staging.yaml` and `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (three sites), per (j). **Amends by reference, leaving the records byte-untouched:** `L2-DL-001` (4) and (6), `A3-DL-002` (2) and (7), and `A3-DL-003` (c) — each states or relies on the `MUST_MATCH` reading; each was written in good faith on the same false premise, and this log's convention is amendment by reference rather than rewriting history. `docs/execution-map.md`'s A3-CLOSE bullet carries the same reading and is likewise left byte-untouched: it is a record of what a packet shipped, the `A3-DL-004` (n)(3) disposition.

- **Effects.**
  - **Added (`native/`):** `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `capacitor.config.json`, `.gitignore`, `tools/stage-webdir.js`, and the generated-and-committed `android/` project, whose `AndroidManifest.xml` carries the (e) hand edit and whose `res/xml/{data_extraction_rules,backup_rules}.xml` are new.
  - **Added (`app/tests/`):** `support/ship-list.js` (extracted, per (b)), `storage-seam.spec.js`, `native-shell.spec.js`.
  - **Changed (`app/`, dev/CI-only files only):** `tests/delivery-contract.spec.js` (requires the extracted parser; assertions and test count unchanged), `tests/server.js` (two delivery profiles, a servable root), `tests/support/seed.js` (a `parityProfile` option), `tests/behavior.spec.js` (the service-worker block skips under `capacitor`, with the (h) reason inline), `playwright.config.js` (the `native` project, a second `webServer`, the widened `contract` `testMatch`). **No shipped `app/` file is touched** — not `index.html`, `sw.js`, `manifest.json`, `offline.html`, `kb-v1.json`, `icons/` or `m/` — and no baseline in `tests/__baselines__/` is rewritten.
  - **Changed (harness):** `scripts/parity-suite.sh` stages the web root before running; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gains the `android` job; `.pre-commit-config.yaml` excludes `native/android/` from the two auto-fixing hooks and states why. The read-only validators still run repo-wide.
  - **Changed (build-configs, COMMENT-ONLY):** `app/cloudbuild.yaml`, `api/cloudbuild.yaml`, `api/cloudbuild.staging.yaml` — per (j)/(k). **Every executable line, flag, step and substitution is byte-untouched**, the `A3-DL-003` (e)(2) / `A3-DL-004` (g) posture.
  - **Changed (spine):** `docs/RUNBOOK.md` — the three corrected `MUST_MATCH` sites, a new **Substitution matching — what is not protected** section carrying the (m) split and the open debt, a new **Android shell (Capacitor)** section with the numbered owner-run APK procedure and the on-device smoke, and two additions to the parity-suite section. `docs/INVARIANTS.md` — `LSC-P1-INV-001`, `LSC-P1-INV-002`. `docs/execution-map.md` — the milestone block and the namespace split.
  - **Untouched, and verified so:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/RUNTIME-INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/product/**`, `README.md`, `docker-compose.yml`, everything under `api/**` except the two build-config header comments, `app/Dockerfile`, `app/nginx.conf`, `app/docker-entrypoint.sh`, and every prior decision-log entry.
  - **Operability: none this packet** (ADR-013 / contract §4.7). No knob and no signal is added. Nothing qualitative or tunable is introduced: the application id, `webDir`, scheme and hostname are **build identity**, not policy, and they are pinned by `LSC-P1-INV-002` — a test that reds on change is a stronger guarantee than a `changed_in` field, and the typed surface (`api/theygrow_api/parameters.py`) is Python-side and untouched. `PARAMETERS_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays **5**; no `theygrow_api.signals` taxonomy entry, no `emitted_now` change, no producer added or removed; no GA4 event, since no shipped `app/` file changes. The toolchain versions follow the existing pin-and-refuse precedent (`scripts/parity-suite.sh` ↔ `app/package.json`). **No new Python runtime import**, so the mypy hook's `additional_dependencies` are unchanged.
  - **§4-safe, with one thing named rather than waved past.** No corpus record, database row, credential, host, user, password or connection string enters the repository; no live identifier enters a contract or spine file; the parity suite still blocks the analytics beacon, so CI generates no third-party egress. The APK inherits the shell's existing GA4 egress unchanged — that is (o), and it is open with a stated deadline, not settled. The backup hardening in (e) **removes** an egress the platform would otherwise have performed by default.
  - **Debt recorded, not fixed:** the `substitutionOption` switch (j), with what would close it; the unverified `ALLOW_LOOSE` claim (k); the open PWA merge-trigger expectation (m); a release signing config and key custody (n); the analytics decision (o) with its deadline; the service-worker disposition (i), assigned to L1-P2; and `AGENTS.md` §8 / §3 reconciliation, assigned to milestone close.
  - **Validation-honesty caveat** (M4-CLOSE discipline). `pre-commit run --all-files` green; the full non-visual parity suite green (**294 passed, 6 skipped**, zero failures) across `contract`, `dom-desktop`, `dom-mobile`, `behavior` and `native`; the extraction proven behaviour-preserving by an unchanged test count (162 → 162); and both new invariants proven to **bite** by deliberate negative checks — an undeclared `localStorage` read in a surface module, and a stray file in the staged web root, each producing the intended red before being reverted. **What that does not prove.** The **visual** projects were not run: they are valid only inside the pinned container and the Docker daemon needs an owner `sudo`. **The APK has never been built** — this machine has no JDK, no Android SDK and no Gradle, and the `android` CI job's first run is the first proof the shell compiles. **Nothing has run on a device:** that the app launches, that data survives a cold restart, that the backup exclusions are honoured by the OS, and what the service worker actually does inside the WebView are all owner-run observations (`docs/RUNBOOK.md`, "Android shell (Capacitor)"), and (i) stays formally open until the last of them is made.

## LSC-DL-002 — L1-P2 `local-schema-and-journal`: the schema freezes, the wrapper and its encryption are chosen together against primary sources, and three of the packet's own premises are corrected

- **Date.** 2026-08-12
- **Type.** Packet — L1-P2, the second packet of milestone **L1 "local structured core"**, and the point at which the local schema **freezes**: after the first live record, changing it means migrating a family history that exists nowhere else. Adds the DDL, the JS store, three test layers, six enforced invariants and a fifth CI job. **Product behaviour is unchanged on the web channel:** `app/m/v1/core/storage.js` and every call site are untouched, the parity baselines are unchanged and unre-blessed, and the store is inert wherever there is no Capacitor bridge.

- **Ladder reorder, recorded because it changes what this packet is.** The approved ladder is now **P1 capacitor-shell-parity → P2 local-schema-and-journal → P3 export-contour → P4 write-path-and-migration**, by owner act (vault ADR-046 §2.4). `docs/execution-map.md` carried the pre-reorder order and is corrected in this packet.

- **Decision.**

  a. **The wrapper is `@capacitor-community/sqlite` 8.1.1, and it is confined to raw SQL.** Chosen because it is the maintained Capacitor-8 plugin (peer `@capacitor/core >=8.0.0` against our 8.5.0, MIT, published 2026-08-06) that binds a **bundled** SQLite rather than the Android system one — which guarantees neither FTS5 nor a modern version, and that is the whole risk. Usage is confined to connection lifecycle plus raw `execute`/`executeSet`/`run`/`query`, declared as an allowlist in `app/m/v1/store/config.js` and enforced by test. None of its opinionated machinery is load-bearing: its JSON import/export is not our export contour (P3), its upgrade versioning is not our migration ledger (slot 14), and its sync tables would put `sql_deleted`/`last_modified` in our schema — which, per its own `Database.deleteSQL`, silently rewrites `DELETE` into a soft-delete `UPDATE`. Those two names are therefore **reserved** by `LSC-P2-INV-003`. The boundary in one line: **the wrapper is reversible, the schema is not.**

  b. **Encryption is chosen WITH the wrapper, not after it.** SQLCipher AES-256 through the same AAR (`net.zetetic:sqlcipher-android:4.17.0`), `androidIsEncryption: true`, on **from database creation**, so no plaintext database file ever exists on the device. The passphrase is minted on the device from `crypto.getRandomValues` (256 bits), never derived from anything the parent types, and never leaves the device. Where the plugin keeps it was **read in its vendored Android source rather than assumed**: `EncryptedSharedPreferences` behind an `AndroidKeyStore` `MasterKey` (`AES256_GCM`), in `CapacitorSQLite.java`. Biometric unlock is off — it would gate the family's own data behind a second failure mode. The **export** key is a different question and stays open for P3.

  c. **FTS5 yes, ICU no — verified by primary source, and the requirement's wording is corrected rather than the substance dropped.** `sqlcipher/sqlcipher-android` at `v4.17.0`, `sqlcipher/src/main/jni/sqlcipher/Android.mk`, compiles `-DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5` (with FTS4, FTS4_UNICODE61, JSON1, RTREE) and contains **no** `-DSQLITE_ENABLE_ICU` and links no ICU library; `sqlite.org/fts5.html` lists four built-in tokenizers (`unicode61`, `ascii`, `porter`, `trigram`), none of them ICU. Measured, not inferred: with `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, `ЁЛКА` matches `ёлка` (Cyrillic case folding works) but `ёлка` does **not** match `елка` and `растёт` does not match `растет` — `remove_diacritics` is Latin-script only, and `porter` is documented English-only. **ICU would not have closed that gap either**; its value is dictionary segmentation for scripts without spaces. The capability actually at stake is therefore a **fully rebuildable** index, which the schema secures: the FTS table holds no normalization decision, so any L2 word-form strategy is a rebuild, never a journal migration. **The upstream requirement still names ICU as mandatory.** That wording — not the substance — is what is wrong, and correcting it upstream is a milestone-close task; this entry records the divergence rather than marking the acceptance line satisfied.

  d. **The shipped assets import nothing from the npm tree, and the production web path acquires no bundler.** Read on disk at the pinned version: `@capacitor/android` 8.5.0 ships `capacitor/src/main/assets/native-bridge.js`, which the native layer **injects** into the WebView and which defines `Capacitor.nativePromise(pluginName, methodName, options)`; plugin registration is native-side through `capacitor.plugins.json`. So the store calls the plugin by name with zero JavaScript from `node_modules`, both channels stay byte-identical under `LSC-P1-INV-002`, and the handoff's premise that "native plugins force a build step" does not hold. **The named exit from buildless, decided here rather than discovered in P4:** the exit is **not taken in L1**. Its trigger is the first time a native dependency requires JavaScript we cannot author ourselves inside the shipped asset set. When that trigger fires the exit is **vendoring** — a version-pinned, hand-reviewed, checked-in file under `app/m/v{N}/vendor/` — and not a bundler, because vendoring preserves byte-identity between channels, the ship-list guard, the `CACHE_VERSION` discipline and the immutable-asset rule, all of which a bundler breaks. `BridgeSmokeTest` is what tells the difference, and it has **not yet run** (see the validation caveat).

  e. **The DDL is a shipped, publicly fetchable asset, and that is a decision rather than a side effect.** `app/m/v1/store/schema/001-core.sql` lives under the versioned mount, so `COPY m/` ships it in **both** channels and it is fetchable from the production web origin by anyone. One artifact is what makes the three test layers honest — the WebView fetches it, the desktop tests apply it, and the Android instrumented test reads it out of `assets/public/` — and a second copy would be a second thing to drift. The exposure is accepted with its reason stated: the whole buildless web channel is public by construction, the file contains **schema, not data**, and the moat is the canon, not the DDL. Recorded here so it cannot resurface later as an undiscussed exposure.

  f. **One append-only spine, typed detail tables.** `journal_entry` carries `seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` plus the fields every entry has (slot 1 author, slot 2 subject and visibility class, slot 11 event time and entry time held separately with their own UTC offsets, slot 16 id minted at creation); `assertion`, `confirmation` and `child_attribute` hold the kind-specific fields 1:1. One spine buys one monotonic cursor, one place to enforce append-only, one ordered log to reconstruct state from, and one list to model in a CRDT. Three independent append-only tables were rejected: the filing cursor would need a merged order across three sequences.

  g. **`seq` is local ARRIVAL order and no projection may use it — a defect the merge-semantics run found in this packet's own first draft.** The initial views picked the winning row per group with `max(seq)`. Modelling the journal in Automerge and Loro showed the failure directly: two devices holding an identical merged history assign `seq` differently, so a projection keyed on it makes them disagree about current state. Every projection now orders by `(entry_at_utc, id)`, a total order every replica computes identically, and `seq` keeps the one job it is right for — the resumable filing cursor, which must follow arrival precisely so that an entry about January written in March is not skipped. The counter-example is kept as a test rather than a comment.

  h. **Mutable state is expressed as projections, never as overwritten rows.** Stopped-time (slot 8), refresh/disputed status (slot 13) and every child attribute including gestational age and the three markers are journal events; the current value is a view. This is the conservative reading of slot 10 and it costs one join. `journal_cursor` is the single deliberately mutable row — a cursor is a position, not history — and the diary `record` stays overwrite-edited exactly as accompanying rule 1 states.

  i. **Slot 12 has three states, not two, and carries no default.** `record.sensitivity` is nullable with a two-value CHECK: `NULL` is **undeclared**, distinct from both `sensitive` and `not_sensitive`. A `DEFAULT` of not-sensitive would make "the family reviewed this and said it is fine" indistinguishable from "nobody was ever asked", which manufactures precisely the retro-labelling problem the slot exists to prevent — there is nothing to retro-label an accumulated corpus with. What a proactive surface does with an undeclared record is **projection-time policy and belongs to L5**, not a schema default. Owner decision; not a vault-verification item.

  j. **Slot 7 is recorded on the assertion and computed at projection time, and the grounding is written down so a later packet cannot re-open it by accident.** `assertion.prerequisite_propagation` is a two-value enum capturing author intent; the implication itself is applied by a pure function over the projection, with the KB prerequisite graph **injected** rather than imported. The grounding: slot 1 defines a mark as an **attributed assertion**, and ADR-015 governs provenance — materialising implied prerequisites as journal rows would fabricate assertions the parent never made, so projection-time computation is the only form compatible with the slot. Implied rows are returned marked `derived`, with a null author and a pointer to the authored assertion they came from.

  k. **Identifiers are UUIDv4 from `crypto.randomUUID()`, minted at creation.** No coordination needed, so they survive the L7 merge as the CRDT keys; no embedded timestamp to leak in a "safe id"; no dependency. Local ordering is `seq`, so a sortable id would buy nothing. Slot 16 says ids cannot be handed out retroactively, and the append-only triggers make that structural: an id cannot be changed after the fact.

  l. **The privacy shape is smaller than the model needs, on purpose.** `participant` has **no name column** and `child` has **no name column** — attribution needs an id, not an identity, and named participants arrive with L7 grants. The child's name is an attribute event inside the encrypted store. Nothing is emitted anywhere by this packet.

  m. **Three test layers, chosen so that the un-runnable claim is as small as possible.** (1) Desktop, Python + the standard library's SQLite, in the existing `quality` job — schema invariants, projections, the closed lists, the cursor, disk-full and index rebuild. It applies the DDL **through a faithful port of the wrapper's own statement splitter**, because that splitter is a heuristic: it splits on `";\n"` and re-joins a trigger body only when a fragment trims to exactly `END`, so a trigger written across lines would be cut in half and fail **on the device** while passing every ordinary desktop test. The DDL therefore keeps **every trigger on one line**, and that rule is enforced by test rather than by convention. (2) Merge semantics, in the `contract` project, against both CRDT candidates. (3) The real engine, on an emulator. What remains un-runnable off-device is now only what genuinely requires the engine — which is the point of (1) and (2).

  n. **The instrumented job is not a per-push gate, by owner decision on spend, and the consequence is stated rather than hidden.** `android-instrumented` runs on `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` only: the repository is private, so an emulator boot on every push is billable minutes spent re-proving a schema that changes once. The cost is that a regression introduced by a later packet is caught at PR time rather than at push time, possibly several commits after its cause. `workflow_dispatch` is added at the workflow level so the owner can run it on demand.

  o. **The sixteen slots and the five rules, enumerated rather than claimed.** The slots are mapped one-by-one in `app/tests/schema/test_store_slots.py::SLOT_COVERAGE`, each naming the schema object that carries it **and** the test that exercises it, with both asserted live. The five accompanying rules are enumerated in the same file's `RULE_COVERAGE`: rule 1 (diary edited by overwrite) → `test_store_append_only::test_the_record_is_editable_by_overwrite`; rule 2 (deleting a record does not revoke its marks) → `test_store_append_only::test_deleting_a_record_does_not_revoke_its_marks`; rule 3 (a state snapshot is a derived projection) → `test_store_projections::test_state_at_a_past_date_is_reconstructed_from_the_journal`; rule 4 (retrieval indexes are derived and recomputed on edits) → `test_store_corruption::test_the_index_is_fully_rebuildable_from_the_records`; rule 5 (the export artifact stays human-readable and self-describing for years without the app) → **deferred to L1-P3**, because it is a requirement on the export contour rather than a slot in this schema. Four closed here, one addressed with its address.

  p. **Three of the handoff's premises did not survive contact with the repository, and were reported rather than served.** (1) "CI triggers on `pull_request` only, so the `android` job has never run" — false: the workflow has triggered on `push` since M1-P3, and run `31549578012` shows `android: success` at `fbe6340`. The scope item was **withdrawn on owner confirmation**; no edit was spent on it. The real gap was different and larger — `assembleDebug` proves the shell compiles and nothing about the engine — which is what (m)(3) addresses. (2) "Native plugins force a build step" — false, see (d). (3) "A default profile always exists is an assumption the tracker relies on and nothing enforces" — the opposite is on record: auto-creating one was **rejected** as an owner decision in the A0 spa-polish entry, in favour of honest degradation at the write. The defensible form of the item was implemented instead: no family datum can exist without an author and a subject (`LSC-P2-INV-005`), and bootstrap creates the `is_self` participant and **no child**.

- **Rationale.** The packet's one irreversible artifact is the schema, so everything else was arranged to protect it. That is why the wrapper is confined to raw SQL and the encryption chosen in the same breath (a swap later must not touch stored bytes); why the projections are views rather than tables (a projection rule can be corrected, a materialised snapshot cannot); why mutable state is event-sourced (the conservative reading costs a join and removes a class of irreversible loss); and why the merge run happened before the freeze rather than after — it found (g), which would have been a silent divergence between two family devices years later, discovered as "the app disagrees with itself". The three premise corrections follow the same rule as `LSC-DL-001` (k): a claim carries its provenance, and a scope item justified by a false premise is reported, not quietly performed.

- **No dedicated ADR by design at the repo layer.** Decided upstream: **PDR-026** §4 body + amendment 2026-08-04 + overlay 2026-08-11 (the sixteen slots and the five rules; L1 as the single freeze point); **PDR-033** (slot 6 composition, the structural invariant, the closed do-not-collect list); **ADR-046** owner block 2026-08-12 (§2.1 merge semantics as the seventeenth slot, plain SQLite, both libraries checked, choice deferred to L7; §2.5 bundled-SQLite wrapper with encryption chosen alongside; §1 corruption detection, supply-chain discipline, filing cursor; §2.4 the ladder reorder; §2.3 the export key still open); **ADR-043** §1/§2/§5; **PDR-031** §1/§2/§6; **PDR-025** §2/§3/§6 + overlay 2026-08-12; **ADR-042** §3.2/§3.3; **ADR-015**; **ADR-040** §3; **PDR-021** OQ#6; **PDR-024** §3. This entry records what the repository did with those.

- **Alternatives considered.**
  1. **Write an in-repo minimal Capacitor plugin over `net.zetetic:sqlcipher-android` directly.** Genuinely attractive — smaller Java surface, none of `androidx.room`/`biometric`/`security-crypto`/`jeep-sqlite`, exact error granularity. Rejected for this packet: it spends the schema-freeze packet's budget on the one component that is replaceable, and hand-rolls Keystore custody the plugin already ships. Reconsider at P3/L7 if the wrapper obstructs.
  2. **Commission a custom SQLCipher AAR built with `-DSQLITE_ENABLE_ICU`.** Rejected — an owned native build in the supply chain, tens of megabytes of ICU data, an NDK/`minSdk` question (Android's public `libicu` is API 31+ against `minSdkVersion 24`), and it still would not fold `ё`/`е` or lemmatise Russian. See (c).
  3. **`DEFAULT 'not_sensitive'` on `record.sensitivity`.** Rejected on owner correction — see (i).
  4. **Materialise implied prerequisites as journal rows.** Rejected — see (j).
  5. **Key projections on `max(seq)`.** Written, then rejected when the merge run showed it diverging across replicas — see (g).
  6. **Store the state-at-a-date snapshot.** Rejected — accompanying rule 3 says a snapshot is a derived projection, not a stored file. Bound the as-of date through a one-row `projection_context` table instead, since SQLite views take no parameters, so the projection has exactly one definition shared by the app and the tests.
  7. **A separate database file for the private area.** Rejected — a table-level partition with `v_shared_journal` as the declared, tested export set gives the same guarantee now and keeps a second file (and a second key) out of a packet that has no sync to serve.
  8. **Give `assertion.source_record_id` a foreign key with `ON DELETE SET NULL`.** Rejected — an FK action would MUTATE an append-only row. Provenance degradation is derived by outer join instead, which is also what makes `v_assertion_provenance` able to say `degraded` out loud (ADR-015).
  9. **Run the desktop schema tests in Node via `node:sqlite`.** Rejected — FTS5 in Node's bundled SQLite is unverified, and this packet does not get to assume a capability it is chartered to verify. Python's is verified and already gated.
  10. **Auto-create a default child at bootstrap.** Rejected — it re-opens a decision the owner already made. See (p)(3).
  11. **Precache the DDL in the service worker.** Rejected — only the native channel fetches it, and that channel does not use the worker; `cache.addAll` is atomic, so adding a file no code path requests only grows the install payload.
  12. **Run the instrumented job on every push.** Rejected on owner decision — see (n).
  13. **Disable service-worker registration in the native build.** Not taken **and not decided**: see the debt note below.

- **Supersedes.** None. **Corrects** the pre-reorder ladder in `docs/execution-map.md`, per the reorder note above, and the "fifteen NON-ENTRY modules" count in `app/index.html`, which this packet's own additions made false.

- **Effects.**
  - **Added (`app/m/v1/store/`):** `schema/001-core.sql` (the frozen DDL), `config.js`, `errors.js`, `bridge.js`, `store.js`, `journal.js`, `boot.js`.
  - **Added (tests):** `app/tests/schema/` (Python: `__init__.py`, `conftest.py`, `harness.py` and seven `test_store_*.py` modules), `app/tests/merge-semantics.spec.js`, `app/tests/store-supply-chain.spec.js`, `app/tests/store-unit.spec.js`, and `native/android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/theygrow/{StoreEngineTest,BridgeSmokeTest}.java`.
  - **Changed (shipped `app/` files — the first product-file change of this milestone):** `m/v1/app.js` (one import; `initNativeStore()` fired and deliberately not awaited), `index.html` (six `modulepreload` hints, and the corrected module count), `sw.js` (`CACHE_VERSION` `v9` → **`v10`** and six precache entries — required because the shell's import graph grew, and `A1-P4-INV-001`/`A1-P6-INV-001` assert both lists against it).
  - **Changed (native):** `native/package.json` + `package-lock.json` (the pinned plugin), `native/capacitor.config.json` (`plugins.CapacitorSQLite.androidIsEncryption`), the `cap sync`-generated `android/capacitor.settings.gradle`, `android/app/capacitor.build.gradle` and `android/app/src/main/assets/capacitor.plugins.json`, and `android/app/build.gradle` (androidTest-only dependencies).
  - **Changed (harness):** `app/playwright.config.js` (three specs into the `contract` project), `app/package.json` + `package-lock.json` (two dev-only CRDT libraries), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (a `pytest app/tests/schema` step, `workflow_dispatch`, and the `android-instrumented` job), `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (the mypy hook covers `app/tests/schema`; `additional_dependencies` **unchanged** — the new Python imports the standard library and pytest only).
  - **Changed (spine):** `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (`LSC-P2-INV-001`…`006`), `docs/execution-map.md` (the ladder reorder and the P2 entry), `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (the store's on-device smoke and the emulator job).
  - **Untouched, and verified so:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/RUNTIME-INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/product/**`, every build-config, `app/Dockerfile`, `app/nginx.conf`, `app/docker-entrypoint.sh`, `app/kb-v1.json`, `app/manifest.json`, `app/offline.html`, `app/icons/`, every prior decision-log entry, and everything under `api/**`.
  - **Operability (ADR-013 / contract §4.7).** **Knobs: seven, all in one place.** `app/m/v1/store/config.js` holds the database name, schema version, DDL url and name, SQLite version floor, journal mode, busy timeout, integrity-check policy, cursor batch size and passphrase bits — each with `changed_in: LSC-DL-002`, none as a scattered literal, and the object frozen at runtime with a test that says so. The typed versioned surface of ADR-013 is `api/theygrow_api/parameters.py`, which is server-side and untouched by a device-local packet; this follows the standing front-side precedent set by `CACHE_VERSION` (`PWA-DL-001`). `PARAMETERS_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays **5**. **Signals: none this packet.** No taxonomy entry, no `emitted_now` change, no GA4 event; a store-open failure is logged to the device console (engine text only, never family text) because there is no write path yet for a signal to describe. **No new Python runtime import.**
  - **§4-safe.** No family data, credential, host or live identifier enters the repository. The DDL is schema, not data, and its publication is decided in (e). The store adds **no egress of any kind**: it opens a local encrypted file and fetches one same-origin local asset.
  - **Debt recorded, not fixed.** (1) **The service-worker disposition inside the WebView stays OPEN.** `LSC-P1-INV-001`'s scope and the execution map both assign it to this packet; it is **not** in this packet's approved scope list, and it is a product-behaviour change to the native channel, so it was not taken unilaterally. It is carried to **L1-P4**, the packet that changes native-channel behaviour anyway, and it is flagged rather than closed. (2) The export key (P3). (3) The ICU wording upstream, per (c). (4) The analytics decision from `LSC-DL-001` (o), with its unchanged deadline.
  - **Validation-honesty caveat** (M4-CLOSE discipline). Green locally: `pre-commit run --all-files` and `--files` over the new untracked paths; `pytest app/tests/schema` (**81 passed**); the `contract` project (**277 passed**), which is where the merge-semantics run, the supply-chain guard and the store unit tests live. **What that does not prove.** The browser-driven parity projects (`dom-desktop`, `dom-mobile`, `behavior`, `native`, `visual-*`) **could not be run on the development machine at all**: its Playwright browser is missing system libraries (`libnspr4.so`) that only a privileged install can provide, so the claim "no product behaviour changed" rests on the `parity` CI job and on the owner-run container, not on a local run. **The four device claims are now closed on the emulator, and this paragraph is corrected rather than left standing.** It read that nothing in this packet had touched a device and that `BridgeSmokeTest`/`StoreEngineTest` had never executed; both were true when written and are no longer. The job was run twice by `workflow_dispatch`. Run `31606284003`: nine of eleven passed — the injected bridge reaches the plugin with **no** bundled JavaScript (the premise (d) rests on), the bundled engine compiles FTS5 in, the DDL applies to SQLCipher through the wrapper's splitter, the engine clears the version floor, the database is encrypted, WAL is available, the append-only triggers fire and the index rebuilds. Run `31612297495`: **all eleven passed**, including `the_app_opens_its_encrypted_store_at_boot` — the app opens its store at boot **through the shipped modules**, in WAL, at schema version 1, with the `is_self` participant bootstrapped. Neither run's failures were engine facts: both were harness defects, one of them this packet's own (the boot probe imported a path-absolute specifier from `WebView.evaluateJavascript`, which has no base URL of its own; the shipped modules resolve the same specifier from a page module and were never implicated) and one inherited (below). **What still rests on CI rather than on a local run is unchanged:** the browser-driven parity projects, for the reason given above.
  - **Two inherited leftovers of the generated Android project — which is what makes it a pattern rather than a bug.** The `android-instrumented` job's first real executions turned up two defects that were neither this packet's design nor the engine's behaviour, but debt that arrived with `npx cap add android` in L1-P1 and sat unobserved. (1) The scaffolded `ExampleInstrumentedTest` asserted capacitor's own placeholder application id `com.getcapacitor.app` against this app's `app.theygrow`; the expectation was stale, the packaging was right, and the literal was corrected. (2) `capacitor-cordova-android-plugins` resolves `kotlin-stdlib` 1.8.22 (through `androidx.appcompat`) alongside the `kotlin-stdlib-jdk7`/`jdk8` 1.6.21 shims (through `org.apache.cordova:framework`); Kotlin folded those shims' classes into the stdlib at 1.8, so `checkDebugAndroidTestDuplicateClasses` finds ~20 classes in two jars and fails the run. **The masking mechanism is the same one in both directions, and is worth naming:** gradle abandons a build at the first failing task, so while `:app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` was red the cordova module's check was never reached at all — run `31606284003` executes only `:app:checkDebugAndroidTestDuplicateClasses` — and the duplicate-class defect could surface only once every assertion passed. A red job hid a second red. Underneath both sits (n): the emulator job is not a per-push gate, so generated-project debt accumulates between PRs with nothing looking at it. **Fixed in `native/android/build.gradle`** — a dependency constraint raising the two shims to the stdlib line, on `androidTest` configurations of that one module, chosen over an exclude because the version is what is wrong, not the presence. Placement is the load-bearing part: the defective module's own `build.gradle` is rewritten by `@capacitor/cli` on every `cap sync` and is not committed, so a fix written there would vanish at the next sync while still reading green; the root file is generated once by `cap add` and never touched again. Nothing reaches the shipped APK's graph. **Also changed:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now dumps `adb logcat` inside the emulator step and uploads it on every run — the emulator is destroyed when the action returns, and a store that fails to open would otherwise report only a poll timeout with its reason left on a machine that no longer exists.

## LSC-DL-003 — L1-P3 `export-contour`: the family history gets a way out that needs no key, no account and no company, and the packet's own inherited scope is corrected against an owner gate

- **Date.** 2026-08-12
- **Type.** Packet — L1-P3, first checkpoint. *(Namespace note: continues the `LSC-DL` namespace opened by `LSC-DL-001`; packets keep `L1-P{k}`. The "Entry format" header is intentionally left unedited, per the `L2-DL-002` / `A3-DL-002` precedent.)*
- **Scope narrowed by owner gate, recorded because it changes what this packet is.** The approved scope for P3 as this repository recorded it — `docs/execution-map.md`, "encrypted dump, self-describing file export, restore procedure in the RUNBOOK, and the export-key question (still an open owner fork)" — was **superseded by an owner gate closed immediately before the packet opened**. P3 now ships exactly **one** object: the durable, unencrypted, keyless artifact. The encrypted operational snapshot, its key and its recovery channels move to **L7**, with the relay and the key-scope model that are its only consumers. The pre-migration rollback copy was redefined by the same gate as an **operational** byte-for-byte snapshot of the encrypted database file taken after a WAL checkpoint and restored on the same device; it is not an export, does not reuse this contour, and is addressed to the first schema migration (L2 or later). The export-key question is therefore **closed, not carried**: this artifact has no key. Three shipped comments and one spine file said otherwise and are corrected here.
- **Executed in two checkpoints on one branch, by owner instruction.** This entry covers the first: the artifact, the sink, the surface and the docs, with **no print layer**. The PDF/A-2b print layer, its vendored font and ICC profile, its structural checker and its veraPDF verification land in the second checkpoint, and amend this entry rather than replacing it. The split exists because the print layer is comparable in size to the entire rest of the contour and carries the conformance question, and a failure inside it should not sit in the same unreviewable diff as a working artifact.
- **Decision.**
  - **a. Two objects, not one, because the requirements are opposite.** Privacy wants the family's history encrypted; readability across decades forbids it, because a key is lost long before the data is. One object cannot serve both, so there are two, and only the unencrypted one is on this rung. The artifact needs no key, no passphrase, no account, no subscription check and no network: it is produced entirely on the device and would still open if the vendor disappeared.
  - **b. The artifact's field names ARE the frozen schema's column names.** The published vocabulary is one that is already designed, already reviewed and already documented, rather than a second one invented for the export and kept in sync with the first forever. `seq` is the one column deliberately withheld — see (d).
  - **c. One declaration file, three readers, and a fourth copy inside every archive.** `app/m/v1/export/declaration.json` holds the format id, the file list, every dataset's query, every column and a plain-Russian explanation of what each field means. The builder reads it, `app/tests/export/` drives its assertions from it, and a **verbatim** copy travels inside the artifact's `index.json`. This is the `001-core.sql` arrangement applied to the export, and it is what makes "self-describing" checkable rather than asserted: the blind reader in `app/tests/export/blind_reader.py` navigates by the embedded copy alone and imports nothing but the Python standard library.
  - **d. The artifact is ordered by `(entry_at_utc, id)`, and `seq` does not travel.** `seq` is local arrival order; two devices holding identical histories assign it differently, so an artifact ordered by it would differ between them. The pair is the total order every replica computes identically — the same rule the projections use, for the same reason, found by the L1-P2 merge-semantics run.
  - **e. Determinism is stated precisely rather than approximately.** Same journal and same `exported_at_utc` gives a byte-identical archive; same journal and a different export time gives archives differing in `MANIFEST.json` alone. The weaker second half is what makes the first half useful — it says the variation is in one named place instead of smeared across the archive — and both directions plus an anti-vacuity direction are tested.
  - **f. Nothing is compressed.** Zip method 0, STORED. DEFLATE output is not byte-stable across implementations or versions, which would make (e) unstateable across devices; a stored archive is recoverable by hand if its central directory is ever damaged; and media does not travel this channel, so the bytes saved would be small. The zip writer is hand-written for the same reason the store imports nothing from npm: vendoring a compressor would add a supply-chain surface and a second thing that must still behave identically in 2044.
  - **g. Scope is the REQUESTING PARTICIPANT, not "all private areas" — a narrowing taken on owner instruction.** The parent's own private records belong in the parent's own archive; a co-parent's do not. On this rung there is one participant, so behaviour is identical either way. It is declared this way because the format is **published**: a declaration promising "all private areas" would already have committed the product, at L7, to putting someone else's private records into a third party's archive. The parameter binds by name and an unknown name raises rather than binding `NULL`.
  - **h. Media does not travel, and the interface says so before the button.** Two sentences — that media is not in the archive, and that there is no cloud backup of this data — appear in the modal that precedes the action, verbatim, and again inside the artifact's own README, because the interface will not exist when the README is read. Both are asserted as exact strings so they cannot drift into a hedge one word at a time.
  - **i. `attachments/` ships empty and explains itself.** The approved scope lists "attachments as-is" alongside "media is NOT included"; the reconciliation taken is that media never travels this channel, and the directory exists so the structure does not have to change when a non-media attachment class arrives. Recorded as a reading of an apparent tension, not as a derivation.
  - **j. The sink is a first-party Android plugin over `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT`, not a filesystem plugin.** SAF needs **no storage permission at all**: the system picker returns a URI for the single document the parent chose, and the plugin can write that document and nothing else — it cannot list, read, delete, or pick a path. `@capacitor/filesystem` would have granted a far wider capability than the contour needs and added an npm dependency to a shipped surface that deliberately has none. One method in the plugin, one method on the app-side allowlist, and the count is asserted.
  - **k. Written on an explicit human action and at no other moment.** No timer, no retry, no queue, no lifecycle listener anywhere in the contour; the surface listens for `click` and nothing else. An unencrypted archive appearing on the filesystem without a person asking for it in that moment is the failure this forbids, and it is compiled into a gate rather than left as an intention.
  - **l. Full archives, never incremental.** A chain loses everything after the first broken link, and this object exists precisely for the case where something has already gone wrong.
  - **m. The web channel gets no archive, and says so instead of hiding.** Off Capacitor the store is inert by construction and there is no journal to project. The surface ships to both channels byte-identically and detects capability at runtime — the P1/P2 pattern. **The consequence is named rather than buried:** a parent using only the PWA has their marks in `localStorage` and no archive until they use the Android app. Exporting `localStorage` directly would mean a second published format for data that P4 is about to migrate.
  - **n. The export modules join the shipped import graph statically.** The ship-list walker models static imports only and fails closed on a dynamic one, so lazy-loading the builder would have made it invisible to the gate that proves modules are shipped and precached. The store graph pays the same cost for the same reason; what it costs is ten `modulepreload` hints the browser fetches without evaluating.
  - **o. `declaration.json` is NOT precached, and the reasoning is the DDL's.** `app/sw.js` already declines to precache `001-core.sql` because only the native channel fetches it and that channel does not use the worker. Both halves hold here as well — and by (m) the web channel does not run an export at all — so precaching the runtime-fetched artifacts would cost bytes to precisely the channel that cannot use them. The ten JS modules **are** precached, because the import graph reaches them and an installed client must not boot offline with a broken graph.
  - **p. The RUNBOOK gets a "reading the archive without the app" procedure, not a restore procedure.** The execution map promised "restore procedure in the RUNBOOK", but restore implies import, and import is L6; writing one here would document a capability that does not exist.
  - **q. The footer's right-edge pin is bound to the activities button by id, not to whatever is last.** `.filter-toggle-btn:last-child { margin-left: auto }` was correct with two buttons and silently wrong with three: the export button inherited the pin and **«Подходящие активности» moved 605 px left**, out of the right edge and into the left cluster. This was found by measuring the re-blessed PNGs against `HEAD` rather than by looking at the screenshots — the desktop diffs began at x≈383, far left of where a merely-appended button could start, and the purple-ink spans went from `[(30,382), (1003,1249)]` to `[(30,382), (398,645), (1057,1249)]`. The rule is now `#activitiesBtn { margin-left: auto }`, and the export button sits **before** activities in DOM order, in the left cluster: an export is a rare, deliberate act that does not need the visual weight of the right edge, and this leaves both existing controls exactly where they were. A positional selector that pins "whatever happens to be last" is a trap for the next control added; an id says what it means.
  - **r. The mobile footer DOES jump on filter toggle, and it took three measurements to establish it — the sequence is the lesson, so it is recorded rather than tidied.** **(1) The first measurement was right for the wrong reason.** Pixel analysis of the baseline PNGs reported the footer at 69 px normally and 55 px with the ZPD filter active. Both detectors behind it were unsound: one hunted the footer's `border-top` as a 1 px `#dddddd` line, which is the DESKTOP rule — the mobile border is `0.5px solid rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)` — so it was locking onto a table gridline; the other took the topmost full-width row whose edge pixels are white, which the empty table area satisfies exactly as well as the footer does. The conclusion happened to be correct; the instrument did not support it. **(2) The second measurement was sound and wrong.** `app/tests/footer-height.spec.js` drives a real browser, toggles the filter and reads `getBoundingClientRect()` — a proper instrument. On the development machine it reported 68.78 px in both states and no jump, so the claim was withdrawn and the fix removed. **(3) The container settled it.** `scripts/parity-suite.sh` in the pinned container reds that same test: **68.78 px → 55 px on toggle**. The jump is real, the pin is reinstated (w), and the withdrawal recorded in the previous revision of this entry is itself withdrawn. **What is separately true:** the −14 px content shift measured between `HEAD` and the three-button build of `shell-zpd-empty-state.png` was caused by this packet's own third footer button and left with it (u) — a different effect that was briefly conflated with this one.
  - **r-bis. The rule that falls out of it, offered as standing practice rather than as a note on this packet.** **A claim about rendered geometry counts only from the pinned container; a local run is good for logic and not for pixels.** `app/tests/visual.spec.js` already says the visual baselines are container-only, and `scripts/parity-suite.sh` already refuses to bless them elsewhere — but the assumption underneath was that the restriction is about *screenshot diffing*. It is not. It is about **layout**: the same declarations resolve to different boxes here and there, because font metrics differ, so any assertion that reads a measured size or position inherits the same restriction even when it takes no screenshot. This packet removed a correct fix on the strength of a local number and needed the arbiter to put it back. **Proposed for the contract at milestone close, not adopted unilaterally here:** a browser-driven measurement is evidence only from the container; locally it may falsify (a red is still a red) but it may not confirm. Note the asymmetry, which is what makes the rule cheap to follow — a local run that goes red is still worth acting on; a local run that goes green proves nothing about geometry.

  - **s. Positional selectors in a control strip are a trap, and this packet sprang it twice in one footer — so the strip was swept.** Both traps had the same shape: a rule that says *where* a control sits while meaning *which* control it is. `.filter-toggle-btn:last-child { margin-left: auto }` meant "the activities button hugs the right edge" and said "whatever is last"; `footer button:nth-child(3) { flex: 1 1 auto }` meant "the newly added button", said "the third one", and after the DOM reorder selected «Подходящие активности» instead. Both are now bound by id (`#activitiesBtn`, `#exportBtn`). The sweep also found the one positional rule that is **correct and was left alone**: `footer button:not(:last-child)::after` draws a divider after every button but the last, which is n−1 dividers for n buttons — genuinely about position, right at any count, and rebinding it to an id would break it. **The rule worth keeping:** in a strip of sibling controls, bind a declaration by identity when it is about a particular control, and by position only when the geometry itself is the intent. The test is whether the rule still means the same thing after a sibling is inserted. **Also recorded rather than quietly fixed:** `#exportBtn { flex: 1 1 auto }` restates the value the block's base rule already gives every footer button, so it is inert at any binding — it was a defensive restatement when it was written and it still is. It was rebound rather than deleted because deleting it is a judgement about someone else's intent that this packet was not asked to make.
  - **u. The export control lives in the HEADER, not the footer — owner act, a scope amendment rather than a defect fix.** It sits immediately left of the chat control: a downward arrow, the "get a file out" convention. Deliberately **not** a floppy disk, which means "save inside the app" and is besides a dead object to label an artifact whose whole purpose is being readable in twenty years. On desktop it is icon **plus** a visible text label; on mobile the label is hidden and the icon stands alone. `aria-label` and `title` carry the same string as the visible label, asserted equal by test, so the two viewports can never end up naming the same action differently. The footer returns to its two original buttons and its markup is byte-identical to `HEAD` again — the `dom-*/control-footer.html` baselines that this packet had moved now match without being blessed at all.
  - **v. «Чат сообщества» becomes an icon — owner act, and named here because P3 did not originally charter it.** This is a deliberate change to an **existing** control that the export packet did not set out to touch, recorded separately so the PR does not read as if an unrelated edit slipped in. Three things changed. The glyph is now a plain outline paper plane authored in-repo — the previous one was a filled mark inside a circle, close enough to Telegram's own to be a trademark question, and a generic paper plane is the ordinary convention for "message"; no icon font, no package, no external fetch. The control is icon-only on **both** viewports; on mobile it previously hid the icon and injected the words «Чат сообщества» through a `::after` pseudo-element, which is text that cannot be selected, cannot be translated by a page translator and is not an accessible name. And the name moved into the markup: `aria-label`/`title` are now «Чат сообщества», matching the label that used to be visible, in place of a long marketing `title` and an `aria-label` that named a third-party product.
  - **w. The footer control height is pinned to two lines, and the pin ships with the detector for what pinning costs.** Mechanism: `height: calc(2lh + 16px)` with `overflow: hidden` on the mobile footer controls, so the height stops depending on how many lines a label takes. `lh` is the element's own line height, so `2lh` is **two lines by definition** in whatever metrics the engine is using — and that is precisely why the declaration is the right form. The identical declaration resolves to ~49.8 px on the development machine and ~68.78 px in the pinned container; a measured pixel constant would have been correct in exactly one of the two environments, which is the trap (r) walked into from the other direction. `16px` is the vertical padding from the same rule under `box-sizing: border-box`; the 36 px touch floor it replaces is covered with room to spare. Rejected: a pixel `min-height` (per above, and it still lets a longer label grow the box), and stacking both filter labels in a grid cell so the box takes their maximum — genuinely label-proof, but it means restructuring the button's DOM and the code that swaps its text, a write-path change this packet has no business making. **The pin trades a visible failure for an invisible one**, so `app/tests/footer-height.spec.js` asserts, in both filter states at 412×760, that no control's `scrollHeight`/`scrollWidth` exceeds its client box — a label that outgrows two lines now reds there instead of losing a line where nobody looks. Shown to bite before being trusted: narrowing the reserve to `1lh` reds it with `needs 50px inside 33px` in both states. Its sibling assertion — that toggling the filter does not move the footer — is the one the container used to overturn (r), and it is not adjusted to accommodate anything. **Known limit:** `lh` needs Chrome/WebView 109 or newer; on anything older the declaration is invalid and dropped and the footer reverts to the jumping behaviour, which the toggle assertion would then report from the container. **Unverified at the time of writing:** the pin is reinstated on the container's evidence, and per (r-bis) it cannot be confirmed locally — the container run is what closes it.
  - **y. The chat control becomes visually secondary, as a consequence of (u) rather than as a styling preference.** Once the export control carries a label and the chat control does not, two identically-filled purple boxes at very different widths read as *one button whose label failed to render* — the eye infers truncation, not hierarchy. The grounding is in the decision layer: the archive is the only material form of a permanent product promise (free, local, keyless, readable even if the vendor is gone, PDR-020 §3 / PDR-022), while the community link is a convenience. Primary versus secondary is what the two controls actually are, so the size difference should read as rank. The chat control is now outline — transparent ground, `--primary-purple` border and glyph, no shadow, lavender on hover — against the export control's solid fill, on both viewports. Both accessible names are unchanged.
  - **z. The print layer ships as PDF/A-2b and CLAIMS it, with the certifying check in the job that already pays for expensive verification.** Owner resolution of E1, and it is a fourth branch rather than one of the three the plan offered: ship the conformance **and** buy the verdict, but put the verdict where costly checks already live. The hand-written structural checker (`app/tests/export/test_pdf_structure.py`, standard library only) stays in the free per-push gate and covers what reading the bytes can establish — no `/Encrypt`, every `FontDescriptor` carrying a `FontFile2`, an `OutputIntent` with an embedded `/N 3` profile, an unfiltered XMP packet declaring `pdfaid:part` 2 / conformance B, XMP dates agreeing with the document information dictionary, a trailer `/ID`, and an xref whose every offset is followed to the object it claims to start. The certifying half is **veraPDF `--flavour 2b`, added to the existing `android-instrumented` job**, which already sets up Java 21 and is `pull_request` + `workflow_dispatch` only. **The consequence is stated rather than hidden, and it is the trade already accepted for the device layer: a conformance regression is caught at PR or on dispatch, not at push, so a red can arrive several commits after its cause.** The fixture it validates is built by the shipped builder through the same `app/tests/export/harness.py` the pytest suite uses (`emit_fixture.py`, standard library, no pytest install), so the file veraPDF certifies is the file the tests assert on rather than a third thing made for the validator. **The validator itself could not be pinned, so its drift is detected instead — the second of the two routes, taken only after the first was checked and found unavailable.** A real pin was attempted first, on the same discipline the font and the ICC profile get: `veraPDF/veraPDF-apps` publishes **no GitHub releases at all**, `veraPDF/veraPDF-library` tags carry source with **zero binary assets**, and <https://verapdf.org/software/> links exactly two unversioned URLs (`/rel/` and `/dev/`) — there is no versioned installer to pin a URL or a SHA-256 to. So `VERAPDF_EXPECTED_VERSION` is declared as a knob in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with `changed_in: LSC-DL-003`, and the install step **fails** when the installed version differs, with an error naming what to do about it. A silent upgrade of the tool that certifies our public PDF/A claim must arrive as a red run and a deliberate decision, not as a line in a log nobody reads. The URL also moved to the canonical `/rel/` path the download page actually publishes.
  - **z-bis. The first conformance gate could never pass, and the print layer was conformant all along.** Run `31637683475` failed the `Validate the print layer against PDF/A-2b` step. The verdict itself was **PASS**: veraPDF 1.30.2 printed `PASS …/archive.pdf 2b`, and the machine-readable report recorded `isCompliant="true"` with **144 rules passed, 0 failed, 2779 checks passed, 0 failed**. What failed was the gate's own success condition — `grep -q 'compliant="true"'` — because veraPDF writes the attribute as **`isCompliant`, with a capital C**, so the lowercase substring occurs in no report, passing or failing. The step would have gone red on a perfect file every time. **A gate that cannot pass is worth exactly as little as one that cannot fail**, and a substring match against another tool's output is how both happen. The verdict is now parsed as XML and every field carrying it is checked — `isCompliant`, `failedRules`, `failedChecks` — plus the anti-vacuity one: a report that performed **zero checks** is not a pass. The parser was exercised against the real report (exit 0) and against three doctored ones — non-compliant, empty, zero-checks — which fail with a named cause. **Two consequences worth recording.** The claim was never in doubt and no retitling was applied; and because the step sits before the emulator, run `31637683475` produced **no device evidence at all** — the instrumented tests never ran.
  - **z-ter. A Gradle wrapper bootstrap failure was classified CLASS B — upstream — on evidence that settles it, and the boundary of that evidence is recorded with it.** Run `31640121268` failed the `android` job in 11–17 s with `java.net.SocketException: Unexpected end of file from server`, thrown from `org.gradle.wrapper.Install.forceFetch` via `GradleWrapperMain.main` while reading `https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-8.14.3-all.zip`. **Read the stack first: this is the wrapper fetching Gradle ITSELF**, before any build script is evaluated or any dependency resolved, so nothing in this repository beyond `distributionUrl` can influence it. **What settles the class:** commit `0f8ae0a` produced two CI runs created in the same second — `31640121253` (push) and `31640121268` (dispatch) — and their `android` jobs both started at `20:56:20Z`. One went **green**, one **red**. Same job, same commit, same configuration, same second; no configuration defect can produce that. The same URL also downloaded successfully at `20:58:59Z` in `android-instrumented` on that commit. **The boundary, stated so nobody writes past it:** the logs establish the CLASS, not the upstream's reason. Whether it was per-VM egress reputation, a CDN edge, or rate limiting is not determinable from here, and a mechanism must not be written into this log that the logs do not support — the re-run at `21:10:28Z` failed while running alone, which already refutes the tidy "two concurrent jobs hit the CDN" story. **The next red of this shape** — sub-20-second `android` failure, `GradleWrapperMain` in the stack, `services.gradle.org` in the line above — is this, and should be recognised rather than re-diagnosed. **No retry loop, no `--offline`, no mirror:** if the reset recurs it must still surface as a red run.
  - **z-quater. Two changes follow from it, both narrowing exposure rather than masking it.** **(1) The wrapper takes `-bin` instead of `-all`.** The `-all` archive is **224 584 249 bytes (214 MiB)** against `-bin`'s **137 393 837 bytes (131 MiB)**; the extra 83 MiB is the Gradle sources, which exist so an IDE can offer them and which neither CI nor this project reads. Same host, same version — a smaller transfer through the path that reset, not a fix for the reset. **(2) `android` no longer runs on `workflow_dispatch`.** A dispatch on an already-pushed commit duplicates the entire workflow, so the same APK was being built twice at the same instant — that duplication is what produced the green/red pair above, and it has been quietly doubling the cost of the owner decision that keeps the emulator off the push path. **No evidence is lost on the dispatch path:** the certified PDF verdict and the device run are unaffected, and the installable APK now comes from `android-instrumented`, which already produces it via `:app:packageDebug` on its way to the emulator and uploads it under the **same artifact name and retention**, so `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s "download `theygrow-debug-apk`" holds unchanged whichever path produced it. That upload is gated to dispatch only, because on `pull_request` both jobs run and two uploads sharing one artifact name fail the run under `upload-artifact` v4 — verified by enumerating all three events and confirming exactly one publisher each.
  - **z-quinquies. Deferred, with the reason recorded rather than left implicit: `gradle/actions/setup-gradle`.** It would cache the wrapper distribution itself — which `actions/setup-java`'s `cache: gradle` does not, since that caches `~/.gradle` dependencies and not `wrapper/dists` — and so would remove the repeated fetch rather than shrink it. **Not taken now, for two reasons.** It is a **new third-party action executing in our pipeline**, the same supply-chain class as the veraPDF decision one round earlier (debt item (0)), and it deserves the same deliberate treatment rather than arriving as a side effect of an incident. And its benefit **overlaps heavily with (1) above**: most of the exposure is the transfer size, which just fell by 39%. **What would justify taking it:** a recurrence after the `-bin` change, or any second consumer of Gradle caching appearing in CI — at which point the action is evaluated on its own merits, pinned by commit SHA rather than by tag, as its own decision.
  - **aa. A hand-written PDF writer, because there is no other route to PDF/A here.** Not a preference: Android's `PdfDocument` and print pipeline emit PDF but not PDF/A — no OutputIntent, no `pdfaid` metadata, and subsetted fonts without the `CIDSet` a subset requires — so a conformant file has to be assembled deliberately. `pdf.js` writes a Type0/Identity-H font with a CIDFontType2 descendant, `/CIDToGIDMap /Identity`, a `ToUnicode` CMap, an XMP packet and an OutputIntent; `ttf.js` reads the six tables a PDF font dictionary needs (`head`, `hhea`/`hmtx`, `maxp`, `cmap` formats 4 and 12, `OS/2`, `post`) and nothing else. **The font is embedded whole, not subsetted**, because a subset needs a `CIDSet` and a six-letter prefix and getting either wrong is a conformance failure only a validator would catch. The print layer is built from the SAME text the archive's `text/` files carry, so it is the printable form of those files rather than a second rendering that could disagree with them. Extraction is asserted by round trip, not by presence: the test walks the CMap and reads the first page back, checking Cyrillic survives and no replacement character appears.
  - **bb. Two vendored binaries, and the payload deviates from what the plan estimated.** PDF/A requires every font to be embedded and there is no Cyrillic base-14 face, so any PDF this product emits — conformant or not — carries a font. **PT Sans Regular (SIL OFL 1.1, ParaType)** is vendored unmodified with its licence file, which the OFL requires to travel with any redistribution and which a test asserts is shipped. **It is 443 KB, not the ~120 KB this packet assumed when planning**, because the upstream web build carries `kern` (144 KB) and `hdmx` (34 KB) tables the writer never touches. Stripping them was rejected: it would mean the shipped bytes are no longer the bytes the SHA-256 can be checked against upstream, and a hand-rolled table-directory rewrite is a new class of defect for a saving the web channel does not pay anyway (see the precache decision below). The OutputIntent profile is **sRGB-v2-micro.icc, 456 bytes, CC0** — a complete ICC v2.1 matrix/TRC sRGB profile, verified by reading its header and tag table rather than trusted from its filename, and two orders of magnitude smaller than a stock sRGB profile that would otherwise be paid per exported artifact. Both are pinned by SHA-256 in `app/tests/export-contour.spec.js`; provenance, licences and the size reasoning are in `app/m/v1/export/assets/PROVENANCE.txt`.
  - **cc. The two binaries ship but are NOT precached, on the DDL precedent rather than by default.** `app/sw.js` already declines to precache `001-core.sql` because only the native channel fetches it and that channel does not use the service worker. Both halves hold here and a third is stronger: by (m) the web channel cannot export at all, so precaching the font and the profile would spend ~443 KB of an installed web client cache budget on bytes it can never use. The ten-plus **JS modules** are precached, as before, because the static import graph reaches them and an installed client must not boot offline with a broken graph. A test asserts both directions — the binaries shipped and absent from the precache, `pdf.js` present in it — so neither can drift.
  - **dd. The determinism promise is narrowed by one file, and the artifact says so in its own words.** PDF/A requires `/CreationDate`, `/ModDate` and matching XMP dates, so the print layer cannot be clock-free the way the text files are. `declaration.json` now states that two files move when the export time moves — `MANIFEST.json` and `print/archive.pdf` — rather than one. The test was **not** relaxed to match: it asserts the differing set is exactly those two, and then masks the two date fields and the derived `/ID` and asserts the two PDFs are byte-identical beneath them. So the promise weakened by one named file and the assertion did not.
  - **x. Four false statements are corrected, and one gate is de-vacuumed.** `app/m/v1/store/config.js` and `store.js` both said the export key was an open question for P3; `docs/execution-map.md` carried the pre-gate P3 scope; `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (`LSC-P1-INV-001` Scope) still described P3 as the write path, from before the L1-P2 reorder. Separately, `app/tests/schema/test_store_slots.py`'s `RULE_COVERAGE[5]` held a deferral string that the gate only checked for the substring `L1-P3`; it now resolves to a live test, which required teaching `_resolve` to import a dotted, package-qualified id.
- **Rationale.** The export contour was pulled ahead of the write path so that the first family records are recoverable *before* they are written. That ordering only means anything if the artifact is genuinely independent of us — hence keyless, offline, uncompressed, self-describing, and proven by a reader that has never heard of this repository. Everything else in the packet follows from taking that independence literally rather than nominally.
- **No dedicated ADR by design at the repo layer.** Realises vault PDR-020 §1 (two objects with opposite requirements), §2 (self-describing, not self-executing), §3 (free always, offline, keyless; GDPR art. 20 portability), §4 (full snapshots; media does not travel and the interface must say so), §7 (the manifest carries canon and app version); PDR-026 §4 fifth accompanying rule (export durability), closed here; PDR-031 §1 (the journal is the source of truth, the export is a projection); PDR-022 (the perpetual free core); PDR-016 (publication discipline, engaged because the format shape becomes public); ADR-043 §2 (the contour pulled forward from L3); ADR-046 owner block + addendum 2026-08-12 §2.3 (ladder separation: artifact on L1, encrypted snapshot and key on L7) and §2.4 (the pre-migration copy is an operational rollback snapshot, addressed to L2+); ADR-015 (honest degradation, the shape the zero case and the absent-value rendering take); ADR-013 / contract §4.7 (operability); ADR-037 (buildless in both channels).
- **Alternatives considered.**
  1. **One object serving both privacy and durability.** Rejected — the requirements are strictly opposite; see (a). This is PDR-020 §1's own finding and the gate's.
  2. **A self-extracting archive.** Rejected upstream on four independent grounds (PDR-020 §2), and rejected again here on a fifth: an executable is the one artifact form guaranteed not to run in 2044.
  3. **An HTML viewer as the readability guarantee.** Rejected — permissible as convenience, never as the guarantee (PDR-020 §2). Not built this packet.
  4. **DEFLATE compression.** Rejected — see (f).
  5. **A vendored zip library.** Rejected — a hundred lines of header arithmetic against a permanent supply-chain surface.
  6. **`@capacitor/filesystem` as the sink.** Rejected — see (j).
  7. **A Blob download from the WebView.** Rejected — Capacitor's Android WebView has no reliable download listener, and it would take the destination choice away from the parent.
  8. **`v_shared_journal` as the scope anchor.** Rejected — it declares what *sync* may ship at L7, a different question with a different threat model; using it would have withheld the parent's own private records from their own backup.
  9. **Exporting all private areas regardless of requester.** Rejected on owner instruction — see (g).
  10. **Exporting `localStorage` on the web channel.** Rejected — see (m).
  11. **Hiding the export action on the web.** Rejected — a missing button teaches a parent nothing about where their data is, which is the opposite of what the two plain sentences exist to do.
  12. **Lazy-loading the builder.** Rejected — see (n).
  13. **A Python re-implementation of the builder for the tests.** Rejected — it would prove the two agree, not that the shipped artifact is right. The suite shells out to `node` on the shipped module instead.
  14. **Reading the artifact in tests with the app's own modules.** Rejected for the same reason, more sharply: it would prove nothing at all about surviving the app's absence.
  15. **Deriving `child_profile` / `child_marker` from the existing SQL views.** Rejected — those views expose no visibility column, so they could not be scoped by requester; the artifact declares `child_attribute_current` with the winner rule and the scope filter written out instead.
- **Supersedes.** None. **Corrects** the P3 scope line in `docs/execution-map.md` (which named an encrypted dump and an open export-key fork, both removed by the owner gate), the `LSC-P1-INV-001` Scope sentence in `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (which described P3 as the write path, from before the L1-P2 reorder), and the export-key sentences in `app/m/v1/store/config.js` and `app/m/v1/store/store.js`. **Amends by reference, leaving the record byte-untouched:** `LSC-DL-001` (e), which says "the deliberate export contour is **L1-P4**" — pre-reorder numbering; and `LSC-DL-002`'s debt item (2), "The export key (P3)", which is **closed** by (a): this artifact has no key, and the key that does exist belongs to L7.
- **Effects.**
  - Added (`app/m/v1/export/`): `declaration.json`, `config.js`, `errors.js`, `zip.js`, `text.js`, `readme.js`, `build.js`, `readout.js`, `sink.js`, `run.js`. Added `app/m/v1/surfaces/export.js`; `native/android/app/src/main/java/app/theygrow/ExportSinkPlugin.java`; `app/tests/export/` (harness, blind reader, three test modules, the node driver); `app/tests/export-contour.spec.js`; `native/android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/theygrow/ExportSinkTest.java`.
  - Changed: `app/index.html` (one footer button, one modal, ten `modulepreload` hints), `app/m/v1/app.css` (export modal styles, scoped to `#exportModal`), `app/m/v1/app.js` (one import, one `wireExport()`), `app/sw.js` (ten precache entries), `app/playwright.config.js` (the `contract` project matches the new spec), `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the export suite and the Node it needs), `app/tests/schema/test_store_slots.py` (rule 5 closed; `_resolve` accepts a dotted id), `app/m/v1/store/{config,store}.js` and `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (false statements corrected).
  - **No baseline is blessed in this packet's working tree.** An earlier pass blessed the two DOM `control-footer.html` files locally and a container run re-blessed 16 PNGs; **all of them were restored to `HEAD`** once the measurement above found (q). Blessing against code that was about to change would have put churn in the diff for no gain, so the whole set — DOM and PNG together — is blessed once, in the pinned container, against the corrected code. After (u) and (v) the expected set changed, and the change is itself a check on the reasoning: with the export control out of the footer, **both `control-footer.html` DOM baselines match `HEAD` again without being blessed**, and `visual-*/control-footer.png` should move only by the footer's new pinned height (w). What moves instead is the header — both `dom-*/header.html`, both `visual-*/header.png`, and every `shell-*.png` and full-viewport `modal-*.png`, since those capture the header and the footer alike. `header.png` moving is expected now for the first time in this packet: (u) and (v) change the header's own contents, which is a different cause from the footer reflow that never reached it.
