  - Untouched, and verified so: `app/m/v1/core/storage.js` and every one of its call sites (P4's to change), `app/m/v1/store/schema/001-core.sql` (frozen; no DDL change), `docs/RUNTIME-INVARIANTS.md`, `api/` in its entirety.
  - **Operability (ADR-013 / contract §4.7).** **Knobs: eleven, in one new place.** `app/m/v1/export/config.js` holds the format id and version, the declaration url and name, the two zip timestamp constants, the compression method, the text line width, the filename pattern, the mime type, the app version and the canon url — each with `changed_in: LSC-DL-003`, none as a scattered literal, the object frozen at runtime with a test that says so. A **second** device-local surface rather than an extension of `store/config.js`, whose own docstring scopes it to "every qualitative knob **the store** introduces". The front-side precedent chain is `CACHE_VERSION` (`PWA-DL-001`) then `store/config.js` (`LSC-DL-002`). The typed versioned surface `api/theygrow_api/parameters.py` is server-side and untouched; `PARAMETERS_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays **5**. **Signals: none this packet.** No taxonomy entry, no `emitted_now` change, no producer added or removed, and **no new GA4 event** — the analytics egress question opened by `LSC-DL-001` (o) is still open and an export is not the packet that should widen it. An export failure is reported to the parent in the interface and to the device console as engine text plus a reason code. **No new Python runtime import**, and the mypy hook's `additional_dependencies` are unchanged because the new suite is standard library plus pytest.
  - **§4-safe.** No child PII can reach telemetry or logs from this packet, because it adds no telemetry surface at all. The one summary the contour returns carries byte counts and row counts only; the console line on failure carries an error name and the engine's message. The artifact itself is family data by design — that is its purpose — and it is written only to a location a person chose, never transmitted.
  - **Debt recorded, not fixed.** (0) **veraPDF is fetched from an unversioned URL and executed in CI on every run of the `android-instrumented` job.** That is a third party running code in our pipeline, which the supply-chain discipline applied to `@capacitor-community/sqlite`, the vendored font and the ICC profile would not otherwise permit — all three are pinned to exact versions or exact bytes. It is accepted here because upstream publishes nothing pinnable (see (z)), and it is bounded three ways: the archive reviewed at 1.30.2 is recorded by SHA-256 as provenance of the bytes seen, the version is asserted so an upgrade reds rather than slips through, and the job is `pull_request` + `workflow_dispatch` only so the fetch is not on the push path. **What would close it:** vendoring the validator (33 MB into the repository, which is worse), building it from the `veraPDF-library` source tag (a Maven toolchain in CI for one check), or an upstream versioned URL. None is worth doing now; it is named so the next person weighing a CI download has the precedent stated rather than inferred. (1) The **PDF print layer** is the second checkpoint of this packet, not deferred out of it. (2) The `visual-*` baselines await an owner-run container pass, above. (3) The service-worker-in-WebView disposition stays OPEN, carried to **L1-P4** by `LSC-DL-002`, untouched here. (4) The analytics decision from `LSC-DL-001` (o), with its unchanged deadline. (5) `docs/execution-map.md`'s P2 line said "Nothing has run on a device or an emulator", which `LSC-DL-002`'s corrected validation caveat had already overtaken; corrected here.
  - **Validation-honesty caveat** (M4-CLOSE discipline). Green locally: `pytest app/tests/schema app/tests/export` (**106 passed**); the `contract` project (**433 passed**), which now includes the export contour's twenty guards; `pre-commit run --all-files` plus `--files` over every new untracked path. The DOM-level projects were run this time and are green (**61 passed, 3 baseline diffs**, all `control-footer.html`, re-blessed as above) — the development machine's Playwright browser was made to launch against a locally extracted `libnspr4.so`, which is **not** the pinned container and is why only DOM baselines were blessed there. **What none of this proves.** The `visual-*` projects did not run, for the reason above. **Nothing in this packet has run on a device or an emulator:** `ExportSinkTest` has never executed, so the claim that the SAF sink writes the archive correctly, truncates a longer previous write, and that the first-party plugin registers at all, rests on review and not on evidence — and `android-instrumented` is not a per-push gate, so the first signal arrives at PR or on `workflow_dispatch`. **And the artifact is provably correct while being nearly empty:** until L1-P4 lands the write path, nothing writes family data to the journal, so every assertion here is about a seeded fixture and the format, not about a family's actual history.

## LSC-DL-004 — L1-P4 `write-path-and-migration`: the app starts using what three packets built, this family's history moves without being touched, and two questions the milestone had deferred twice are closed with evidence

- **Date.** 2026-08-13
- **Type.** Packet — L1-P4, the milestone's last. *(Namespace note: continues the `LSC-DL` namespace opened by `LSC-DL-001`; packets keep `L1-P{k}`.)*
- **Executed in five checkpoints on one branch**, each with its own report: C1 the invariants as failing tests, C2 the read/write seam, C3 the write path and the import, C4 the signal surface and its guard, C5 the service-worker disposition and the docs. The split exists because the packet turns three inert packets on at once, and a defect in the seam should not sit in the same unreviewable diff as a defect in the import.

### Premises corrected rather than served

Four of the five premises the packet's handoff carried did not hold against the code, and each changed what shipped.

- **a. "Every call site changes; the largest mechanical change of the milestone" — false, and this was the most consequential correction.** `core/zpd.js` never reads storage: the completed set is always *passed in*. Only five sites call `getCompletedSkills()`, and every one of them reads a projection. Holding that projection in memory left all five **synchronous and untouched**, and made the async boundary exactly two functions wide — boot and write. The seam was roughly a tenth of the size described, and keeping it that small is what let the packet turn on the write path with **no DOM and no visual baseline moving**.
- **b. Which keys move was also over-stated.** Three of the six `localStorage` keys are UI preference state — accordion, ZPD filter, onboarding dismissal. The frozen schema has nowhere to put them (`child_attribute` is a closed list of eight, asserted `extra == set()`), so a home for them would be a schema change. They stay in `localStorage` on both channels, behind the one declared door.
- **c. "Signal-payload privacy lint, deferred from P3" — no such deferral exists.** `LSC-DL-003`'s debt list has six items and this is not one; nothing in `docs/`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` records it. More importantly there was **no client-side signal surface to lint**: `emitted_now` existed only in `api/theygrow_api/signals.py`. So this packet **created** the surface, its seam and its guard — larger than "a lint", and planned as such.
- **d. "A store-open failure signal was deferred to this packet" — overstated.** `LSC-DL-002` says "Signals: none this packet" and chose a console log *instead of* inventing a telemetry surface. A rationale, not an address. It is still a good reason to declare the signal now, and this packet does.
- **e. "The journal exists and nothing writes to it" — true for family data, and verified.** But `store.js` writes housekeeping on every open, and **`closeStore()` is defined and never called**, so `clean_shutdown` is never set back to 1. That matters now, because the new store-open signal reports `previous_run_clean` and it will read false on every launch but the first. Recorded, not fixed — see the debt list.
- **f. Two things the handoff did not name but the code forced.** Nothing creates a `child` row, deliberately, and `journal_entry` has a NOT NULL foreign key to it — so the write path had to mint children, and a child with no name cannot render a profile button, which makes the import **profiles and marks**, not marks alone. And consensus per skill has no view: `v_child_skill_state` carries no consensus column, so expressing the half-confirmed state is a query-time join, because adding a view would be a schema change.

### Decision

- **a. A mark is an attributed assertion, and it carries a confirmation by its own author.** The owner decision on legacy marks phrases the outcome as "the author's assertion, **confirmed by one**" — two components, not one — and `001-core.sql` says so at the `confirmation` table. If an authored mark carried only the assertion, the same act would produce two different consensus states depending on which packet wrote it. So the pairing is unconditional, and `origin` is the only thing separating an imported mark from one made this morning. **The alternative was counting the author as an implicit confirmer inside the projection**, and it was rejected twice over: it would double-count against the migration shape the frozen schema prescribes, and it would put a consensus rule in a projection that every L7 device would have to reimplement identically — where a fact written into the journal survives, a rule living in a projection drifts between app versions, which is the whole posture of an append-only store. **The cost is accepted rather than incidental: two journal entries per tick, forever, and L7 inherits it.**
- **b. A migrated mark wears the import date, and the archive says so.** A legacy mark carries no date; `event_date_local` is NOT NULL, so something must go in it. The import date goes in, the nullable instant stays NULL — the schema's own way of saying only the date is known — and `origin = 'migrated_legacy'` marks the row. Birthdate and a fabricated observation date were both rejected as inventing history. **Detectable in the database is not enough**: the archive is the decades-horizon record and its reader has no database and nobody to ask, so `child_skill_state` gained an `origin` column and an explicit `event_date_basis` (`observed` | `import_date_unknown`), the `journal_entry` field explanations say what a migrated date is, and the README gained a section about it. Without that, a reader in 2044 opens `text/skills.txt` and finds three hundred skills mastered on a single afternoon. It cost no renderer change — `text.js` renders whatever columns the declaration names — which is the L1-P3 architecture working as designed.
- **c. Import idempotence is a derived id, and there is no ledger.** Every imported id is a SHA-256 over `derivedIdNamespace` and the tuple it identifies, shaped as a version-8 UUID so it is indistinguishable in form from a minted one. A second run computes the same ids, reads back which the store holds, and appends the remainder. **The journal is the only record of what has been imported**, so there is no second truth to drift out of step with it. `STORE_CONFIG.derivedIdNamespace` carries its version inside the value: **changing it re-imports the family's entire history as a second set of entries the append-only journal can never be rid of**, and the knob says so where it is declared.
- **d. Consent is per profile, and the reversible path won.** The modal lists each profile by name with its mark count and a checkbox, everything ticked by default; an unticked profile is simply offered again next time. The grounding is the one the decision layer already uses for irreversible choices: prefer the option that keeps the reversible path open. **An unimported profile can be imported later; a permanent child row cannot be removed.** This did not clear the escalation-list test — no irreversible schema slot, no promise changed, no egress created — and was decided rather than asked.
- **e. The two channels diverge after this packet, and this milestone does not resolve it.** Stated in those words because it is the honest answer. The **web** channel is unchanged: `localStorage` is its whole world. The **native** channel reads and writes only the journal; `localStorage` is read by the import, never written for family data, never cleared. A mark made on the web after an import lands only in `localStorage` and native does not see it until the import is run again — which native will offer, because the offer is keyed on what is missing rather than on whether an import ever ran. **Marks made natively never reach the web at all, ever.** The import is a one-way, parent-triggered bridge, not a reconciliation: it cannot merge a skill marked on one channel and revoked on the other. **Resolution belongs to L7**, the rung where two devices holding one history is the entire subject. So a parent does not discover this alone, the import modal states it in plain Russian *before* the press — the export modal's precedent, where the sentence that matters stands before the button — and the RUNBOOK records it. The web PWA is left silent deliberately: a notice there is a web-channel product change that would move baselines to say something only native users can act on.
- **f. On native, a store that will not open refuses the write rather than falling back.** The fallback to `localStorage` was genuinely recoverable — a later import would pick it up — and was rejected anyway: it re-opens the second door this milestone exists to close and leaves the journal and the browser disagreeing with nothing to reconcile them. The tick is refused, the checkbox goes back, and a modal says the mark was **not** saved and that existing data is unharmed (ADR-015).
- **g. The selected child is a pointer, not history.** On the journal backend, which child a parent was last looking at is stored under the existing `childDevTracker_currentProfile` key, holding a child id. It is the same class of thing as the accordion state, so it goes through the one declared Web Storage door rather than taking a slot in a frozen schema — and `core/storage.js` needed no change at all, which is what lets `LSC-P1-INV-001` still prove the import creates no second door.
- **h. The client signal surface exists, and its only sink is the device console.** Three kinds, all `emitted_now`: `store.open`, `history.import`, `write.refused`. A payload value may be a number, a boolean, `null`, or a member of the closed code list declared for its field — **there is no code path that accepts a free string**, so a payload cannot carry family text. `emitSignal` never throws outward; a refusal is counted. **Adding any network sink is a separate owner decision on the escalation list (PDR-027 §2), and that is written in the taxonomy module's own docstring** — where the next person to add a signal will read it, because that is the moment the surface would otherwise grow a network leg without anyone deciding to. Store failures are classified from the error **class**, never its message: engine messages carry file paths and statement text.
- **i. The service-worker disposition is closed, with evidence.** The native channel registers no worker and purges one a previously installed APK left behind, together with its shell caches — a runtime branch in the same shipped file, so byte identity holds. What is deleted is the losable cache ADR-043 permits, never family data, and never on the web. The question had been raised in `LSC-DL-001` (i), declined by `LSC-DL-002` as outside scope, and carried past `LSC-DL-003`; `docs/RUNBOOK.md` called it "the one open question the repository cannot settle". It could be settled; it needed a device. `WebViewStorageTest` now measures it and **prints the probe facts** — whether `serviceWorker` is in `navigator` at all, what `caches.keys()` returns — so the next reader finds an observation rather than an opinion.
- **j. GA4 is stripped from the native channel. This closes `LSC-DL-001` (o) FOR THE NATIVE CHANNEL ONLY.** Owner decision, taken with the milestone in view. Implemented as a runtime branch preserving byte identity, the same shape as (i). The loader tag had to move too, not only the events: stopping the events while still fetching `gtag.js` leaves the egress in place, because the request itself carries the device address and the user agent. **Whether the WEB channel should carry analytics at all remains OPEN**, under the escalation list, with its own address at the milestone close — this entry does not mark that item done.

### Grounding

- **Rationale.** The packet's one irreversible act is the first family record written to the journal, so everything else was arranged around it. That is why a mark is a pair rather than a fact (a) — a projection rule can be corrected on one device and diverge on another, a fact written into the journal cannot — and why the pair is unconditional rather than assembled per case: a consensus rule that lives in a projection is a rule every L7 device has to reimplement identically, which is the shape of a defect that appears years later as "the app disagrees with itself". It is why idempotence is a *property of the ids* rather than a ledger (c): a ledger is a second truth, and the append-only journal cannot be rid of what a drifted ledger causes it to write twice. It is why the import cannot write to its source (`LSC-P4-INV-002` (3)) by not importing a writer rather than by not calling one — the negative is enforced at the module boundary, where a later edit to a body cannot reopen it. And it is why the migrated date is carried into the *artifact* rather than only into the database (b): the decades-horizon reader has no database and nobody to ask, so a fact that is only detectable in SQL is, for them, not recorded at all. The two deferred questions were taken here for one reason each: the service-worker disposition (i) because P4 changes native-channel behaviour anyway and there is no later packet in this milestone, and the analytics strip (j) because the milestone is the last point at which the native channel's egress can be decided before an APK reaches anyone.
- **No dedicated ADR by design at the repo layer.** Realises vault **PDR-021** (the consensus model; "confirmed by one" as the general function's answer, not a special case — the direct grounding for (a)); **PDR-026** §4 (the sixteen slots, now written to rather than declared) and its fifth accompanying rule, closed at L1-P3 and exercised here for the first time with real records; **ADR-043** §5 (the explicit `localStorage` → native import, which must not mutate or delete its source) and §2 (WebView storage permitted only as a losable cache — the direct grounding for (i)); **ADR-046** §2.4 (the ladder that puts the write path last); **ADR-015** (honest degradation — the shape the refusal in (f) takes, and the reason a store that will not open refuses rather than falls back); **PDR-031** §1 (the journal is the source of truth and every projection is derived); **PDR-027** §2 (egress as an owner decision — the reason the signal surface's console-only sink in (h) is a boundary and not an implementation detail, and the reason (j) is an owner decision rather than a cleanup); **ADR-013** / contract §4.7 (operability: knobs and signals declared where they are used); **ADR-037** (buildless in both channels, which is why (i) and (j) are runtime branches rather than a build-time fork). This entry records what the repository did with those.
- **Alternatives considered.**
  1. **Count the author as an implicit confirmer inside the projection**, instead of writing the confirmation. Rejected — see (a): it double-counts against the migration shape the frozen schema prescribes, and it moves a consensus rule from data into code that every L7 device must reproduce exactly.
  2. **An import ledger** — a table or a flag recording what has been carried across. Rejected for derived ids (c): the ledger is a second record of the same fact, and the failure it introduces (ledger written, journal not, or the reverse) is precisely the interrupted-run case the derived ids make harmless.
  3. **Birthdate, or a fabricated observation date, for a migrated mark.** Rejected as inventing history (b). The import date with a NULL instant and an explicit `event_date_basis` says what is actually known.
  4. **All-or-nothing consent** for the import, instead of per profile. Rejected on the reversible-path rule (d): an unimported profile can be imported later, a permanent `child` row cannot be removed.
  5. **Fall back to `localStorage` when the native store will not open.** Rejected (f) even though it was genuinely recoverable: it re-opens the second door the milestone exists to close.
  6. **A separate `core/history.js` seam module**, as the plan listed. Rejected in execution and recorded as a plan deviation under Effects: `core/state.js` already owned the in-memory model and the live bindings `surfaces/profile.js` reads.
  7. **Stripping the service worker and GA4 in the native build**, or shipping a second file, instead of runtime branches. Rejected — either forks the channels' bytes and destroys `LSC-P1-INV-002`, which is the guarantee the whole native channel is verified through.
  8. **Stopping the GA4 events but leaving the loader tag.** Rejected (j): the request to `googletagmanager.com` itself carries the device address and the user agent, so the egress would survive the fix meant to remove it.
  9. **Clearing `localStorage` after a successful import.** Rejected for this packet and left as an explicit owner action (debt 4) — a destructive step taken automatically on the strength of an import that has never run on a real family's history.
- **Supersedes.** None. **Corrects** the `LSC-P1-INV-001` Scope sentence in `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, which still assigned the service-worker disposition to **L1-P2** — an assignment `LSC-DL-002` superseded without editing the line, so it was false for two packets; the service-worker bullet in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s on-device smoke, which called it "the one open question the repository cannot settle"; and export step 7 in the same file, which stated "expect the archive to be nearly empty" as a standing expectation and would now tell an owner that a correct archive was wrong. **Amends by reference, leaving the record byte-untouched:** `LSC-DL-001` (i), the service-worker question, and (o), the analytics egress — (o) is closed here **for the native channel only** and stays open for the web; `LSC-DL-002`'s debt item 1, which carried the disposition to this packet; and `LSC-DL-003`'s debt item (3), the same carry restated.

### Effects

- **Operability.** Two knobs, both `changed_in: LSC-DL-004` — `derivedIdNamespace` and `legacyImportProbeBatch`, on the existing `STORE_CONFIG` device-local surface. Three signal kinds declared **and** emitted in the same packet, on a **new client-side taxonomy** (`app/m/v1/core/signals.js`) that did not exist before; payloads are counts, durations, booleans and closed codes only, enforced structurally rather than by review. **No new network egress** — the sink is the device console, and the native channel's existing GA4 egress was *removed*, not extended.
- **Behaviour change worth naming.** `trackEvent('skill_complete', …)` previously fired **before** the write and unconditionally. It now fires **after a confirmed write**. The old order reported actions that had not happened yet and, on the native path, could have reported ones that never would. The parity assertions — one event on a successful tick, zero on a refused one — still hold on the web branch.
- **Plan deviation, stated.** The plan listed a separate `core/history.js` as the seam module. It was folded into `core/state.js`, which already owned the in-memory model and its persistence and whose exported live bindings `surfaces/profile.js` reads directly; a separate module would have duplicated those bindings or forced an unrelated surface to change. `repo-local.js` and `repo-journal.js` stayed separate, which is where the two-backends symmetry actually lives.
- **A guard that failed open, found by mutation and made sound.** The signal-payload scan first matched call sites with `/emitSignal\(\s*([^)]*?)\s*\)/`. `[^)]*?` stops at the first close paren, so a violating call — `emitSignal('write.refused', { reason: getCurrentProfile().name })` — was captured only as far as `getCurrentProfile(`, and the family-text scan never saw `.name`. **The guard reported green on precisely the shape a violation takes.** It now balances parens and refuses any payload containing a call at all, which is what makes the scan sound rather than merely better: with no nested parens there is nothing left to hide behind. Established by mutating the tree in three directions — an undeclared kind, a value read off family text, and no call sites at all — and confirming each goes red. Had the mutation proof not been asked for, it would have shipped green and hollow.
- **Invariants.** `LSC-P4-INV-001`…`004`. `docs/INVARIANTS.md`'s `LSC-P1-INV-001` Scope is corrected in place: it still assigned the service-worker disposition to **L1-P2**, an assignment `LSC-DL-002` had already superseded without editing the line, so it was false for two packets.
- **Tests before implementation.** Contract §4 invariant 10 was applied in full: C1 landed the migration and write-path invariants as failing tests, checkpointed red on a local commit that was deliberately not pushed, so the branch history carries the ordering as evidence while CI never ran on a knowingly red tree.
- **§4-safe — stated in full, because this packet both creates a telemetry surface and removes an egress, and the two have opposite failure modes.** **What can reach a payload:** a number, a boolean, `null`, or a member of the closed code list declared for that field. That is the whole set. **What cannot:** a free string — there is no code path that accepts one, so a child's name, a skill title, a profile label or anything a parent typed cannot be carried, and the guarantee is *cannot* rather than *does not*. Nor can a value be smuggled in shaped as something else: an undeclared kind, an undeclared field, a nested object, an array, a function and `undefined` are each refused at the boundary, a refusal is counted rather than swallowed, and `emitSignal` never throws outward so a telemetry bug cannot take the write path down with it. **How that is enforced, in three places rather than by review.** (1) `app/m/v1/core/signals.js` validates every value against the declared type or code list at emit time. (2) `app/tests/signal-payload.spec.js` scans **every shipped JavaScript module** expanded from `app/Dockerfile`'s COPY list and asserts that each `emitSignal` call site names a declared kind with literal keys, that no payload value is derived from an identifier holding family text, and that **no payload computes a value inline** — a call inside a payload is refused outright, which is what makes the family-text scan sound rather than merely present, since with no nested call there is nothing left to hide behind. (3) The guard's own soundness was established by **mutation, not inspection**: an earlier form of it failed open on exactly the shape a violation takes and was replaced (see the guard bullet above). **Store failures are classified from the error class, never its message** — engine messages carry file paths and statement text, which is family-adjacent by construction. **Egress:** the surface's only sink is the device console; it reaches no network primitive, no emitter hands a signal to the analytics shim, and the absence of a network leg is asserted rather than assumed, so one cannot be added as an implementation detail of adding a signal — adding it is an owner decision on the escalation list (PDR-027 §2). The packet's net effect on egress is **negative**: the native channel's inherited GA4 request to `googletagmanager.com` is removed, loader included, and nothing is added. **The family data this packet writes** goes to one place — the SQLCipher-encrypted journal on the device — and the import reads `localStorage` on the same device and transmits nothing. No credential, host, user, password, connection string or live identifier enters the repository.

### Debt recorded, not fixed

1. **`closeStore()` is defined and never called → addressed to the L1 milestone close.** `clean_shutdown` is never set back to 1, so every launch after the first pays an `integrity_check` and the new `store.open` signal reports `previous_run_clean` **false on every launch but the first**. The signal reports the true state — the defect is upstream of it, not in it. Not fixed here because the cause is a native-lifecycle question — whether the WebView reliably fires `pagehide` before process death — that deserves its own evidence rather than a guess inside the write-path packet. **Carried to the milestone close with an address rather than left in a list**: `docs/RUNBOOK.md` step 2 of the L1-P4 owner sequence says to expect the false reading and not to treat it as a store fault, because that is where an owner reading `adb logcat` will meet it; `docs/execution-map.md`'s L1 block carries it as one of the two side-finds the close must dispose of.
2. **The stale `cap sync` artifact under `native/android/app/src/main/assets/public/` → addressed to the L1 milestone close.** On the development machine that directory is missing `store/` and `export/` entirely. It is gitignored and harmless to the build — `npm run sync` re-stages before every build — but it is the first thing a person looking for "the shipped set" will open, and it will mislead them. **Carried with an address**: `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s Android-shell section names it where the staging rule is stated, and `docs/execution-map.md`'s L1 block carries it as the second side-find for the close.
3. **The web channel's analytics question stays OPEN** — see Decision (j). The native half is closed here; the web half is not, and this entry does not mark `LSC-DL-001` (o) done.
4. **Clearing `localStorage` after a successful import** is a separate, explicit owner action and is not in this packet.
5. The veraPDF unversioned-URL debt from `LSC-DL-003` (0), unchanged.
6. **SQLite journal-mode contention in the instrumented job → addressed to the L1 milestone close.** Run `31680204645`'s logcat carries four lines of it: `E SQLiteLog: (5) statement aborts at 2: database is locked; [PRAGMA journal_mode=delete]`, each followed by `W SQLiteConnection: Could not change the database journal mode`, at 08:09:01.623 and 08:09:08.253. That is the app opening its store at boot while a test holds the same file — **two writers on one database**. Benign in that run: every store test passed and the failure was elsewhere. Not fixed here, and deliberately not papered over, because "benign" is a property of this run's timing and not of the arrangement: contention that resolves by luck resolves differently under a slower emulator, and the failure it would produce is intermittent, which is the most expensive kind to diagnose later. **Carried with an address**: `docs/execution-map.md`'s L1 block lists it with the other side-finds the close must dispose of.

### Validation-honesty caveat (M4-CLOSE discipline)

**What actually ran, on the tree this entry describes.** `scripts/parity-suite.sh` in the **pinned container** (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble`), full suite, every project including the two `visual-*` ones: **652 passed, 6 skipped, zero failures**, and — the number that matters more than the pass count — **zero baseline writes**. No snapshot moved, no `--update-snapshots` was passed, and `git status` is byte-identical before and after the run, which is the packet's central behavioural claim (the write path was turned on with no DOM and no visual baseline moving) measured rather than asserted. `pytest app/tests/schema app/tests/export`: **133 passed** — up from `LSC-DL-003`'s 106, the difference being this packet's projection tests. `pre-commit run --all-files` green, plus `--files` over the untracked `WebViewStorageTest.java`. The 6 skips are declared in committed test code and predate this packet: four are the `native` project's service-worker update-channel tests, skipped because that channel is inert in the Capacitor shell, and two are viewport-independent captures taken once in `dom-desktop`.

**What none of this proves, stated plainly because the gap is larger than usual here.**

- **`WebViewStorageTest` has now run once, and it measured a document that had not booted. Decisions (i) and (j) are still unobserved, and the gap is worse than "not yet run".** Run `31680204645` (`workflow_dispatch`) executed all sixteen instrumented tests. Fifteen passed; `the_native_shell_sends_nothing_to_analytics` failed on its own anti-vacuity guard — `IS_NATIVE_SHELL` read **`false`** — and the diagnosis is a defect in the harness, not in the disposition: `pollFor` waits only while a value is `null`, every probe was wrapped in `String(...)`, which never is, so each answered on its first evaluation, milliseconds after the activity resumed and before the shipped modules ran. **The sibling test's green was the more dangerous result**: zero registrations and no shell cache are trivially true of a page that has not yet run `sw-register.js`, and its anti-vacuity guard used `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()`, which the injected bridge makes true before a single shipped byte executes. So the enforcement of `LSC-P4-INV-004` exists, has run, and has not yet observed the thing it asserts. The harness is fixed — both tests now wait on a sentinel the app itself produces (populated `#tableBody tr[data-skill-id]` rows, the same gate `app/tests/support/seed.js` uses), the anti-vacuity guard is re-anchored on `IS_NATIVE_SHELL` rather than on the bridge, and the pre-boot reading is printed beside the post-boot one so the gate's effect stays visible — but **no assertion was weakened, no product code was touched, and the corrected tests have not themselves run on a device.** Until `android-instrumented` runs again, (i) and (j) remain implemented and unobserved.
- **What the failed run did settle, and it matters.** `'serviceWorker' in navigator` is **`true`** in this Android WebView (`[probe]`, logcat, 08:09:05.255). The API is present, so the purge branch in `app/m/v1/sw-register.js` is **load-bearing rather than a no-op** — the possibility the test's own comment left open ("if the API is absent the guard is a no-op and the disposition still holds") is closed in the direction that makes the guard necessary. `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` is `true` on the device, which is what makes the byte-identical runtime branch reachable at all. Both readings are properties of the WebView rather than of the app's boot state, so they survive the harness defect.
- **The parity suite cannot see either native branch.** Both of its channels serve `native/www` over plain HTTP with **no Capacitor bridge injected**, so `IN_NATIVE_SHELL` and `IS_NATIVE_SHELL` are false in every project and both channels take the **web** branch. The suite's green is therefore proof that the web channel is unregressed — which is a real and load-bearing result — and proof of nothing at all about the native channel's service-worker or analytics behaviour.
- **For the same reason, the parity suite exercises the `localStorage` backend, not the journal one.** `LSC-P4-INV-001`'s and `002`'s contract-project specs drive a **recorder**, not a database: they prove the statements, the values and the transaction grouping, and prove nothing about SQLite, SQLCipher or the plugin executing them. That half belongs to `StoreEngineTest` and the append-only triggers, in the same not-per-push job.
- **The one place SQL meaning is checked against the real frozen schema** is `pytest app/tests/schema` — a real SQLite database carrying the real `001-core.sql`, with the projection query read out of `app/m/v1/store/journal.js` rather than retyped. That is why the 133 matters more than its size suggests, and it is still not a device.
- **The import has never run against a real family's history** — only against fixtures. The interruption property, the derived-id idempotence and the revoke-then-reimport case are all proven against a recorder at fixture scale, and `legacyImportProbeBatch` has never been exercised at a size where batching is what makes it finish.
- **The owner sequence in `docs/RUNBOOK.md` has not been executed.** Steps 1–8 are written from the design, not from a run; step 1 in particular requires an APK built from a commit *before* this packet, which nobody has built.

## LSC-DL-005 — L1-P5 `lsc-close`: the milestone closes on evidence rather than on assertion — the device disposition is observed, the two contract statements the first packet deferred here are made true, and the debt that survives is stated with what would close it

- **Date.** 2026-08-13
- **Type.** Packet — L1-P5, the milestone close-out of **L1 "local structured core"**. *(Namespace note: continues the `LSC-DL` namespace opened by `LSC-DL-001`; packets keep `L1-P{k}`. The "Entry format" header is intentionally left unedited, per the `LSC-DL-003` / `L2-DL-002` / `A3-DL-002` precedent.)*
- **Docs only.** No product code, no schema, no migration, no test, no assertion, no new invariant. Nothing under `app/`, `native/`, `api/`, `scripts/` or `.github/` is touched, and no parity baseline moves.

### Decision

- **a. The service-worker and analytics disposition is OBSERVED, and `LSC-DL-004`'s validation caveat is corrected in the opposite direction.** That caveat says "(i) and (j) remain implemented and unobserved" and "the corrected tests have not themselves run on a device". **Both sentences have been false since run `31683691498`.** Read from the run rather than taken on report: `workflow_dispatch`, head `460bd397b5b13b5a250089cccaf3c753ea41b20f`, conclusion **success**; `android-instrumented` ran 08:48:19 → 08:56:58 UTC — **8m39s** — with **16/16** instrumented tests completed, **0 failed**, `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 6m 1s`; the `android` job was `skipped`, which is what `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'` does on a dispatch run. So the corrected `WebViewStorageTest` ran on the emulator and passed, and **`LSC-P4-INV-004` is enforced, run, and observed** rather than enforced and unobserved. The green is not the vacuous one the previous run produced: the harness now waits on a sentinel the app itself produces (populated `#tableBody tr[data-skill-id]` rows) and re-anchors anti-vacuity on `IS_NATIVE_SHELL` rather than on the injected bridge, so a document that has not booted can no longer answer for a document that has.
- **b. What that run does and does not cover, stated as two claims rather than one.** A fresh emulator image has no prior installation, so there is nothing on it to purge. The job therefore proves **no service-worker registration and no shell cache under the app's own prefix exist after a booted native app** — the end state `LSC-P4-INV-004` asserts. It does **not** prove **a prior registration is actually purged**: that needs a pre-P4 APK installed first, and it remains the owner-run sequence in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, steps 1 → 2. The distinction is not pedantry — the purge branch is the half that protects an *existing* installation, and it is the half no emulator run has yet exercised.
- **c. This packet owes no emulator dispatch, and making one a precondition of the PR would be theatre.** It changes no shipped byte, so the device layer cannot move: `LSC-P1-INV-002` byte-identity holds trivially, and there is nothing for `WebViewStorageTest` to re-measure that `31683691498` did not measure on the same shipped bytes. The push run covers `quality`, `parity`, `eval` and `android`; `android-instrumented` is `pull_request` + `workflow_dispatch` only (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the standing owner decision on CI spend), so **the milestone PR re-runs it once on its own trigger** — and nothing in this packet gates on that result. **The device claim of this milestone rests on `31683691498`.**
- **d. The two contract edits `LSC-DL-001` deferred here by name are landed.** They are its rejected alternative 15 — "Reconcile `AGENTS.md` §8's layout block and §3's intent-level entry now. Rejected — contract edits stay out of packets and land at milestone close" — and this is that close. **§8:** the layout block gains `native/`, and the **Current** paragraph, which described one delivery channel, now states two — the served PWA and an Android APK built from `native/`, whose web root is assembled from `app/Dockerfile`'s `COPY` list, so both channels carry byte-identical assets and the production web path stays buildless in both. **§3:** the monorepo entry widens to three subtrees (and loses its "the split lands in M2" future tense, four milestones after the split landed); a new intent-level entry states the platform inversion this milestone exists to perform — on the Android channel the family's marks live in an on-device, encrypted, append-only, schema-bearing store which **is the source of truth**, WebView storage is a **losable cache**, and the export contour is produced on the device and needs no key, account or subscription.
- **e. The ADR-008 entry is SCOPED rather than left to collide, and the scoping is written in the decision layer's own terms.** Two unqualified "single source of truth" statements in one section make one of them read as false. The decision layer resolves this by amendment: the ADR-008 entry **describes the *server* contour and reads as a specification of rung L4, not as a statement about current storage** — the source of truth for family data is the device. That is the wording used, deliberately in preference to "the server-side corpus", which would have been a claim about the *shape of the data* when the amendment is a claim about **which rung the statement belongs to**. No live-infra identifier enters `AGENTS.md` in the process (`M1-P3-INV-002`); the operational state of any server-side store stays where it belongs, in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`.
- **f. The three side-finds `docs/execution-map.md` and `LSC-DL-004` addressed to this close are disposed of, not re-listed.**
  1. **SQLite journal-mode contention in the instrumented job** (`LSC-DL-004` debt 6) — **stays OPEN.** It is the app opening its store at boot while a test holds the same file: two writers on one database, benign in run `31680204645` by timing rather than by arrangement, and the failure it would eventually produce is intermittent. **What would close it:** serialise the app's boot-time store open against the instrumented tests, or give the tests their own database file, and re-observe on the emulator. Not fixed here — it is a change to test or product behaviour, and this packet ships neither.
  2. **`closeStore()` is defined and never called** (`LSC-DL-004` debt 1) — **stays OPEN.** `clean_shutdown` never returns to 1, so `store.open` reports `previous_run_clean` false on every launch but the first and each launch after the first pays an `integrity_check`. The signal is honest; the defect is upstream of it. **What would close it:** evidence on whether the Android WebView reliably fires `pagehide` before process death — and if it does not, a disposition that does not depend on it. Deliberately not guessed inside a close-out.
  3. **The stale gitignored `cap sync` artifact** under the generated Android project's `assets/public/` (`LSC-DL-004` debt 2) — **CLOSED as documented-not-fixed.** It is gitignored, `npm run sync` re-stages before every build, and `docs/RUNBOOK.md` warns against reading it as the shipped set at the exact point a reader meets it. **What would close it properly:** a staging step that cleans the directory rather than writing over it. That is a change to `native/tools/stage-webdir.js`, which this packet does not touch.
- **g. The ICU wording divergence keeps its substance and changes its address.** `LSC-DL-002` (c) measured it: the bundled engine compiles FTS5 and **not** ICU, ICU would not have folded `ё`/`е` or lemmatised Russian anyway, and what the schema secures instead is a **fully rebuildable** index — the FTS table holds no normalization decision, so any later word-form strategy is a rebuild and never a journal migration. What is wrong is the **upstream requirement's wording**, which still names ICU as mandatory, and the repository cannot correct it: the decision layer lives outside this repo. **This is the owner-side close task after merge**, the same posture `L2-DL-004` recorded for the upstream annotation of a milestone's entries. The repo record is complete as it stands and no acceptance line is marked satisfied here.
- **h. The (r-bis) geometry rule is OFFERED to the contract, not adopted by the packet that wrote it.** Stated in full so the owner can accept or redirect in one act: *a claim about rendered geometry counts only from the pinned container; a local run is good for logic and not for pixels.* The asymmetry is what makes it cheap to follow — a local run that goes **red** is still worth acting on, a local run that goes **green** proves nothing about geometry, because the same declarations resolve to different boxes here and there and font metrics are the reason. It would belong in `AGENTS.md` §9 (working conventions). **It is not written there by this packet**, because the contract surface this close is authorised to touch is §8 and §3, and a working convention adopted by the agent that proposed it is not a contract decision.
- **i. The next-track choice is recorded as open, and nothing is proposed.** It is an owner decision taken in the decision layer at milestone close. `docs/execution-map.md` carries it at the M5 line as a standing open item and marks **no** new **Current** track — the `L2-DL-004` and `A3-DL-003` posture. Advancing or resolving it here would be the repo answering a question that was never addressed to it.

### Rationale

A close-out earns its place only by doing what no packet inside the milestone could. Each item here passes that test for a different reason, and they are worth naming separately because "it was left to the close" is otherwise indistinguishable from "it was left".

The contract edits (d) could not land in P1–P4 because contract edits stay out of packets — `LSC-DL-001` did not defer them for convenience, it recorded the deferral as a rejected alternative with a rule attached. The map bump could not land in P4 because a packet cannot cite its own commit SHA, which is the same reason `L2-DL-004` and `A3-DL-003` exist. The device evidence (a) could not be recorded by P4 because it did not exist yet: the run that produced it ran **on** P4's final commit, after the entry describing that commit was written — which is exactly the situation a validation-honesty caveat is for, and exactly the situation an amendment-by-reference is for once the caveat is overtaken. The side-find dispositions (f) needed a place where all three could be weighed against each other rather than each being deferred by the packet that found it; two of them survive as open debt, and saying so once, with what would close each, is worth more than three separate carries. And (g), (h) and (i) are each a case of the repository correctly declining to decide something: an upstream wording, a contract convention, and a milestone sequence, all of which are the owner's.

The one thing this entry refuses to do is soften (b). It would have been easy to write "the disposition is observed" and stop; the run does not support the sentence without its boundary, and a close-out that overstates its evidence is worse than one that has none, because nobody re-checks a question the ledger says is settled.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Rewrite `LSC-DL-004`'s validation caveat in place.** Rejected — this log's convention is amendment by reference (`A3-DL-003`: the A3 entries are "left byte-untouched and amended from `A3-DL-003` instead"; `LSC-DL-004` amends `LSC-DL-001` (i) and (o) the same way). The caveat was true when written; an entry records what a packet knew, and rewriting it destroys the only evidence that the gap was ever seen. In-place correction stays reserved for spine files, which is where this packet does correct in place.
2. **Dispatch the emulator once more before the PR.** Rejected — see (c). No shipped byte changes; it would re-verify an unchanged device layer at emulator cost, and the PR event runs the job anyway.
3. **Record "the purge is observed".** Rejected as false — see (b). A fresh emulator has nothing to purge.
4. **Add the device-store entry to §3 and leave the ADR-008 entry unqualified.** Rejected — two unqualified source-of-truth statements in one section, one of which would then read as false.
5. **Scope the ADR-008 entry as "the server-side corpus".** Rejected on owner correction — "corpus" is a claim about the shape of the data, whereas the amendment is about **which rung the statement belongs to**. The entry now says *server contour* and *specification of rung L4*, which is what is actually true of it.
6. **Adopt the (r-bis) rule into `AGENTS.md` §9 now.** Rejected — see (h).
7. **Fix `closeStore()`, or the journal-mode contention, in this packet.** Rejected — both are product or test behaviour changes, and one of them turns on a native-lifecycle fact nobody has measured. A close-out that quietly ships a fix is a close-out nobody can review as a close-out.
8. **Leave the two "carried to the L1 milestone close" pointers in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`.** Rejected — after the close they point at an event that has happened, which turns a live instruction into a dangling reference.
9. **Record the observation as a new invariant, or annotate `LSC-P4-INV-004` with it.** Rejected — `docs/INVARIANTS.md` is enforced-only (`AGENTS.md` §10) and a close-out enforces nothing new; the invariant's Statement and Scope were already written to be true of an emulator observation. That the observation now exists is a decision-log fact, not an invariant fact, and `docs/INVARIANTS.md` ends this packet byte-untouched.
10. **Mark a next track `Current`.** Rejected — see (i).

### Supersedes

None. **Corrects in place** (spine files, statement-level): `docs/execution-map.md`'s L1-P4 bullet, whose side-find sentence said "**Both** are recorded in `LSC-DL-004` (debt 1 and 2) and **both** are stated in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`" — a count left from when two side-finds were listed rather than three, with (0) recorded as debt **6** and appearing in no RUNBOOK line — and whose last sentence, "The milestone PR opens here", was overtaken by the existence of this packet; the M5 line's stale "post-Б1 … next planning pass" framing of the standing next-track decision; and three statements in `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (the two "carried to the L1 milestone close" forward references, and step 2's "the instrumented job asserts this", which claims more than a fresh emulator can — see (b)). **Amends by reference, leaving the record byte-untouched:** `LSC-DL-004`'s validation-honesty caveat, per (a).

### Effects

- **Changed (contract):** `AGENTS.md` — §8's layout block and **Current** paragraph, §3's monorepo entry, a new §3 device-store entry, and the ADR-008 entry's scoping clause. The contract-integrity gate (`M1-P3-INV-002`, `scripts/check-contract-integrity.sh`) was run **before and after** these edits and is green in both directions; `AGENTS.md` is a `CONTRACT_FILES` member, so this is verification rather than assumption — the `A1-DL-008` precedent.
- **Changed (spine):** `docs/execution-map.md` — the L1 block closed (milestone **Done**, P4 **Done** @ 460bd39, this P5 line), the two corrections above, and the next-track line restated as the standing open owner decision. `docs/RUNBOOK.md` — three statement-level corrections, no section rewritten. `docs/decision-log.md` — this entry.
- **Untouched, and verified so:** `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/RUNTIME-INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/product/**`, `README.md`, and everything under `app/`, `native/`, `api/`, `scripts/`, `.github/`, `data/`. No parity baseline is rewritten.
- **Operability: none this packet** (ADR-013 / contract §4.7). No knob is added to `app/m/v1/store/config.js`, `app/m/v1/export/config.js` or `api/theygrow_api/parameters.py`; `PARAMETERS_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays **5**. No taxonomy entry in `api/theygrow_api/signals.py` or `app/m/v1/core/signals.js`, no `emitted_now` change, no producer added or removed, no GA4 event — no shipped `app/` file changes. **No new Python runtime import**, so the mypy hook's `additional_dependencies` are unchanged.
- **§4-safe.** No family datum, corpus record, credential, host, user, password, connection string or live identifier enters any file. **Net egress change: zero** — the packet adds no request and removes none; the native channel's GA4 removal was `LSC-DL-004`'s, and the web channel's is an open owner decision (below).

### Debt that survives the milestone, each with what would close it

1. **The `substitutionOption` switch** (`LSC-DL-001` j) — no build-config declares it, so the typo protection three configs claimed never existed; the Step 0 emptiness guard is what protects. **Closes when** a second delivery channel makes a mismatched substitution survivable, or when the switch is flipped deliberately and the resulting red is accepted as the intended failure mode.
2. **The unverified `ALLOW_LOOSE` claim** (`LSC-DL-001` k) — **closes when** it is observed in the live trigger configuration rather than asserted from a document.
3. **The PWA merge-trigger expectation stays OPEN, per build-config** (`LSC-DL-001` m) — the PWA trigger's substitutions are unknown from the repository, so what a merge does there is not a designed expectation and is not recorded as one. **Closes when** the trigger's substitution set is read and the expectation stated per config.
4. **Release signing configuration and key custody** (`LSC-DL-001` n) — the APK is debug-signed, no release keystore exists in the repository or in CI. **Escalated at this close** (below); no keystore, password, alias or secret value enters the repository under any branch of that decision.
5. **The web channel's analytics question** (`LSC-DL-001` o, `LSC-DL-004` j) — closed for the native channel only. **Escalated at this close** (below).
6. **veraPDF is fetched from an unversioned URL** (`LSC-DL-003` 0) — bounded by a recorded SHA-256 of the reviewed archive, an asserted version, and a job that is not on the push path. **Closes when** upstream publishes a versioned artifact, or the validator is built from its source tag. Unchanged this milestone.
7. **SQLite journal-mode contention** — (f)(1), with what would close it.
8. **`closeStore()` never called** — (f)(2), with what would close it.
9. **The import has never run against a real family's history** — only fixtures, and `legacyImportProbeBatch` has never been exercised at a size where batching is what makes it finish. **Closes when** the owner runs it on the real device against real browser history, which is step 3 of the RUNBOOK sequence.
10. **The owner-run L1-P4 sequence in `docs/RUNBOOK.md` has not been executed** — steps 1–8 are written from the design. Step 1 needs an APK built from a commit *before* P4, which nobody has built. **Closes when** the sequence is run once.
11. **Clearing `localStorage` after a successful import** is a separate explicit owner action and no packet performs it. Until it is taken, migrated marks have two homes — which is the reason (b) of the escalation below is bounded today.
12. **The two delivery channels diverge after P4** — the import is a one-way, parent-triggered bridge. Reconciliation is **L7's**, with the relay and key-scope model that are its only consumers. Not this milestone's, and deliberately not re-opened here.
13. **The parity suite structurally cannot see either native branch** — both of its channels serve the staged web root over plain HTTP with no Capacitor bridge injected, so both take the web branch. **Closes when** something drives the real WebView, which is what `android-instrumented` is for.
14. **The ICU wording upstream** — (g). Owner-side after merge.
15. **The upstream decision layer is not yet annotated** for `LSC-DL-001`…`005`. The repo log is the **working copy**; annotating the decision layer is the owner-side close task after merge (`L2-DL-004` posture).

### Escalations raised at this close (batched, delivered in the packet plan)

- **The web channel's analytics.** `LSC-DL-004` (j) removed GA4 from the native channel — loader included, since stopping the events while still fetching the loader leaves the egress in place. The PWA is unchanged and still emits under `GA-DL-001`. Public exposure + third-party egress, escalation list. Both branches were put to the owner with the one this packet would take marked; **execution is a separate packet under either branch**, because it is a product change to a shipped file and this close ships none.
- **Release signing and key custody, with the deadline restated so it is true rather than merely conservative.** The loss window does not open when an APK is distributed; it opens **the moment marks exist that were made natively and live nowhere else**. Today the exposure is bounded and recoverable — the import leaves `localStorage` intact (debt 11) and the export contour (`LSC-DL-003`) produces a durable artifact needing no key — so a reinstall is survivable. A **native-only mark has no second home**, and a debug-signed install cannot be upgraded in place by a release-signed APK: the upgrade path is uninstall-then-install, and uninstall takes the app sandbox with it. So the decision is due **before the first native-only mark exists on a device that matters**, which is earlier than first distribution and is the honest form of the deadline. The options are unchanged by this restatement; only when they must be chosen is.

### Validation-honesty caveat (M4-CLOSE discipline)

**What actually ran, on the tree this entry describes.** `scripts/parity-suite.sh` in the **pinned container** (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble`), full suite including both `visual-*` projects: **652 passed, 6 skipped, zero failures**, and **zero baseline writes** — `git status --porcelain` is identical before and after the run and no snapshot moved, which for a docs packet is the whole point: a documentation change that moves a rendered baseline has done something it did not intend. `pytest app/tests/schema app/tests/export`: **133 passed**, unchanged from `LSC-DL-004`. `pre-commit run --all-files` green with **zero modified files**. `scripts/check-contract-integrity.sh` green **before and after** the `AGENTS.md` edits. The diff is confined to `AGENTS.md` and three files under `docs/`.

**What none of this proves.** Nothing here is evidence about the device: no test in this packet's validation touches the emulator, and it should not — the tree's shipped bytes are unchanged, and the device claim rests on run `31683691498` and on its stated boundary (b), not on anything run today. The parity suite's green proves the **web** channel is unregressed and, by its own structure, says nothing about either native runtime branch. The two escalations are raised, not answered; the debt above is stated, not discharged; and the upstream decision layer still carries the pre-close wording for every `LSC-DL` entry, this one included.

## EMV-DL-001 — EMV-P1 `export-modal-visibility`: the export contour becomes reachable, the fix is delivered on a new mount because a published one cannot be rewritten, and the guard that watched this surface is given the half it was missing

- **Date.** 2026-08-13
- **Type.** Packet — EMV-P1, first packet of **EMV "export-contour reachability + L1 promotion"**. *(Namespace note: opens the `EMV-DL` namespace; packets are `EMV-P{k}`. The "Entry format" header is intentionally left unedited, per the `LSC-DL-003` / `L2-DL-002` / `A3-DL-002` precedent.)*
- **Scope.** One CSS rule, one page-driven test, one static guard, and the mount bump the rule's delivery requires. No schema, no migration, no new storage, no new egress, no new network surface, no build toolchain.

### Decision

- **a. The defect, and its true extent, read from the code rather than from the report.** `app/m/v1/app.css` declares `.modal { display: none }` and no `.modal.show`. **Four** elements carry the bare `.modal` class, not the three the handoff named: `#createProfileModal`, `#importModal`, `#storeUnavailableModal`, `#exportModal` (`app/index.html:252/277/295/308`). The fourth is the one that matters to the diagnosis: `#createProfileModal` is opened and closed with **inline** `style.display` (`surfaces/profile.js:112/116`), so it never depended on the missing rule, works today, and is unaffected by adding it — inline style wins over a class rule either way. The other three are opened by `classList.add('show')` and were dead: handler complete, class present, element `display: none`. One rule revives all three. Separately, `.skill-modal` also has no `.show` rule and this is **not** a defect — `#skillModal` is inline-style-driven too, which is why the guard below takes call sites as its subject rather than elements.
- **b. The rule is `display: block`, not `flex`.** `.modal-content` centres with `margin: 10% auto`, and the ≤767 px branch sets `margin: 0` with `100vw`/`100dvh` — both block-flow. `.activities-modal.show { display: flex }` pairs with `align-items`/`justify-content` that `.modal` does not declare. `block` is also what `#createProfileModal` has rendered with since before this packet, under a baseline that already exists.
- **c. The fix ships on a NEW mount, `/m/v1/` → `/m/v2/`, with `CACHE_VERSION` `v11` → `v12`. Decided outside the packet.** The plan raised this as a scope-boundary escalation, because the approved scope said the rule would land in `app/m/v1/app.css` and it does not. **The orchestrator resolved it as Branch A**, on this provenance: `docs/RUNBOOK.md` → **Module mount** (`A1-DL-004`) forbids rewriting the bytes of a published immutable mount — "a one-character CSS fix included" — and reaching already-installed clients is a decisive item of the packet's own scope. The mechanism, spelled out because "the fix is live once merged" is exactly the assumption this milestone exists to distrust: `app/sw.js` serves static assets **cache-first**, so an installed client keeps its cached `/m/v1/app.css` indefinitely, and a `CACHE_VERSION` bump alone refills the new generation **through the 30-day immutable HTTP cache**, which can hand back the same stale bytes and then survive every later bump. Navigation is **network-first**, so a shell repointed at `/m/v2/` arrives on the next navigation, and `/m/v2/app.css` exists in no HTTP cache and no Cache Storage generation — it is fetched from the network on first use. `app/m/v1/**` ends this packet **byte-untouched** (vault ADR-024: a published immutable asset is never rewritten or removed in place).
- **d. The mount-bump checklist was incomplete, and executing it is what showed that.** `docs/RUNBOOK.md` step 2 lists `app/index.html` and `app/sw.js`. Since L1-P2 and L1-P3 the mount also contains **self-referential absolute URLs**: `STORE_CONFIG.schemaUrl` and `EXPORT_CONFIG.declarationUrl` / `fontUrl` / `iccUrl`. A copy-forward that left them at `/m/v1/` would make the new generation fetch the frozen one's DDL, declaration, font and colour profile — working today by byte-identity, broken the day `v1` retires. All four are repointed in the `v2` copy, each carrying a `changed_in: EMV-DL-001` line beside its original rationale, and the RUNBOOK step gains the sub-step it was missing.
- **e. The guards that named the mount as a literal are made to follow it.** Thirty-five literals across ten spec files, plus three Python path constants, pinned `m/v1`. Left alone they would keep asserting against the **frozen** generation after the bump — shipped, present on disk, answering 200, and not the bytes anyone runs. That is a guard staying green for the wrong reason, which is the same failure class as the defect this packet fixes, so it is not left for later: `currentMount()` in `app/tests/support/ship-list.js` and `current_mount()` in `app/tests/schema/harness.py` derive the mount from the shell, fail closed on anything but exactly one version, and every literal now routes through them.
- **f. The behavioural claim is carried by a CLICK, and the static guard is explicitly not allowed to stand in for it.** `app/tests/behavior.spec.js` navigates, clicks `#exportBtn`, and asserts the modal is visible and computes to `display: block`, then that the close control returns it to `none`. `app/tests/show-rule-coverage.spec.js` asserts the separate, **static** property — that every `classList.add('show')` in the shipped mount targets an element carrying a class for which `app.css` declares a `.show` rule. Both were mutation-tested rather than reasoned about; the measurements are in the caveat below.
- **g. What is asserted about `#importModal` and `#storeUnavailableModal`, worded to match what runs.** Both are revived by the same rule and both get an assertion, and that assertion is: **the rule resolves these elements to `display: block`** — the class is applied in-page and the computed style is read in a real browser. It is **not** a claim that either modal becomes visible in use. Neither trigger is reachable on the web branch: `offerImportIfPending()` returns before touching the DOM without a native store handle, and `showStoreUnavailable()` sits behind `canRecord() === false`, which the web channel never reaches because `core/state.js` puts it on the localStorage backend. The behavioural claim for those two is `android-instrumented`'s and stays residual debt (`LSC-DL-005` debt 13).
- **h. The parity suite proves the WEB branch only, on both of its channels.** The `native` project serves the staged APK web root over plain HTTP with no Capacitor bridge injected, so it takes the same branch the `behavior` project does. The new click test therefore runs twice, at two viewports, against two delivery surfaces, and proves the web branch twice. What the native branch renders behind the same class is not claimed here.

### Rationale

The defect is worth more than its one-line fix, because of how it survived. Every guard over this surface was green throughout: the two non-negotiable sentences were in the shell, the control was in the header immediately left of the chat control, its accessible name was one string in three places, the sink was one method wide, no export module could reach the network. All of that was true. All of it was read out of source text. The property that was false — a parent presses the control and sees a modal — was the only one no test executed, and it is the only one the parent has.

So the packet's shape follows from the diagnosis rather than from the symptom: the rule, plus a test that performs the action a parent performs, plus a guard for the static half that nothing was watching, plus honest wording everywhere about which of the two carries which claim. The mount bump is not scope creep bolted on; without it the rule reaches nobody who already has the app installed, and a fix that does not reach installed users defeats the packet.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Edit `app/m/v1/app.css` in place and bump `CACHE_VERSION` only.** Rejected — `A1-DL-004`. `cache.addAll` refills through the immutable HTTP cache; the stale copy can win and then persist across every subsequent bump. Two lines of diff, and a fix that might reach nobody.
2. **Ship the CSS and tests now, cut the mount bump as the next packet.** Rejected by the orchestrator with the escalation (Branch B in the plan). Between the two merges the repository would contain a rewritten published immutable asset — the state `A1-DL-004` exists to make impossible — and promotion would gate on the second packet anyway.
3. **Bulk-replace `v1` → `v2` in the specs.** Rejected — it would leave exactly the same trap for the next bump. Derived, fail-closed helpers instead.
4. **Derive the mount from `import.meta.url` inside the shipped modules**, ending the knob repointing forever. Rejected **for this packet** — a behaviour change to shipped runtime modules, outside the shape of a visibility fix. Recorded here as the candidate it is.
5. **Retire `/m/v1/` in the same packet** to avoid shipping two generations. Rejected — `docs/RUNBOOK.md` item 3 makes retirement a separate owner cleanup, "never part of the bump packet".
6. **Inject a fake Capacitor bridge into the page to exercise the native branch of the export modal.** Rejected — `app/tests/store-unit.spec.js` already rules that covering the bridge with a fake proves the fake. Modal *visibility* is CSS and is identical across channels by `LSC-P1-INV-002`; the native branch is `android-instrumented`'s.
7. **Let the static guard carry the visibility claim** (it is cheaper and runs in the free per-push job). Rejected as the exact error under repair: it cannot execute a click, and the mutation below shows precisely how far it does not reach.

### Effects

- **Changed (shipped):** `app/m/v2/**` — new mount, copy-forward from `app/m/v1/` and verified byte-identical before editing; then, in `v2` only, the `.modal.show` rule, the four repointed knob URLs and one self-referential comment path. `app/index.html` — 45 mount references repointed. `app/sw.js` — 44 `OFFLINE_URLS` entries and comments repointed, `CACHE_VERSION` `v11` → `v12`. **`app/m/v1/**` is byte-untouched**, and `diff -r` says so.
- **Changed (tests):** `app/tests/show-rule-coverage.spec.js` (new), the export-modal block in `app/tests/behavior.spec.js` (new), `currentMount()` in `app/tests/support/ship-list.js`, `current_mount()` in `app/tests/schema/harness.py`, the mount literals in ten specs and three Python constants, and the `contract` project's `testMatch` in `app/playwright.config.js`.
- **Changed (spine):** `docs/INVARIANTS.md` — `EMV-P1-INV-001`. `docs/RUNBOOK.md` — the Module-mount checklist's missing sub-step, and the live promotion-smoke curls moved to the current mount. `docs/execution-map.md` — the EMV block and this packet's line. `docs/decision-log.md` — this entry.
- **Untouched, and verified so:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/RUNTIME-INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/product/**`, `README.md`, `api/`, `scripts/`, `.github/`, `data/`, and `app/m/v1/**`. **No parity baseline moves** — audited before any edit: zero mount literals across all 44 baseline files (the only `v1` hits are SVG path data, `M12 3v11`, in the export icon).
- **Operability (ADR-013 / contract §4.7): no new knobs and no new signals.** Four **existing** knob values are repointed by the bump, each gaining `changed_in: EMV-DL-001` provenance; `PARAMETERS_SCHEMA_VERSION` is untouched, no taxonomy entry is added to `app/m/v2/core/signals.js`, no `emitted_now` changes, no emitter is added or removed, no GA4 event. Opening the export modal still emits nothing, deliberately.
- **§4-safe.** No family datum, credential, host or live identifier enters any file. **Net egress change: zero.**
- **No new Python runtime import**, so the mypy hook's `additional_dependencies` are unchanged.
- **Not live on merge.** ADR-020: a merge deploys a zero-traffic revision. Promotion is a separate manual owner act, and nothing in this packet performs or implies it.

### Debt recorded, not fixed

1. **Two mount generations ship to both channels** — `/m/v1/` and `/m/v2/`, including a duplicate of the ~443 KB of print-layer assets, so the APK grows by roughly 900 KB. **Closes when** the owner retires `v1` (`docs/RUNBOOK.md` Module mount, item 3), which is a separate cleanup by design.
2. **The mount version is still hand-repointed in four shipped knobs on every bump.** Alternative 4 is what would close it.
3. **The trigger paths of `#importModal` and `#storeUnavailableModal` remain unexecuted by any automated test** — unreachable on the web branch, and `android-instrumented` does not currently drive either. Carried, not silently absorbed by (g)'s narrower assertion. **Closes when** the instrumented job drives a store-open failure and a pending legacy import on the device.

### Validation-honesty caveat (M4-CLOSE discipline)

**What actually ran, and where.** Agent-run on the host, outside the pinned container: `PARITY_NO_DOCKER=1 scripts/parity-suite.sh --project=contract` — **619 passed**, including the seven new show-rule-coverage tests, all six call sites resolved by name. `--project=behavior` — **17 passed**, including the new click test and the three pre-existing service-worker tests, which now exercise the update channel with `CACHE_VERSION v12`. `pytest app/tests/schema app/tests/export` — **133 passed**, unchanged in count from `LSC-DL-004` and now executing the `v2` mount's DDL and builder, which is the point of (e). `pre-commit run --all-files` — green, with **zero** files rewritten by the formatting hooks; it caught two real defects in this packet's own work first (a `no-any-return` in the new Python derivation, and a **live revision identifier** in `docs/execution-map.md` that `M1-P3-INV-002` correctly refused — identifiers belong in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`). Both were fixed, not suppressed.

**The mutations, as measurements rather than intentions.** *Mutation A* — the `.modal.show` rule deleted from the shipped mount: the click test red with `Expected: visible / Received: hidden`, which is the production symptom reproduced verbatim, and the static guard red on exactly three of its six call sites — `#exportModal`, `#importModal`, `#storeUnavailableModal` — with `#activitiesModal`, `#onboardingModal` and `#profileDropdown` still green. The guard reproduces the defect's boundary precisely. *Mutation B* — `openExportModal()`'s body emptied, the rule intact: the click test red on the same assertion; every **coverage** assertion in the static guard **green**, because the call site is gone and there is nothing left to cover. The one thing that reddened is the guard's own anti-vacuity test, and only because it names `exportModal` by hand — empty any other surface's handler and that file is green end to end. This is the measured demonstration that the static guard cannot carry a runtime claim, and it is why the packet does not let it. Both mutations were reverted and the two files verified byte-identical to their pre-mutation SHA-256.

**The baseline question, answered with what ran rather than with what was expected.** The audit came first, before any edit: **zero** mount literals across all 44 baseline files (the only `v1` hits are SVG path data, `M12 3v11`, in the export icon). Then the markup-level projects were actually run on the host — `dom-desktop` + `dom-mobile` (**30 passed, 1 skipped**) and `native` (**26 passed, 5 skipped**, the staged APK web root, which is also where the new click test runs a second time, at the mobile viewport). `git status --porcelain app/tests/__baselines__` is **empty** after every run: no snapshot moved and none was written, which `updateSnapshots: 'none'` makes a real assertion rather than a default.

**What none of this proves.** The `visual-desktop` / `visual-mobile` projects — the pixel baselines — are **owner-run in the pinned container** (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble`) and did **not** run here; the host has neither the container nor its font set. Per `LSC-DL-005` (h) a host run is good for logic and not for pixels, so the dom/native greens above are evidence about **markup and behaviour** and are **not** evidence about rendered geometry. Nothing in this packet should change a pixel — the rule only takes effect on elements carrying `show`, and no visual baseline captures that state — but that remains an expectation with a stated basis until the container run confirms it, and if a visual baseline moves it is a red to investigate, never a silent re-bless. No automated test in this repository proves that an **already-installed** client refreshes: the delivery argument in (c) is derived from the worker's own strategies and the cache semantics `A1-DL-004` records, and its end-to-end confirmation is the owner-run promotion smoke against the tagged revision. And the whole suite continues to prove the **web** branch only, on both of its channels, per (h).

## EMV-DL-002 — EMV-P2 `runtime-claim-rule`: a claim about runtime behaviour counts only when a test has executed it, and the rule ships with the detector that makes its own negative case provable

- **Date.** 2026-08-13
- **Type.** Packet — EMV-P2, second packet of **EMV "export-contour reachability + L1 promotion"**. Docs only.
- **Scope.** Four Markdown files: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, this log, `docs/execution-map.md`. No code, no test, no schema, no invariant, no knob, no signal, no network surface.

### Decision

- **a. The rule lands as `AGENTS.md` §11 "Evidence bar" — one normative home, and that home is the contract rather than the Claude-Code overlay.** A claim about **runtime** behaviour counts only once a test that **executes** that behaviour has executed it; a guard is **static** when its own code never starts the product — no page, no emulator, no process — and a static guard cannot carry a runtime claim however precisely it reads the source that would produce it. Scanning for **static** properties stays legitimate and remains preferred where it fits: presence of a file, absence of an import, shape of markup, composition of the ship list, provenance of a knob. `AGENTS.md` is the operating contract for **any** agent working here, and `CLAUDE.md`'s own conflict rule gives `AGENTS.md` product, architecture, scope and **invariants** while reserving `CLAUDE.md` for Claude-Code operational specifics — a standard of evidence is the former, not the latter. The section is placed immediately after §10 because the two are the same kind of rule: §10 sets the bar for what may be claimed as **enforced**, §11 sets the bar for what counts as **proof** of a runtime claim.
- **b. `Historical artifacts` renumbers §11 → §12, and this falsifies no citation.** Verified rather than assumed before the edit: the only occurrence of `§11` anywhere in the tracked tree was the `AGENTS.md` `Historical artifacts` header line itself, and every external citation — in this log, `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/execution-map.md`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `api/**` docstrings and shipped comments — is to §3, §4, §6, §7, §8, §9 or §10.
- **c. The detector ships with the rule, named in three parts, because an obligation without a detector is an intention.** **Check** — of every guard behind a claim, ask whether it could stay green with the handler body emptied or the shipped rule deleted, and whether its own code starts the product; if it cannot execute and boots nothing, what it carries is a static property whatever the claim says. **Admissible hits** — the static list in (a), which is what makes a negative result provable rather than merely absent. **Moment** — plan authoring, plan review, and acceptance of the execution report.
- **d. The satisfied case must leave a trace, or the rule is unverifiable in the direction that failed.** The Moment part, and the `CLAUDE.md` Plan-shape pointer with it, require a packet with no runtime claim to say so outright — "no runtime claims this packet" — rather than leaving the Validation section silent. This is the admissible-hits half applied to the plan itself: an absent statement reads to the next reader as *not checked*, which is indistinguishable from *checked and empty*, and that ambiguity is exactly what let four L1 claims pass unexamined.
