## RSN-DL-002 — RSN-P2 `signed-release-build`: the release APK is built by a workflow that touches the key as rarely as possible, and its signature is checked by a comparator that is provably able to go red

- **Date.** 2026-08-15
- **Type.** Packet — RSN-P2, the second packet of the **release-signing** milestone.
- **Scope.** `.github/workflows/release.yml` (new), `scripts/verify_release_signature.py` (new), `native/android/release-signing/cert-sha256.txt` (new), `app/tests/release/**` (new), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (two added steps), `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (the mypy target list), `native/android/.gitignore` (PKCS12 patterns). No shipped web byte, no schema, no migration, no product behaviour. Landed @ `19f62af`.

### Decision

- **a. The signed build lives in its OWN workflow with two triggers — tag push `v*` and `workflow_dispatch` — and deliberately no `push` on branches.** Every run decodes the release keystore, so the number of runs that touch that secret is minimised on purpose (`solo-shortcuts-registry` C-2: the keystore living in Actions is an accepted shortcut whose downside is irreversible, and the mitigations available today are the no-echo rule and not running this often). Bolting it onto `ci.yml` would touch the key on every commit.
- **b. The workflow publishes nothing.** No release is created, no asset uploaded, no `gh` invoked, and `permissions` stays `contents: read`. Widening pipeline permissions is a controlled class (PDR-018), and ADR-047 records automated asset publication as a separate decision that **has not been taken**. The owner downloads the artifact and publishes both files by hand — ADR-020, and on this channel there is no automatic delivery at all.
- **c. The verdict is a comparator in a file, not a `grep` in the workflow, because a detector has to be provably able to go red.** The release workflow's positive path only ever runs with the real keystore secret on an owner-triggered run; an inline shell check could therefore never be executed by an ordinary secret-free CI run, and its ability to fail could only be asserted by reading it. `scripts/verify_release_signature.py` is executed instead — by `app/tests/release/` against synthesised `apksigner` output, and by the `android` job against a **real** `apksigner` reading a **real** debug APK, whose certificate is by definition not the release certificate, where the correct verdict is exit **3** specifically. Any other code there means the detector is broken in a way that would otherwise surface for the first time on a release run.
- **d. The `certificate` in the parse pattern is load-bearing.** `apksigner` prints both `Signer #1 certificate SHA-256 digest:` and `Signer #1 public key SHA-256 digest:` for the same signer, and they are **different values**. A pattern matching "SHA-256 digest" alone would compare a public-key digest against a certificate fingerprint and be wrong in both directions — red on a correctly signed APK, and, if a baseline were ever recorded from the same wrong line, **green on an incorrectly signed one**. `app/tests/release` pins it with output that carries the public-key lines and no certificate line. The pattern also tolerates the `Signer (minSdkVersion=…, maxSdkVersion=…) #1` form newer build-tools emit.
- **e. The baseline is COMMITTED, human-readable, and never a secret.** `native/android/release-signing/cert-sha256.txt` holds one fingerprint in the uppercase colon-separated form `keytool` and the Play Console print, so it can be compared to the source of truth by eye; `apksigner` prints lowercase and colon-free and the comparator normalises **both** sides, so neither format is privileged. It is a fingerprint **of** a certificate, not key material. Moving it into an Actions secret would destroy the detector — the expected value would then live in the same store as the key it checks — and a test asserts the file keeps saying so.
- **f. Each release run ARMS the detector before trusting it, on an input generated in-run.** The arm-check derives a differing fingerprint from the live baseline by flipping its last nibble, feeds it through the comparator, and requires exit 3 before the real verdict runs. It is deliberately **not** a committed fixture: a fixture can be edited into agreement with a broken comparator, and the step would then pass while proving nothing. Derived in-run it tracks the baseline automatically and cannot drift. A green release run therefore carries its own evidence that the comparator was live **in that run** rather than borrowing it from a test that ran elsewhere.
- **g. The artifact is named from what the build EMITTED.** `versionName`/`versionCode` are read from `output-metadata.json` rather than re-derived from git: re-deriving would agree with itself even if the APK disagreed, and the filename is a claim about the APK. A static `latest` name is wrong outright — the owner publishes this file by hand, and a release page must never carry two different binaries under one name. The `.sha256` sidecar is in `sha256sum`'s own format so a downloader can `sha256sum -c` it in place, and it is computed in the run that produced the APK so what is published is what that run made.
- **h. The decoded keystore lives only under `RUNNER_TEMP`, and cleanup is `rm`, not `shred`.** `printf` is a shell builtin writing to a pipe, so the base64 never becomes a process argument and never appears in `/proc`; the file is `chmod 600` under a `0700` directory; the upload path is a dedicated subdirectory, never `RUNNER_TEMP` itself. The removal step runs `if: always()` and fails the job if the file survives. `shred` on an overlay filesystem does not deliver what its name promises, and the runner VM and its disk are destroyed with the run — claiming otherwise would be worse than doing the honest thing.
- **i. Runs are serialised and never cancelled in flight** (`concurrency: release`, `cancel-in-progress: false`). Two simultaneous runs would both have the keystore decoded on disk, and a cancelled run can be killed before its cleanup step completes.
- **j. PKCS12 patterns are added to `native/android/.gitignore`.** The generated file names `*.jks` / `*.keystore` — the formats ADR-047 did not take — while `build.gradle` sets `storeType 'PKCS12'` and the CI fail-closed leg mints a throwaway `.p12`. *(The same asymmetry at the two levels above was closed at the milestone close — `RSN-DL-003` (f).)*
- **k. The comparator and its suite join the mypy target list on the existing terms** — standard library only (`argparse`, `re`, `shutil`, `subprocess`) plus pytest, so the hook's `additional_dependencies` are unchanged; `app/tests/release` carries an `__init__.py` for the same collision reason as its siblings.

### Rationale

The expensive failure in this milestone is not a red release run — it is a **green** one that proved nothing. Two mechanisms can produce that: a comparator that cannot tell keys apart (d), and a check whose ability to fail was never observed (c, f). Both are addressed by executing the detector against inputs that must make it red, on every push and again inside each release run, so that the one run nobody can rehearse — the one holding the real key — is the only new thing on the day.

The rest follows from the shortcut this milestone accepts. Keeping a signing key in Actions is a solo-developer trade with an irreversible downside, so the mitigations that remain available are used in full: fewest possible runs (a), narrowest possible permissions (b), shortest possible life on disk (h), and no path by which a value reaches a log.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Extend `ci.yml` with a release job behind an `if:`.** Rejected — the keystore would be decoded on runs that have nothing to do with a release, and the trigger surface would be the whole push traffic (a).
2. **Publish the release from CI with `contents: write`.** Rejected — PDR-018 controlled class, and ADR-047 leaves CI-side publication explicitly undecided. Carried forward as an open decision (`RSN-DL-003`).
3. **`grep -i "$FINGERPRINT"` over `apksigner` output.** Rejected — see (c); also substring-matching a hex string is the over-matching failure class this repository has already been bitten by.
4. **Keep the baseline in an Actions secret** so the fingerprint is "private". Rejected — it is public information, and co-locating it with the key destroys the detector's independence (e).
5. **A committed fixture for the arm-check.** Rejected — see (f).
6. **Name the artifact `theygrow-latest.apk`.** Rejected — hand publication plus a static name is how a page ends up serving two different binaries under one name (g).
7. **`shred` the decoded keystore.** Rejected as a claim the filesystem cannot honour (h).
8. **Cancel in-flight runs on a new one.** Rejected — cleanup may not complete (i).
9. **Have the workflow also verify the debug APK, for symmetry.** Rejected — that check belongs where it is free and already runs: the `android` job, where it doubles as the comparator's negative leg (c).

### Supersedes

None. Builds on `RSN-DL-001` — the workflow supplies exactly the three environment variables that entry's guard requires, and its `fetch-depth: 0` is what keeps that guard's versionCode leg from firing.

### Effects

- **Added:** `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `scripts/verify_release_signature.py`, `native/android/release-signing/cert-sha256.txt`, `app/tests/release/{__init__.py,harness.py,test_verify_release_signature.py}`.
- **Changed (CI):** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `pytest app/tests/release` in `quality`, and *The signature comparator rejects a foreign certificate* in `android`. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` — the mypy target list.
- **Changed (hygiene):** `native/android/.gitignore` — `*.p12` / `*.pfx`.
- **Enforced:** `RSN-P2-INV-001`.
- **§4-safe.** The only value this packet commits is a certificate fingerprint, which is public by construction. **Net egress change: zero** — the workflow reaches GitHub's own artifact store and nothing else.
- **No new knobs and no new signals.** Exit codes and `THEYGROW_RELEASE_*` tokens are a CLI contract consumed by CI steps, not an operational signal surface.
- **No new Python runtime import** — standard library only (k).

## RSN-DL-003 — RSN-CLOSE `release-signing` close-out: the milestone closes on a procedure that says which of its own steps have never been run, and on a roll-up addressed to the packet that will close the legs it leaves open

- **Date.** 2026-08-15
- **Type.** Packet — RSN-CLOSE, the close-out of the **release-signing** milestone (`RSN-P1` @ `ea70259`, `RSN-P2` @ `19f62af`).
- **Scope.** Docs and ignore hygiene: `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, `docs/decision-log.md`, `docs/execution-map.md`, `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `native/.gitignore`, `.gitignore`. No workflow, no Gradle, no comparator, no test, no shipped byte, no schema, no migration, no invariant enforcement added by this packet itself, no knob, no signal, no new egress. **Landed this packet.**

### Decision

- **a. The RUNBOOK states, inside itself, which of its steps are proven and which the owner executes for the first time.** A release procedure that reads as if everything has been done before is the failure mode here, and the whole workflow has **never run on any trigger**. The section therefore opens with a two-column table: proven **on every push** (the comparator's two red legs, the guard's two signing legs, `check-yaml` on the workflow file) against first-executed-by-the-owner (the secrets decoding, the keystore opening, the alias resolving, the **positive** verdict, the arm-check, the `output-metadata.json` read-back, `sha256sum -c`, the upload, the keystore removal), and the steps themselves carry a **(first execution)** marker so the boundary survives being read out of order.
- **b. The two red outcomes with different cures are written apart, at length, and neither cure is "relax the check".** A **secret** failure (`…KEYSTORE_DECODE_FAILED` / `…KEYSTORE_UNREADABLE` / `…KEY_ALIAS_ABSENT`) is cured by **re-minting the secret, never the key** — the distinction is spelled out because a new key is a new application identity, a stale committed baseline and a second uninstall-reinstall for every family device, i.e. a five-minute fix mistaken into a data-loss event. A `THEYGROW_RELEASE_CERT_MISMATCH` has exactly two causes, the run prints both fingerprints labelled so no second run is needed to tell them apart, and the baseline branch is documented as the **two-file edit** it actually is (`native/android/release-signing/cert-sha256.txt` **and** the `EXPECTED` constant pinned in `app/tests/release/test_verify_release_signature.py`) — an owner who changes only the first gets a red `quality` job with no explanation attached.
- **c. The first-install consequence is stated as a data event, not as an installation note, and the wording constraint on it is load-bearing.** The release APK is signed by a different key than the installed debug build, so Android will not update over it; the install is uninstall-then-install and the app sandbox goes with it. Export first if the sandbox holds anything. **And the app-side export does not protect the family's real history** — that history is in the browser's `localStorage` under the production origin, is untouched by any uninstall, and must not be cleared until the browser→app transfer path exists (ADR-043 §3 and its 2026-08-15 annotation; the migration bridge reads the WebView's own storage). This is done now because the window in which a reinstall costs nothing closes with the first diary packet (ADR-047 consequences).
- **d. The restorability check is documented in TWO legs, and the difference between them is stated rather than smoothed over.** ADR-047 §7 names the `apksigner verify --print-certs` leg against a previously signed APK as the restorability check. That leg cannot fail when a backup is unreadable — it never opens a backup — so as written it does not verify what it claims. The RUNBOOK therefore carries **(a) the backup leg** — `keytool -list -v` against **each** backup copy with the password from its separate home, fingerprint compared to the committed baseline — named as the leg that **discharges the C-2 obligation**, and **(b) the artifact leg** — `apksigner`, or the shipped comparator reusing the same baseline — named as the leg that proves a **published binary** is still ours. Both are documented; neither is softened; (b) is explicitly not allowed to stand in for (a). *(The vault-side correction of ADR-047 §7's own wording is the owner's; this packet's obligation was that the RUNBOOK be true.)*
- **e. The two statements this milestone falsifies are corrected, in place and statement-scoped.** `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s "It is **debug-signed**: no release keystore exists, and none is created by this packet" — the debug artifact is still debug-signed and that path is unchanged, but a release keystore now exists and key custody is no longer "a later explicit decision"; the corrected step also points at the first-install warning, since the two builds cannot install over each other. And `native/.gitignore`'s "Nothing in this packet produces a release key (debug signing only)". A **third** statement of the same class was surfaced by this packet's own containment check — not by going looking — in a file already being edited: `LSC-P1-INV-002`'s Scope in `docs/INVARIANTS.md` read "the APK is debug-signed and no release keystore exists". It is corrected statement-scoped, under the standing rule that no known-false statement survives an edit pass in a file the packet already has open; the rest of that entry stands byte-untouched. All three are marked as corrections at the point of correction, per house style. **No other stale text was swept** — that is a milestone-close side-find class with its own venue, not a licence to sweep, and the two candidates found and left are named in the roll-up below.
- **f. The keystore ignore asymmetry is closed here rather than carried to a fourth packet** (owner direction at plan approval, and the right call): `native/.gitignore` and the repository-root `.gitignore` gain `*.p12` / `*.pfx` (the root file carried **no** keystore pattern at all), so all three ignore files now know the format actually in use. Two lines against a gap whose failure mode is a private key in git history — which no later commit removes — and the kind of asymmetry that never earns its own packet. The document-side mitigation stands alongside it: keystore material is handled **outside** this tree, and the RUNBOOK says so at the step where a reader would otherwise reach for a scratch file.
- **g. Two invariants are recorded, each naming its gate AND its cadence, because the cadences are not equal.** `RSN-P1-INV-001` is enforced **on every push**. `RSN-P2-INV-001`'s release-side leg runs **only on owner-triggered release runs and has never executed** — a weaker thing than a per-push gate, and the entry says so rather than blurring it; what runs on every push is the comparator's ability to go red, which is what makes the release-time verdict worth anything. Both are `Landed in` their own packet (`RSN-P1` / `RSN-P2`), not this one: this close-out enforces nothing new (`AGENTS.md` §10) and records what the branch's earlier packets enforce.
- **h. No new `Current` track.** The next-track choice is the standing open owner decision recorded at the M5 line — the `LSC-DL-005` / `EMV-DL-004` posture. The milestone flips to **Done**, with the flat statement that the release workflow has never run carried into the map itself rather than left in this entry.

### Rationale

The milestone's remaining risk is not in the code — it is that the one person who will ever run this procedure will run it once, under time pressure, against a workflow nobody has watched execute, on devices holding data that exists nowhere else. Everything above is aimed at that hour: a document that distinguishes what is known from what is about to be found out (a), cures that cannot be confused with each other (b), a data warning placed before the irreversible step rather than after it (c), and a periodic check that actually verifies the thing it claims to verify (d).

### Alternatives considered

1. **Fold the close-out record into `RSN-DL-002`.** Rejected at owner direction — the `EMV-DL-004` / `LSC-DL-005` precedent gives a close-out its own address, and the roll-up below needs one that the packet eventually closing those legs can cite.
2. **Document the restorability check as ADR-047 §7 words it, one leg.** Rejected — see (d); it would put a check in the runbook that cannot fail for the reason the check exists.
3. **Carry the `.gitignore` asymmetry as a fourth packet.** Rejected at owner direction — see (f).
4. **Write the release procedure as a clean sequence without the proven/unexecuted split.** Rejected — `AGENTS.md` §11 applied to prose: the document would read as a record of things that had been done, and every one of them would be a first.
5. **Sweep the other stale statements while in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`.** Rejected — scope, and the standing rule that contract/docs staleness is a close-out **side-find** with its own venue. Only statements this milestone itself falsified are corrected (e).
6. **Add the release channel to "What runs today".** Rejected for this packet — it is not false today, so it is not in the corrected set; left to the next RUNBOOK-touching packet (roll-up below).
7. **Widen `notify.yml` so release runs notify Telegram.** Rejected — a behaviour change in a docs packet, and the owner triggers a release run and watches it (roll-up below).
8. **Restate the certificate fingerprint in the RUNBOOK for convenience.** Rejected — one home only; a second copy is a second thing to correct on any rotation, and the value is already pinned in two places (the baseline file and the test).

### RSN-CLOSE — what this milestone carries forward

**1. Three guard legs have never executed, and one of them is the leg this milestone's contract rests on.** `native/android/app/build.gradle`'s guard has four failure paths; the `android` job executes two (`THEYGROW_RELEASE_SIGNING_MISSING`, and `THEYGROW_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_UNREADABLE` via the unopenable-keystore branch). Unexecuted: the `KEYSTORE_UNREADABLE` **path-is-not-a-readable-file** branch; `THEYGROW_RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS_ABSENT`; and **`THEYGROW_RELEASE_VERSIONCODE_UNRESOLVED`**, which is the one the release workflow's `fetch-depth: 0` contract rests on — nothing has ever made it fire, so "a shallow checkout fails the release closed" is implemented and unobserved.

*What would close it, worked out and not taken here:* extend the existing `android`-job step with a third and fourth leg, minting the same throwaway PKCS12 and passing the **correct** password and alias so the first three checks pass. Because that job's `actions/checkout` runs at the default depth 1, **the tree is already shallow** — the versionCode leg fires with no extra setup, at the cost of one Gradle configuration and no build, in the free per-push gate rather than the dispatch job. The alias-absent and bad-path legs are the same step with a wrong alias and with `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PATH` naming no file. **Named dependency:** if the `android` job ever gains `fetch-depth: 0`, the versionCode leg needs its own shallow clone (`git clone --depth 1 file://$PWD`) or it will silently stop testing anything.

**2. Release runs produce no Telegram notification, and that was left alone deliberately.** `.github/workflows/notify.yml` is a `workflow_run` listener scoped to `workflows: ["CI"]`, so `Release` completions notify nothing. Widening it is a behaviour change and outside a docs packet; it is also the weaker case for notification — a release run is owner-triggered and watched, unlike the push traffic notification exists for. *What would close it:* one line in `notify.yml`'s `workflows:` list, in a packet that can watch a release run afterwards.

**3. Publishing the asset from CI is undecided, not deferred by accident.** It would require `permissions: contents: write` — a controlled class (PDR-018) — and ADR-047 records it as a separate decision that has not been taken. Until it is, publication is owner-run and the RUNBOOK's hand-publication steps are the procedure of record. *What would close it:* an owner decision, then a packet that adds the permission at job scope with the upload step and nothing else.

**4. Smaller, named so they are not rediscovered:** `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s "What runs today" describes the delivery channels without the signed Android release (not false, so not corrected here — see alternative 6); `LSC-DL-001` (n) and `LSC-DL-005`'s escalation 4 still say the APK is debug-signed with no release keystore, and are **deliberately left byte-untouched** — this log records what a packet knew and amends by reference (`A3-DL-003`, `LSC-DL-005` alternative 1), which is what `RSN-DL-001`'s Supersedes block does; and the RUNBOOK's owner-fill placeholders for the two backup locations, the password's separate home and the key alias remain unfilled, by the standing rule that recording an identifier is a deliberate owner action rather than a documentation default.

### Supersedes

None. **Corrects in place** (statement-level): `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s debug-signing step and `native/.gitignore`'s signing-material comment, both falsified by `RSN-DL-001`. **Extends** rather than replaces the standing debt roll-ups (`LSC-DL-005`, `EMV-DL-004` blocks A–C): the items above are this milestone's own and do not restate theirs.

### Effects

- **Changed (spine):** `docs/RUNBOOK.md` — one added section (**Release build + APK distribution (RSN, owner-run)**), the corrected debug-signing step, and one cross-reference sentence under **Drill cadence**. `docs/execution-map.md` — the RSN track block. `docs/INVARIANTS.md` — `RSN-P1-INV-001`, `RSN-P2-INV-001`, plus the statement-scoped correction to `LSC-P1-INV-002`'s Scope (e). `docs/decision-log.md` — `RSN-DL-001`, `RSN-DL-002`, this entry.
- **Changed (hygiene):** `native/.gitignore` (comment corrected; `*.p12` / `*.pfx` added), `.gitignore` (keystore block added).
- **Untouched, and verified so:** every shipped byte — `app/index.html`, `app/sw.js`, `app/m/**`, `app/kb-v1.json`, `app/Dockerfile`, `app/nginx.conf`, `app/manifest.json` — plus `.github/workflows/**`, `native/android/app/build.gradle`, `scripts/**`, `app/tests/**`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/RUNTIME-INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/product/**`, `README.md`, `api/**`, `data/**`. No parity baseline is written; no `CACHE_VERSION` bump is owed, since no shipped byte moved.
- **§4-safe.** No family datum, no secret value, no live-infra identifier enters any file; the certificate fingerprint is referenced by path and never restated. **Net egress change: zero.**
- **No new knobs and no new signals** (ADR-013 / contract §4.7) — this packet documents an existing procedure and changes no runtime surface.
- **No new Python runtime import**, so the mypy hook's `additional_dependencies` are unchanged.
- **No new invariant is enforced BY this packet**; the two entries record enforcement landed in `RSN-P1` / `RSN-P2` (`AGENTS.md` §10).

## RSN-DL-004 — RSN-P3 `detector-parse-fidelity` (checkpoint A, diagnose): the detector that went red for an unnamed reason is made to say what it saw, and its red stops hiding the next detector's verdict

- **Date.** 2026-08-15
- **Type.** Packet — RSN-P3, opened **after** the `release-signing` close-out (`RSN-DL-003`) because the gate built by `RSN-P2` went red on the first real run of the thing it was built to prove. It is the **diagnose** half of a two-half packet: the repair is `RSN-P4` / `RSN-DL-005`, planned once the run's output exists.
- **Scope.** `scripts/verify_release_signature.py` (diagnostics added; parse, comparison and exit codes untouched), `app/tests/release/harness.py` (a stub-apksigner factory), `app/tests/release/test_apksigner_invocation.py` (new), `app/tests/release/test_verify_release_signature.py` (diagnostic assertions added), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (one `if:` on an existing step, plus comments), `docs/decision-log.md` (this entry). No shipped web byte, no schema, no migration, no product behaviour, no workflow logic beyond that one condition, no knob, no signal, no new egress. **Landed this packet.**

### The evidence this packet starts from

CI run **31894850072**, job `android`, step *The signature comparator rejects a foreign certificate*: the comparator returned **4** (`THEYGROW_RELEASE_CERT_UNPARSEABLE`) against the debug APK, where the whole point of that step is that it returns **3**. What the log rules in and out on its own is small: apksigner was found (not 7) and exited zero (not 8), so a binary ran and produced something; nothing in what was parsed matched the certificate-digest pattern. Everything past that was hypothesis, and the log contained nothing with which to choose between hypotheses.

### Decision

- **a. Checkpoint A repairs nothing. It makes the detector self-diagnosing, and the push IS the measurement.** At least two explanations survive that log and they need opposite repairs — a certificate block on the parsed stream in a line shape neither handled variant covers (repair: the pattern, plus a fixture built from the real bytes), or nothing on the stream that is read / not the binary we think (repair: the invocation). Shipping a candidate fix alongside the diagnostic would destroy the measurement: a green would not say which change earned it. So what is parsed (stdout), what is matched (the **certificate** line, never the public-key one, `RSN-DL-002` (d)) and the exit codes the two workflows branch on are **deliberately unmoved** by this packet.
- **b. Widening the pattern to make the symptom go away is excluded by construction, not by intention.** A looser pattern is exactly how a public-key digest gets compared against a certificate fingerprint — green on a wrongly signed APK. The decoy test that pins this (`test_does_not_read_the_public_key_digest`) stands untouched and binds the repair packet too.
- **c. The three verdicts that are blind by construction now print what they saw.** `THEYGROW_RELEASE_CERT_UNPARSEABLE`, `…APK_UNVERIFIED` and `…APKSIGNER_ABSENT` emit, to stderr, under the token line: how apksigner was resolved (path, the build-tools directory it came from, **every** candidate considered with the winner marked, and the state of each SDK-root environment variable — candidates deduplicated by resolved path, because the runner image points **both** SDK-root variables at one directory and a block reporting four tools where two exist would be untrustworthy about precisely the thing it exists for), the argv, the exit code, per-stream byte/line/marker counts, and a bounded excerpt of **both** streams. `ABSENT` was in no handoff scope line and is included anyway — it is the same function, the same records, and the third way this step can go red without saying why. A **mismatch** deliberately gets **no** block: it already prints both fingerprints labelled, and an excerpt there would print certificate output on every owner release run for nothing.
- **d. The block ends on a one-line `READING:` that names which explanation the bytes support.** Nothing arrived on stdout while stderr carried output → *invocation defect, not a pattern defect*. A `Signer`/`certificate` block on stdout that no line matched → *pattern defect, read the lines below verbatim*. Output on stdout mentioning neither → *not `apksigner --print-certs` output; check which binary was resolved*. The reader who needs this has the run log and **nothing else** — no checkout, no source — and leaving the distinction to be inferred from raw bytes is how a red gets diagnosed by guesswork, which is the failure this packet exists to end. The line is derived from the bytes and never touches the verdict.
- **e. The excerpt is bounded on three axes and says what it dropped.** 24 lines per stream, 160 characters per line, a hard 4 000-character cap per stream; every omission is **counted** in the footer, and an empty stream is named as `(EMPTY — nothing at all arrived here)` rather than shown as blank space — "stdout was empty" is a distinct diagnosis from "stdout was one newline" and the rendering has to carry that difference. A silently truncated excerpt would be its own kind of lie.
- **f. The one line that can carry a person's name is redacted, and only that line.** `Signer #N certificate DN: CN=…` becomes `… DN: <redacted: N chars>`. The excerpt is apksigner's public certificate output, not key material (ADR-047 detector (c)) — but the same discipline applies to how it is emitted, and a DN adds nothing to identifying a key that the hex digests do not already give. The **label** survives on purpose: "a certificate block was present" is one half of the distinction in (d). This is a conservative default chosen in planning rather than an escalation, because there is no design fork left once the value is gone.
- **g. One red must not hide another's verdict, and the mechanism must not itself be a way to lose a red.** The fail-closed detector (`assembleRelease` × two legs) never ran on 31894850072 — steps default to `if: success()` — so the milestone still does not know whether those legs pass. It now carries `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`. **Both detectors stay ordinary hard failures**: no `continue-on-error`, no summarising gate step, and therefore **no line whose deletion turns two reds into a green job**. Deleting this one condition costs only the second verdict on runs where the first already failed; the job is still red from the first. Verified against the job rather than against Actions folklore: the comparator step runs python against an already-built APK and mutates nothing the fail-closed step needs, and the same semantics are already relied on in this file by the `eval` job's `Upload scorecard` step, which exists precisely because the step before it exits 1. Known consequence, stated rather than hidden: after an unrelated earlier failure this step also runs and will likely red for that same cause; its red is then secondary.
- **h. The diagnostic is executed, not merely read — by a stub apksigner planted in a fake SDK.** `fake_apksigner()` writes an executable stub under `<root>/build-tools/<version>/`, so `pytest app/tests/release` now drives the **`--apk`** entry point end to end on every push with no Android SDK: which binary is resolved out of several (integer-tuple version order — `9.0.0` sorts above `36.0.0` as a string, and picking the older tool is one of the ways this detector could red for a reason unrelated to any signature), what the block prints, that the bound holds, that the DN is gone, and — first — that the verdicts did not move. **What it does not prove:** anything about what a real apksigner prints. That claim belongs to the `android` job and to nothing else, which is the whole shape of the gap this packet was opened by. The suite is POSIX-only and says so.
- **i. The packet is numbered RSN-P3 in the existing namespace, after a close-out.** A close-out closes a milestone, not a namespace, and this repairs `RSN-P2`'s own detector; a new milestone namespace would put the repair of a gate further from the gate than its own failure was.

### Rationale

The prior class of defect on this repository, twice, is a check that goes **green** for a reason other than the one named. This is its mirror — **red** for a reason other than the one named — and it is diagnosed the same way: by making the tool say what it actually saw, rather than by reasoning about what it probably saw. The distinction matters because the two live explanations here have opposite repairs, and the repair that would make the symptom disappear fastest (a looser pattern) is precisely the one that reintroduces the green-for-the-wrong-reason failure at release time.

The second half is about what a red costs. A detector whose failure stops the job also stops every detector after it, so one unexplained red bought silence about an entirely separate claim — and the cure for that must not be a mechanism (a gate step, a `continue-on-error`) whose own deletion would downgrade two reds to a green.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Ship a candidate parse fix now, with the diagnostics.** Rejected — see (a). It is the difference between measuring and guessing, and a green would then be uninterpretable.
2. **`continue-on-error: true` on both detectors plus a summarising gate step.** This was the approved plan's design and it is **rejected at owner direction, correctly**: it creates exactly one line — the gate — whose deletion demotes two reds to a green job, in a repository whose named defect class is the false green. `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` delivers the same "both report" property with no such line.
3. **A second job for the release guards, so each detector reds independently.** Rejected — it duplicates checkout, Node, Java, `npm ci` and `cap sync` on every push against the standing CI-spend decision, and the fail-closed leg needs the synced Gradle project that job already has.
4. **Upload the raw apksigner output as a build artifact instead of excerpting it.** Rejected — more machinery and more exposure for certificate output than a bounded in-log excerpt, and an artifact is not where someone reading a red step looks.
5. **Invoke `apksigner --version` on the failure path to pin the format.** Rejected — a second guessed invocation on a path that is already failing, when the build-tools **directory name** is the version and is already reported.
6. **Redact nothing.** Rejected — see (f). **Redact the DN line entirely** was rejected in the other direction: it destroys half of the distinction in (d).
7. **Do the repair in this same packet once the run prints.** Rejected at owner direction — a change whose design is admittedly not decidable before the output exists cannot be executed under a plan that could not design it. That is what per-packet Plan Mode is for.

### Supersedes

None. **Extends** `RSN-DL-002` (c) and (d): the comparator's ability to go red was proven before it ever ran for real, and this entry records what that first real run then cost to interpret — the detector could say *that* it failed and not *what it saw*. It falsifies nothing in `RSN-DL-001`–`003`.

### Effects

- **Changed:** `scripts/verify_release_signature.py` (diagnostics; `find_apksigner` now returns the choice **and** the candidate set; the `APK_UNVERIFIED` path's previously unbounded stdout/stderr dump is replaced by the bounded renderer). `app/tests/release/harness.py` (`fake_apksigner`), `app/tests/release/test_apksigner_invocation.py` (new, 12 tests), `app/tests/release/test_verify_release_signature.py` (5 added tests). `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — one `if:` line on the fail-closed step, plus comments on both detector steps. `docs/decision-log.md` — this entry.
- **Untouched, and verified so:** every shipped byte (`app/index.html`, `app/sw.js`, `app/m/**`, `app/kb-v1.json`, `app/Dockerfile`, `app/nginx.conf`, `app/manifest.json`), `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `native/android/app/build.gradle`, `native/android/release-signing/cert-sha256.txt`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, `docs/execution-map.md`, `api/**`, `data/**`. No parity baseline is written; no `CACHE_VERSION` bump is owed, since no shipped byte moved.
- **§4-safe.** No family datum, no secret value, no live-infra identifier enters any file. The diagnostic emits a bounded excerpt of a **public** certificate block with distinguished names redacted, on failure paths only, to a CI log. **Net egress change: zero.**
- **No new knobs and no new signals** (ADR-013 / contract §4.7). No exit code, no `THEYGROW_RELEASE_*` token, and no CLI flag is added, removed or renumbered — that set is the contract two workflows branch on.
- **No new Python runtime import** (`argparse`, `os`, `re`, `shutil`, `subprocess`, `sys`, `pathlib`, `typing` — all already in use), so the mypy hook's `additional_dependencies` are unchanged.
- **No new invariant.** `RSN-P2-INV-001` stands as written and nothing in it becomes false: the `android` step still runs the real apksigner and still requires exit 3, and the comparison still reads the certificate digest. Its **Enforced by** now *understates* what enforces it (the fail-closed step's `!cancelled()` condition; the stub-driven `--apk` suite) — a statement-scoped touch-up deferred to the repair packet, which will be editing that entry anyway.
- **The claim this milestone still cannot make:** "the comparator returns exactly 3 against a foreign certificate on a real APK with the real tool." It is executed by the `android` job and by nothing here. Until a run shows it, it is **unproven**.

## RSN-DL-005 — RSN-P4 `detector-pattern-repair` (checkpoint B, repair): the pattern is widened to the shape the tool actually prints, and the five near-misses beside it each get a test saying no

- **Date.** 2026-08-15
- **Type.** Packet — RSN-P4, the **repair** half of the two-half packet `RSN-DL-004` opened. Its design was deliberately not attempted before the measurement existed; the measurement is CI run **31896998977**.
- **Scope.** `scripts/verify_release_signature.py` (the parse pattern, its comment block, two messages that named the old shape, one resolution line on the `--apk` path), `app/tests/release/fixtures/apksigner-buildtools-37.0.0.txt` (new — the first recorded apksigner bytes in this repository), `app/tests/release/harness.py` (`recorded_output`, `scheme_qualified_output`), `app/tests/release/test_recorded_apksigner_output.py` (new), `app/tests/release/test_verify_release_signature.py` and `test_apksigner_invocation.py` (added tests), `docs/decision-log.md`, `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, `docs/execution-map.md`. No shipped web byte, no schema, no migration, no product behaviour, no workflow file, no Gradle, no exit code, no token, no knob, no signal, no new egress. **Landed this packet.**

### The evidence this packet starts from

CI run **31896998977**, job `android`, step *The signature comparator rejects a foreign certificate*. RSN-P3's diagnostic block answered in one run what the previous run could not answer at all: apksigner resolved to `build-tools/37.0.0` out of six candidates, exited **0**, put **1026 bytes on stdout** and **nothing at all on stderr**, and the READING line named a **PATTERN defect**. The wrong-stream hypothesis — the other live explanation, and the one that would have needed the opposite repair — died on that empty stderr.

The line the tool prints is `V2 Signer: certificate SHA-256 digest: <64 hex>`. The pattern that stood required `Signer` at the start of the line **and** a `#N` on it, so it missed that line **three ways at once**: the line is scheme-qualified, it carries no `#N` anywhere on this build-tools version, and `Signer` is followed by a colon. The detector had therefore returned 4 on every push since RSN-P2, and failing **closed** on a shape it did not recognise is the correct behaviour of the thing this packet repairs (ADR-047 §8): the artifact a family installs is trusted because this check ran, so failing open is the worst outcome available to it.

### Decision

- **a. The pattern is widened in COVERAGE OF LINE SHAPES and in nothing else.** It accepts four prefixes on one line — the observed `V2 Signer:`, the classic `Signer #N`, the rotation-aware `Signer (minSdkVersion=…, maxSdkVersion=…) #N`, and the two combined — and `certificate` and `SHA-256` remain mandatory and adjacent. Every digest it will accept is still a certificate SHA-256. The RUNBOOK's standing sentence — *"Do not widen the comparator… A detector that cannot tell two keys apart is worth less than no detector, because it is believed"* — is the constraint this decision is written against, not an obstacle to it.
- **b. The older shapes are KEPT, not replaced.** The release workflow and the `android` job need not run the same runner image, and `release.yml`'s in-run arm-check writes the classic shape. A repair that swapped one exact shape for another exact shape would be the same defect pointed at a different version.
- **c. The five near-misses each get their own test, and the public-key one gets a second in the positive direction.** The recorded output is the perfect adversarial fixture because it carries all five at once: certificate SHA-1, certificate MD5, public key SHA-256, public key SHA-1, public key MD5. Each is refused alone; the whole block minus its certificate line is refused with all five still present; and the public-key SHA-256 — 64 hex characters, indistinguishable by shape from the answer, belonging to a different key — is additionally asserted to produce **exit 3, not 0**, when a baseline is set to it. `RSN-DL-002` (d) predicted this line would be "green on an incorrectly signed one"; this packet **measured** it. A comparator mutated to accept `public key` returns `THEYGROW_RELEASE_CERT_OK` and exit **0** against a public-key digest. One refinement the measurement adds: when both lines are present the mutant reads **two** digests and exits 6, so the silent green needs the certificate line to be absent or a baseline recorded from the wrong line — narrower than "always", and still a green verdict on a key that signed nothing.
- **d. The class is bounded to one line — `[^:\n]`, not `[^:]`.** Character classes match newlines, and under `re.MULTILINE` the anchors are per-line while the class is not, so `[^:]` would join a `Signer` line to a `certificate SHA-256 digest:` line further down whenever no colon fell between them — reading a digest that is not on the signer line at all. Real output always intervenes a colon, so this was **latent rather than live**; latent is exactly what surfaces on the next tool version, which is the lesson this whole packet is. Caught in plan review, pinned by its own test, and the separators are horizontal-only `[ \t]` for the same reason. *(Owner correction during plan approval, applied as given.)*
- **e. One recorded fixture, and only one.** `app/tests/release/harness.py` builds its comparands programmatically and said so; the defect was invisible to all of it **because** every shape in it was a shape this repository already believed in. So exactly one file of real tool bytes is kept, with a `#` provenance header naming run, job, step, tool path, build-tools version, runner image and date — the `cert-sha256.txt` convention, header inside the file because provenance in a second file is provenance that can be read without.
- **f. The fixture is a record of SHAPE and never of a value, and its DN is reconstructed rather than observed.** The digests belong to the **debug** key, which is minted per run; nothing may ever compare a release APK or the committed baseline against anything in that file. The DN's value is redacted before it reaches a log (`RSN-DL-004` (f)), so the run recorded only `<redacted: 33 chars>`; the file carries the canonical Android debug DN, which is exactly 33 characters and brings the transcription to exactly the **1026 bytes and 18 lines** the run reported. That is corroboration, stated as corroboration: no log states the value. The byte and line counts are asserted by the suite, so a transcription that drifted reds rather than quietly becoming a fixture of something no tool printed.
- **g. Multi-scheme is the COLLAPSE case, and it is now stated and tested.** An APK signed under several schemes prints one signer block per scheme carrying the **same** certificate. `evaluate` builds a **set** of digests, so those collapse to one identity and the verdict is the ordinary one; exit 6 is reserved for **genuinely different** certificates, which is what key rotation or an undecided re-sign produces. Both directions are tested. Honestly bounded: the recorded output is **v2-only** (`Verified using v3 scheme: false`), so the multi-scheme tests run on synthesised input and prove the **comparator's** behaviour on that shape — not that apksigner prints it.
- **h. "Highest build-tools wins" is KEPT, re-examined against the evidence rather than reaffirmed by habit.** The parse shape demonstrably depends on the tool version, which is an argument for pinning, and a pin the image later drops now fails with a diagnosable exit 7 rather than a mysterious one, which is an argument against fearing it. It is kept anyway, on an asymmetry: the defect measured here was a parser too narrow, not a tool that floated, and pinning 37.0.0 would freeze the blind spot instead of removing it. A pin correct for one runner image can be absent on the other — and there exit 7 lands on an owner who has already cut a tag. A floating tool with a shape-tolerant parser degrades to a red that one run explains; a pin degrades to a blocked release.
- **i. The price of (h) is paid in the open: every verdict of the `--apk` path now names the tool that produced it.** One line — `apksigner: <path> (found via build-tools/<version>)` — on stdout, carrying no `THEYGROW_RELEASE_*` token and parsed by nothing. The full resolution block stays confined to the three blind verdicts (4, 7, 8), which is asserted rather than assumed. The reason is exactly this packet's history: the shape changed under a version bump nobody watched, and a **green** run that does not record which tool it passed against cannot be diffed against the next green run, so the next change is discovered by the red that follows it. *(Raised as an escalation because it extends the handoff's declared scope; resolved by the owner in favour of adding it.)*
- **j. Three statements this packet's own edits falsified are corrected in the files it already had open**, and no others: the script's `CERT_UNPARSEABLE` message and its READING line, both of which quoted the narrow shape as though it were the only one (they now name the accepted family from a single shared constant, so ledger and message cannot drift); `harness.py`'s "rather than storing recorded files"; and `test_apksigner_invocation.py`'s description of the stub as a `#!/bin/sh` shell script, which `fake_apksigner` stopped being when RSN-P3 made it Python.

### Rationale

The detector's whole worth is that its verdict is machine-checked, and for two packets it has been returning a verdict that said "I cannot read this" about output that was sitting in front of it. RSN-P3 refused to guess and bought the measurement; this packet spends it. The widening is deliberately asymmetric — generous about the **prefix**, which is what varies by tool version and signing scheme, and immovable about `certificate SHA-256`, which is what makes the comparison mean anything. That asymmetry is the entire content of ADR-047 detector (a): a comparator matching a public-key digest would satisfy its letter and defeat its purpose.

The recorded fixture exists because this milestone has now produced, on its fourth appearance in a different guise, the repository's own recurring defect class: **an assertion that passes or fails for a reason other than the one it names**. The suite was green while the detector was broken, because the suite only ever asked the comparator about shapes the repository had imagined. The general answer is not a better imagination; it is the diagnostic block, which converted an unreadable red into a named cause in one run and is what a future shape change should be diagnosed by. `RSN-DL-004` built it; this entry records that it worked, on the first occasion it was asked to.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Pin build-tools to 37.0.0 and stop parsing anything else.** Rejected — see (h). It repairs the environment instead of the parser, and moves the failure to a moment when the owner has already cut a tag.
2. **Match `SHA-256 digest:` and drop the `certificate` literal.** Rejected, and now rejected with a measurement rather than an argument: the mutant returns exit **0** and `THEYGROW_RELEASE_CERT_OK` on a public-key digest (see (c)).
3. **Replace the old shapes with the observed one.** Rejected — see (b).
4. **Synthesise the new shape in `harness.py` and skip the recorded fixture.** Rejected — see (e). It is the shape nobody imagined; a builder is the wrong instrument for it, because the builder is the thing that was wrong.
5. **Record the fixture from a locally built APK instead of from the run log.** Rejected — the development machine has no Android SDK (`docs/RUNBOOK.md`), and bytes from a different tool on a different image would pin a shape that never failed here.
6. **Assert the fixture's digest against the committed baseline.** Rejected as a category error, and warned against inside the fixture itself: the recorded digest is an ephemeral debug key's.
7. **`[^:]` for the signer-line class.** Rejected — see (d). It crosses newlines.
8. **Leave the detector's output untouched, since the pattern repair does not need it.** Rejected at owner direction — see (i).
9. **Correct only the count in `docs/execution-map.md`'s "Done, in three packets" and leave the missing packet lines.** Rejected — arithmetically true and substantively misleading; the count cannot be made honest without the bullets it counts.
10. **Sweep the other stale sentences found while in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`.** Rejected — the standing rule (`RSN-DL-003` (e)): only statements this packet falsified, plus known-false text in files already open. What was found and left is named in the execution report rather than fixed.

### Supersedes

None. **Repairs** what `RSN-DL-002` (d) built and **spends** what `RSN-DL-004` measured; both entries are left byte-untouched, per this log's amendment convention. It **narrows one claim** made in `RSN-DL-002` (d) and repeated in `docs/execution-map.md`: a pattern matching "SHA-256 digest" alone goes **green on an incorrectly signed APK only when the certificate line is absent or the baseline was recorded from the wrong line** — with both lines present it reads two digests and exits 6. The direction of the claim stands; its "in both directions" is more precise now that it has been executed rather than reasoned about.

### Effects

- **Changed (comparator):** `scripts/verify_release_signature.py` — `_CERT_DIGEST` widened and bounded to one line; the comment above it rewritten as a **shape ledger** naming the four accepted shapes and the five refused near-misses; `ACCEPTED_SHAPE` added so the ledger, the unparseable verdict and the READING line share one string; the `CERT_UNPARSEABLE` and READING messages rewritten; `$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT` added to the apksigner-absent message, which named only `$ANDROID_HOME` though the resolver has always read both; one resolution line on the `--apk` path; module docstring extended with the repair.
- **Added (evidence):** `app/tests/release/fixtures/apksigner-buildtools-37.0.0.txt` — 18 recorded lines behind a `#` provenance header. `app/tests/release/test_recorded_apksigner_output.py` — 13 tests. `harness.py` — `recorded_output`, `scheme_qualified_output`.
- **Changed (suites):** `test_verify_release_signature.py` — 4 added tests (scheme-qualified; scheme-qualified + SDK range; multi-scheme collapse; multi-scheme conflict). `test_apksigner_invocation.py` — 2 added tests and the resolution-line assertion on the existing exit-3 test; two docstring corrections. **59 tests pass**, from 40.
- **Changed (spine):** `docs/INVARIANTS.md` — `RSN-P2-INV-001` (the **Enforced by** touch-up `RSN-DL-004` deferred here, plus Scope) and `RSN-P1-INV-001` (its two executed legs move from implemented to **observed**). `docs/RUNBOOK.md` — the exit-4 row, the exit-7 row, and the proven-on-every-push placement. `docs/execution-map.md` — the track header's packet count, the P2 line's proven-able-to-go-red claim, and the missing **P3** and **P4** bullets. `docs/decision-log.md` — this entry.
- **Soundness by mutation, measured, three ways, each reverted and the tree verified green again (59 passed):** restoring the pre-RSN-P4 pattern reds **7** tests, all and only the ones about the new shapes and the recorded bytes; letting the pattern accept `public key` alongside `certificate` reds **27**, including every near-miss test by name and the recorded-output verdict; widening the class back to `[^:]` reds **exactly one** — the cross-line stitch test written for it, which is the whole reason that test exists.
- **§4-safe.** No family datum, no secret value, no live-infra identifier enters any file. The fixture is a **public** certificate block for a throwaway debug key, with the one line that could carry a person's name reconstructed as the canonical Android debug DN and labelled as not observed. **Net egress change: zero.**
- **No new knobs and no new signals** (ADR-013 / contract §4.7). No exit code, no `THEYGROW_RELEASE_*` token and no CLI flag is added, removed or renumbered — that set is the contract two workflows branch on. The line added by (i) carries no token and is parsed by nothing.
- **No new Python runtime import** (`argparse`, `os`, `re`, `shutil`, `subprocess`, `sys`, `pathlib`, `typing` — all already in use), so the mypy hook's `additional_dependencies` are unchanged.
- **No new invariant** (`AGENTS.md` §10). The property "the comparison reads the certificate digest, never the public-key digest beside it" is already inside `RSN-P2-INV-001`'s Statement; this packet strengthens its evidence rather than enforcing something new.
- **What this run also produced, and no run had before:** the fail-closed step **executed for the first time** and both its legs passed (`ok: THEYGROW_RELEASE_SIGNING_MISSING`, `ok: THEYGROW_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_UNREADABLE`), moving `RSN-P1-INV-001`'s central claim from implemented to **observed**; and `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` did exactly what `RSN-DL-004` (g) chose it for — the comparator was red and the fail-closed detector still reported its own verdict in the same run. Both were read out of the run log directly, not taken on report.
- **The claim this packet still cannot make.** "The comparator returns exactly 3 against a foreign certificate, on a real APK, with the real tool." It is executed by the `android` job and by nothing here: the fixture suite proves the pattern reads the **recorded** shape, not that the tool still prints it. **Unproven until a run shows it green.**
- **Amended 2026-08-16 by `XPT-DL-002`** *(pointer only; every word of this entry stands as written)*. The claim above was discharged the same day this entry was written, by the `android` job of CI run **31898815923** — the step passed, and passing is exit 3 by its own guard — and it has since held on `main`. What that run did **not** settle, and what remains open, is enumerated there; note in particular that 31898815923 is the address of a job verdict and **not** a green run.

## XPT-DL-001 — XPT-P1 `export-payload-transfer-fix`: the archive stops riding the call that opens the file picker, because that call is persisted into saved instance state and the parcel killed the process

- **Date.** 2026-08-16
- **Type.** Packet — XPT-P1, first packet of **XPT "fix-export-empty-archive"**. *(Namespace note: opens the `XPT-DL` namespace; packets are `XPT-P{k}`. The "Entry format" header is intentionally left unedited, per the `LSC-DL-003` / `EMV-DL-001` / `RSN-DL-001` precedent.)*
- **Scope.** The transfer mechanism between the export writer and the native sink, the mount bump its delivery requires, one signal, two knobs, and the tests that execute the repair. No schema change, no artifact-format change, no new permission, no new dependency in a shipped surface, no new egress.

### Decision

- **a. The defect is a measurement, and the repair follows it rather than a theory.** The owner captured the crash on the family device on 2026-08-15 (`adb logcat -b crash`): `TransactionTooLargeException: data parcel size 4630924 bytes`, with `capacitorLastPluginCallOptions [size=2313920]` and `capacitorLastPluginCallBundle [size=2313952]` in the bundle stats, thrown at `activityStopped`. Read against the vendored Capacitor source, every number in that trace is accounted for: `Plugin.startActivityForResult` records the launching call as `bridge.pluginCallForLastActivity`, and `Bridge.saveInstanceState` writes its options JSON out **twice** — once directly, once inside the plugin's own `saveInstanceState()` bundle. 2 × 2 313 920 ≈ the parcel. The archive that did this was **1.73 MB**, well under the sizes this repair is tested at, and the process died *after* the system had created the empty document and *before* a byte was written — which is why the file was stably 0 bytes with the right name and the app said nothing.
- **b. Stage first, pick last.** `saveArtifact()` now opens a transfer (`beginTransfer`), sends the archive in chunks (`appendChunk`), and only then calls `createDocument`, whose options are `{transferId, filename, mimeType, totalBytes}` — a few hundred bytes. The plugin accumulates the chunks in a buffer in the app's own process and writes them to the chosen document on the picker's result, exactly as before.
- **c. The launching call is guarded fail-closed, so the defect cannot return quietly.** `createDocument` rejects any option key outside the declared four, and rejects options above `LAUNCH_OPTIONS_MAX_BYTES` (4096, mirroring `EXPORT_CONFIG.sinkLaunchOptionsMaxBytes`). Both refusals happen before the intent is built. The guard exists because the app-side edit that reintroduces a payload is a one-line edit that looks harmless in the file where it happens.
- **d. The picker does not open unless the whole archive is in hand.** `createDocument` also refuses if the staged byte count is not exactly the `totalBytes` the app declared. The system creates the document the moment the parent presses Save, so any failure after that point is visible to them as a broken file; refusing earlier turns it into "nothing happened", which is the honest outcome and the one that cannot leave a wrong file behind.
- **e. No temporary file, and the buffer does not outlive the export.** Staging to app-private cache was considered and rejected: it would put an unencrypted copy of the family's history on disk in a location nobody chose (`ADR-046`, `AGENTS.md` §4). The buffer is allocated once at the declared size — a doubling buffer would hold two multi-megabyte copies at every growth step — and dropped on success, on cancel, and on `handleOnDestroy`. `writeDocument` streams it out with `writeTo` rather than materialising a second copy with `toByteArray`, so peak memory on the native side is one archive, not two.
- **f. Delivered by copy-forward bump, `/m/v2/` → `/m/v3/`, `CACHE_VERSION` v12 → v13.** The repair only runs on the native channel, where the mount is read out of the APK and no HTTP cache is involved, so the bump buys this fix nothing functionally. It is done because the rule is that bytes at a published mount URL are never rewritten (`A1-DL-004`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md` "Module mount"), and "this particular changed byte happens to be unreachable on the web" is the reasoning that erodes such a rule rather than an exception to it. `/m/v1/` and `/m/v2/` stay on disk byte-untouched; three generations now ship, and retiring `v1` stays the separate owner cleanup the RUNBOOK says it is.
- **g. The allowlist grows from one method to three, and the boundary is restated rather than weakened.** What `ALLOWED_SINK_METHODS` protects is that the plugin cannot read, list, delete, or write to a path of its own choosing. Two of the three methods touch no filesystem at all; the third is the one that writes, to the same single document. `app/tests/export-contour.spec.js` asserts the exact set, so the list still cannot grow without a deliberate test edit.
- **h. Two knobs, one mirrored across the bridge.** `sinkChunkBytes` (262144) keeps every call an order of magnitude under the binder limit whatever a future Capacitor version chooses to persist. `sinkLaunchOptionsMaxBytes` (4096) is the app's copy of a bound the plugin has to hold; the two languages share no config surface, so the number is written twice and asserted equal, the arrangement `STORE_CONFIG.sqliteVersionFloor` already has with `app/tests/schema/harness.py`. `MAX_STAGED_BYTES` (64 MiB) stays Java-only: it bounds the process's own heap and the app could not act on it if it knew it.
- **i. One new signal, `export.run`.** Counts and timings only — `outcome`, `archive_bytes`, `chunks`, `export_ms` — emitted from the surface, sink the device console, no network leg. It exists because the defect it follows was **invisible from the device**: the process died with the picker in front, so the app printed nothing and the only evidence was the file. The owner-run device smoke is the one leg no test automates, and this line is what that leg now reads.
- **j. The parcel assertion carries a control, in the same run.** "The saved state is small" would stay green if the measuring instrument were broken. So `ExportTransferTest` measures the real saved state at the instant of launch **and** measures a synthetic bundle in the old shape, carrying a payload the size of the one from the crash, through the same function — and requires the control to exceed the bound the real one must stay under. Both numbers are logged.
- **k. Two pinned mount literals in the test tree are repaired here, because this bump is what makes them wrong.** `app/tests/export/build-artifact.mjs` built the artifact with `m/v1/export/build.js` and `app/tests/schema/test_write_path_projection.py` read `m/v1/store/journal.js`, both while `harness.py` beside them derived the mount from the shell. They were green because the generations differed only in values those suites do not read; after this bump they would have been two generations behind. `docs/RUNBOOK.md` step 2.7 said no test edit is needed at bump time, which these two made false; the sentence is corrected with them.

### Rationale

The repository's recurring defect class is an assertion that passes for a reason other than the one it names, and this packet is a clean instance of the same class one level down: every existing test of the sink used a fixture of a few hundred bytes, so the size of the fixture *was* the defect's hiding place. The repair is therefore stated in two halves that fail independently — a **structural** one (the payload cannot be on that call, enforced by the plugin and executed by a test that builds its own violating input) and a **behavioural** one (an archive several times past the binder limit is written whole, executed end to end in the app on a device). Neither is a scan of source text.

The mount bump is the expensive part of the packet and buys the fix nothing; it is done anyway because the alternative is to make an exception to an invariant on the grounds that this particular violation is harmless, which is how invariants stop being enforced.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Open the picker first, then stream chunks straight into the SAF `OutputStream`.** Rejected — it holds a content-resolver stream open across bridge round trips, and a failure mid-stream leaves a partially written document that the parent has already been shown a Save dialog for. That is the same user-visible shape as the defect.
2. **Stage the archive to an app-private cache file.** Rejected — see (e).
3. **Keep one method and fold the chunk append and the finish into it behind a `last: true` flag.** Rejected — a smaller surface bought with a mode flag, for no boundary gain.
4. **Override `Plugin.saveInstanceState()` to return an empty bundle.** Rejected — it treats the symptom in one Capacitor version's internals (and `Bridge` writes the options string itself regardless), leaving the payload on the call for every other path that touches it.
5. **Edit `/m/v2/` in place, since the sink is inert on the web channel.** Rejected — see (f).
6. **Drive the real system file picker with UiAutomator so the SAF round trip is executed literally.** Rejected — the standing decision since L1-P3 is that driving another app's UI is an assertion this repository does not make. The saved-state measurement plus its control covers the property the picker trip is about; the real picker stays the owner's device smoke.
7. **Defer the signal.** Rejected — see (i).
8. **Defer the two pinned mount literals as side-finds.** Rejected — see (k).
9. **Delete the document when a write fails.** Rejected — it would add a delete capability to a plugin whose whole argument is that it has none.

### Supersedes

None. **Repairs** the transfer built in `LSC-DL-003` (the export contour and its first-party sink); that entry is left byte-untouched, per this log's amendment convention. It **narrows one claim** implicit in it — "the bytes are streamed straight out; nothing is written to a temporary file on the way" was true and remains true, but it described a path that could not survive an archive of realistic size, which no test then in the tree would have shown.

### Effects

- **Added (mount):** `app/m/v3/**` — copy-forward of `app/m/v2/**` (47 files), with the change made in the new directory only.
- **Changed (in `app/m/v3/` only):** `export/sink.js` (staged transfer; module header records the measurement); `export/config.js` (three self-referencing URLs repointed, two knobs added, allowlist grown to three); `store/config.js` (`schemaUrl` repointed); `store/schema/001-core.sql` (one comment naming its own generation); `core/signals.js` (`export.run`); `surfaces/export.js` (emits it); `export/run.js` (`chunks` in the summary).
- **Changed (delivery):** `app/index.html` (44 mount references), `app/sw.js` (46 references plus `CACHE_VERSION` v12 → v13).
- **Changed (native):** `ExportSinkPlugin.java` — three plugin methods, the staged buffer, the fail-closed launch guard, `writeDocument(…, ByteArrayOutputStream)`; `MountAddress.java` — two javadoc examples repointed (`EMV-P5-INV-001` caught both); `build.gradle` — one `androidTestImplementation` line for espresso-intents.
- **Added (evidence):** `ExportTransferTest.java` — the end-to-end run past the binder limit, the saved-state measurement with its control, and the guard fired against an input the test builds itself. `app/tests/export-sink-unit.spec.js` — 7 off-device tests of the shipped `sink.js` against a fake Capacitor, registered in the `contract` project.
- **Changed (suites):** `ExportSinkTest.java` (the byte-path and truncation tests move to the staged-buffer seam); `app/tests/export-contour.spec.js` (the allowlist set, and a new test that the ceiling and the option-key set agree on both sides of the bridge); `app/tests/export/build-artifact.mjs` and `app/tests/schema/test_write_path_projection.py` (mount derivation, see (k)); `app/tests/support/prev-generation.js` and `app/tests/upgrade-path.spec.js` (prose the bump falsified); `app/playwright.config.js`.
- **Changed (spine):** `docs/INVARIANTS.md` — `XPT-P1-INV-001`, `XPT-P1-INV-002`. `docs/RUNBOOK.md` — the export smoke, and the "Module mount" step-2.7 correction. `docs/decision-log.md` — this entry.
- **Soundness by mutation, measured, each reverted and the tree verified green again:** putting `base64` back on the `createDocument` options reds exactly one test — `export-sink-unit.spec.js`'s "it carries exactly four small values"; changing the Java ceiling to 8192 reds exactly the new cross-bridge agreement test; hiding `app/m/v3/export/build.js` reds `pytest app/tests/export` with 4 failures and 33 errors, which is what proves the repaired driver now builds with the mount the shell runs rather than with `v1`.
- **§4-safe.** The new signal carries counts and timings and no free string is representable in it. No filename and no document URI is emitted anywhere. **Net egress change: zero.**
- **No schema change, no artifact-format change.** `formatVersion` stays 1, the zip layout, entry names, fixed DOS timestamps and STORED method are untouched, and the DDL differs from `v2`'s only in a comment that names its own generation.
- **What this packet cannot prove here.** Everything Android. The instrumented tests, the espresso-intents interception and the archive that comes out the other end are executed by `android-instrumented` and by nothing on the development machine, which has no SDK and no Gradle. And the **real system file picker** is executed by the owner's device smoke and by nothing at all in CI — that was true before this packet and is unchanged by it.

## XPT-DL-002 — XPT-P2 `docs-green-run-references`: the repository stops understating what the comparator's first passing run discharged, and stops short of overstating it

- **Date.** 2026-08-16
- **Type.** Packet — XPT-P2, second and closing packet of **XPT "fix-export-empty-archive"**. **Docs-only.** No source file, no test, no workflow, no config, nothing under `app/m/**`.
- **Scope.** `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (`RSN-P1-INV-001`, `RSN-P2-INV-001`, `XPT-P1-INV-001`, `XPT-P1-INV-002` — evidence status only), `docs/decision-log.md` (a pointer bullet on `RSN-DL-005`, and this entry), `docs/execution-map.md` (this packet's own bullet), `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (one sentence — see (g)). No new invariant and none removed; no schema, no artifact format, no exit code, no `THEYGROW_RELEASE_*` token, no CLI flag, no knob, no signal, no new egress. **Landed this packet.**

### The evidence this packet starts from

`RSN-DL-005` closed on a claim it could not make — *"the comparator returns exactly 3 against a foreign certificate, on a real APK, with the real tool"* — and marked it **unproven until a run shows it green**. That run had in fact already happened, hours later on the same day: the `android` job of CI run **31898815923** (`pull_request`, branch `feat/release-signing`, commit 637660b, 2026-08-15T17:37:05Z), where the step *The signature comparator rejects a foreign certificate* **passed**. Three places in the repository went on saying otherwise, and a fourth said something that had become outright false. This packet is the correction, and its whole difficulty is that the correction of an understatement is the easiest place in the world to plant an overstatement.

What the run's own output carries, quoted rather than remembered:

```
THEYGROW_RELEASE_CERT_MISMATCH: the APK is NOT signed by the expected key.
  apksigner reported: <64 hex>
  baseline expects:   <64 hex>
apksigner: /usr/local/lib/android/sdk/build-tools/37.0.0/apksigner (found via build-tools/37.0.0)
```

### Decision

- **a. Exit 3 is recorded as an INFERENCE from the step's guard, not as a number anybody read.** The log prints no status code. The step's wrapper is `if [ "${status}" -ne 3 ]; then … exit 1`, so a green step **is** exit 3 — sound, and stated with its provenance attached, because "the log says 3" would be false and this packet is about the exactness of evidence claims. What the log *does* show is the mismatch verdict with **both sides printed and labelled**, and the tool that produced it: `apksigner` out of **build-tools 37.0.0**, named by the resolution line `RSN-DL-005` (i) added for exactly this purpose — the first green whose tool is on the record, which was the argument for adding it.
- **b. Run 31898815923 is the address of a JOB verdict, never of a green run, and every sentence written here is checked against that.** The run's own conclusion is `failure`: its `quality` job failed at *Ruff format (check)* — the defect 7d2ff2c repaired — and every step behind it was **skipped**, including `pytest (release signature comparator)`. So this run discharges the real-tool leg and says **nothing** about the per-push suite in the same run. The handoff, and `docs/execution-map.md`'s own forward-looking P2 line, both called it "green run 31898815923"; that phrasing is the same class of error this packet exists to end, pointed the other way, and it is not reproduced anywhere in the repository.
- **c. "First" has two addresses, and both are named.** Commit 637660b produced two runs three seconds apart — `pull_request` **31898815923** and `push` **31898813639** — and the `android` job was green in both. Naming only the one the handoff carried would make the record look more single-threaded than it is.
- **d. The claim is anchored additionally on the runs where it held with everything else green — including on `main`.** Runs **31899849136** (push, 7d2ff2c), **31899851227** (`pull_request`, 7d2ff2c, `android-instrumented` green in the same run) and **31900363700** (push on `main`, commit fa744a2, the merge of PR #23) all completed green end to end, with the comparator step printing the same shape from the same build-tools version **and** `pytest app/tests/release` passing in the same run. This extends the handoff's scope, which named one run; it is done because anchoring a "now proven" amendment solely to a run whose own conclusion is `failure` would itself be an understatement, and because the property holding on the **default branch** is a materially stronger and separately checkable fact.
- **e. No fingerprint value enters any amended text, and the record proves why the rule is right.** The APK under test is **debug**-signed by a key the runner mints per run: the `apksigner reported` digest on 31898815923 and on 31900363700 are two **different** 64-hex values. A recorded tool output is a record of **form**, never of value (kit rule 2026-08-15) — so no digest is transcribed, in either apksigner's lowercase form or the committed colon-separated one, and a diff-level check enforces it. The `baseline expects` value is the committed public baseline and is likewise not copied: it already lives at `native/android/release-signing/cert-sha256.txt` and a second copy is a second thing to drift.
- **f. The still-open half is written into the SAME amendment as the discharge, not into a separate place a reader can miss.** Named there: (1) `.github/workflows/release.yml` has **never executed on any trigger** — the workflow is registered and active and its run list is empty; (2) the comparator's **positive** verdict against a real release-signed APK has never been observed, every executed leg to date being a negative one by construction, because the positive path needs the real key; (3) three guard legs of `RSN-P1-INV-001` remain unexecuted — the "path does not name a readable file" branch of `THEYGROW_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_UNREADABLE`, `THEYGROW_RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS_ABSENT`, and `THEYGROW_RELEASE_VERSIONCODE_UNRESOLVED`, the last being the leg the release workflow's `fetch-depth: 0` contract rests on. (3) is not asserted from memory: the fail-closed step prints exactly **two** `ok:` lines on 31898815923 and again on 31900363700, and no others. This packet does not repair any of them; `RSN-DL-003` already works out what would.
- **g. A fourth place was not merely understating — it was false, in the highest-consequence place the claim appears, and it is corrected in place.** `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s release procedure, in the *"What is proven, and what the first run executes for the first time"* table, read *"**The first half is proven; the second is not yet.** That step has returned **4**, not 3, on every run since it landed."* Both halves stopped being true at 31898815923 and have been untrue on `main` since fa744a2. That table is what the owner reads immediately **before** the first release run, so leaving it while amending three other places to say the opposite would have made the docs contradict each other precisely at the moment of use. **Scope extension, recorded as one** — the file was outside the approved allowlist; the fork touches no escalation-list item (PDR-027) and was resolved in favour of correcting it. Bounded to **that sentence**: the table row, the section, and every procedure step are untouched, and the section's *"No run of the `Release` workflow has ever happened, on any trigger"* is **verified true** and stands verbatim.
- **h. This milestone's own two invariants get the discipline PROSPECTIVELY, so the milestone does not open the debt it is closing.** `XPT-P1-INV-001` and `XPT-P1-INV-002` named `android-instrumented` as their enforcer but said nothing about whether it had run. It has not: **no run of any workflow exists on branch `fix/export-empty-archive`** and no pull request is open for it, so nothing has executed against the branch tip. Both entries now carry a **Not yet observed.** field saying so — and, unlike the RSN entries whose debt sat unaddressed for two packets, each names **what discharges it and when**: a green `android-instrumented` job on this milestone's pull request against the branch tip, at which point the field is replaced by an **Observed.** one naming that run, as a scheduled pre-merge step of this milestone. Neither predicts the outcome, and making that replacement is **not** this packet's work.
- **i. `RSN-DL-005` is amended by a POINTER, and every word of it stands.** This log's convention is amendment by reference with the record left byte-untouched (`A3-DL-003` (b), `A3-DL-004`, `LSC-DL-005` alt. 1, which also fixes the boundary: *"in-place correction stays reserved for spine files"*). A strictly silent amendment would nonetheless leave a reader of that entry alone with the understatement, so it gains one appended pointer bullet — additive, dated, naming this entry, replacing nothing. In-place correction is applied where that same rule says it belongs: `docs/INVARIANTS.md` and `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, the live contract and procedure files.
- **j. `RSN-P1-INV-001` is amended too, though it never carried the "unproven until green run" qualifier.** The handoff's paraphrase attributed that phrase to both RSN entries; only `RSN-P2-INV-001` carries it. What `RSN-P1-INV-001` carries is an **Observed.** block whose window — the step skipped behind a red comparator, "from RSN-P2 until RSN-P4, every run" — is what 31898815923 closes: the step ran there with the comparator **ahead of it green**, so it would have run under the old `if: success()` as well.
