The mark path stops collapsing every failure into one code — bounded to that.** Owner correction at plan review, and it is the same ADR-046 §1.1 subject on the path the family uses most: after this milestone a tick is a native write, so a full disk lost a mark silently and advised a restart. `.catch(() => false)` became `.catch(storeFailureCode)`, the signal carries `failure_class`, and the dialog reveals one of two paragraphs. Nothing else on that surface moved, and it carries an executing leg rather than a string assertion.
- **j. `storeFailureCode` was extracted rather than copied.** The class→code map already existed privately in `core/state.js` for the OPEN path; two write paths need it now. It is unary and accepts an error or a class name, so it stands directly in a `.catch()` — which is what made (i) three lines. `store/` gains no import edge into `core/`: the closed list stays in `store/errors.js` and is asserted equal to `SIGNAL_CODES.failure_class` by a test, the way `transfer-seam.spec.js` holds the mirrored refusal list.
- **k. `required` came off the diary's fields, and this is a decision about whose voice a refusal speaks in.** With `required`, the browser intercepts the submit and shows ITS bubble — its wording, its language, nowhere near `#diaryStatus` — and the shipped refusal never runs. On the surface where a parent has just written about their child, the refusal must be the product's sentence. The fields carry `aria-required="true"`, which keeps the semantics for assistive technology and triggers no native validation, and `surfaces/diary.js` owns every refusal. Found by a new test going red, not by review.
- **l. ADR-046 §1.3, answered for the object that will actually be filed.** The journal spine keeps its cursor. For the DIARY the answer is `(entry_at_utc, id)` — the same total order every projection in the frozen schema already uses — with the position living in `schema_meta`, which is a mutable key/value table. **`record.rowid` is NOT the answer**, and the test demonstrates why rather than asserting it: delete the highest row and the next insert takes its number back, so a cursor holding it would skip the new entry. No column, no table, no migration: the item closes as verification, with two tests and no code.
- **m. Mount `/m/v5/` → `/m/v6/`, `CACHE_VERSION` v15 → v16.** Forced, not chosen: this packet changes `app.js`, `app.css`, three surfaces and four store modules, and bytes at a published mount URL are never rewritten. **The cost is stated rather than absorbed** — a SIXTH generation ships, `app/m/` is now ~4.7 MB, all of it served `immutable, max-age=2592000`, and retiring `/m/v1/`–`/m/v4/` remains deferred with nothing scheduled against it.
- **n. The release-address guard learned that a frozen generation is not a second declaration.** `export-contour.spec.js` asserted the APK address appears exactly once in the shipped tree, excluding only the RUNNING mount's `channel/config.js`. The first copy-forward since `DIA-P2` introduced that knob produced a second copy of the same declaration and the guard went red on a defect that did not exist. It now excludes `m/v{N}/channel/config.js` for any generation; the defect it is really about — the address in markup or in a module beside the knob — is still caught across every other shipped file, frozen generations included.
- **o. The area race is written down rather than assumed away.** Two saves racing both miss the lookup, both mint an id, and the result is two private areas for one child. The cost is one untidy row and **no lost entry**, because the read is scoped by owner, child and class and never by a single area id; re-running the same statements is a genuine no-op by `ON CONFLICT`. Both outcomes are executed against the real DDL. A deterministic id would have removed the race and was rejected: it would have to hash under `derivedIdNamespace`, whose value is documented as the legacy import's and whose version bump would then silently mean something for the diary too.

### THE ARTEFACT GAP — stated here because from this packet a parent's diary text exists in exactly one place

**From DIA-P3 onward, the family's diary lives on the device and nowhere else, and the export archive does not carry it.** `export/readout.js` reads the journal and `schema_meta`; `export/declaration.json` (`format: theygrow-archive`, `format_version: 1`, `schema_contract: lsc-journal-v1`) describes journal datasets. The `record` table is in neither. So the one artefact this product offers a family for the next twenty years — unencrypted, needing no key, no account and no subscription (ADR-043) — preserves their marks and their journal history and **not a word of what they wrote**.

This packet does not design the fix and does not extend the format. The archive is a **published contract** and this is an owner decision. What a decision would need to weigh: whether a `participant_private` record belongs in a human-facing projection at all (PDR-020 §1/§2 — the artefact is for humans and must not become the rollback mechanism; PDR-025 §3 — subject and visibility class on derived state; and the leak argument in PDR-026's 2026-08-11 annotation, which is the reason the record is private in the first place); if it does, whether the quote-basis stays out of it while the record text goes in; and what `format_version` a change like that costs.

**One consequence is already live and should not wait for the decision:** the diary's corrupt-store refusal used to tell the parent to save the archive at the first opportunity. That sentence was TRUE for marks and FALSE for the thing they were looking at — at the worst possible moment the product advised the one action that does not save a diary entry. It now says what the archive does and does not preserve. A vaguer sentence was rejected: a parent reading it is deciding what to do in the next five minutes.

### Rationale

The rules this packet owes are all of the form "these two things look alike and are not". A mark and a diary entry are both something a parent writes down about a child on a day; one is an attributed assertion in an append-only journal and the other is private text edited by overwriting. Event time and entry time are both timestamps on the same row; one is often unknown and the other never is. "Never declared" and "declared not sensitive" are both absences of a warning. Each pair has a cheap wrong answer that looks tidier than the right one, and each right answer is only stable if the code says why — so the reasons are in the modules, not only here.

The disk-full work is a different kind of obligation. ADR-046 §1 argues that a journal which silently fails to record an observation breaks the single source of truth invisibly, which is worse than a crash. Until this packet the product had the machinery for that argument and none of the behaviour: the classifier existed, the type existed, the closed code existed, and every one of them terminated in a dialog that said the store had not opened. What P3 adds is not classification — that was there — but the last few metres of it: a sentence a parent can act on, a text field that still holds what they wrote, and an executing test that produces a real `SQLITE_FULL` from the real engine rather than asserting a string.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Widen `journal_entry.kind` to carry diary entries.** Rejected — a schema edit on a frozen file, which is an escalation and not a decision, and it would make the diary append-only, contradicting the rule this packet owes.
2. **`child_shared` for the diary area.** Rejected — it puts the very text PDR-026's annotation protects into the set L7 may ship.
3. **A sensitivity checkbox in the compose form.** Rejected — a projection-time question (L5) the surface cannot act on, and asking it now would collect a declaration nothing consumes.
4. **A time field beside the date, or defaulting the event instant to `now` when the day is today.** Rejected as false precision; the schema's paired CHECK exists to express "day known, moment not".
5. **Ship `deleteRecord` unused, behind a confirm dialog.** Rejected — see (e).
6. **A second banner for the saved entry, matching the archive's.** Rejected — the list the parent is looking at already says it.
7. **A deterministic diary-area id derived through `derivedId`.** Rejected — see (o).
8. **Keep `required` and let the browser refuse.** Rejected — see (k).
9. **Drive the disk-full refusal from a page test with a fake store.** Rejected — reaching it needs a store that opens, and a fake would prove the fake (the same shape `DIA-DL-004` alternative 9 rejected for the export). It is `DiaryEntryTest`'s, on a device.
10. **Fix the mark path's collapse in a later packet.** Rejected at plan review — the arming and the helper were both being built here, so doing it now cost three lines and one string, and doing it later cost a packet.
11. **Assert the disk-full sentence statically, since the device leg is unobserved until dispatch.** Rejected — a static guard cannot carry a runtime claim (`AGENTS.md` §11), and asserting the string would have created exactly the appearance of coverage that rule exists to prevent. `diary-surface.spec.js` says in its own header that it does not touch that sentence.

### Two recurring classes this milestone has now met more than once

**1. A blanket mount substitution falsifies `changed_in` provenance lines. Twice now.** A copy-forward bump repoints every `m/v{N}` in the shell — and the same substitution rewrites the HISTORY lines beside the knob, turning "v14 -> v15 with the /m/v5/ mount bump" into a false statement about a bump that never happened. It was caught by eye at DIA-P1 and again here, in `app/sw.js`, before anything ran. The cure is procedural because the lines are prose: `docs/RUNBOOK.md` step 2 now says to exclude `changed_in` lines from the substitution and to re-read them afterwards. **The general shape:** a repoint is safe for lines that describe the CURRENT address and unsafe for lines that describe a PAST one, and only a reader can tell them apart.

**2. Substring matching over code and SQL bites where token or declaration matching would not. Four times in this milestone and its neighbours**, each one found only because something else went red:
   - a guard that read a COMMENT about `sw-register.js` as a reference to it;
   - `onNewIntentDISABLED` matching a scan for `onNewIntent`;
   - `.includes('autoVerify')` matching the string inside a comment that explained it;
   - and, in this packet, `"UPDATE" not in read` reding on the shipped diary query because the column `updated_at_utc` contains those letters.
   Three of the four failed OPEN (green while wrong) and the fourth failed CLOSED (red while right), which is why the class is worth naming rather than the individual bugs: the failure mode is not the direction, it is that a substring has no idea what a token is. **What closes it, case by case:** word boundaries where the subject is a token, a declaration-shaped anchor (`const NAME = …`) where the subject is a constant, and a parser rather than a scan where the subject is structure — the lesson `signal-payload.spec.js` already carries from `LSC-P4-INV-003`.

### Supersedes

None. **Extends** `LSC-DL-002` (the frozen schema, whose `record` table this is the first user of), `LSC-DL-004` (the write path's shape, which the diary's own path deliberately does not imitate), `DIA-DL-001` (the derived mount, which made this bump need no repointing inside the generation) and `DIA-DL-004` (the channel composition this reuses, and the confirmation lesson it recorded).

**Amends in place:** `app/tests/export-contour.spec.js`'s single-declaration predicate — see (n). **Corrects, in files this packet already edits:** the diary's corrupt-store refusal, which advised an archive that does not carry diary text (see the artefact gap); `app/index.html`'s module-hint comment, which had said "twenty-one" through four packets while the list grew to forty-six; and `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s line 9, which explained the inline analytics shim as required by the Telegram link's `onclick` — that link went with DIA-P2, and the shim's remaining callers are the install-prompt IIFE.

### Effects

- **Added:** `app/m/v6/**` (copy-forward of `v5`), of which two files are new — `store/records.js` and `surfaces/diary.js`; `app/tests/diary-write.spec.js`; `app/tests/diary-surface.spec.js`; `app/tests/schema/test_diary_write_path.py`; `native/.../androidTest/.../DiaryEntryTest.java`.
- **Changed:** `app/index.html` (mount repoint, the diary control, `#diaryModal`, the disk-full paragraph, two hints, the hint-count sentence), `app/sw.js` (`CACHE_VERSION` v16, two new entries), `app/transfer.html` (mount repoint), `app/m/v6/{app.js,app.css,core/state.js,core/signals.js,store/boot.js,store/config.js,store/errors.js,surfaces/channel.js,surfaces/skill-completion.js}`, `app/playwright.config.js`, four test files (`export-contour`, `behavior`, `schema/harness.py`, `schema/test_write_path_projection.py`), `app/tests/schema/test_store_cursor.py`, `native/.../StoreEngineTest.java`, and the docs spine.
- **Three invariants added, two of them carrying an unobserved half.** `DIA-P3-INV-003` is green on every push. `DIA-P3-INV-001` and `DIA-P3-INV-002` are green on every push in their off-device halves and land **Not yet observed** in their device halves: their only executors are `DiaryEntryTest` and the new `StoreEngineTest` leg, and `android-instrumented` runs on `pull_request` and dispatch only.
- **Three knobs, all new, all with `changed_in` provenance** (`diaryAreaTitle`, `diaryAreaVisibility`, `diaryListLimit`). **One new signal kind** (`diary.write`) and one existing kind extended (`write.refused` gains `failure_class`). **No new closed code was needed** — every value was already declared.
- **§4-safe.** `diary.write` carries `outcome`, `failure_class`, `chars` and `write_ms`; `chars` is a LENGTH and the only thing that tells a refused empty entry from a refused real one. Nothing a parent wrote can reach a payload structurally: `emitSignal` accepts numbers, booleans, null and declared codes, and there is no path that takes a free string. Family text reaches the DOM only through `textContent` — no `innerHTML` anywhere in the new surface. **Net egress change: zero.** No GA4 event, no dimension, no request added by any page.
- **Two baselines moved, and the negative control is named:** `dom-{desktop,mobile}/header.html`, +27 lines each, for the diary control and its comment. **Zero visual PNGs moved** — the DOM gains a header child, the pixels do not, because the control ships `hidden` and the web channel never reveals it. `#diaryModal`'s markup is captured by no baseline, which is how `#importModal` and `#exportModal` have always been treated.
- **What this packet cannot do, stated rather than implied.** The development host has no Android SDK and no Gradle, so `DiaryEntryTest.java` and the new `StoreEngineTest` leg have never been built, dexed or run. They ARE type-checked on the host against fetched `androidx.test` jars and faithful stubs for the three collaborators, and the JavaScript embedded in them is parsed by `node --check` after placeholder substitution — which found one genuine unbalanced brace in the arming script before any dispatch. Both are checks, not runs.
- **A falsifiable prediction.** On the next `android-instrumented` dispatch, `fillToCeiling` should report `state=full` after a handful of filler rows, and both disk-full legs should then reach their refusal and succeed again once the ceiling is released. If instead `state=budget` is reported, the database had more free space than the filler loop was budgeted to consume and the arming — not the product — is what needs raising; if the legs refuse but do NOT succeed after release, the refusal was never about a full disk and every disk-full assertion in this packet is measuring something else.
- **Amended by reference, 2026-08-17 — see `DIA-DL-006`.** Run 31971968427 falsifies one statement in this entry and one in its prediction, and the log's convention for a past entry is a pointer rather than a rewrite (`A3-DL-003` (b), `XPT-DL-002` (i), `DIA-DL-002`). (1) **"A parent writes in the app" was not true as shipped.** `surfaces/diary.js` spread `...who`, an identifier the module never declared, so every create threw a `ReferenceError` before any bridge call and every parent got the generic refusal. Everything this entry says about the write path's SHAPE stands — the statements, the transaction, the overwrite semantics, the two times, the NULL sensitivity are all as described and all proven by `pytest app/tests/schema` — but the surface never reached them. (2) **The prediction's two branches did not cover what happened.** `fillToCeiling` reported `state=full` on a genuine refusal, so branch one did not fire; the diary legs never got as far as the release, so branch two could not. The mark leg failed for a third reason the prediction did not model: the arming was full for the shape it FILLED (`record`) and not for the shape under test (the journal), and the mark landed on a store this entry's arming had just called full. Nothing else here is edited, and `DIA-P3-INV-001` / `DIA-P3-INV-002`'s **Not yet observed.** fields are untouched — the re-dispatch discharges them, not the repair.

- **Amended by reference, 2026-08-17 — the artefact gap is DECIDED, and this entry's account of it is now a description of a temporary state rather than of an open question.** The owner gate ran on 2026-08-17 and chose: **the long-lived artefact WILL carry diary text**, and the work is addressed to **L3**, where the narrative artefact already sits in the roadmap. Recorded in the vault as an annotation to PDR-020. Everything this entry says about the gap remains true of the code as shipped — `export/readout.js` reads the journal and `schema_meta`, `export/declaration.json` describes journal datasets, and `record` is in neither — but the sentence "what an owner decision would weigh" has an answer now, and the honest wording of the state is: **until L3 ships, a parent's diary text exists in exactly one copy on one device, and the archive carries marks and journal history only.** That is a state with an address, not a property of the product. Two things a later packet does not have to re-derive: the artefact's scope is the **exporting participant's own private area** and never the other parent's — `LSC-P3-INV-003` already enforces exactly that shape, and PDR-026's leak argument is about sharing **between participants**, which stays in force; and the parent-facing wording in `surfaces/diary.js` (the corrupt-store refusal) is already true of both today and L3, because it says what the archive does and does not carry rather than what it never will. Nothing else here is edited. See `DIA-DL-008`.

## DIA-DL-006 — DIA-P3R `diary-save-repair`: the diary never saved anything, and the reason nobody knew is that its success path had no executor

- **Date.** 2026-08-17
- **Type.** Packet — DIA-P3R, repair packet of **L2 "local diary"**, on branch `feat/l2-local-diary`, following the dispatch `DIA-DL-005` scheduled. One packet, one report.
- **Scope.** The three faults run 31971968427 exposed — one in the product, one in a fixture's use of the SQLite binding, one in the mark leg's arming and wait — and the coverage gap underneath all of it. **Out:** P4's scope (the FTS index, search, the closing milestone docs, the embedded-JS parse guard scheduled there); any change to the diary's product behaviour beyond making the save path work as specified — no new refusal, no new field, no schema touch; the artefact gap (the archive carries no diary text), which stays an owner decision recorded in `DIA-DL-005`.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was repaired

**(a) The product. Measured, three times over.** `app/m/v6/surfaces/diary.js` called `createRecord({ ...who, … })` where the module declares `author()` and nothing declares `who`. Logcat carries the same line once per save the run attempted — 21:00:29.623, 21:00:34.965, 21:00:38.566 — `File: https://localhost/m/v6/surfaces/diary.js - Line 278 - Msg: [diary] the entry was not recorded: ReferenceError who is not defined`. The throw happens BEFORE any bridge call, so `write_ms` was 0 and no `CapacitorSQLite` call appears in the leg's window; the catch classified it `other` and the parent read the generic refusal. Four `DiaryEntryTest` legs red on it.

**(b) The fixture. Measured.** `StoreEngineTest:270` set the page ceiling with `execSQL`, which routes to `executeForChangedRowCount`; `PRAGMA max_page_count = N` returns a row, and the binding refuses a statement that yields one — `SQLiteException: unknown error (code 0): Queries can be performed using SQLiteDatabase query or rawQuery methods only`. The release at `:314` had the same shape AND sat after the assertions, so a red leg never reached it. **The same shape does not exist in `DiaryEntryTest`:** its arming already goes through `bridge.pragma()`, which routes to `query()` for exactly this reason and says so where it does it.

**(c) The mark leg. NOT established by the run, established here, and it is not the product's.** `a_full_disk_withdraws_the_tick_and_says_why` reported `checkbox=checked;modal=hidden;diskFull=hidden;unavailable=visible`. Two independent faults, both in the leg:

  1. **The mark was WRITTEN.** At 21:00:24.566 the `executeSet` left for native; at **21:00:24.770** it came back `{"changes":{"changes":4,"lastId":1,"values":[]}}`, and at 21:00:25.166 the projection returned `"child_id":"dia-p3-diskmark-child" … "assertion_id":"16defec0-7303-41a4-804c-849fa9436863"` — the same journal id that `executeSet` carried. Four journal rows landed on a store the arming had called full 4 ms earlier. **So the ARMING is what needed raising, and the product was never reached at all.** "Full" is a property of the next write, not of the file: the filler exhausts what `record`'s pages will take, and small rows into `journal_entry` / `assertion` / `confirmation` fitted in those tables' own partially-filled leaves.
  2. **The verdict was read 200 ms before the bridge answered.** The wait returned as soon as `box.checked` was true, which `box.click()` makes true synchronously. It reported the document mid-act — including `unavailable=visible`, which is only the resting state of a paragraph that ships without `hidden` (`app/index.html`). The leg never observed any outcome, in either direction.

**(d) One leg poisoned the next, in this same run.** The mark leg failed at its first assertion and never reached its release, so the diary leg after it armed against a still-clamped store and logged `arming: state=full;rows=0` — zero filler rows written because the first was already refused, reported as a successful arming. The store outlives every `ActivityScenario` in the process, so one leg's leftovers are the next leg's premise.

**(e) And the two store-unavailable paragraphs are mutually exclusive — checked, not assumed.** The run could not say, because the modal never opened. `showStoreUnavailable` assigns BOTH notes on every call from one boolean (`diskFullNote.hidden = !diskFull`, `unavailableNote.hidden = diskFull`), it is the only writer of that modal's `show` class, and its only two callers pass either nothing (generic) or the classified code. So exactly one paragraph is visible whenever the window is actually up, and the leg's own "both explanations were shown at once" assertion would have passed had it waited. **No defect; C3 introduced no second-paragraph bug.**

### Decision

- **a. The repair is one line, and the finding is not the line.** `const who = author();` now stands where `author()` is already guaranteed non-null; `:252` is byte-unchanged, because the intent was right and only the name was missing. What cost a packet is the answer to "why did nothing catch it": **the diary's SUCCESS path had no executor anywhere off-device.** `diary-surface.spec.js` reaches the surface with a simulated shell and no store behind it, so `isNativeStore()` is false and every leg there ends in a refusal BEFORE the try block. The only executor of the resolving branch was an emulator that runs on `pull_request` and dispatch.

- **b. So the success path gets an executor that runs on every push, and the rule it was hiding behind gets its boundary drawn.** `app/tests/diary-save.spec.js` drives the shipped `saveEntry` against a seam installed at the BRIDGE boundary (`window.Capacitor.nativePromise`) that RESOLVES, so the whole chain `saveEntry → store/boot.js → store/records.js → store/bridge.js` executes. **It proves** that the surface asks the store with the author the store minted and the child on screen, survives the answer, re-renders, and shows the parent their entry; and that an edit is an overwrite of the same row. **It proves nothing about SQLite** — no SQL is executed, no DDL applied, no constraint, trigger, transaction, index or encryption exists. Its own header says so, and so does the seam's. `DIA-DL-005` alternative 9 — do not fake a store to reach the DISK-FULL refusal — **stands untouched**; what was wrong was applying it to the success path too, which is a different claim.

- **c. The seam fails closed and matches nothing loosely.** Every statement is matched by EXACT EQUALITY; the diary and journal statements are READ out of the shipped modules (`RECORDS_SQL`, `RECORD_INSERT_SQL`, `CHILDREN_SQL`, …, through a port of `harness.py`'s `js_string_constant`); the pragmas are built from the shipped knobs the page itself imports; and anything unmatched THROWS with the statement in the message. This is `DIA-DL-005`'s own "substring matching bites" class, one layer out: a responder that answered an unrecognised statement with an empty result would let a leg pass while the surface asked for something else entirely.

- **d. The arming now proves itself for EACH SHAPE, and refuses to call anything but a full disk full.** `fillToCeiling` reaches the ceiling with record-shaped filler and then again with journal-shaped probes — the mark path's own transaction, an entry plus its detail, with `kind='note'` and a NULL skill so the probes that land move nothing in the projected skill state — and returns both refusals (`refusal`, `journalRefusal`) rather than deriving the second from the first. Each leg asserts on its OWN act's shape. A rejection whose class is not `StoreDiskFullError` is now rethrown: a constraint violation reported as fullness would arm nothing and say it had. **The probes that land are not deleted and cannot be** — the append-only triggers refuse DELETE on `journal_entry`, which is the property the schema is built on. That is the price of arming that path at all; it is bounded by the record filler running first, and the count is returned so it is a measured cost rather than a silent one.

- **e. A wait keys on something the app SETS, never on something the click set.** Both of the tick's outcomes are written after the write resolved: a refusal un-ticks the box and shows the window, a success adds `skill-completed` to the row. Either means it has decided; `box.checked` is true by construction. This is the same defect class `DIA-DL-002` (b) and `DIA-DL-003` (b) recorded for the transfer legs — a wait that cannot tell "not yet" from "answered" — met for the third time, and named here as such.

- **f. A release belongs where it runs whatever the assertions did.** Both disk-full legs in `DiaryEntryTest` and the full-database leg in `StoreEngineTest` now release in a `finally`, through a helper that LOGS instead of asserting: an exception thrown from a `finally` replaces the failure the leg was reporting, and a cleanup that hides the red it was cleaning up after is worse than no cleanup. In `StoreEngineTest` the leak was bounded — the ceiling sits on a per-test probe database `@After` deletes — and it moves anyway, for one rule across both files.

- **g. The "identifier that does not exist" class gets a narrow guard, and the narrowness is stated rather than hidden.** `app/tests/undeclared-reference.spec.js` flags a SPREAD of a name a shipped module never declares. It is not `no-undef` and does not pretend to be: that needs a scope-accurate parser, this repository carries no eslint on purpose, and the cost of going wider was measured before the file was written — a crude free-identifier sweep over the mount surfaces 82 distinct unresolved names, some 35 of them legitimate globals and the rest the sweep's own misses. Restricted to spreads the ambiguity disappears: the mount holds five `...` sites, four are rest parameters, and the fifth was `who`. **It covers the shape that shipped, not the class**; the class is bought by (b), which executes the path.

- **h. No mount copy-forward, stated so nobody wonders.** `/m/v6/` was created on this branch, the branch is not deployed, and `/m/v6/` exists nowhere else — an unpublished generation is not frozen, so a bump would buy nothing and cost a seventh shipped generation.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Fix `...who` by inlining `...author()`.** Rejected — same behaviour, and it puts a call in an argument position the neighbouring guard treats as a smell. The hoisted binding makes the name the module already reads real, and leaves the defect line byte-unchanged in the diff.
2. **Add the resolving leg to `diary-surface.spec.js`.** Rejected — that file states of ITSELF that nothing about an entry being written is claimed there. A new file, and a correction to the one paragraph of that header which had drawn the rule too wide.
3. **Fake `createRecord` instead of the bridge.** Rejected — it would assert that the surface calls a function the test wrote. The chain `...who` broke is exactly the chain a bridge-boundary fake makes execute.
4. **Leave the mark leg's arming alone and weaken its assertion.** Rejected — it would report luck as evidence, which is the failure the class comment already names.
5. **An `@After` rather than a `finally` for the release.** Rejected — an `@After` would have to launch a fresh `ActivityScenario`; the `finally` keeps the one that is open.
6. **A general `no-undef` scan, or nothing at all.** Both rejected — see (g). The measurement is why, and both halves of it are in the file.
7. **Defer the milestone-record correction to P4's docs tail.** Rejected at plan review — `docs/execution-map.md`'s "a save lands one `record` row" is false as shipped, it is about this packet's own subject, and the file may be read by anyone between now and P4. Corrected statement-scoped: that clause and nothing else.
8. **Arm the journal path with an `assertion`-shaped probe carrying a skill id.** Rejected — the probes that land cannot be deleted, and a skill-bearing one would move `v_child_skill_state`, which the acts under test read. `kind='note'` with a NULL skill is what the schema's paired CHECK makes expressible.

### Supersedes

None. **Amends by reference, leaving the record byte-untouched:** `DIA-DL-005`, which gains one appended pointer bullet — its "a parent writes in the app" claim was not true as shipped, and its falsifiable prediction had two branches, neither of which is what happened. **Corrects, in files this packet already edits:** `DiaryEntryTest`'s class comment, which claimed the arming proves itself when it proved itself for one shape only; `diary-surface.spec.js`'s header paragraph, which drew "a fake would prove the fake" over the success path as well as the disk-full one; and `docs/execution-map.md`'s P3 clause about a save landing a `record` row.

### Effects

- **Added:** `app/tests/diary-save.spec.js`, `app/tests/support/page-bridge.js`, `app/tests/undeclared-reference.spec.js`.
- **Changed:** `app/m/v6/surfaces/diary.js` (one line added), `native/.../androidTest/.../DiaryEntryTest.java` (wait predicate, arming stage, two `finally` releases, class comment), `native/.../androidTest/.../StoreEngineTest.java` (two PRAGMA calls re-routed, one `finally` release), `app/playwright.config.js` (two `testMatch` entries), `app/tests/diary-surface.spec.js` (header only), `docs/execution-map.md` (one clause), `docs/decision-log.md` (this entry plus the pointer bullet). **Nine files.**
- **No schema change, no new knob, no new signal, no new signal kind, no new closed code.** `diary.write` and `write.refused` are untouched. **Net egress change: zero.**
- **No invariant added, and no invariant discharged.** `DIA-P3-INV-001` / `DIA-P3-INV-002` keep their **Not yet observed.** fields; the re-dispatch discharges them.
- **No baseline moved.** Nothing rendered changes: the repair makes a path that always threw complete instead.
- **What this packet cannot do, stated rather than implied.** The host has no Android SDK and no Gradle, so every device-leg claim here is **unobserved at the time of writing**: the fixture repair, the raised arming and the corrected wait are reasoned and type-checked, not executed. The two `androidTest` files ARE type-checked on the host with OpenJDK 21 against `androidx.test:core:1.6.1`, `runner:1.6.2`, `monitor:1.7.2`, `ext:junit:1.2.1`, `junit:4.13.2` and an API-34 surface with the stubs `DIA-DL-002`/`-003` used, and their embedded JavaScript is parsed by `node --check` after placeholder substitution. Both are checks, not runs. The browser leg and the source scan, by contrast, are executed on every push and their bite is demonstrated below.
- **The guard's bite, demonstrated rather than asserted.** With `const who = author();` deleted — the shipped defect, restored — `diary-save.spec.js` reds twice over: on a list that never gains a row, and on `seed.js`'s console-error guard reporting `[diary] the entry was not recorded: ReferenceError who is not defined`, the same sentence the emulator logged. `undeclared-reference.spec.js` reds naming `who`, while the ten other guards that read the same file stayed green. Restored, all pass.
- **A falsifiable prediction.** On the next `android-instrumented` dispatch, `fillToCeiling` should report `state=full` with `refusal=full:StoreDiskFullError` AND `journalRefusal=full:StoreDiskFullError`, and both disk-full legs should reach their refusal and succeed again once the ceiling is released. If `journalRefusal` reports `budget`, the journal's own pages had more room than 200 probes consume and the second stage needs raising in turn. If the mark leg now refuses but the tick does NOT stick after release, the refusal is still not about a full disk. And if `an_entry_a_parent_writes_lands_in_the_store` still reds, the fault is not the one this packet repaired — the browser leg says the surface asks correctly, and only the device can say what happens next.

## DIA-DL-007 — DIA-P3R2 `diary-disk-full-class`: the wrapper's rollback was speaking for the write, so a full disk asked a parent to try again instead of to free space

- **Date.** 2026-08-17
- **Type.** Packet — DIA-P3R2, second repair packet of **L2 "local diary"**, on branch `feat/l2-local-diary`, following the dispatch `DIA-DL-006` scheduled. One packet, one report.
- **Scope.** The two faults run 31979084821 exposed — one in a fixture's assertion, one in the seam both write paths share — and the ADR-046 §1.1 requirement underneath the second. **Out:** P4's scope (the FTS index, search, the closing milestone docs); the artefact gap, which stays an owner decision recorded in `DIA-DL-005`; the install prompt; the analytics surface; retiring old mounts; any change to the schema, to `RECORD_INSERT_SQL`'s column list, or to what the surface says when the store is merely unavailable.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was repaired

**(a) Neither disk-full leg reached the product.** Both died in ARMING, at `DiaryEntryTest.fillToCeiling(DiaryEntryTest.java:597)`, with `err:StoreError:ExecuteSet: Failed in rollbackTransactioncannot rollback - no transaction is active (code 1)`. So run 31979084821 says nothing directly about what a parent would have read — and the mechanism it does establish is the one the product runs on.

**(b) The mechanism. Measured, and it is the wrapper's.** Logcat 23:30:40.036-40.038, on the arming's journal probe — `bridge.executeSet([...], { transaction: true })`, the mark path's own shape:

  ```
  (13) statement aborts at 123: database or disk is full; [INSERT INTO journal_entry (…)]
  (1)  statement aborts at 1: cannot rollback - no transaction is active; [ROLLBACK;]
  Sending plugin error: {…"methodName":"executeSet","success":false,"error":{"message":
    "ExecuteSet: Failed in rollbackTransactioncannot rollback - no transaction is active (code 1)"}}
  ```

  `SQLITE_FULL` is one of the errors SQLite aborts the transaction on, so the wrapper's ROLLBACK finds nothing to roll back and fails; and the wrapper issues it from a `finally` (`@capacitor-community/sqlite`, `SQLite/Database.java:483-487`), so the throw from that `finally` DISCARDS the disk-full exception the `catch` was carrying. `execute` (`:434`) and `runSQL` (`:637`) carry the identical block.

**(c) Nothing of the original survives to classify from — three ways, each checked.** The bridge payload has exactly one field under `error`: a message. The wrapper rethrows with `new Exception(e.getMessage())`, so no cause is chained. And there is no code field. `classifyStoreFailure` therefore had a string reading "cannot rollback", which carries none of `DISK_FULL_MARKERS`.

**(d) And the mask is CONDITIONAL, which is worse than a plain defect.** In the same run the arming's record fillers — single `bridge.run` calls — surfaced the engine's own words: `{"methodName":"run",…,"message":"Run: database or disk is full (code 13)"}` at 23:30:39.691 and 23:30:39.783. Same `finally`, opposite outcome, decided by whether the ROLLBACK happens to succeed. Whether a parent was told the truth was luck, and no amount of observing which way it fell would have fixed it.

**(e) What that would have cost a parent, had the legs reached the product.** `createRecord` (`records.js:200-219`) and `appendEntries` (`journal.js:169-176`, reached from `appendMark`) both write through `executeSet` with `transaction: true`. A masked refusal classifies as `StoreError` → `storeFailureCode` returns `other` → the diary shows *"Запись НЕ сохранена. Ваш текст остался в поле — попробуйте нажать «Сохранить» ещё раз."* and the mark path shows the store-did-not-open paragraph, which tells them to restart the app. Neither frees space. That is the ADR-015 failure ADR-046 §1.1 exists to prevent, and `docs/execution-map.md` recorded the requirement as closed.

**(f) The fixture fault, and it accused a product that was right.** `an_entry_a_parent_writes_lands_in_the_store` failed `expected:<null> but was:<set>` on `eventAt`. `readBack` reads rows from `loadRecords` → `RECORDS_SQL`, which selects seven columns and not `event_at_utc`; `row.event_at_utc` was therefore `undefined`, and `undefined === null` is false. `RECORD_INSERT_SQL` writes the pair as literal `NULL` and always did. The leg had never once observed slot 11.

### Decision

- **a. The seam drives the transaction; the classifier is not touched.** `store/bridge.js`'s `executeSet` now issues `beginTransaction`, sends the set with `transaction: false`, and issues `commitTransaction` — and on failure attempts `rollbackTransaction`, SWALLOWS its error, and rethrows the original. The rule, stated in the file: **the failure that caused the rollback outranks the rollback's own failure.** `DISK_FULL_MARKERS` is byte-untouched.

- **b. One repair, at the one door both paths already go through.** `records.js:200` (diary) and `journal.js:171` (mark) are `executeSet`'s only callers, and `DiaryEntryTest`'s arming imports the same shipped module (`import(u('store/bridge.js'))`, `:600`). So the diary path, the mark path and the arming that gates both legs are covered by one change rather than by parallel edits that could drift.

- **c. Atomicity is KEPT, which is why this shape and not the simpler one.** Dropping `transaction: true` at the call sites would have been smaller and is safe for the diary — the record insert is last, so the only residue is an empty area the next write adopts through `AREA_LOOKUP_SQL`. It is NOT safe for the mark: `appendEntries` writes four rows and `journal_entry` carries the eight append-only triggers that refuse DELETE (LSC-P2-INV-001), so a half-written mark could never be cleaned up. `fillToCeiling`'s own doc already records that asymmetry — its journal probes cannot be deleted, its record fillers can.

- **d. `beginTransaction` sits outside the `try`.** If BEGIN itself fails there is no transaction to roll back, and attempting one would reintroduce exactly the masking this removes.

- **e. The three new plugin methods bound a CLASS OF CAPABILITY, and that is the test they had to pass.** `ALLOWED_PLUGIN_METHODS` is a supply-chain boundary, not documentation. None of `beginTransaction` / `commitTransaction` / `rollbackTransaction` can address a path, enumerate anything, or delete anything: they control a transaction on a database the app has already opened, which is strictly less reach than `execute` and `run` already carry. Decided here rather than escalated, at plan review.

- **f. And the allowlist is now pinned as an EXACT SET, so this cannot become a precedent.** The existing guard was one-directional — it stopped a call site reaching past the list and said nothing about the list growing. `app/tests/store-supply-chain.spec.js` now also asserts the membership exactly, so a fourth method costs a deliberate edit to a named list rather than riding on the argument made once in (e).

- **g. `overwriteRecord` stops asking for a transaction too, on a STATIC finding.** One UPDATE is already atomic, so the wrapper transaction bought nothing and re-opened the same window: `runSQL` carries the identical `finally`. A parent whose disk fills while CORRECTING an entry is on the write path too. Labelled honestly — this instance is established by reading the wrapper, not by an artefact; in this run the `run` fillers fell the clean way.

- **h. The fixture asks for what it asserts, and a column that was never selected now says so.** `readBack` issues its own `SELECT event_at_utc, event_utc_offset_min FROM record WHERE id = ?` through the same bridge `journalCount` uses, rather than widening a product query to serve a test — the diary surface has no use for the event instant. Its reduction returns **`absent`** as a third answer, distinct from `null` and `set`, so the next assertion written against an unselected column reds naming the fixture instead of accusing the write path. That is the class the run caught, not just the instance. The write leg now asserts BOTH halves of the pair, which is what the schema's paired CHECK is about and what the leg was always claiming to observe.

- **i. `page-bridge.js` learns the envelope rather than being loosened.** The in-page seam fails closed on unknown methods (`DIA-DL-006` (c)), so the seam change red four `diary-save` legs — correctly. It now answers the three transaction methods and refuses everything else exactly as before. It does not SIMULATE a transaction: it holds rows in an array and has nothing to begin, and pretending otherwise would be a fake proving a fake.

- **j. NAMED DEBT, deferred and not lost: `bridge.run`'s `transaction = true` default.** `store/store.js` still relies on it at **`store.js:133, 160, 164, 172 and 238`**. Those are writes on the OPEN path, so if one is ever masked the same way, `store.open`'s `failure_class` is wrong AT BOOT — the same class of harm one layer earlier, and reaching a parent through a different sentence. Not swept here because `store.js` is not a file this packet opens and the change wants its own evidence. A comment at `bridge.run` records the trap; this bullet is the durable address for it.

- **k. No mount copy-forward, and the reason is unchanged.** `/m/v6/` was created on this branch, the branch is not deployed, and it exists nowhere else — an unpublished generation is not frozen (`DIA-DL-006` (h)), so `v6` is edited in place and `CACHE_VERSION` is not bumped.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Widen `DISK_FULL_MARKERS` to match the rollback message.** Rejected, and not merely deprioritised: a marker matching "cannot rollback" would classify every unrelated transaction failure as a full disk, and a parent would be told to free space when space is not the problem. `store-seam.spec.js` carries a leg that fails if this is ever done — a `no such table` failure inside the same envelope must stay `StoreError`.
2. **Classify from the original error's code or cause.** Rejected because it is not reachable — see (c). Three independent losses, any one of which is fatal on its own.
3. **Drop `transaction: true` at the two call sites.** Rejected — see (c). Smaller, and wrong for the mark path.
4. **Retry the write once when the refusal names a rollback.** Rejected — a retry on a full disk fills nothing and delays the sentence the parent needs; and a retry behind the parent is what `diary-write.spec.js` already asserts the write path does not do.
5. **Have the fixture assert `eventAt` from a statement it writes itself, without the `absent` sentinel.** Rejected — it fixes the instance and leaves the class. The sentinel is two lines and turns a report obligation into an enforced property.
6. **Extend `RECORDS_SQL` to select the event pair.** Rejected — it changes a product query to serve a test, and the diary surface never reads the event instant.
7. **Put the seam leg in `store-unit.spec.js`.** Rejected on contact with that file: its header says outright that bridge claims needing a fake do not belong there. `diary-write.spec.js` was rejected too — it would scope a rule the mark path depends on to the diary. Hence a file of its own.
8. **Model the wrapper's internal rollback masking inside `fake-bridge.js`, so the off-device leg reproduces the device defect.** Rejected — that masking happens inside Java, below the bridge, and a fake that simulated it would be asserting our own theory of the wrapper back to us. The device legs carry that claim; the off-device leg carries the seam's contract.

### Supersedes

None. **Extends** `DIA-DL-005` (h) and (i), whose refusal wording is what this packet makes reachable, and `DIA-DL-006`, whose raised arming is what exposed the seam. **Amends by reference, leaving the record byte-untouched:** `DIA-DL-005`, whose ADR-046 §1.1 claim was true of the classifier and not of the path that feeds it. **Corrects, in files this packet already edits:** `docs/execution-map.md`'s P3 clause, which states that a full disk reaches the parent as itself on the diary and on the mark path — untrue as shipped, for the reason in (b).

### Effects

- **Added:** `app/tests/store-seam.spec.js`.
- **Changed:** `app/m/v6/store/bridge.js` (executeSet rewritten, two comment blocks), `app/m/v6/store/config.js` (three allowlist entries, provenance comment), `app/m/v6/store/records.js` (one flag, one comment), `app/tests/support/fake-bridge.js` (`rollbackFailsWith`, envelope-aware `transactions()`), `app/tests/support/page-bridge.js` (three methods answered), `app/tests/store-supply-chain.spec.js` (exact-set leg), `app/playwright.config.js` (one `testMatch` entry), `native/.../androidTest/.../DiaryEntryTest.java` (`readBack`, one assertion added, two doc blocks), `docs/execution-map.md` (one clause), `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (one **Enforced by** line), `docs/decision-log.md` (this entry). **Twelve files.**
- **No schema change, no new knob, no new signal, no new signal kind, no new closed code.** `STORE_FAILURE_CODES` is untouched. `ALLOWED_PLUGIN_METHODS` gains three entries — a declared surface, not a knob, and pinned by (f). **Net egress change: zero.**
- **No invariant added, and no invariant discharged.** `DIA-P3-INV-001` / `DIA-P3-INV-002` keep their **Not yet observed.** fields. `DIA-P3-INV-002` gains `store-seam.spec.js` under **Enforced by** for the seam half only; the parent-facing half is still the device's to answer.
- **No baseline moved.** Nothing rendered changes.
- **What this packet cannot do, stated rather than implied.** The host has OpenJDK 21 but no Android SDK and no Gradle, so every device-leg claim is **unobserved at the time of writing**. `DiaryEntryTest.java` is checked two ways that are checks and not runs: `javac`'s parser accepts it with no syntax error (all 96 diagnostics are missing packages and symbols, since no `android.jar` or `androidx.test` jars are present on this host — a weaker check than `DIA-DL-006`'s, which had them), and its embedded JavaScript is parsed by `node --check` after placeholder substitution. The `absent` sentinel's reduction IS executed off-device against all three shapes, including the exact defect shape.
- **The bite, and an honest account of which half it carries.** With `executeSet` reverted to the shipped one-liner, `store-seam.spec.js` reds three of five legs; restored, all five pass. Those three red on CALL ORDER — the seam no longer issuing its own transaction. The classification assertions do NOT bite off-device, because the masking they defend against happens inside the Java wrapper, below the bridge, where no fake of ours reaches. So the evidence for the product defect is the device run quoted in (b), and this file is a regression guard for the seam's contract. Saying otherwise would be the fourth thing `AGENTS.md` §11 lists.
- **A falsifiable prediction, and the detector it must be READ against.** On the next `android-instrumented` dispatch, `fillToCeiling` should report `state=full` with both `refusal=full:StoreDiskFullError` and `journalRefusal=full:StoreDiskFullError` — the arming's own probe goes through the repaired seam, so if the seam still masked, the arming would still rethrow. Both disk-full legs should then reach their refusal. **AND THE CONTROL IS THE PART THAT MUST BE QUOTED, NOT ASSUMED.** Our rollback attempt hits the same failing `ROLLBACK`; if Android's transaction stack does not unwind after it, the connection is wedged and later writes fail. That failure is invisible behind two green assertions earlier in the same leg, and it surfaces only at `releaseCeiling` — so the report on that dispatch quotes, for BOTH legs, what happened AFTER the release: the control press that must save (`"listed"`, then `count=1`) and the control tick that must stick (`checkbox=checked`). A leg that refuses correctly and then cannot write again has not passed. And if `an_entry_a_parent_writes_lands_in_the_store` reports `eventAt=absent`, the second statement did not return the pair and the fault is this packet's, not the product's.
- **The prediction, CHECKED — `android-instrumented` run 31982061125 (`workflow_dispatch`, `feat/l2-local-diary`), success; `DiaryEntryTest` 4/4, `StoreEngineTest` 9/9.** Every branch it named came back the way it said, and the two it offered as falsifiers did not fire. `fillToCeiling` reported `state=full` with **both** `refusal=full:StoreDiskFullError` and `journalRefusal=full:StoreDiskFullError`, on both legs — the arming's own probe goes through the repaired seam, so a seam that still masked would have rethrown there. **The control was read, not assumed**, which is the part this bullet exists to bind: `tick after release: checkbox=checked;modal=hidden;diskFull=visible;unavailable=hidden`, and the diary leg's post-release press saved and read back `count=1`. So the connection is NOT wedged by swallowing the rollback's error — and the rollback does still fail, twelve times in this run, now under `methodName: rollbackTransaction` (00:31:41.834) rather than replacing the write's own failure. **No `executeSet` error in the run carries rollback text**, and the engine's words cross intact: `"ExecuteSet: database or disk is full (code 13)"` at 00:31:41.827. `eventAt=absent` did not appear — the sentinel never fired, and the write leg read `eventAt=null;eventOffset=null;entryAt=set`. Recorded here as evidence against this entry's own prediction; the discharge itself lives in `docs/INVARIANTS.md` under `DIA-P3-INV-001` / `DIA-P3-INV-002`, and no new decision was taken.

## DIA-DL-008 — DIA-P4 `diary-fts-and-close`: a parent searches the diary, the word-form question is answered in the query rather than in the index, and the milestone closes

- **Date.** 2026-08-17
- **Type.** Packet — DIA-P4, fourth and last packet of **L2 "local diary"**, on branch `feat/l2-local-diary`. Five checkpoints on one branch (the store path and its measurement; the surface, the signal and the delivery; the device legs; the embedded-JS parse guard; this docs tail), each with its own execution report and its own commit.
- **Scope.** Search over the diary through the FTS index the frozen schema has carried since L1-P2. The word-form strategy ADR-046 §2.5 left to this milestone, decided and **measured**. The rebuild path PDR-026 §4 rule 3 promises, answered as *who triggers it and when*. The embedded-JS parse guard scheduled at P3's C4 review. The milestone's closing docs and its debt list. **Out:** the archive gap, now decided and addressed to L3 (see `DIA-DL-005`'s pointer); the install prompt; the analytics surface; clearing browser `localStorage`; retiring `m/v1`–`m/v5`; the privacy-policy and consent surface; any narrative or thematic layer; any vector index; media. **No schema change: no slot, no column, no trigger, no migration.**

### What the artefacts establish

**(a) The word-form ceiling, measured across four settings before anything was decided.** Forty queries a parent might type against fifteen ordinary diary sentences, with the expression produced by the **shipped** builder under `node` and run against the real frozen DDL on desktop SQLite 3.45.1:

| ceiling | queries that found their entry | extra documents | what the setting costs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **3 (shipped)** | **37 / 40** | 4, across 4 queries | misses only stem mutations: `сесть`, `пойти`, `спит` |
| 4 | 31 / 40 | 1 | also loses `села`, `сели`, `пошёл`, `спать`, `есть`, `зубы` |
| 5 | 26 / 40 | 1 | also loses `растут`, `встать`, `вставать`, `бегать`, `уснуть` |
| 6 | 22 / 40 | 1 | also loses `книжка`, `книжку`, `книжке`, `машина` |

The plan proposed **4**. The measurement rejected it, and the knob shipped at **3**: the asymmetry the plan had not accounted for is that a prefix bridges the END of a word, so a query LONGER than what was written cannot reach it unless the ceiling cuts both down. Going 3 → 4 buys the removal of one extra result and costs nine everyday queries.

**(b) Two staleness probes are DEAD on this engine, and both are recorded as executed assertions rather than as warnings in a comment** — because the next reader who wants a cheap staleness check will reach for exactly these two. `SELECT count(*) FROM record_fts` counts the CONTENT table on an external-content index and returns the same number whether the index is whole or empty; and FTS5's argument-less `integrity-check` PASSES over an index emptied by `delete-all`. Only the `rank`-argument form (`INSERT INTO record_fts (record_fts, rank) VALUES ('integrity-check', 1)`) raises.

**(c) What the device engine says about the `rank` form is not yet known, and that is why the product does not use it.** `StoreEngineTest::the_index_repairs_itself_after_delete_all` runs both forms against an emptied index and LOGS the outcome — recorded, not required, the same posture as the `ENABLE_ICU` line beside it. The dispatch will fill this in; the design does not wait for it, because a probe that must itself be version-gated is more moving parts than the repair it would guard.

**(d) The index does not fold `ё` to `е`, on the device.** `StoreEngineTest::russian_tokenization_behaves_as_measured_off_device` has asserted that since L1-P2, and the new engine leg asserts it again from the other side — `"елк"*` alone must NOT find `Ёлка`. That negative is what makes the query-side alternation necessary rather than decorative, and if it ever flips, the assertion says so in its own message.

### Decision

- **a. The word-form strategy is QUERY-SIDE, and that is the whole answer to ADR-046 §2.5.** The tokenizer is frozen with the schema (`unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`); FTS5 is compiled without ICU (`LSC-DL-002`), and ICU would have folded nothing and lemmatised nothing anyway. So there is no stemmer to install and no tokenizer to swap — what is left is what the QUERY asks for. Every word a parent types is searched as a **prefix**, in **every ё/е spelling of itself**, and all the words must appear. The consequence worth stating out loud: because the normalisation lives in the query, moving the ceiling needs neither a migration **nor a rebuild**. It is the cheapest possible answer to a question that was framed as momentous, and the reason it is cheap is that PDR-026 §4 rule 4 kept the index free of normalisation decisions.
- **b. Three knobs carry it, with their measurement attached** (`store/config.js`, all `changed_in: DIA-DL-008`): `diarySearchStemChars` = 3 by (a), `diarySearchVariantCeiling` = 8 (a word with n such letters has 2ⁿ spellings, so the count is bounded and a word past the bound is searched exactly as typed — a miss the parent can act on rather than a query that grows on its own), `diarySearchLimit` = 200 (a bound on the RENDER, declared apart from `diaryListLimit` so tuning one does not silently move the other).
- **c. Every term is quoted, and that is a safety property rather than a style.** `"`, `*`, `-`, `(`, `^` and bare `NEAR` are operators in FTS5's grammar and ordinary punctuation in a sentence about a child. Unquoted, `сел "OR` is a syntax error and the search dies in front of someone who did nothing wrong. Nothing has to be escaped inside the quotes either: the tokeniser has already dropped everything that is not a letter or a digit, so a `"` cannot survive to reach one. Seven punctuation shapes are executed as a parametrised leg.
- **d. Words are joined with `AND`, and results keep the list's own order.** Two words typed mean both are wanted. `bm25` was available and was not used: one pane, one order, and a parent recognises their own diary by date. Recorded as a limitation rather than absorbed.
- **e. THE REBUILD IS THE APP'S JOB, at the one moment staleness is observable, at most once per session.** PDR-026 §4 rule 3 establishes that the index is derived and rebuilt; it does not name the trigger, so the trigger is decided here. **Not the parent:** they cannot tell a stale index from a word-form miss, and a "rebuild the index" control would hand them our internals to diagnose (ADR-015). **Not the open path:** `store/store.js` already runs `PRAGMA integrity_check` there and — because `closeStore()` is never called — that happens on effectively every launch, so a re-index bolted to it would be paid at every start. So: an empty result over a diary that HAS entries triggers one rebuild and one re-run of the same query, and the flag is set BEFORE the rebuild runs, because a rebuild that fails will fail again and retrying it on every ordinary miss would make every miss slow for the rest of the session. *(The plan carried this as `[verify vs vault]`; the tag came off at plan review — the choice is derivable from rule 3 plus ADR-015, and the provenance is recorded here rather than re-opened.)*
- **f. The parent is told nothing about the repair, and that is the honest choice rather than the quiet one.** They were not asked, there is nothing for them to do, and the answer they wanted arrives. It is readable where an operator reads things: `rebuilt=true` in `diary.search`, which the RUNBOOK smoke names.
- **g. THREE EMPTY CASES ARE THREE SENTENCES, AND A REFUSAL IS A FOURTH THING.** `#diaryEmpty` (no entries at all — and the search form is withheld entirely, because a search over an empty diary can only answer "nothing found", which reads as a fault when the truth is that nothing has been written). `#diarySearchEmpty` (entries exist, none matched) carries the honest-degradation content: it names the SOURCE condition, then says the search matches word beginnings and does not parse Russian word forms, then offers the shorter word. And `#diarySearchStatus` for a search that **did not run** — because "nothing matched" is an assertion about the DIARY and a store refusal is an assertion about US, and saying the first when the second is true tells a parent they never wrote something they did write. That is the ADR-046 §1 class of silent lie arriving on a read path.
- **h. `DIA-P4-INV-002`, and the one place the write path and the search path deliberately differ.** The term a parent types is the most family-identifying string this app has ever held. It reaches exactly two places: the bound parameter of a parameterised statement, and the input where they left it. It reaches no payload (structurally impossible — `emitSignal` takes numbers, booleans, null and declared codes), no statement text, and no console line. The **difference from the write path**: `surfaces/diary.js` prints the engine's message on a failed WRITE (the body is a bound value and the engine does not echo it) and prints **only the class name** on a failed SEARCH (an FTS5 parse error would carry the whole expression, which is derived from what the parent typed). Three runtime legs assert the absence, one per path — found, not found, refused — each with an in-leg anti-vacuity check that the signal actually fired.
- **i. `diary.search` carries counts, a timing, a boolean and closed codes.** `tokens` is how many WORDS the query held, in the same sense `diary.write`'s `chars` is a length; `results` is how many entries came back; `rebuilt` is the one fact about this path invisible from anywhere else. On failure `tokens` and `results` are **omitted rather than sent as 0**, because neither is known when the query never ran.
- **j. THE PARSE GUARD IS A GATE NOW, AND TWO OF ITS LEGS ARE WHAT KEEP IT HONEST.** `app/tests/embedded-js-parse.spec.js` reconstructs the JavaScript embedded in Java string literals across the instrumented suites and runs `node --check` over each — **103 snippets across 6 files** on every push. Two rules are requirements rather than taste, and both come from a measurement taken before the guard existed (P4 C3): comments are stripped by a character walker **before** literals are scanned, because the ad-hoc tool treated a double-quoted phrase inside a `//` comment as a Java string and red on `fillToCeiling`, a chain green on a real device in run 31982061125 — a guard that cries wolf is worse than no guard; and a chain the scanner cannot fully reconstruct is **never guessed at**, it goes in a declared skip table with its file, its line and its reason, and an undeclared one reds. **The two legs nobody may switch off on the first inconvenient red**, because a 700-line reader is code and rots like any other: (1) the **arm-check**, which mutates a snippet the suite really checks and requires the same checker to reject it, both sides asserted; and (2) the **census**, which counts every fully-literal chain in the tree opening `(function` and requires each to be covered by something the guard actually read. The census exists because the guard **failed its own arm-check once**: built without `await` in its position list, it went green against a brace deliberately removed from `DiaryEntryTest.searchFromTheSurface`, leaving that file's largest scripts invisible and the guard briefly NARROWER than the ad-hoc tool it replaces. Deleting either leg turns this file back into a scan that reports green because it stopped looking. **What it does not cover** is stated in its own header: JavaScript reaching the device by any path other than the five declared call positions and one named resolution step — a snippet assembled across methods, built by a loop or a `StringBuilder`, passed through a collection, or composed from a constant in another file. And it is only a PARSE.

### The three recurring classes this milestone met more than once

Recorded together, once, because each was met twice or more and a class met twice is not an incident.

- **1. Blanket mount substitution falsifying `changed_in` provenance — twice** (DIA-P1, DIA-P3; both times in `app/sw.js`, both times caught by eye). A repoint is safe for a line describing the CURRENT address and destructive for one describing a PAST bump: `sed` rewrites `changed_in: … v14 -> v15 with the /m/v5/ mount bump` into a claim about a bump that never happened. **No guard is possible** — the two kinds of line are prose and differ only in tense. The countermeasure is procedural and lives where the act happens: `docs/RUNBOOK.md` → **Module mount (owner-run version bump)**, step 3, which excludes `changed_in:` lines from any blanket substitution and re-reads them afterwards. This packet needed no bump, so the rule was not exercised again here.
- **2. Substring matching where token or declaration matching was needed — four times.** A comment mentioning `sw-register.js`; `onNewIntentDISABLED`; `.includes('autoVerify')`; and `"UPDATE"` found inside `updated_at_utc`. The standing countermeasure is the one `support/page-bridge.js` states and this packet reused twice: match statements by **exact equality** and throw on a miss (the seam), and read constants out of the shipped module rather than retyping them (`js_string_constant` and its JavaScript port). C4's guard is the same rule applied to a scanner: it refuses a chain it cannot read whole instead of matching part of one.
- **3. A class rule beating the `hidden` attribute — twice** (`.header-action` at DIA-P2, found by `channel-composition.spec.js` on its first run; `.diary-search` at DIA-P4, found by `diary-search.spec.js` on its first run). Both times the element shipped `hidden=""` and rendered anyway, because `display` in a class rule outranks the browser's user-agent style for the attribute. **AND HERE THE ANSWER TO "IS THERE A CHEAP GUARD" IS YES** — unlike `no-undef` at DIA-P3R, which was rejected because doing it by hand needs a scope-accurate parser and a crude sweep red 80 times to catch one defect. This one needs neither a parser nor an allowlist: in a booted page, for **every** element in the shipped shell that carries the `hidden` attribute, assert `getComputedStyle(el).display === 'none'`. It is about ten lines in the existing behavior spec, it executes the real cascade rather than reading CSS, it generalises to every future element instead of to a list of known ones, and it would have caught both instances on the packet that introduced them. **It is not built in this packet** — C5 is docs-only and a guard is code — so it is carried as debt item 9 below, with this design attached so the next packet does not re-derive it.

### The debt this milestone hands on, in one place

Carried here rather than scattered across five entries, because a debt list nobody can address is a debt list nobody reads.

1. **`bridge.run`'s `transaction = true` default on the OPEN path** — `store/store.js:133, 160, 164, 172, 238`. A masked failure there makes `store.open`'s `failure_class` wrong at boot: the same harm as `DIA-DL-007` (b), one layer earlier, reaching a parent through a different sentence. A comment at `bridge.run` records the trap; `DIA-DL-007` (j) is its original address.
2. **`overwriteRecord`'s `changed < 1` branch has no executor.** The refusal is written and reasoned and nothing anywhere drives it.
3. **Weak wait predicates in `ExportTransferTest` and `WebViewStorageTest`** — the class `DIA-DL-006` repaired in the mark leg (a predicate that settles on state the document already holds). P4 fixed the shape in the new search leg by keying on the control's own disabled/enabled transition, and gave that assumption an off-device executor; the two older suites were not touched.
4. **No Espresso arm around `pickTransfer`** (`HistoryTransferTest:361`) — the plugin's own launching call has no arm proving the intent it builds.
5. **`ExportTransferTest`'s host type-check gap** — the `espresso-intents` jar is not fetched by the host type-check recipe, so that file alone is checked more weakly than its siblings.
6. **The `.export-status` naming debt, now four ids wide.** `#importStatus` and `#diaryStatus` were styled by a class named after the export surface; P4 added `#diarySearchEmpty` and `#diarySearchStatus` to the same class. Renaming a shared class is its own packet, and it moves DOM baselines.
7. **Five frozen generations still ship under `app/m/`** (`v1`–`v5` beside the current `v6`). Retiring them is an owner decision about installed clients, not a cleanup.
8. **FIRST-ORDER CANDIDATE FOR THE NEXT MILESTONE'S OPENING, not a flat-list entry: `closeStore()` is defined and never called.** It is not a latent tidiness item — it has an **observable symptom in every dispatch this milestone ran**: every `store.open` signal in the logcats reports `previous_run_clean=false`, including on runs whose previous close was orderly. `core/signals.js` records that as a fact about the signal; what has never been named is its cost, which is that `PRAGMA integrity_check` runs at **effectively every launch** on the family's device — a full scan of the family history, paid by the parent, every time they open the app. It costs them time at every start, it grows with their history, and it is also what forecloses the cheapest home for any future index maintenance (see decision (e)). It should be opened, not scheduled.
9. **The `[hidden]` cascade guard designed in the recurring-classes section above** — ten lines, executes the real cascade, would have caught both instances. Not built here because C5 is docs-only.

- **Continued, 2026-08-18 — items 10, 11 and 12 live in `DIA-DL-010` and this list is not rewritten to hold them.** Two are the `surfaces/diary.js` defects DIA-P5 surfaced and deliberately did not fix (an unguarded `await` in `renderList`, and a save the store ACCEPTED being reported to the parent as «Запись НЕ сохранена»); the third is `webContentsDebuggingEnabled`, on by default in the build the owner installs. Nothing above is edited.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Change the tokenizer, or add a second FTS table with a different one.** Rejected: it is a DDL edit against a frozen schema, and a second index is a second thing to keep in step for a gain the query already delivers.
2. **Fold `ё` to `е` in the query.** Rejected on the measurement: the index folds neither into the other, so folding one way simply moves the miss to the other spelling. Both are asked for.
3. **`bm25` relevance ordering.** Rejected — see (d). Available, and declined deliberately.
4. **A parent-facing "rebuild the index" control.** Rejected — see (e). It asks a parent to diagnose our internals.
5. **Repair on the open path, beside `integrity_check`.** Rejected — see (e), and see debt item 8 for why that path is the wrong home twice over.
6. **Gate the repair on FTS5's `integrity-check`.** Rejected: the argument-less form does not detect the divergence at all, and the `rank` form's availability on the bundled engine is unmeasured. Recorded in (b) and (c) so the rejection is readable rather than remembered.
7. **Compare `count(*)` between `record` and `record_fts`.** Rejected as **measured vacuous** — see (b).
8. **A separate `store/search.js` module.** Rejected: searching records is the record's concern, the scoping predicates are the same three the read path uses, and a second module would be a second place for "whose diary is this" to be answered — at the cost of ship-list, precache and hint edits for no separation the file did not already have.
9. **Re-type the word-form rule in Python for the measurement.** Rejected for the reason `js_string_constant` exists: a rule re-typed in a test is a copy, and the copy is what drifts. The measurement runs the shipped builder under `node` through a temp root carrying `{"type":"module"}`, verifying every copied file byte-for-byte first — the technique `app/tests/export/build-artifact.mjs` already documents.
10. **Let the parse guard approximate a chain with a Java operand by substituting a stand-in.** Rejected: it would make four more snippets checkable and would make the guard's answer about a script it half-read. They are declared instead.

### Supersedes

None. **Extends** `LSC-DL-002` (the frozen index and its measured tokenizer, whose first product user this is), `DIA-DL-005` (the diary this searches), `DIA-DL-006` (the executor rule its browser legs follow) and `DIA-DL-007` (the seam and the `{ transaction: false }` discipline the rebuild call inherits). **Amends by reference, leaving the record byte-untouched:** `DIA-DL-005`, whose artefact gap is now decided and addressed to L3. **Corrects, in files this packet already edits:** `LSC-P3-INV-001`'s parenthetical "(until L2)" about `text/diary.txt`; `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s statement that the archive question is an open owner decision, and its promotion-smoke mount example, which still named `/m/v5/` after the P3 bump; and `docs/execution-map.md`'s P3 clause about what an owner decision would weigh.

### Effects

- **Added:** `app/m/v6/store/records.js` search section (`RECORD_SEARCH_SQL`, `RECORD_COUNT_SQL`, `FTS_REBUILD_SQL`, `buildDiaryMatch`, `searchRecords`); `app/tests/schema/test_diary_search.py`; `app/tests/schema/diary-match.mjs`; `app/tests/diary-search.spec.js`; `app/tests/embedded-js-parse.spec.js`.
- **Changed:** `app/index.html` (the search form and two status paragraphs inside `#diaryModal`), `app/m/v6/{app.css,core/signals.js,store/boot.js,store/config.js,surfaces/diary.js}`, `app/playwright.config.js` (two `testMatch` entries), `app/tests/support/page-bridge.js`, `native/.../androidTest/.../{StoreEngineTest,DiaryEntryTest}.java`, and the docs spine.
- **Four knobs, all new, all with `changed_in` provenance** (`diarySearchLimit`, `diarySearchStemChars`, `diarySearchVariantCeiling`, `ftsRepairPolicy`). **One new signal kind** (`diary.search`). **No new closed code** — `outcome` already carried `complete` / `refused` / `failed`.
- **Three invariants added:** `DIA-P4-INV-001` (whose diary a search returns) and `DIA-P4-INV-003` (the derived index repairs itself) green per-push in their off-device halves and landing **Not yet observed** in their device halves; `DIA-P4-INV-002` (no term reaches a payload, a log line or telemetry) green on every push.
- **No schema change, no migration, no new plugin method. Net egress change: zero.**
- **No baseline moved, and it was checked rather than argued for the DOM half:** the `dom-desktop` / `dom-mobile` suites ran green against the existing baselines, because `#diaryModal` is captured by none of them — the same treatment `#importModal` and `#exportModal` have always had. On the visual side no baseline captures that modal either, and the four full-page shots render it `display: none`.
- **A defect found and fixed inside the packet:** `.diary-search` rendered in an empty diary because a class rule beat `hidden` — the second instance of recurring class 3, caught by the new spec on its first run.
- **What this packet cannot do, stated rather than implied.** The host has OpenJDK 21 and no Android SDK or Gradle, so the device legs have never been built, dexed or run. They ARE type-checked against fetched `androidx.test core 1.6.1` / `runner 1.6.2` / `monitor 1.7.2` / `ext:junit 1.2.1` / `junit 4.13.2` and an API-34 surface with the three stubs `DIA-DL-002` used — the fuller check, not `DIA-DL-007`'s parser-only fallback — and their embedded JavaScript is parsed by the guard this packet ships. Both are checks, not runs.
- **A falsifiable prediction, and the numbers it must return.** On the next `android-instrumented` dispatch, `DiaryEntryTest` should be **5/5** and `StoreEngineTest` **11/11**. Three numbers arrive with it and none of them exists yet: `fts rebuild: records=5 ms=…` from the engine leg, and `search wait as the parent experiences it: repairing=… ms, ordinary=… ms` from the surface leg. Each is logged with its corpus attached — five short sentences, two short entries, an emulator — because a rebuild re-tokenises every record and a parent with three years of entries is a different measurement that nothing here reaches. The falsifiers: if `delete-all` is unsupported on the SQLCipher build, both repair legs red at the destroy step rather than at the repair, and the whole self-heal design needs re-opening; if `сесть` or `спит` MATCHES, this engine has stemming the desktop one does not and decision (a) can be revisited; and if the surface leg reports `found=0` after the destroy, the repair did not reach the parent — which is the only claim in this packet that a green off-device suite cannot substitute for.

- **Amended by reference, 2026-08-17 — the prediction above is CLOSED, and it was falsified by none of the three things it named. See `DIA-DL-009`.** Run **32012897363** returned `StoreEngineTest` **11/11** as predicted and `DiaryEntryTest` **4 of 5**, not 5/5. All three numbers arrived and are on the record — `fts rebuild: records=5 ms=2` and both forms of `integrity-check` under tag `LSC`, and `search wait as the parent experiences it: repairing=22 ms, ordinary=21 ms` under tag `DIA` (`DIA-DL-009` (f)). None of the three falsifiers fired: `delete-all` is supported on the SQLCipher build and the repair legs reached their repair, no stemming appeared, and the surface leg did not report `found=0`. What went red was `a_full_disk_refuses_the_entry_and_keeps_the_text`, on an arming fault this prediction did not model and could not have — the fixture proved the store full for a 200-character row and then licensed a leg that writes 26. That is a fourth falsifier, and it is the subject of `DIA-P4R`. Nothing else here is edited.

- **Amended by reference, 2026-08-17 — the `rank`-argument `integrity-check` is now MEASURED on the bundled engine, closing the unknown that alternative 6 and finding (b) were left resting on. See `DIA-P4-INV-003`'s Observed field.** On `android-instrumented` run **32044006357**, `StoreEngineTest` logged `fts integrity-check over an emptied index: bare=did not raise | rank=1=raised: database disk image is malformed (code 267)`. Three consequences, stated plainly for whoever later wants a cheap staleness probe rather than left to be re-derived. **(1) The argument-less form is useless for this, on the real engine and not only on desktop SQLite** — it passed over an index this run had just emptied, exactly as (b) recorded off-device. **(2) The `rank` form works, in the narrow sense that it raises**, so the availability half of alternative 6's rejection has dissolved: that rejection now stands on ground (1) and on decision (e)'s trigger design, and on nothing about availability. **(3) But what it raises is `database disk image is malformed (code 267)`, which is the wording of CORRUPTION, not of staleness** — so a probe built on it would tell an operator the family's store is damaged when the truth is that a derived index needs rebuilding. Anyone reaching for it owes that distinction a translation. **Nothing shipped changes:** the product still rebuilds unconditionally on the observable symptom, once per session, per decision (e); this measurement removes a reason the rejection rested on and does not re-open the decision. Nothing else here is edited.

## DIA-DL-009 — DIA-P4R `arming-at-the-act-size`: a refusal says the store is full for the write that was performed, and the fixture was performing a different one

- **Date.** 2026-08-17
- **Type.** Packet — DIA-P4R, third repair packet of **L2 "local diary"**, on branch `feat/l2-local-diary`, following the dispatch `DIA-DL-008` scheduled. One packet, one report.
