- **Scope.** The one fault run 32012897363 exposed — in the arming that licenses `DiaryEntryTest`'s diary disk-full leg — the evidence that same fixture had already issued and that this repository had already cited as proof, and the findability defect that made the run's own numbers cost a full diagnostic round. **Out:** the diary's product behaviour, which was right and is not touched; the schema; the mount (no copy-forward — `/m/v6/` is unpublished, `DIA-DL-006` (h)); the **Not yet observed.** fields of `DIA-P4-INV-001` and `DIA-P4-INV-003`, which a dispatch discharges and a repair cannot; `native/android/app/capacitor.build.gradle`, which is generated and outside this packet.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was repaired

**(a) The failing leg accuses a fixture, not a product.** Run **32012897363** (`workflow_dispatch`, this branch): `quality`, `parity` and `eval` green, `StoreEngineTest` **11/11**, `DiaryEntryTest` **4 of 5**. The red is `a_full_disk_refuses_the_entry_and_keeps_the_text` — `expected:<refused-disk-full> but was:<listed>`. Logcat carries the whole sequence in under a second: the `INSERT INTO record` refusal at 09:03:44.919, its FTS block's refusal at .935, the journal probe's at 45.201, the arming's own line at 45.287 — and at **45.345 the app's own signal, `[signal] diary.write outcome=complete failure_class=none chars=26 write_ms=44`**, on the store the arming had just called full. (The leg's `refusal verdict: listed` at .716 is this fixture reporting; the write itself is the signal at .345.) The app said what was true: it was not full for the write it was asked to make.

**(b) The mechanism, and nothing in it is a defect in SQLite.** `PRAGMA max_page_count` bounds the pages of the FILE, not its occupancy. A statement refused for want of a page is aborted and leaves the file no larger than it found it, so the slack inside partially-filled leaves is still there afterwards — and a shorter row fits in slack a longer one could not use. "Full for a 200-character row" and "full for a 26-character row" are different statements, and the fixture was proving the first while the leg under it needed the second.

**(c) The evidence this fixture had already issued, and this repository had already cited as proof.** On run **31982061125** the same leg **passed**, with an arming line **byte-identical** to the failing run's: `state=full;rows=1;ceiling=43;refusal=full:StoreDiskFullError;journalRows=19;journalRefusal=full:StoreDiskFullError`. `docs/INVARIANTS.md:426` quotes that exact string as the evidence the arming was genuine in both shapes. Two runs, one string, opposite verdicts. **The green was a page layout rather than a property, and it was reported as evidence, in this repository's own record, for two packets.** That — not the red — is the finding of this packet.

**(d) Reproduced on the development host, and labelled as what it is.** On a local emulator on this host (AVD `theygrow-api34`, API 34 `google_apis` x86_64), the unmodified tree at `d97eef6` reds the same leg with the same message at `DiaryEntryTest.java:340`, with the arming line byte-identical to both runs above. This is a **local** run and a development instrument only: it shortens the edit loop from a dispatch to a minute, and it discharges nothing. The evidence that re-establishes an invariant stays the owner's `android-instrumented` dispatch, on a fresh image with a key minted for the run.

**(e) Off the device, the same question answers in half a second.** Desktop SQLite 3.45.1 against the real frozen DDL, ceiling clamped to `page_count`, a row per transaction as the app writes them: the 8000-character stage is refused **immediately** (0 rows), the 200-character stage writes **8** and is refused, and then the act's own 26 characters write **4 more** before that size is refused in turn — after which **10 of 10** further attempts at that size are refused, and a journal write still lands on top of all of it. Every number in this packet's off-device leg is that measurement, not an expectation carried into it.

### Decision

- **a. THE CLASS, and it is the decision this packet exists to record. An arming's refusal proves the store full for THE WRITE IT PERFORMED and for no other, so a leg that refusal licenses must perform a write of the same SHAPE **and** the same SIZE CLASS — and the arming must continue until a write of that kind is refused.** Shape and size are two coordinates of one rule, not two rules; either one wrong makes the arming a statement about a write nobody is testing. **And size has a DIRECTION, which is what tells the two halves of this fixture apart.** A refusal bounds every write no wider than the one refused and reaches nothing narrower, so an arming whose last refused write is *no larger* than the act is sound, and one whose last refused write is *larger* proves nothing. The record filler stopped 200 characters wide against a 26-character act — the unsound direction. The journal probe commits one entry and its detail where `markSkill` commits two of each, so it sits on the sound side, which is why the mark half needed no repair (`DIA-P3-INV-002`'s amendment says the same thing in the enforced file). The corollary is the part that keeps it honest: an arming that stops early has not proved less, it has proved something **else**, and a leg built on it can pass or fail for reasons that have nothing to do with its subject.

- **b. `fillToCeiling` grows a third record stage, and it is the last of the record stages rather than the last stage.** The sequence is `big(8000) → small(200) → act(the entry's own text) → journal`. The journal stage stays at the end because its probes are **undeletable** — the append-only triggers refuse `DELETE` on `journal_entry`, which is the property the whole schema rests on — so moving it earlier would permanently shift every record stage after it and change what the arming measures for good. The answer gains `actRows` and `actRefusal` beside the existing fields, and a `state=act-budget` guard in the shape `budget` and `journal-budget` already have: an act stage that exhausts its budget without meeting a refusal is a store that does not converge, which is a finding to diagnose and not a run to retry.

- **c. The leg asserts the refusal that licenses it, and the one that used to stands in the line unasserted.** `a_full_disk_refuses_the_entry_and_keeps_the_text` now asserts `actRefusal`; `refusal` — the small stage's — is still reported and is asserted by nobody. It is kept because it is the field that made 31982061125 and 32012897363 comparable at all, and comparing them is what turned a red leg into a finding about a green one.

- **d. THE PEDIGREE, THREE LEVELS DEEP, IN THE ORDER THEY WERE FOUND AND WITH WHAT EACH COST.**
  1. **`DIA-DL-005` armed one shape and treated it as the store.** Filler rows into `record`, and "full" pronounced on their refusal. It cost nothing at the time, because nothing had run yet.
  2. **`DIA-DL-006` found the SHAPE mismatch, and found it behind a RED dispatch.** The filler exhausted `record`'s pages while the mark leg's act wrote into `journal_entry` and `assertion`, whose own leaves had room; the mark landed on a store the arming had just called full, and run 31971968427 said so out loud. Cost: one dispatch, and a red that named itself.
  3. **This packet found the SIZE mismatch, and found it behind a GREEN.** The green was 31982061125, it was page layout rather than property, and — **this is the level worth saying plainly** — the repository reported it as evidence: `DIA-P3-INV-002` recorded the diary half as observed and quoted the arming string as the reason. The cost is not a dispatch. It is that a claim of observation stood in the record for two packets on a run that had not observed it, and only a later red on the identical string could distinguish the two.

  The three levels are one progression: arm by shape → arm by the RIGHT shape → arm by the right shape **at the act's size**. What moves each time is not the fixture's diligence but how much of the act it reproduces.

- **e. The check that would have caught this without a device now exists, and it lives beside the disk-full test it is about.** `app/tests/schema/test_store_corruption.py::test_a_full_store_still_takes_a_row_of_the_next_size_down` fills three sizes to refusal, then states the defect as a **positive fact** — after the 200-character refusal, rows of the act's size still land — then that the act's size converges over ten attempts, then that a journal write lands after the record-shaped refusal. It runs in `quality` on every push, against the real frozen DDL, and every count it measures goes into the assertion message so a future red is read rather than re-derived. It cannot see SQLCipher or the plugin, and it is not offered as a substitute for the device leg; it is the executor for the ARITHMETIC the device leg's arming depends on.

- **f. THE C3 NUMBERS WERE NEVER LOST, AND THE VOID FINDING IS RECORDED BECAUSE A VOID FINDING IS STILL A FINDING.** The three numbers `DIA-DL-008` predicted were all present in run 32012897363's own logcat: line **71913** carries both forms of `integrity-check` (`bare=did not raise | rank=1=raised: database disk image is malformed (code 267)`) and **71914** `fts rebuild: records=5 ms=2`, both under tag **`LSC`**; the search waits are at line **64368** under tag **`DIA`**, measured rather than expected: `repairing=22 ms, ordinary=21 ms`. The engine leg logs under one tag and the diary leg under another, so a reader grepping the diary's tag for the engine's numbers finds nothing and concludes nothing arrived. The budget that would have gone on recovering them goes to `docs/RUNBOOK.md` instead: step 2 now names the tag per number, and states the rule this cost a diagnostic round for want of — **a claim about a run is read from THAT run's artefact**, and the uncommitted `ci-artifacts/` directory holds whatever the last writing run left there, which is not necessarily the run being discussed.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Lower the small stage from 200 characters to something under the act's length.** Rejected: it replaces one guess about size with a smaller guess about size. A stage at the act's own size is not a tighter number, it is the right question — and it stays right when the act's text changes.
2. **Assert `actRows > 0` in the leg as well.** Rejected: zero is a legitimate outcome. If the small stage happens to exhaust the last usable slack, no act-sized row lands and the leg is still correctly armed. Asserting the count would red on a store that was arguably better armed than usual.
3. **Search for the boundary — halve the filler size until any write is refused.** Rejected: it arms for a size nothing writes. The only size that licenses this leg is the one the leg performs.
4. **Change the product to refuse a write when the engine is near its ceiling.** Rejected outright, and it is worth stating as a decision rather than an omission: the app was **right**. The store was not full for that entry, the entry was saved, and a product taught to refuse writes that would succeed would be a real defect introduced to make a fixture's mistake look like a truth.
5. **Mark the diary half unobserved and wait for the milestone PR.** Rejected: the fixture would keep issuing the same string, and the next green would be indistinguishable from the last one.
6. **Splice the act's text into the arming script by Java concatenation.** Rejected on the parse guard: a chain with a non-literal operand is one `reconstruct()` refuses, so the fixture's largest script would leave the checked set and enter `DECLARED_SKIPS` — `DIA-DL-008` (j) built that table to shrink, not to absorb. The text goes in through a `__ACT__` placeholder and `.replace(...)`, the pattern every other snippet in the suite already uses, and the chain stays checked.

### Supersedes

None. **Extends** `DIA-DL-006`, which named this class one coordinate short of it — shape without size — and whose `journalRefusal` is the half that was right all along. **Amends by reference, leaving the records byte-untouched:** `DIA-DL-008`, whose falsifiable prediction is closed by a pointer bullet at the foot of its Effects rather than rewritten. **Amends `docs/INVARIANTS.md`'s `DIA-P3-INV-002` in a neighbouring field** (form B, the `RSN-P2-INV-001` precedent): the diary half of (b) is withdrawn with the reason, the mark half is re-affirmed with the reason it was never in doubt, and the quoted arming line at `:426` is left **byte-untouched** — the point of the amendment is that the string is real and proves less than it was read as proving. **Corrects, in files this packet already edits:** `fillToCeiling`'s own comment, whose second paragraph said the filler ran "first in large pieces, then in small ones, so that what remains free is smaller than any row the acts under test write" — untrue as measured, and the sentence this packet is about. It now names the third stage and the rule underneath it.

### Effects

- **Changed:** `native/android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/theygrow/DiaryEntryTest.java` (the `AN_ENTRY` constant, the act-sized stage and its comment, the leg's precondition, both `fillToCeiling` call sites), `app/tests/schema/test_store_corruption.py` (the new leg and its constant), `app/tests/embedded-js-parse.spec.js` (`DECLARED_SKIPS` re-pinned to the two moved lines — **no entry added or removed**), and the docs spine (`docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/decision-log.md`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, `docs/execution-map.md`).
- **No product change of any kind.** No shipped module, no schema, no knob, no signal, no markup, no mount. **Net egress change: zero.** No baseline moved, and none could: nothing this packet touches renders.
- **One test constant is duplicated across a language boundary on purpose.** The act's sentence exists in `DiaryEntryTest.AN_ENTRY` and in `test_store_corruption.ACT_SIZED_BODY`; no shared source spans Java and Python, and what keeps them honest is that each names the other and both are cited from this entry. If they drift, the off-device leg measures a size the device leg does not write — which is this packet's own defect, one level out, and is worth watching for.
- **The local emulator is new to this branch's working environment and changes what a report can claim, but not what a doc can.** `DiaryEntryTest` now runs on this host in about a minute, so the bite was demonstrated locally both ways: red before the change with `refusal verdict: listed`, green after with `refusal verdict: refused-disk-full` and `actRows=1;actRefusal=full:StoreDiskFullError` in the same line. A local run is not CI — the debug key is stable across builds and the sandbox survives reinstalls, where CI mints a key per run and starts clean — so **`DIA-P3-INV-002`'s withdrawn half is re-established by the owner's dispatch and by nothing here.**
- **A falsifiable prediction, and what would refute it.** On the next `android-instrumented` dispatch, `DiaryEntryTest` should be **5/5**, and the diary leg's arming line should carry `actRefusal=full:StoreDiskFullError` with a small non-zero `actRows`. The falsifiers: **`state=act-budget`** means 400 act-sized writes were accepted after the 200-character refusal — convergence behaves differently under SQLCipher's page overhead than under desktop SQLite, and (e)'s ten-of-ten measurement does not transfer; **the leg still reporting `listed`** with `actRefusal` present would mean size class is not the mechanism and (b) is wrong about why the entry fitted; and **the mark leg red at its `journalRefusal` assertion** would mean the act stage left the store in a state where the journal loop exhausts its 200 probes without meeting a refusal — the answer would then be `state=journal-budget`, which carries no `journalRefusal` field at all and reds at `field()`. That would make (b)'s ordering argument incomplete rather than wrong.

## DIA-DL-010 — DIA-P5 `family-text-out-of-the-device-log`: the app's own code never wrote the family's words down, and the framework underneath it wrote all of them

- **Date.** 2026-08-18
- **Type.** Packet — DIA-P5, of **L2 "local diary"**, on branch `feat/l2-local-diary`. One packet, one report. **This entry is also the address `DIA-P4-CLOSE` resolves to.** That close-out — the pass that replaced the three **Not yet observed.** fields on run 32044006357 — is cited by `docs/INVARIANTS.md` and `docs/RUNBOOK.md` and never got a decision-log id, so those citations pointed at nothing. A close-out whose entire content is "the fields were replaced, here is the run" does not need an id of its own more than it needs a referent; it gets one here, in the entry that repairs the same two files.
- **Scope.** The privacy leak `DIA-P4-INV-002` denied: what the Capacitor bridge writes to logcat, on any build the owner installs. The diagnostic channel that closing it costs, and its replacement. An executor for the claim, on a device. The invariant's correction, in both directions. **Out:** the diary's product behaviour, untouched; the two `surfaces/diary.js` defects, which get debt entries and no fixes; the release-build path and key custody beyond the disclosure decision below; `webContentsDebuggingEnabled`, which is the same default on the same build through a different door and is debt 12; the nine debts `DIA-DL-008` hands on; everything L3+ gates. **No mount copy-forward, and it is checkable rather than asserted: zero bytes under `/m/v6/` change.**

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was repaired

Read from run **32044006357**'s own artefact, fetched for this packet rather than taken from the uncommitted `ci-artifacts/` directory — the rule `DIA-DL-009` (f) exists for.

- **The trace.** `Bridge.callPluginMethod` (`Bridge.java:826-837`) logs `", methodData: " + call.getData().toString()`: the whole argument object of every plugin call, for every plugin, bound values included. **707** such lines in that run.
- **What was in them, split by emitter, because the two are separate mechanisms and lumping their counts hides the smaller one.** Across BOTH emitters that run carried the child's name on **31** lines, the birthdate on **31**, one diary body on **13** and a second on **8**. Of those the **trace** contributed 5, 5, 8 and 1 respectively, plus the SQLCipher **passphrase** in cleartext on **1** — line 63944, `methodName: setEncryptionSecret, methodData: {"passphrase":"2c886a…791e"}`. The remainder — 26, 26, 5 and 7 — came from the JS-side echo below, which is the larger emitter for everything the app READS back.
- **The search side, and the measurement that corrects the handoff.** A grep for the word the parent typed («села») returns **zero**. The shipped prefix ceiling is 3 (`DIA-DL-008`), so what crosses is `("сел"* OR "сёл"*)` — on 4 lines — and `("сес"* OR "сёс"*)` for the miss on a 5th: **one traced expression per search, 5 of the 5 that run performed.** **A needle taken from the input box would have reported this leak as closed.** That is the same class as the `includes('INSERT INTO child')` over-match in AGENTS.md §11, one turn of the screw further in: not a needle that matched too much, a needle that could not match at all.
- **A second emitter, doubling the first from the other side.** With logging on, the injected bridge prints every plugin RESULT to the console — `native-bridge.js:328-331`, `c.dir(JSON.stringify(result.data))` — which is whole rows of diary text, and `BridgeWebChromeClient.onConsoleMessage` forwards that to logcat as well. Every family-carrying line in the whole 74,471-line dump sits under one of the two Capacitor tags — `Capacitor` and `Capacitor/Console`, at whatever priority — and **zero** under any other; the only Cyrillic line outside them is Android's own `ContactLocale` label list.
- **THE LEAK PREDATES L2, and the record has to say so.** The bridge has traced arguments since L1-P1. A child's NAME crosses on the launch that creates the child and on every read of the child list — measured: of the 707 trace lines, the 5 carrying the name are all `executeSet` batches beginning `INSERT INTO child`, and the other 26 appearances are the JS echo of `loadChildren` results. **Not on marks** — `appendMark` binds the child's id, never its name, and saying otherwise would misdirect whoever reads this next. What L2 added is diary text, search expressions, and `DIA-P4-INV-002` — a written claim that the term reaches exactly two places. This packet closes a pre-existing surface and corrects L2's own sentence. It is not "L2 broke privacy".

### Decision

- **a. THE CLASS, and it is why this entry exists rather than a one-line config change. An invariant whose enforcer runs in a different process from its subject is not a weak invariant, it is an invariant about something else.** `DIA-P4-INV-002`'s runtime legs watch a Playwright *page* console against an in-page fake bridge; the emitter is Java, below that bridge, in a process no browser test starts. No amount of care inside those legs would ever have reached it, and they were green throughout. This is `DIA-DL-009`'s class — a claim whose enforcer cannot see its own subject — met a second time and at a process boundary rather than a fixture one. **The general rule: when a claim names a place ("no log line"), the enforcer has to run where that place is.**
- **b. The gate is closed at the framework, with one key, because the leak is at the bridge's universal chokepoint.** `native/capacitor.config.json` sets `android.loggingBehavior` to `none`. `CapConfig.java:290-304` defaults it to `debug`, which resolves to `loggingEnabled = isDebug` — so the trace was live in **every debug build and silent in every release build** — the second half DERIVED from AGP's defaults and the absent manifest attribute rather than observed, because no release artefact exists (see Effects) — and the debug build is the one `docs/RUNBOOK.md` tells the owner to install on the phone that holds the family's real history. One key shuts both emitters, because `JSExport.getGlobalJS` hands the same flag to the WebView, so the JavaScript half stops echoing results as well.
- **c. AND IT COSTS THE DIAGNOSTIC CHANNEL OUTRIGHT, WHICH WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN FEARED.** All **41** `[signal]` lines in run 32044006357 carry tag `Capacitor/Console` — i.e. they ride the very `Logger` this packet switches off — and the dump holds **zero** `chromium: [INFO:CONSOLE` lines, so nothing else was logging them. Capacitor's own `%cresult %c` markers are produced by the JavaScript and dropped by `isValidMsg` while `onConsoleMessage` still returns `true`, and they appear zero times: on this WebView build a console message a client claims is handled produces no second, Logger-independent copy. **So the blunt switch alone would have left `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s own §4 verification steps with nothing to read.**
- **d. `SignalConsoleClient` carries the channel instead, and the allowlist is one literal prefix.** A `BridgeWebChromeClient` subclass, installed from `MainActivity.load()`, overriding `onConsoleMessage` alone: a message that begins with `[signal] ` goes to `android.util.Log` under tag `TheyGrowSignal`, and **every other line is dropped**. **The allowlist is stricter than the gate it replaces, and that is the point rather than a side effect.** A signal payload cannot hold a free string by construction (`core/signals.js` admits numbers, booleans, null and declared codes; `app/tests/signal-payload.spec.js` asserts that shape on every push), so what survives is §4-safe structurally. What is dropped includes this app's own `console.error` sites — `store/boot.js`, `surfaces/diary.js`, `surfaces/import.js` — which pass an engine message through, and an engine message is exactly the string that can embed statement text. The channel now **fails closed**: a line has to be a signal to be written, rather than merely not known to be unsafe.
- **e. It extends `BridgeWebChromeClient` rather than `WebChromeClient`, and it is installed in `load()` rather than anywhere more obvious. Both are traps rather than preferences.** The superclass's constructor registers two `ActivityResultLauncher`s, and `ActivityResultRegistry.register` throws once the activity is at or past `STARTED` — so this line in `onStart`, `onResume` or `onPostCreate` is **a crash on the family's first tap**, not a subtle regression. `load()` is called from `BridgeActivity.onCreate`, which is the window, and Capacitor registers those same launchers from inside that very call stack today, which is what says the moment is legal. Subclassing rather than replacing keeps the file chooser, media capture, the geolocation prompt, `onPermissionRequest`, the JS dialogs and fullscreen working against this instance's own launchers; a plain `WebChromeClient` would have broken every one of them silently, most visibly the file chooser the import path needs. **Nothing is missed in the gap:** `loadWebView()` ends with an asynchronous `loadUrl` and the UI thread is still inside `onCreate` at the swap, so no page script has run.
- **f. The forwarder emits in EVERY build, ungated.** Contract §4.7 scopes the signal channel by **payload safety**, not by build type: a channel carrying only counts, timings, booleans and declared codes is §4-safe wherever it runs. Gating on `FLAG_DEBUGGABLE` would put the release build's behaviour behind a branch no test executes, and would leave the owner's §4 verification step unavailable on the artefact the family actually installs (ADR-047). Raised in the plan as a fork tagged `[verify vs vault]`; **resolved by plan review, 2026-08-17**, on that reading of §4.7. The tag is off and this is the provenance.
- **g. THE EXECUTOR, AND ITS THREE CONTROLS, WHICH ARE THE WHOLE POINT.** `DeviceLogTest` boots the app, puts a name, a birthdate, a diary entry and a search expression across the real bridge through the shipped modules, reads this process's own log through `UiAutomation.executeShellCommand("logcat -d …--pid=")` — instrumentation runs **in** the app's process, which is what makes that filter the right one — and counts six needles. An absence assertion goes green for three different reasons and only one of them is the truth, so each of the other two is closed by an assertion of its own. **(1) The matcher arms itself in-run:** the same counter is first run over a synthetic line built in the shape run 32044006357 produced, carrying this suite's own needles, and every needle must be found in it. **(2) The capture proves itself:** a Cyrillic control marker written *before* the app launches must be found — one mechanism that bounds the window without `logcat -c` (which needs shell and would destroy the CI job's artefact for every other suite), proves the reader reaches this process, and proves Cyrillic survives the read, the failure that would zero every needle at once. **(3) The reader's scope proves itself:** a second unfiltered dump must carry a line from another process. **And the channel is asserted alive in the same window through the same reader** — a suite that only asserted an absence on a channel it had just silenced would be a test that can only go green. **The needle scan runs over the whole process rather than over this leg's window**, because the claim is about the process and a full run holds seven other suites' traffic in it — marks, imports, transfers, exports — that this leg never performs.
- **h. The primary needle is the trace channel itself, not any fixture string.** `methodData: ` must appear **zero** times. A per-string needle is hostage to the fixture, to the prefix arithmetic and to the escaping; the channel needle is hostage to none of them, and zero of it means the emitter is silent whatever the fixture says. The five family needles stay because a red should be legible to a human, and because `passphrase` is worth naming separately: `store/store.js` mints it only when `isSecretStored()` is false, so whether the needle is armed depends on the sandbox rather than on the test. **Measured rather than reasoned, and the reasoning was wrong first:** this entry originally said the needle was vacuous on a warm local device and live only on CI's fresh emulator. It is armed on both — every instrumented run on this host comes up without a stored secret and mints one, and the arm-check below caught it doing so.
- **i. AND THE NEEDLE CARRIES THE JSON ESCAPING, learned the same way everything else here was.** `JSObject.toString()` escapes the quotes, so the expression reaches logcat as `(\"под\"*)`. An unescaped needle was measured returning **zero against a log that was leaking**, during this packet, by the person writing the guard. It is in the file's comment because the next reader will reach for the unescaped form too.
- **j. THE PASSPHRASE DISCLOSURE — decided, not deferred, and recorded as an accepted deviation with a named end.** Owner gate, 2026-08-17, recorded as an annotation to ADR-046 in the vault: **the store is NOT re-keyed now.** Two triggers end that: **(a) immediately**, if this device's logs or a bugreport ever left the owner's hands; **(b) at L4 regardless**, where the store is opened for accounts anyway and the re-key happens as hygiene rather than as an emergency. **The bounds, recorded so a later reader can re-judge without re-deriving:** reading the line needs local access to the log buffer — `adb` with debugging authorised, or a shared bugreport; the buffer is volatile and has rotated many times; and the same debug build exposes strictly more through `chrome://inspect`, which is debt 12 and still open. This is a state with an address, not a property of the system.
- **l. THE GUARD THIS PACKET NEARLY SHIPPED WITHOUT, and it is the same class as the packet's own subject.** The static leg reads `native/capacitor.config.json` — the SOURCE. The value the runtime reads lives in `assets/capacitor.config.json`, which is **generated by `cap sync` and gitignored**. `Logger.shouldLog()` returns true when the config is null and `CapConfig` swallows a missing or malformed asset and carries on with defaults, so the whole gate **fails open**: an APK assembled where the sync was skipped or died after `tools/reset-sync-target.js` traces everything again, and both the source-reading guard and a behaviour-only device leg would have gone green on it. So `DeviceLogTest` gained a second leg that reads the knob **out of the APK's own assets**, the way `MountAddress` reads the shell — the artefact under test rather than the repository that hopes to describe it. **Armed by hand and retained:** with the key deleted from the generated asset, both legs red together — the declaration leg naming the missing key, the behaviour leg returning `child-name=1;birthdate=1;diary-body=1;search-expression=1;trace-channel=25;store-passphrase=1`. CI does sync (`ci.yml:288`, `:645`), so this is a fail-open default rather than a live defect; the leg is what makes that a checked statement instead of a hope.
- **k. `DIA-P4-INV-002` is amended in a neighbouring field and its Statement is left byte-untouched** (form B, the `RSN-P2-INV-001` precedent `DIA-DL-009` also used). The reason is that the Statement is **true again** after this packet, and was **true all along about the app's own code** — the amendment's job is to say which half was false, for how long, why the named enforcer could never have seen it, and what makes it true now. Rewriting the sentence would hide exactly the thing worth keeping: that a claim of this shape stood in an enforced-only file for a whole milestone. The same sentence is restated in `app/m/v6/surfaces/diary.js:196-200`; that comment is **left byte-untouched** on the shipped-comment precedent, and it too is true again — its address is here so it is citable.

### The debt this milestone hands on — items 10 to 12

Extends `DIA-DL-008`'s list of nine rather than restating it. Numbering continues from it.

10. **`renderList` awaits `loadRecords` with no `try/catch`** — `app/m/v6/surfaces/diary.js:122`, the await at `:155`. Its only in-file caller is `clearSearch` (`:188-191`), which is awaited from `:252`, `:306` and `:430`. A store refusal during a list render therefore rejects into whatever awaited it, and the surface has no handler of its own for it. Not a §4 breach and not fixed here; it is the mechanism debt 11 rides on.
11. **A save the store ACCEPTED is reported to the parent as «Запись НЕ сохранена», and that is a user-visible lie.** `app/m/v6/surfaces/diary.js:430` — `await clearSearch()` sits **inside** `saveEntry`'s try, after the write succeeded and after `diary.write outcome=complete` has already been emitted at `:416-421`. A rejection there runs the catch at `:432`, emits a **second** `diary.write` with `outcome=failed`, and shows `REFUSAL[…]` — the sentence that tells a parent their entry was not saved, about an entry that was. **This is ADR-015 inverted**: honest degradation exists so the app never claims more than happened, and here it claims *less*, which is the same defect pointing the other way and costs the parent their trust in the list rather than their text. It also puts two contradictory signals on the wire for one save. Named as a lie rather than as a control-flow smell because that is what a parent experiences. **Both debts are one failure mode with two addresses**, and either fix alone closes it: a `try/catch` in `renderList`, or moving the confirmation refresh out of the try.
12. **`webContentsDebuggingEnabled` defaults to on in a debuggable build** — `CapConfig.java:286` → `Bridge.java:618`, a separate `isDebug`-defaulted knob that `loggingBehavior` does not touch. Same default, same build, same phone, different sink: `chrome://inspect` over an authorised adb connection reaches the DOM, the JS heap and WebView storage directly. Named in the same vault annotation as **deliberately still open**. Kept out of this packet's code because it is a different sink from logcat and its own operability trade; **closes with one key beside `loggingBehavior`** — `"webContentsDebuggingEnabled": false` — whenever the owner decides the inspection is worth less than the exposure.
13. **`HistoryTransferPlugin.refuse(code, evidence)` takes a free string, and nothing structural stops family text reaching it** — `native/android/app/src/main/java/app/theygrow/HistoryTransferPlugin.java`, the `refuse` helper and its ~15 `android.util.Log` call sites under tag `TheyGrowTransfer`. That tag never passed through `com.getcapacitor.Logger`, so this packet's knob does nothing to it, and `DeviceLogTest` drives none of its paths. Today the evidence strings are scheme+host, key names, counts and class names, and two of them already echo externally supplied text verbatim (an undeclared query key, a non-numeric `bytes`) — bounded by review rather than by construction, which is precisely the difference `emitSignal` was built to remove. **Closes when** the plugin's diagnostics are constrained the way signal payloads are, or when an executor covers that tag.

### Alternatives considered

1. **The config key alone, without a replacement channel.** Rejected on the measurement in (c), and on a second ground that matters more: it would leave the executor able to assert only an absence on a channel it had just silenced — a test that can only go green. It also turns `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s store check **silently green on a broken store**, which is worse than a step that fails.
2. **Allowlist the app's wider bracket vocabulary** — `[store]`, `[diary]`, `[export]`, `[import]`, `[transfer]`, `[handoff]` — so no diagnostic is lost. Rejected: those lines pass `error?.message` through, and the engine's message is the string that embeds statement text. The information the `[store]` line carried survives as `store.open`'s `outcome` and `failure_class`, in closed-code form, and the engine's own words still reach logcat ungated through the plugin's `RetHandler` lines (13 in the local run: 10 `database or disk is full (code 13)` and 3 `cannot rollback - no transaction is active`).
3. **A code-level second gate** — `Logger.config = new CapConfig.Builder(this).setLoggingEnabled(false).create()` in `MainActivity`. Rejected: it creates a second, hidden source of truth for a knob whose declared home is a config file, and would make a future deliberate re-enable mysteriously ineffective. The regression it defends against — the key going missing — is caught per-push by the static leg and on dispatch by the device leg. Two lines if that judgement is ever revisited.
4. **Keep family text out of bridge arguments.** Structurally impossible, and worth recording as measured rather than assumed: the trace is at the bridge's universal chokepoint, every JS→native path funnels through `MessageHandler.postMessage` → `callPluginMethod`, and the SQLite plugin's whole surface takes `{statement, values}`. Inlining values into the SQL would keep them crossing as `statement`, add injection, and additionally reach `libsqlcipher.so`'s own ungated `", while compiling: "` path.
5. **Wait for an upstream fix.** Dead, and settled rather than guessed: `@capacitor/android@8.5.0` is both what is vendored and `latest`, and upstream `main` still carries `", methodData: "` at the same line of the same file.
6. **`adb shell setprop log.tag.Capacitor SILENT`.** Rejected as an enforcer: an app cannot set a system property for itself, the setting does not survive a reboot, and nothing in the APK, in CI or in any test can assert it holds on the family's handset — `AGENTS.md` §10 requires an enforcing artifact, and a manual per-device act is not one.
7. **Patch the vendored Capacitor with `patch-package`.** Rejected: `native/node_modules` is gitignored, there is no `patches/` directory and no `postinstall`, and CI runs `npm ci` before `cap sync` — a new build-step dependency for a result one JSON key already gets.
8. **Fix the two `surfaces/diary.js` defects while the packet is open.** Rejected as scope: neither is a §4 breach, both are product behaviour, and debt 11 in particular deserves its own executor rather than a fix smuggled into a privacy packet. They are named with addresses instead, which is the form that survives.
9. **Drive the diary SURFACE in the executor rather than the shipped store modules.** Rejected: the claim is about what the bridge does with an argument, every one of these calls is the same plugin call the surface makes, and driving the surface would have duplicated ~150 lines of another suite's helpers for no additional coverage of the subject. `DiaryEntryTest` continues to own the surface.

### Supersedes

None. **Extends** `DIA-DL-009`, whose class this is a second instance of — a claim whose enforcer cannot see its own subject, this time across a process boundary rather than a fixture one — and `DIA-DL-008`, whose debt list this continues at item 10. **Amends `docs/INVARIANTS.md`'s `DIA-P4-INV-002` in a neighbouring field** (form B), leaving its Statement and its **Enforced by** byte-untouched: what was true about this app's code stays, what was false about the framework underneath is named, and the log half moves to `DIA-P5-INV-001`. **Gives `DIA-P4-CLOSE` a referent** in `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (two citations) and `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (one). **Corrects, in files this packet already edits:** `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s two `adb logcat -s chromium` reads, false when written — those lines were carried under `Capacitor/Console`, and `-s chromium` matched two DNS warnings and no signal at all; `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s `[store]` check, which the allowlist would have made silently green; and `docs/RUNTIME-INVARIANTS.md`'s coverage note claiming no live child-PII data path exists yet, false since L1-P4 and false about the one contour that was leaking.

### Effects

- **Added:** `native/android/app/src/main/java/app/theygrow/SignalConsoleClient.java`; `native/android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/theygrow/DeviceLogTest.java`, in two legs — the behavioural scan and the declaration read; one invariant, `DIA-P5-INV-001`.
- **Changed:** `native/capacitor.config.json` (one key), `native/android/app/src/main/java/app/theygrow/MainActivity.java` (a `load()` override), `app/tests/native-shell.spec.js` (a fourth claim and its header), `app/tests/embedded-js-parse.spec.js` (`DECLARED_SKIPS` — **two entries added**, for the new suite's own plumbing; no entry removed or re-pinned; the guard's checked set grows from 103 snippets across 6 files to **106 across 7**, and `docs/execution-map.md`'s live figure is moved with it), and the docs spine.
- **No product change of any kind, and it is checkable rather than asserted: zero bytes under `app/m/` change.** No shipped module, no markup, no schema, no knob in `store/config.js`, no signal kind, no payload field, no mount, `CACHE_VERSION` unmoved at v16. **Net egress change: zero.** No baseline moved and none could — nothing this packet touches renders.
- **One new operability surface, and one lost.** Gained: logcat tag `TheyGrowSignal`, carrying `[signal]` lines and nothing else, in every build. Lost: the Capacitor diagnostic bulk the CI logcat artefact used to carry — 707 trace lines and 1,478 `Capacitor/Console` lines on run 32044006357, and 342 trace lines on the local pre-change run, which was `DiaryEntryTest` alone and therefore not comparable with the 35-test runs quoted elsewhere in this entry. Among what goes with them is `store/boot.js`'s engine message on a failed open. That loss is accepted and recorded rather than glossed: it is the reason the artefact exists (`ci.yml`'s own comment), and what replaces it is `store.open`'s closed-code `failure_class` plus the plugin's ungated `RetHandler` lines.
- **What the local emulator establishes, and what only the dispatch can.** The full instrumented suite ran **36/36, zero failures** on an API-34 image on this host — `DiaryEntryTest` 5/5, `StoreEngineTest` 11/11, `DeviceLogTest` 2/2, across all nine instrumented classes — and the whole run's 7,387-line device-wide logcat carries **0** occurrences of every needle, **42** `[signal]` lines all under `TheyGrowSignal`, and exactly **one** line bearing any Cyrillic at all: this suite's own control marker. The bite was demonstrated both ways: red before the change with `child-name=1;birthdate=1;diary-body=2;search-expression=1;trace-channel=25;store-passphrase=1`, green after. **A local run is not CI** — the debug key is stable here and the sandbox survives reinstalls, and the passphrase needle is only live on a first launch, which CI's fresh emulator is and this warm device is not — so `DIA-P5-INV-001` carries **Not yet observed.** and is discharged by the owner's dispatch and by nothing here.
- **And the release build's silence is DERIVED, not observed, and stays that way until a release artefact exists.** With `loggingBehavior: "none"` the release build is silent for the same reason the debug build now is; it was *already* silent for a second and independent reason, `FLAG_DEBUGGABLE` being clear — but that reason is read out of AGP 8.13.0's own defaults (`BuildType.init()` sets `debuggable` only for a type literally named `debug`) and the absence of the attribute in the source manifest. No release build tree exists on this host and no release APK has ever been produced, so nothing here observes it.
- **A falsifiable prediction, and what would refute it.** On the next `android-instrumented` dispatch, `DeviceLogTest` should be **2/2** and the suite **36/36**, with the leg logging `the diagnostic channel after the gate closed: signals=… storeOpen=1 taggedLines=…` under tag `LOGSCAN`. The falsifiers, each pointing at a different assumption: **the control marker not found** would mean `executeShellCommand` does not read this process's log on a fresh CI emulator, and the whole capture design needs re-opening; **`storeOpen=0`** would mean the chrome-client swap lands too late for the boot signal on a colder device, which is the one ordering claim in (e) argued from the UI thread's contract rather than measured; **`store-passphrase=1` with every other needle at zero** would mean the key crosses by a path the config key does not gate, which is the reverse of what the census found and would be a finding in its own right; and a red in `HistoryTransferTest` or `ExportTransferTest` would mean the inherited chrome-client behaviour does depend on the discarded instance after all, which no test here executes and the owner smoke has to catch.

- **Amended by reference, 2026-08-18 — the prediction above is CLOSED, and none of its four falsifiers fired. See `DIA-P5-INV-001`'s Observed field.** `android-instrumented` run **32074105863** (`workflow_dispatch`, this branch) returned `DeviceLogTest` **2/2** and the suite **36/36** as predicted, and the leg logged the line this prediction named, verbatim: `the diagnostic channel after the gate closed: signals=1 storeOpen=1 taggedLines=1` under tag `LOGSCAN`. Taking the falsifiers in order: the control marker **was** found (`log-scan control контроль-кодировки-225085437518`), so `executeShellCommand` reads this process's log on a fresh CI emulator; `storeOpen=1`, so the chrome-client swap lands early enough for the boot signal on a colder device than this branch's host; `store-passphrase` read **0** on a run whose `store.open` reports `freshly_created=true`, so the key was minted on that run and the trace did not carry it — the reverse of the third falsifier, and the strongest single result of the dispatch; and `HistoryTransferTest` **8/8** with `ExportTransferTest` **2/2**, so the inherited chrome-client behaviour does not depend on the instance the swap discards. **What the run added that the prediction did not model:** seven lines under `TheyGrowTransfer`, the first-party tag the knob does not gate — debt 13, carrying no family text on this run and still covered by no executor. Nothing else here is edited.
## FIU-DL-001 — L3-P1 `store-close-and-first-run`: the store had no way to close, so every launch paid for a scan the family never needed, and every unlock put the first-install screen back over their work

- **Date.** 2026-08-21
- **Type.** Packet — L3-P1, the opening packet of **L3 "first live-install UX"**, on branch `feat/l3-first-install-ux`. One packet, five commit checkpoints, one report.
- **Scope.** The store-lifecycle debt `DIA-DL-008` marked for a milestone's OPENING rather than for a list (debt 8), the launch/resume defect the owner reported from the first live install, and `DIA-DL-010` debt 12. The mount generation those first two force. **Out:** removing the transfer offer and making a fresh install self-sufficient (P2); the two `surfaces/diary.js` defects, debts 10 and 11 (P2); header cosmetics, the pre-install selling screen, the PWA install-prompt removal and the privacy-policy link (P3); diary text in the artefact (P4); `DIA-DL-008` debts 1 and 2, which stay inventoried at all five of their addresses and were deliberately not half-fixed; retiring `m/v1`–`m/v6`; everything L4+ gates.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was repaired

- **`closeStore()` had zero call sites.** Exhaustive grep over the shipped tree, the tests and the native layer: the function is defined at `store/store.js:237`, exported, and called from nowhere — not even re-exported through `store/boot.js`, the door every other store path goes through. `openStore()` clears `clean_shutdown` unconditionally on every open (`markOpen`, called at `store.js:220`), so the marker never returned to 1 and `integrityCheckPolicy: 'after-unclean-shutdown'` evaluated true at every launch. **The knob declared to avoid a full scan of the family's history at every start was buying that scan at every start.** The symptom is on the record in every dispatch this year: `previous_run_clean=false` in every `store.open` line.
- **The resume defect reproduces with no reload, no process death and no manifest fault, which is the finding.** `surfaces/import.js` registers a `visibilitychange` listener whose whole purpose is a return FROM the handoff page, and it called `offerImportIfPending()` unconditionally. That function's terminal branch does `el('importModal').classList.add('show')` when nothing is staged; `closeImportModal()` records no dismissal and `delivered` lives in module memory. On a phone `.modal-content` is `100vw/100dvh`, so what came back over the parent's work on **every** unlock was a full-screen transfer screen — the first screen after an install. The owner's words were "starts over on the same initial screen", and the screen is the one they meant.
- **The native shell was ruled OUT as a cause, and that mattered to the design.** No `bridge.reload()`, `loadUrl` or `recreate()` in any first-party file; `Bridge.onResume` only fans out to plugins; no splash-screen plugin; `configChanges` covers ten values including `density` and `uiMode`; `launchMode="singleTask"`; and on the native channel `sw-register.js` registers no service worker at all, so the web channel's guarded `controllerchange → location.reload()` cannot fire there. Two secondary mechanisms were found and are NOT this class: the onboarding modal re-opens on every real boot unless the checkbox was ticked, and nothing at all about the view is persisted, so a process death is a full restart. Both are cold-start, both are recorded as debt below.
- **`webContentsDebuggingEnabled` reaches the WebView from a second, independent resolution.** `CapConfig.java:286` resolves it from `FLAG_DEBUGGABLE` and `Bridge.java:618` hands the result to `WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled`. `DIA-P5`'s `loggingBehavior` knob does nothing to it.

### Decision

- **a. THE PARK IS DRIVEN BY `visibilitychange` GOING HIDDEN, AND THE CONDITION `DIA-DL-008` DEBT 8 SET IS MET BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY ARGUMENT.** That debt closes "when there is evidence on whether the Android WebView reliably fires `pagehide` before process death, and a disposition that does not depend on it if it does not". The disposition shipped does not depend on `pagehide` at all, and `pagehide` is deliberately not used **even as a belt**, so that no later reader mistakes it for load-bearing. The evidence is a real activity driven to `Lifecycle.State.CREATED` on an emulator: the page learned it was hidden, and the park completed in **51 ms** with the process alive throughout.
- **b. THE STORE IS REOPENED BY THE FIRST CALL THAT NEEDS IT, NOT BY THE RESUME, and the number is why.** Measured on the same run: a cold open that also created the schema cost **1940 ms**; the warm reopen cost **396 ms**. Reopening eagerly on every unlock would spend that on every screen unlock, including the many that touch no data, in a milestone whose whole subject is what the first live install feels like. Lazily, an unlock that touches nothing costs nothing and a parent who opens the diary pays one warm open.
- **c. THE GATE LIVES IN `store/bridge.js`, AND THE ENTRY POINT IS SEPARATE RATHER THAN FLAGGED.** It is in the bridge and not in `store/boot.js` because `export/readout.js` imports `query` from the bridge directly — a gate on the door would have left the export path, which reads the whole journal, ungated. And `openStore()`/`closeStore()` are MADE of bridge calls, so they cannot pass through the gate they operate. A module-level "a transition is running" flag does not solve that: JavaScript has no dynamic scoping, so such a flag exempts every call that happens to run while the transition awaits — including a read issued by a render, which would then reach a half-open store. The exemption has to be about WHO is calling, and the only way to say that in this language is a different function. Hence `lifecycleBridge`, an ungated twin of the same four shapes with the same dispatcher, the same allowlist and the same classifier.
- **d. AND IT COST `store/store.js` ONE IMPORT LINE, WHICH IS THE PROPERTY THAT MADE (c) CHEAP.** Every bridge call in that file is an open-path or close-path call — its only other exports, `mintId` and `derivedId`, touch no bridge — so the whole file switches entry point by destructuring `lifecycleBridge` under the plain names, and **not one statement of its body changes**. In particular the five `run` sites `DIA-DL-008` debt 1 inventories keep their `transaction = true` default: that debt is recorded at five addresses, and fixing one of them here would have made the inventory false for a gain that belongs to its own packet.
- **e. THE CLOSE ORDER IS RESERVE → DRAIN → CLOSE → FLAG, and each step is there for a failure that was reasoned to rather than met.** Reserving first means no new ordinary call can start. Draining (`whenBridgeIdle`) means the calls already in flight finish — and `executeSet`'s transaction path counts as ONE unit for its whole begin/execute/commit sequence, because between the BEGIN resolving and the next statement the count would otherwise touch zero and a park landing there would ask the wrapper to close a database still in a transaction, which it refuses with a message about the transaction rather than about the close. Raising the parked flag LAST means a close that throws leaves the flag down, which is the truthful state: the connection is still open and the app carries on exactly as before.
- **f. THE RESUME FIX IS ONE PARAMETER, AND IT KEEPS THE LISTENER'S ORIGINAL JOB.** `offerImportIfPending({ unsolicited })` — the boot call keeps the default and still offers the transfer, the resume call passes `false`. A parent returning from the handoff page with staged bytes still gets the import, and a refused handoff still reaches them; a parent who merely unlocked their phone gets their app back. **Removing the offer entirely, and making a fresh install self-sufficient, is P2** and is deliberately untouched here.
- **g. ONE NEW SIGNAL KIND AND NO NEW CLOSED CODE.** `store.close` carries `outcome`, `failure_class` and `close_ms`, `emittedNow: true`, emitted from `core/state.js` beside the open reporter. `outcome` reuses `complete` and `failed` from the shared list, because widening `SIGNAL_CODES` widens every kind at once. **A park with nothing to close emits nothing** — the web channel, a page hidden before the store opened, a second hide while already parked — so the count of these lines keeps meaning "closes that happened" and the web channel gains no line at all. It is its own kind rather than a field on `store.open` because the interesting failure is asymmetric: an open that fails is loud, and a close that fails is silent by design, with the cost landing on the parent at the next start.
- **h. NO NEW KNOB.** The trigger is an event, not a tunable. `integrityCheckPolicy` keeps its value and finally means what it says — and both comments that rested on the old truth were corrected in the same pass, in `core/signals.js` and `store/config.js`, statement-scoped, under the standing rule that no known-false statement survives an edit pass in a file the packet already has open.
- **i. DEBT 12 CLOSES WITH ONE KEY, AS `DIA-DL-010` SAID IT WOULD, AND WITH THREE LEGS BECAUSE ONE WOULD HAVE BEEN A FAIL-OPEN.** `"webContentsDebuggingEnabled": false`, explicitly rather than by absence — absence is exactly the state that produced the exposure. Static on every push (the source key), and two device legs: the running bridge's parsed config, and the APK's **own** generated asset, which is gitignored and minted by `cap sync`, so a build assembled where the sync was skipped would pass the source-reading guard and trace nothing about it. **What no leg executes is written into the invariant rather than left implied:** `android.webkit.WebView` has a static setter and no getter, so "chrome://inspect finds nothing" is asserted nowhere by anyone; what is checkable is the value that reaches the setter.
- **j. THE MOUNT BUMPS, AND IT IS THE FIRST BUMP OF L3.** `/m/v6/` → `/m/v7/`, `CACHE_VERSION` v16 → v17. Forced rather than chosen: `/m/v6/` has been published since the L2 merge, and `docs/RUNBOOK.md` **Module mount** item 1 says any byte change under a published version bumps. L2's edit-in-place pattern applied only while v6 was unpublished, and the RUNBOOK sentence recording that has been corrected in place, because it stopped describing the tree the moment L2 merged. The cost is a **seventh** generation shipped and served immutable, stated rather than absorbed. `app/transfer.html` needed repointing alongside `app/index.html` and `app/sw.js` — the ship-list guard caught it, which is what that guard is for.
- **k. THE SUPPLY-CHAIN SCAN WAS TAUGHT THE SECOND CALL SHAPE, RATHER THAN LEFT TO GO QUIET.** `store-supply-chain.spec.js` matched `callPlugin('…')` only. With the lifecycle shapes reaching the plugin through `dispatch('…')`, four shapes would have left its sight while the guard went on passing — the exact failure mode that file exists to prevent. It now matches both spellings, with the reason written where the change is.

### The debt this packet hands on — items 14 to 16

Extends `DIA-DL-008`'s list of nine and `DIA-DL-010`'s items 10-13 rather than restating them. Numbering continues.

14. **The onboarding modal re-opens on every real boot** unless the parent ticked "don't show again" — `surfaces/onboarding.js:27-32`; `closeOnboardingModal` persists nothing when the ✕ or the backdrop is used (`:14-25`). It is the same family as the defect this packet fixed and a **different class**: cold-start, not background/screen-lock, so it is not what the owner reported and not what this scope item names. **Closes when** the onboarding surface is next opened deliberately — what ✕ should mean is a UX decision, not a control-flow tidy-up, and it sits with P3's onboarding work.
15. **Nothing about the VIEW is persisted, so a process death is still a full restart.** There is no router, no `state.view`, no hash route and no scroll restoration anywhere in the mount; what survives is the selected child, the accordion state, the ZPD filter and the onboarding dismissal, through `core/storage.js`. Android freely kills a backgrounded app, and when it does the parent lands on the table with every modal closed. Deliberately not addressed: restoring an overlay the parent did not ask for is the same defect this packet just fixed, pointing the other way. **Closes when** there is a product decision about what "where I was" means — which surface, and whether a parent wants it back.
16. **"chrome://inspect finds nothing" has no machine detector, and cannot have one from inside this repository.** `WebView` exposes no getter for the flag. All three legs assert the value that reaches the setter. **Closes when** someone attaches a debugger by hand and records what they saw, or never, and the invariant's Scope says which.

### Alternatives considered

1. **A marker-only "park" — write `clean_shutdown = 1` and leave the connection open.** Cheaper still, and it closes the harm. Rejected: the packet's scope names `closeStore()` as the mechanism, the close also releases the file handle and lets SQLite checkpoint, and the reopen cost that made the alternative attractive was removed by making the reopen lazy instead (b).
2. **`@capacitor/app`'s `appStateChange`.** Rejected on the argument already in the tree at `surfaces/import.js`: adding a dependency to a shipped surface is a supply-chain act, and this one would still depend on the WebView being alive — buying nothing the DOM event does not already give.
3. **A native belt in `MainActivity.onStop()` driving the park through `bridge.eval`.** Planned as the branch to take if the measurement showed the DOM event did not arrive. It did arrive, so the belt is not shipped: a second trigger on the very event `DIA-DL-008` debt 8 is about would invite the next reader to believe it is load-bearing.
4. **A module-level flag to exempt lifecycle traffic from the gate.** Rejected as unsound, with the reason in (c) — it exempts by timing rather than by identity.
5. **Gating at `store/boot.js`, the door.** Rejected: `export/readout.js` reaches the bridge directly, so the one path that reads the whole journal would have been ungated.
6. **Nulling the store handle while parked.** Rejected: four shipped call sites read a null handle as "this device has no store" and take a different branch, so a backgrounded app would have looked, for a moment after coming back, like an app that never had one.
7. **Fixing `DIA-DL-008` debt 1 at `store.js:238` while that line was open.** Rejected — see (d). A debt inventoried at five addresses is not improved by silently becoming an inventory of four.
8. **Persisting UI/session state so a process death lands the parent where they were.** Rejected as scope and as design: see debt 15.
9. **Opening the app's own SQLCipher database from the instrumented test to read `clean_shutdown` directly.** Rejected: the passphrase lives in `EncryptedSharedPreferences` and asking for it would put the key somewhere new for the sake of an assertion (§4). The app already reports both facts on the `[signal]` channel, so what the test reads is what the app itself says happened — the same line the RUNBOOK smoke reads.

### Supersedes

None. **Closes** `DIA-DL-008` debt 8 and `DIA-DL-010` debt 12, both by their own stated conditions. **Extends** `DIA-DL-007` (the seam that drives its own transaction, whose in-flight accounting the drain reuses) and `DIA-DL-010` (whose debt list this continues at item 14). **Amends `docs/INVARIANTS.md`'s `DIA-P5-INV-001` in a neighbouring field** (form B), leaving its Statement and its **Enforced by** byte-untouched: one item in its Scope enumeration — `webContentsDebuggingEnabled`, listed as untouched — is now closed, and the rest of that sentence stands. **Corrects, in files this packet already edits:** `core/signals.js` and `store/config.js`, both of which asserted that `closeStore()` is never called; `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s L2 note that the mount was not bumped and `CACHE_VERSION` stays v16, and its promotion-smoke mount examples, which still named `/m/v6/`; and `docs/execution-map.md`'s live parse-guard figure of 106 snippets across 7 files.

### Effects

- **Added:** `app/m/v7/` (copy-forward generation); `app/tests/store-lifecycle.spec.js` (5 legs, `behavior`); `native/.../androidTest/.../StoreLifecycleTest.java` (1 leg) and `WebInspectionTest.java` (2 legs); three `the park gate` legs in `app/tests/store-seam.spec.js`; one leg in `StoreEngineTest`; a fifth claim in `app/tests/native-shell.spec.js`; two invariants, `FIU-P1-INV-001` and `FIU-P1-INV-002`.
- **Changed:** `native/capacitor.config.json` (one key); `app/index.html`, `app/transfer.html`, `app/sw.js` (the bump, `CACHE_VERSION` v16 → **v17**); under `app/m/v7/` — `app.js`, `core/signals.js`, `core/state.js`, `store/bridge.js`, `store/boot.js`, `store/config.js`, `store/store.js` (one import line), `surfaces/import.js`; `app/tests/support/page-bridge.js` (the close path, which that seam would otherwise throw on); `app/tests/store-supply-chain.spec.js` (the second call shape); `app/tests/embedded-js-parse.spec.js` (`DECLARED_SKIPS` — two entries for the new suite's plumbing, none removed or re-pinned; the checked set grows from 106 snippets across 7 files to **110 across 8**); `app/playwright.config.js` (one `testMatch`); `StoreEngineTest.java` (one javadoc mount address); and the docs spine.
- **One new signal kind** (`store.close`), **no new closed code**, **no new knob**, **no schema change**, **no migration**, **no new plugin method** (`close` and `closeConnection` were already on the allowlist), **no new npm dependency**, **no rekey**. **Net egress change: zero.**
- **Two DOM baselines moved, and BOTH causes are named because only one is this packet's.** `app/tests/__baselines__/dom-desktop/header.html` and `dom-mobile/header.html`, three lines each. Two lines per file are the mount comments this bump repointed. **The third is not ours:** `#apkBtn` loses `hidden=""` because commit `a8b2ec2` flipped `theygrow-apk-release` to `published` and did not re-bless the baselines, so they were already red on this branch before this packet touched anything. A baseline cannot be half-blessed, so the re-bless carries both; the diff was read line by line before it was written, and no visual PNG baseline was touched or run — those stay container-only and owner-run.
- **A falsifiable prediction, and the numbers it must return.** On the next `android-instrumented` dispatch, the suite should be **40 tests, 0 failures**, with `StoreLifecycleTest` **1/1**, `WebInspectionTest` **2/2** and `StoreEngineTest` **12/12**. Three numbers arrive with it and each is a range rather than a value, because the local run is one sample on one emulator: the park (**51 ms** and **66 ms** locally), the warm reopen (**396 ms**), and the cold open that also creates the schema (**1940 ms**). **The falsifiers:** if `store.close` does not appear on CI's emulator image after `moveToState(CREATED)`, the DOM event is not reliable there and alternative 3's native belt is owed; if the reopen figure is an order of magnitude larger on CI, the laziness in (b) is not enough and the reopen needs to move off the parent's first tap; and if any pre-existing suite reds, the gate has reached traffic it was not supposed to touch — `DeviceLogTest` is the one to read first, because it is the leg that would notice a new line on the device log.

## FIU-DL-002 — L3-P2 `fresh-install-self-sufficiency`: the first screen after an install offered to move a history the app could not see, and the diary lied to a parent about their own child's record

- **Date.** 2026-08-21
- **Type.** Packet — L3-P2, on branch `feat/l3-first-install-ux`. One packet, five commit checkpoints, one report.
- **Scope.** The in-app browser-transfer offer, removed outright by owner decision of 2026-08-21; a fresh install made able to reach a working profile by itself; the diary's no-profile refusal made to offer the act that resolves it; and `DIA-DL-010` debts 10 and 11. The exposure half of `DIA-DL-010` debt 13 rides along, because the tag it names is the one this packet's other half orphans. **Out:** retiring `app/transfer.html`, the envelope, `store/transfer.js`, `store/import-legacy.js` or `HistoryTransferPlugin` — the owner's open question; constraining `refuse(code, evidence)` to a closed vocabulary (the other half of debt 13); header cosmetics, the pre-install selling screen, the PWA install-prompt removal and the privacy-policy link (P3); what ✕ means for the onboarding modal, `FIU-DL-001` debt 14 (P3); diary text in the artefact (P4); `DIA-DL-008` debts 1-2; `FIU-DL-001` debts 15-16; re-blessing the 17 visual PNG baselines, which are container-only, owner-run and already red on `main`; retiring `m/v1`–`m/v6`; everything L4+ gates.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was repaired

- **The offer was the first screen after an install, and it was dead by construction on the channel it opened on.** `app.js:90` called `offerImportIfPending()` at the end of `init()`; with nothing staged its terminal branch (`surfaces/import.js:409-414`) ran `showHandoffOffer(true)` and `el('importModal').classList.add('show')` unconditionally. On a phone `.modal-content` is `100vw/100dvh`, so it IS a screen. What it offered could never work there: `readProfilesRaw()` reads the WebView's own `https://localhost` origin and the family's browser history is on the production origin, so that call had always returned null — `surfaces/import.js:147-160` says so in its own header. **Three off-device fixtures had to dismiss it before they could reach their own subject** (`diary-save.spec.js:77-82`, `diary-search.spec.js:64-66`, `store-lifecycle.spec.js:87-93`), and `HistoryTransferTest`'s class comment carries a paragraph explaining that the boot-time invitation is not a fault of the leg that trips over it. A surface that every neighbouring test has to get out of the way of is a surface the product is working around.
- **After removing it, the one remaining path to a profile had no executor anywhere, on any channel.** Measured rather than assumed: an exhaustive grep for `childName` / `createProfileForm` over `app/tests/` and `native/.../androidTest/` returns **nothing**. `#createProfileModal` is offered from the dropdown (`profile.js:72-76`) and from a tick with no child (`skill-completion.js:100-107`), and what happens after Создать was driven by no test. That was survivable while the transfer offer stood beside it; with the offer gone it is the path a fresh install takes.
- **THE DIARY'S DEAD END IS NOT WHERE THE HANDOFF PLACED IT, AND THE RECORD HAS TO SAY SO.** Opening the diary with no profile is **not** a state whose only exit is a force-close: `renderList` (`diary.js:142-153`) hides the compose button and reveals `#diaryNoChild`, and `#diaryCloseBtn` and `#diaryModalClose` both stay visible and both work. What is true is narrower and still worth fixing: the refusal named a **place** — «Профиль создаётся в меню вверху» — and offered no act, on the one surface where the app already knows exactly which act is missing and already opens that very modal from a neighbouring surface for the identical reason.
- **The real dead end was next to it, and it is debt 10.** `renderList` awaited `loadRecords` at `diary.js:155` with no `try/catch`. `openDiaryModal` adds `.show` at `:303` **before** that await and `list.replaceChildren()` has already run at `:129`, so a store refusal during a list render left the parent looking at **an open diary window with an empty list and not one word of explanation** — `empty.hidden = rows.length > 0` at `:159` is never reached either, so even «Записей пока нет» stayed hidden. A read failure rendered as *you have never written anything*, to a parent who had. Nothing was emitted, so the owner had no line to read either.
- **Debt 11 is the same rejection arriving from the other side, and it reproduces exactly as inventoried.** `await clearSearch()` at `:430` sat **inside** `saveEntry`'s try, after the write succeeded and after `diary.write outcome=complete` had gone out at `:416-421`. Executed on the pre-packet code during this packet: the surface shows «Запись НЕ сохранена. Ваш текст остался в поле — попробуйте нажать «Сохранить» ещё раз.» about an entry the transcript proves was written, and puts two contradictory `diary.write` lines on the wire for one save.
- **The plugin's own log tag was the one sink the DIA-P5 gate never reached.** `HistoryTransferPlugin` called `android.util.Log` directly at **14** sites under tag `TheyGrowTransfer` — 2 `Log.i`, 12 `Log.w`, `refuse(code, evidence)` among them — so `loggingBehavior: "none"` did nothing to it. That is why `DIA-P5-INV-001`'s Scope had to ENUMERATE the tag as untouched and why run 32074105863 measured seven of its lines standing in a capture whose whole subject was a closed gate.

### Decision

- **a. THE OFFER IS DELETED, NOT HIDDEN, AND THE MECHANISM UNDER IT IS KEPT.** Owner act, 2026-08-21. `surfaces/import.js` is gone, `#importModal` is gone from the shell, and `app.js` no longer imports either. `HistoryTransferPlugin`, the envelope, `store/transfer.js`, `store/import-legacy.js` and the handoff page all stay. **A hidden surface is a surface someone re-enables by accident**; a deleted one is a decision with a diff. The test that carries this asserts `#importModal` has a **count of 0** rather than that it is not visible, which is a claim only a deletion can satisfy.
- **b. AND THE RETAINED MECHANISM STAYS INSIDE THE WALKED GRAPH, WHICH IS WHY `store/boot.js`'S RE-EXPORT BLOCK IS NOW LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN CONVENIENT.** With no surface importing them, `store/transfer.js` and `store/import-legacy.js` are reachable only through that block. A module outside the graph is a module the storage-seam scan (`LSC-P1-INV-001`), the supply-chain scan and the ship-list guard never read — so dropping the re-exports would have silently removed four modules from every guard at once while deleting nothing. The comment at `boot.js:196-204` now says that, because the next reader will otherwise tidy it.
- **c. NOTHING IN THE APP CONSUMES THE STAGING PATH ANY MORE, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE INFERRED.** The plugin still receives the Intent, still refuses what it should refuse, and still stages what it accepts; no shipped page code drains it. `page-bridge.js`'s `TheyGrowTransfer` branch is removed with its consumer, and the seam fails closed, so a resurrected offer would throw by plugin name inside whatever leg woke it rather than passing unnoticed.
- **d. THE TWO SIGNAL KINDS THAT LOST THEIR EMITTER ARE FLIPPED TO `emittedNow: false`, NOT DELETED.** `history.handoff` and `history.import` stay declared because the mechanism stays; the flag stops claiming a producer that no longer exists. This is the reverse direction of the defined-not-emitted state `M4-P3-INV-003` was built around, and it is **enforced rather than documented**: `emitSignal` refuses a kind flagged false. `signal-payload.spec.js`'s anti-vacuity leg split in two to match — one half requires every emitted kind to be emittable, the other requires every declared-not-emitted kind to be refused **with a perfectly-formed payload**, so the refusal can only be coming from the flag.
- **e. THE APP ASKS FOR THE CHILD ITSELF, IN THE SLOT THE OFFER VACATED, AND UNDER THREE CONDITIONS.** `offerProfileIfNone()` (`surfaces/profile.js`) opens `#createProfileModal` when the backend is `journal` **and** there are no children. Native-only — a runtime branch, not a second build (PDR-034 §3); the web channel's first visit is not this packet's subject. Store-open-only by construction: a store that did not open lands on the `unavailable` backend, where `createProfile()` returns null, and offering a form certain to refuse is what ADR-015 forbids and what the diary already declines to do. **It re-opens on every launch until a child exists, deliberately** — the condition is ended permanently by the act itself, and in that state there is no work for it to interrupt, which is the difference from `FIU-DL-001` debt 14's onboarding, which recurs forever.
- **f. THE DIARY'S REFUSAL OFFERS THE ACT, AND THE BUTTON CLOSES THE DIARY BEFORE OPENING THE FORM. That ordering is forced, not stylistic.** All four `.modal` elements share `z-index: 100` (`app.css:221-251`), so at equal z the winner is DOM order, and `#createProfileModal` precedes `#diaryModal` in the markup: opened from inside the diary it would render **behind** a full-screen white panel, and the parent would have pressed a button that did nothing. It also keeps the shell's standing property that it never stacks modals, which `index.html` states beside `#diaryModal`. `openCreateProfileModal` is reused from `surfaces/profile.js`; the surface→surface import is the shape `skill-completion.js` already uses, and `profile.js` imports only `core/*`, so the graph stays a DAG.
- **g. BOTH DEBT 10 AND DEBT 11 ARE FIXED, THOUGH EITHER ALONE CLOSES THE PAIR, BECAUSE THEY CLOSE DIFFERENT HALVES.** The `try/catch` in `renderList` closes the silent-empty-diary render — the harm no fix to `saveEntry` touches. Lifting the confirmation refresh out of `saveEntry`'s try makes *nothing after the write can report a failure of the write* a property of the code's shape rather than a consequence of a catch two functions away. **Measured, not assumed:** with only the flag in place the false report is already gone, and with only the `try/catch` in place it is gone too — and with both reverted the leg reds with the parent-visible sentence in the failure message.
- **h. THE LIST REFUSAL IS ITS OWN SENTENCE AND ITS OWN SIGNAL KIND.** `LIST_REFUSAL` is built to `SEARCH_REFUSAL`'s discipline — the list was NOT read, the entries are where they were, here is what to do — because «Записей пока нет» is a statement about the DIARY and a refused read is a statement about US. `diary.list` (`outcome`, `failure_class`, `records`, `list_ms`) is a new kind rather than a reuse of `write.refused`: a list render is a read, and reporting it as a refused write would put a false statement on the one channel the RUNBOOK reads. It emits on **both** outcomes for the reason `store.open` does — a kind that only ever appears on failure cannot be used to prove the path ran.
- **i. AND THE FAILURE PATH IS ASSERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE A FALSE FAILURE REPORT CAN BE "FIXED" BY SILENCE.** Beside the leg requiring that a save the store accepted is never called a failure sits a leg requiring that a save the store REFUSED still says «Запись НЕ сохранена», still names the disk, still leaves the parent's text in the field, and still emits exactly one `diary.write` with `outcome=failed`. That second leg is not optional: without it the first one is satisfied by a surface that says nothing at all.
- **j. THE PLUGIN'S TAG MOVES INSIDE THE GATE; THE TAG STRING AND THE FREE-STRING PARAMETER BOTH STAY.** All 14 sites now call `com.getcapacitor.Logger.{info,warn}(TAG, message)`, which keeps the caller's tag and consults `shouldLog()` — false in **every** build under `loggingBehavior: "none"`. The tag string is kept so the plugin's diagnostics stay findable the day the gate is deliberately opened, and so the existing scans keep their referent. **What this does NOT do is written into the code beside it:** `refuse(code, evidence)` still takes a free `String` where `emitSignal` structurally cannot. The gate removes the SINK, not the SHAPE, so the exposure half of debt 13 closes and the structural half stays open and stays inventoried. After this packet exactly one first-party `android.util.Log` call site remains in the app — `SignalConsoleClient`, which is ungated **by decision** (`DIA-DL-010` (f)) — so the class is swept rather than sampled.
- **k. THE HANDOFF PAGE KEEPS ITS BUTTON AND LOSES ITS PROMISE (escalation E1, resolved by the owner, 2026-08-21: branch A).** Three sentences told the parent the app would finish the transfer — `app/transfer.html:123`, `handoff-page.js:215-216` and `:246-248`. The page still emits the link and still saves the file; nothing in the app picks either up, so those sentences are now false and the page would have been sending a parent to look for a screen that no longer exists. They are corrected and nothing else on that page changes: the button, the link, the file path and the module's bindings are byte-untouched, so re-enabling the consumer later is a surface change and nothing else. **Branch B — stop offering the action on the page too, on the `DIA-P2` precedent that removed the archive control from the web channel — was designed and NOT taken:** it is materially "retiring the page", which the owner reserved as a separate question.
- **l. THE DEVICE LEGS FOLLOW THE MECHANISM DOWN A LAYER RATHER THAN GOING OUT WITH THE SURFACE.** Four `HistoryTransferTest` legs drove `#importModal`. Insurance that nothing executes is a claim, so `a_deep_link_delivers_the_history`, `the_transfer_writes_nothing_to_web_storage` and `no_bridge_call_carries_the_payload` now call `pendingTransfer → drainTransfer → runImport` out of the **shipped** `store/boot.js`, in the app's own document, across the real bridge to the real plugin (`drainAndImport`, which reports what it DID, per `DIA-DL-003`'s rule, and carries the document token for the reason `assertImportedMarks` does). The fourth, `the_receiver_refuses_a_truncated_link`, loses its fallback-UI block outright: what it asserted — one line of explanation and a file button, ADR-048 §3 — is product behaviour that no longer exists, and the plugin half of that leg (refuses by code, stages nothing) stands untouched. **Two of those four were not predicted by the plan and were found by running the suite**, which is recorded here rather than smoothed over.
- **m.
