## FIU-DL-005 — L3-P5 `print-layer-notdef-repair`: the declared degradation substituted a glyph the embedded font does not have, so the print layer drew `.notdef` and stopped being PDF/A

- **Date.** 2026-08-22
- **Type.** Packet — L3-P5, a **repair** packet on branch `feat/l3-first-install-ux`, after P4. It carries its own decision id rather than a labelled block inside `FIU-DL-004`, because the rollup needs a citable address for it.
- **Scope.** The print layer's conformance, and the two gaps the failure exposed rather than caused: that the printed layer had no local executor for a conformance-relevant property of its own bytes, and that the CI step which does have one prints a verdict without evidence. Concretely: no glyph 0 from any text-showing operator; the artifact's own promise made true and held true by a drift guard; a per-push guard with an in-run arm-check; and the failing branch of the validate step made readable. **Out:** everything not required for those four — the reading form, the scope boundary P4 landed, the L4 contour, the `AGENTS.md` §5 gated items, and everything already deferred at `FIU-DL-002`/`003`/`004`. No other change to the workflow.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was repaired

Measured, not reasoned about: the fixture archive was built by the **shipped** builder under `node` and read back.

- **The dispatch.** Run **32530473473** on `f7ee031` (`workflow_dispatch`): `parity`, `quality` and `eval` green; `android-instrumented` **FAILED at step 7**, *Validate the print layer against PDF/A-2b*, **before the emulator started** — steps 9 to 13 skipped, and the red *Upload the debug APK* is a consequence of that, not a second defect. veraPDF: ISO 19005-2:2011 clause **6.2.11.8** testNumber 1, `failedChecks="1"` against `passedRules="143"` / `passedChecks="3098"` — *a PDF/A-2 compliant document shall not contain a reference to the .notdef glyph from any of the text showing operators … in any content stream* — at `root/document[0]/pages[8](20 0 obj PDPage)/contentStream[0](29 0 obj PDContentStream)/operators[9]/usedGlyphs[17]`, glyph id 0.
- **THE CAUSE, AND IT IS THE DEGRADATION ITSELF.** `export/pdf.js` declared `REPLACEMENT = 0xfffd` and `toGlyphs` substituted an uncovered codepoint with `font.glyph(REPLACEMENT)`. **PT Sans does not cover U+FFFD.** Measured through the shipped `ttf.js` against the shipped `PTSans-Regular.ttf`: `glyph(0xFFFD) → 0`, and of the 717 BMP codepoints the font covers, U+FFFD, U+25A1, U+2588 and U+FFFF are all absent. So the branch written to avoid drawing `.notdef` drew `.notdef`. Reproduced locally on the fixture archive: **exactly one glyph-0 reference, at index 17 of one `Tj` run** — the position veraPDF names.
- **A second symptom of the same cause, in the same file.** `toUnicodeCMap` carried `if (used.has(font.glyph(REPLACEMENT))) pairs.push(…)`, which with `glyph(0xFFFD) === 0` wrote a `beginbfchar` entry **for glyph 0**: `<0000> <FFFD>` in the shipped CMap. A mapping for the one glyph the file was forbidden to reference.
- **The class arrived with P4's fixture, and P4's own prediction named it.** The previous dispatch on this branch (**32488397717**, tip `0b8fc14`) had `android-instrumented` green; `seed_family`'s `r-edge` row then seeded 🙂 (U+1F642), which is the first codepoint any export ever handed to that branch. `FIU-DL-004`'s falsifiable prediction reads "veraPDF still green on a print layer that now carries … an uncovered codepoint". It was the uncovered codepoint that broke it.
- **AND THE SUITE WAS GREEN THE WHOLE TIME.** `pytest app/tests/export` was **50 passed** on `f7ee031`, on a tree whose print layer is not PDF/A. That is the defect behind the defect: the printed layer had no local executor for a conformance-relevant property of its own bytes, so the only executor was an owner dispatch, and the class could only surface as a red job at PR time.
- **The red job printed a verdict and no evidence.** Step 7 printed `failedRules=1 failedChecks=1` and stopped. The clause, the object and the reason came out of the `pdfa-validation` artifact by hand, afterwards, by someone who knew the artifact existed. **And `--format text` was no help either**, which is worth recording because it is the obvious place to look: that file is **49 bytes** and reads `FAIL /home/runner/work/_temp/pdfa/archive.pdf 2b`. The evidence was not one `tee` away.

### The decisions

- **(a) The substitution mark is `◊` U+25CA LOZENGE, and its coverage was MEASURED rather than assumed.** That is the whole lesson of the defect: the previous mark was chosen because it is the character that *means* "replacement", and nobody asked whether the font had it. `◊` maps to glyph **606**, with a real two-contour outline in `glyf` and an advance of **505**/1000 em. It was chosen over the other covered candidates because a hollow geometric shape is the nearest thing this font has to the empty box a reader already reads as "nothing could be drawn here"; because it is neither a letter nor punctuation, so it cannot be misread as a word or a sentence boundary in Russian prose; and because it is vanishingly rare in what a parent types.
- **(b) Exactly one glyph, never a marker like `[?]`.** Derived from the code rather than preferred: `pdf.js` emits one glyph per input codepoint and `text.js` bounds a line by **code points**, and that one-to-one relation is what makes `FIU-P4-INV-002` true of the printed page. A multi-glyph substitution would push a printed line past `textLineWidth` and red the width sweep — one of the three legs this packet was required to keep green.
- **(c) The `/ToUnicode` map sends the substitute glyph to U+25CA, not back to U+FFFD.** Mapping it back would have kept P4's sentence literally true for *extracted* text and left `pdf_text.py` untouched. Rejected on two grounds. Identity-H maps per glyph id, not per occurrence, so a `◊` **a parent typed** would extract as U+FFFD — a lie about their character, in the layer that must not lie. And the printed page a person actually reads would still show a mark the declaration did not name, which is the half of the promise that matters most to someone holding a printout. One character, one meaning, in the ink and in the copy-paste.
- **(d) The glyph-0 `beginbfchar` special case is deleted, not repointed.** With the fix, glyph 0 is never in `used`, so the branch is unreachable; and `◊` needs no special case because it is inside the range the CMap builder already scans. Verified on a built artifact: the only `<0000>` left in the file is the codespace range. Repointing it would have left a mapping for `.notdef` in a file that had just removed the reason for one.
- **(e) NO fail-closed throw when the configured substitute is itself uncovered.** The obvious hardening — `renderPdf` raises when `glyph(SUBSTITUTE) === 0` — was considered and **rejected**: it adds a branch this packet cannot execute without shipping a second font, and the property it would guard is already executed **on every push** by `FIU-P5-INV-001` over a real artifact built by the shipped writer from a fixture that seeds an uncovered codepoint. An executed guard beats an unexecuted throw. Recorded here so the choice is checkable rather than merely absent.
- **(f) The mark becomes a KNOB on the export config surface (ADR-013 / contract §4.7), not a literal in the writer.** `EXPORT_CONFIG.pdfSubstituteCodepoint`, with `changed_in` provenance that carries the **constraint** rather than only the value: it must be a codepoint the embedded font covers, and U+FFFD is written down there as the recorded counter-example. That placement is what lets `test_pdf_structure.py` read the knob and require `declaration.json` to name it — the artifact quotes this value to a family, so the two must not be free to drift.
- **(g) Format version stays 2 and `declared_in` stays `FIU-DL-004`.** `formatVersion`'s own rule — directory shape, field set, or the scope of a dataset's rows — is not triggered by a value inside an already-declared field. v2 is unmerged, so what merges **is** v2's public meaning; minting v3 for a promise no reader has ever seen would spend a version number on a correction.
- **(h) The guard lives in the export suite, reads the bytes, and has FOUR anti-vacuity legs.** It slices every stream object by its own declared `/Length` — so the embedded font program cannot confuse a boundary — keeps the streams whose payload starts a text object, and parses `Tj`, `TJ`, `'` and `"`, of which this writer emits only the first: a scanner that knows one spelling goes blind the day an edit uses another. `glyph_runs` **raises** when a text-operator token in a stream produced no parsed run, which is the fail-closed direction. And the substituted glyph must actually appear, so deleting the uncovered codepoint from the fixture reds the guard instead of quietly emptying it. Armed in its own run by a second test that builds `<00030000> Tj` in-run, rather than by mutating shipped code and trusting a human to put it back.
- **(i) The CI touch is ONE invocation placed before an UNCHANGED verdict block.** `scripts/verapdf_failures.py` prints nothing on a compliant report and **always exits 0** — it is evidence, not a verdict — so it can be invoked unconditionally while leaving the step's pass/fail semantics exactly where they were. The diff is **17 insertions, 0 deletions**. The alternative, capturing the heredoc's exit status in the shell and calling the printer inside an `if`, would have made the failing branch literal at the price of restructuring the step's exit plumbing, which is a larger risk to the semantics than the thing it makes literal.
- **(j) The printer is a repo script, and the verdict parser stays inline.** `scripts/verify_release_signature.py` with `app/tests/release/test_verify_release_signature.py` is this repository's established shape for "CI logic that can be executed locally", and it is the only shape in which the extractor is testable at all. Keeping the **verdict** in its heredoc also keeps `export-contour.spec.js`'s `isCompliant` scan pointed where it belongs — that scan exists because a gate that could only ever go red once shipped for two packets.
- **(k) The fixture is the observed report, whole, with its provenance inside it.** 2 124 bytes, sha256 `7392e416…`, downloaded from run 32530473473's `pdfa-validation` artifact with `gh run download`; committed with an XML comment inserted after the declaration and **nothing else changed** — nothing trimmed, nothing reflowed, nothing reconstructed. The header names what may be pinned (the form, and this report's own clause) and lists what may not, by name: the runner path, both duration stamps, `item size`, and every `releaseDetails` version and buildDate. The validator version has a gate of its own and a second copy here would be a second thing to bump and a first to forget.
- **(l) Two false sentences elsewhere were corrected, because this packet is what made them false.** `docs/RUNBOOK.md` step 6 of the export walkthrough told the owner a reader would see `�` (U+FFFD) — the sentence they read to a parent — and `LSC-P3-INV-005` said the same thing twice. Statement-level fixes, in place, with the amendment marked. `AGENTS.md` carries no such sentence; checked rather than assumed.

### The debt this packet hands on — items 26 and 27

Continues `FIU-DL-004`'s list, which ended at 25. Numbering continues.

26. **The extractor's shape is proven against ONE report, carrying ONE rule with ONE failed check.** That is the only failing veraPDF report this repository has ever seen. Its behaviour on several failing rules, on several failed checks per rule, and on a rule element carrying no check at all is executed — but on **synthesised** input, so what those tests prove is the extractor's logic and not that veraPDF emits those shapes. The same split, and the same wording, as `app/tests/release/harness.py` states about itself.
27. **Nothing has LOOKED at the substituted page.** Every assertion in this packet reads glyph ids or text decoded through the file's own CMap. That `◊` renders as a lozenge in a real PDF viewer, and that a parent meeting one can find the sentence in `declaration.json` that explains it, is unobserved. The nearest evidence available is the owner's on-device smoke in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, which opens the artifact.

### Alternatives considered and rejected

1. **Substitute `?` U+003F.** Covered, and rejected: indistinguishable from a question mark a parent typed, in a layer whose whole job is to be honest about what it could not print.
2. **Substitute `¤` U+00A4.** Covered, defensible, and rejected as the weaker of two rare marks: `◊`'s hollow form carries the "nothing could be drawn here" reading on its own.
3. **Drop the character instead of substituting.** Rejected: a silent drop is the failure ADR-015 exists to forbid, and it would make the printed page disagree with the text files by an amount nobody can see.
4. **Fail the export when the font lacks a character.** Rejected: it costs a parent their whole archive over one emoji, and the artifact already has a truthful way to say what happened.
5. **Subset the font, or ship a second one covering more.** Rejected: out of scope by declaration (no new font, no new asset), and it does not close the class — any font has a coverage edge, and the edge is what has to degrade correctly.
6. **Keep U+FFFD and map the substitute glyph back to it in `ToUnicode`.** See decision (c).
7. **Add the throw and leave the guard out.** See decision (e). The inverse — both — was also rejected, as an unexecuted branch bought at the price of a second thing to keep true.
8. **Mint format version 3.** See decision (g).
9. **Move the whole verdict parser out of the workflow into the script.** Rejected: it is a larger CI change than the one permitted, and it would move the `isCompliant` history — and the static scan that watches it — out of the file where a reader of the workflow meets them.
10. **Reconstruct the failing report from the handoff's quotation instead of downloading it.** Rejected while the artifact was still available: a reconstructed fixture proves the extractor reads what we *believe* veraPDF writes. It was kept as the fallback and was not needed.

**Falsifies** `FIU-DL-004`'s prediction, at the clause that prediction named; the outcome is attached to it there. **Amends** `LSC-P3-INV-005`'s statement of the declared degradation, declared at `LSC-DL-003`, and the `print_layer.authority_ru` sentence in the unmerged format v2. **Extends** `FIU-DL-004`, whose debt list this continues at item 26. **Closes** nothing, and opens no invariant but its own.

### Effects

- **Changed, product:** `app/m/v7/export/config.js` (one new knob with its constraint), `export/pdf.js` (the substitution resolves through the knob; the glyph-0 `beginbfchar` case deleted; the DECLARED DEGRADATION block rewritten to state what actually happens and what it cost), `export/declaration.json` (`print_layer.authority_ru`).
- **Changed, tests:** `app/tests/export/pdf_text.py` (`content_streams` and `glyph_runs` added; the comment claiming the reader's fallback is the writer's mark corrected), `test_pdf_structure.py` (the guard, its arm-check, and the declaration drift guard replacing a `U+FFFD` literal), `test_artifact_selfdescribing.py` (the FIU-P4 degradation leg reads the mark out of the artifact's own declaration), `app/tests/export-contour.spec.js` (two static legs on the workflow).
- **Added:** `scripts/verapdf_failures.py`; `app/tests/export/test_verapdf_failure_report.py`; `app/tests/export/fixtures/verapdf-mrr-32530473473.xml` — the first veraPDF bytes in this repository, and the second recorded-output fixture after `app/tests/release/fixtures/`.
- **Changed, CI:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — 17 insertions, 0 deletions, all inside the validate step and all before its verdict block. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` — the new script added to the mypy list; `additional_dependencies` unchanged for the third packet running, the script being standard library only.
- **Changed, docs:** `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (`FIU-P5-INV-001`; two amended sentences in `LSC-P3-INV-005`), `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (one sentence), `docs/execution-map.md`, and this entry.
- **One new knob**, on the surface that already owns the print layer's knobs, with `changed_in` provenance. **No new signal kind, no `emittedNow` flip, no new closed code, no new payload field** — nothing here emits telemetry, and the only new reader of anything is a test. **No schema change, no mount bump** (`/m/v7/` is unpublished and edited in place, `CACHE_VERSION` stays v17), **no format-version bump**, **no new font, no new asset, no new npm dependency**.
- **No baseline moved, and none could have:** this packet changes no markup, no CSS and no surface. The 17 PNGs re-blessed at `f7ee031` stand.
- **A falsifiable prediction, and the numbers it must return.** On the next `android-instrumented` dispatch: step 7 **green**, veraPDF reporting `failedRules=0` with `passedRules` back at **144**, and the job reaching the emulator — so `ExportTransferTest` **3/3** and the rest of `FIU-DL-004`'s prediction gets its first chance to be checked. If step 7 fails again, it now prints the clause, the test number, the description and the first context before it does. Locally, all measured on 2026-08-22: `pytest app/tests/export` **58 passed** (50 before), the four Python suites together **350 passed** (`api` 93 with 88 designed skips, `schema` 140, `export` 58, `release` 59), the five non-visual parity projects **1380 passed** (`contract` 1224 — up 2, both of them this packet's static legs on the workflow — `behavior` 93, `dom-desktop` 14, `dom-mobile` 17, `native` 38, minus the 6 the suite skips by design), the instrumented suite **42 tests, 0 failures, 99.5 s** with `ExportTransferTest` **3/3** — which is `FIU-DL-004`'s number, observed on a local emulator and therefore still owed on CI — and the built artifact carrying **0** glyph-0 references where it carried **1**.

## PPR-DL-001 — PPR-P1 `privacy-policy-page`: the address the app was already told to link now has a document behind it, and nothing announces it yet

- **Date.** 2026-08-22
- **Type.** Packet — PPR-P1, the first rung of the milestone «Privacy policy and first L3 release», on branch `feat/privacy-policy-and-consent` (from `main` @ `cccff4b`). New id namespace: no `PPR-` entry existed before this one.
- **Scope.** **In:** the policy document published as a static HTML page at the fixed apex address `/privacy`; the nginx routing that makes that address serve the document rather than the app shell; the `COPY` line that ships it; the guards for all three; the service-worker repair the second page re-arms; the narrowing of one static invariant leg the document's own wording forces. **Out, by the ladder:** the analytics-consent banner and the «Cookie» footer link, the transfer retirement and the platform-aware download control (all P2, all inside a new `/m/v8/` generation); the declaration flip and the milestone docs tail — `execution-map`, `INVARIANTS`, `RUNBOOK` (P3); every deploy, promotion, release and tag (owner-run).

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. `/privacy` was already a live address that answered 200 with the wrong thing.** `app/nginx.conf` had one catch-all, `location /` with `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html`, so the address `CHANNEL_CONFIG.policyUrl` has named since `FIU-DL-003` served **the app shell** — a skills table under the word «конфиденциальность», with no 404 and no error anywhere to notice it by. This is the failure `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Privacy policy step 5 describes as "a promise about a family's data with nothing behind it", and it was reachable the whole time the link was withheld.
- **b. The second real page re-arms a defect this project has already paid for once.** `app/sw.js` serves navigations network-first and mirrors every successful response into the cache keyed `'/'`, the app shell's offline copy, unless the pathname is named in `NON_SHELL_PAGES`. That list exists because of `DIA-DL-005` (m), where `/transfer.html` was the first page to break the premise. `/privacy` is the second, and it arrives with **two** spellings — the route and the file — because the fetch handler compares `url.pathname`.
- **c. The list's own comment claimed a guard that did not exist.** It said the correspondence with `app/Dockerfile`'s COPY list was asserted by `app/tests/delivery-contract.spec.js`. Nothing asserted it. The omission that sentence was written to prevent is precisely the one this packet had to find by reading the fetch handler.
- **d. The document quotes its own address, and one invariant leg forbade exactly that.** `app/tests/export-contour.spec.js` (`FIU-P3-INV-002`, static half) asserts the literal `https://theygrow.app/privacy` appears in no shipped `.js` or `.html` outside the knob surface. The policy states its own address twice — §1 «Полный текст размещён на сайте по адресу …» and §10 «Действующая редакция всегда размещена по адресу …» — so shipping the document turns that guard red on arrival, and the wording is the owner's and final (PDR-035).
- **e. The hygiene hooks edit owner-authored documents, measured on the first run over this one.** `trailing-whitespace` stripped the two-space Markdown **hard line breaks** from the document's header block, which turns «Продукт / Версия / Дата вступления в силу» from three lines into one run-on paragraph in every renderer. Not foreseen in the plan; found by running the gate.
- **f. The `gitleaks` hook cannot see an unstaged file.** Its entry is `gitleaks protect --verbose --redact --staged` with `pass_filenames: false`, so a green **Detect hardcoded secrets** over new working-tree files is vacuous. The document carries the owner's real name and e-mail by design, so "the hook passed" was not admissible evidence and the scan was run directly instead.

### The decisions

- **a. A COMMITTED, HAND-CHECKED HTML FILE, NOT A BUILD STEP AND NOT A RENDERER.** The web path is buildless by contract and the parity suite serves files from disk. A client-side renderer was refused outright rather than weighed: it needs a script on the one page whose whole value is that it runs none. The cost of hand conversion is drift between `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md` and `app/privacy.html`, and it is bought rather than promised — `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` pairs every heading at its own level, requires the effective date **twice** in the page (the header block and the change-history row), and fails on an unresolved `{{…}}` slot in either file.
- **b. AN EXACT-MATCH LOCATION, PLUS THE TRAILING-SLASH TWIN IN THE SAME MOTION.** `location = /privacy { try_files /privacy.html =404; }` is what removes the shell fallback in both directions — a present file is the document, a missing one is a 404, never the shell. `location = /privacy/ { return 301 /privacy; }` was not in the scope item as written, and is the same defect one character away: `/privacy/` matches no exact location, falls into `location /`, finds no such directory and is answered with the shell. Cache class is the shell's (`max-age=3600, must-revalidate`) and never `immutable`: a new redaction ships at the SAME address, because this document is versioned by its own text and its effective date rather than by its URL — unlike `/kb-v{N}.json` or the module mount.
- **c. THE SERVICE-WORKER REPAIR LANDS HERE, WITH THE GUARD THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT (escalation E1, owner branch (a)).** `NON_SHELL_PAGES` gains `'/privacy'` **and** `'/privacy.html'`; the executing regression leg lives in `app/tests/privacy-surface.spec.js` and was measured by removing the entry, which reds it with `Expected: "shell" / Received: "poisoned"`. The precedent decided the timing: `DIA-DL-005` (m) repaired this same defect in the packet that made it reachable rather than filing it. The comment's false claim is made TRUE rather than deleted — `delivery-contract.spec.js` now asserts the correspondence in both directions, and understands both kinds of entry a navigable page can have: a shipped `.html`, and an extension-less route an exact-match location resolves to one with `try_files`.
- **d. THE INVARIANT LEG IS NARROWED BY EXACTLY ONE FILE, AND THE NARROWING IS PAID FOR (escalation E2, owner branch (a)).** `/privacy.html` is excluded from the "address appears elsewhere" scan, because the document AT the address is not a second place the app is told where to point. What the exclusion gives up is taken back by something stricter on that one file: it may **quote** the address and may never **link** it — no `href` in it may name the address, and the page in fact carries no `<a>` at all. "Declared once" now means one declaration site and one link target, which is the meaning the guard already carried for frozen mount generations. **Two obligations are handed to P3 rather than taken here**, because `docs/INVARIANTS.md` belongs to that packet's docs tail: (i) `FIU-P3-INV-002`'s sentence "its address exists exactly once in the shipped tree" needs one clause — exactly once **as a declaration**, and linked from nowhere but the intro window; (ii) **`PPR-P1-INV-001` is reserved**, and it will state: *the policy address serves the policy document and nothing else — no script, no third-party request, no service-worker registration, and no overwrite of the app shell's offline copy* — enforced by `app/tests/privacy-surface.spec.js` and `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js`, landed in PPR-P1.
- **e. THE TITLE DROPS «Часть А. », AND THAT IS AN ORCHESTRATOR-AUTHORIZED EDIT, NOT AN AGENT'S.** The plan kept the source heading verbatim and tagged it `[verify vs vault]` on the rule that the text is final. The orchestrator resolved it in the other direction: the prefix is an artefact of the owner's larger working document, not part of the policy, so the page `<title>` and `<h1>` — and line 1 of the source document, so the fidelity leg compares equal strings — read exactly «Политика конфиденциальности TheyGrow». **No other word of the document changed**, and the string appears nowhere else in the repo.
- **f. THE EFFECTIVE DATE IS `22.08.2026`, IN BOTH FILES, AND P3 MUST RE-CHECK IT.** Resolved on the day of execution, in the source document and in the page, in both places each states it. **P3 re-checks this literal immediately before flipping the declaration and updates both files if publication slips to a later day** — a policy whose stated effective date precedes the day it became readable is a document that was never in force when it said it was.
- **g. THE DOCUMENT LINKS TO NOTHING.** Every URL in the source is set in backticks; every URL in the page is a `<code>`, including the four third-party policies. Faithful to the source's own presentation, and it turns "this page offers no navigation" into one checkable property instead of a promise — which is also what keeps (d)'s narrowing narrow. Live links to Google, Cloudflare, GitHub and the Israeli supervisory authority are a later editorial pass, since they change the form the owner authored.
- **h. `/privacy.html` STAYS REACHABLE UNDER ITS OWN NAME, AND NO `rel="canonical"` IS ADDED.** Blocking it would need a third location whose only job is to 404 a file that exists. The declared, Play-facing address is `/privacy`; the twin serves the same bytes at the same cache class, and it is named in `NON_SHELL_PAGES` for that reason. A canonical link was rejected on (d): it would be an `href` naming the address.
- **i. THE APK GAINS THE PAGE, DELIBERATELY.** `native/tools/stage-webdir.js` assembles the Capacitor web root from this same COPY list and `LSC-P1-INV-002` asserts byte-identity in both directions, so a stager exception would be a deliberate channel divergence — exactly what that invariant exists to prevent. The cost is one unreferenced HTML document inside the APK; the native shell links the policy at its https address, from the intro window, once the declaration says published.
- **j. THE HYGIENE HOOKS ARE TOLD TO LEAVE TWO PATHS ALONE — an unplanned scope extension, recorded as one.** `docs/privacy-policy-v*` is excluded from `trailing-whitespace` and `end-of-file-fixer` because it is authored elsewhere and copied in verbatim, and its trailing spaces are Markdown semantics (finding (e)); the prefix is version-agnostic on the `m/` precedent, so a later redaction inherits the exclusion instead of losing its line breaks on the day it lands. `app/privacy.html` joins the app/ list on the standing rule that the harness does not churn live-deploy files. The alternative — accept the stripped file — was rejected: it silently damages the owner's document, and it would do so again on every future redaction.
- **k. THE ONE CLAIM NO TEST HERE CAN CARRY IS HANDED ON AS A SMOKE LINE, VERBATIM.** Nothing in this repository runs the real nginx image; the parity suite drives `app/tests/server.js`, a hand-written mirror, and what pairs it to production is the drift guard. **P3 adds to `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Promotion + rollback step 3:** `curl -sI "$TAGGED_URL/privacy"` must be `200`, `content-type: text/html`, `cache-control: public, max-age=3600, must-revalidate` and **not** `immutable`; `curl -s "$TAGGED_URL/privacy" | grep -c '<script'` must be `0`; `curl -s "$TAGGED_URL/privacy" | grep -q 'mainTable'` must find nothing; `curl -sI "$TAGGED_URL/privacy/"` must be `301` to `/privacy`. Only after that does § Privacy policy step 2 — the declaration flip — become available. **No exposure window is opened by deferring it:** nothing deploys before merge (ADR-020) and P3 lands on this branch first.

### Alternatives considered and rejected

- **Render the Markdown in the browser.** One `<script>` and one fetch on a page whose subject is that it collects nothing. Rejected without weighing.
- **Add the page to `SHIPPED_HTML` in the delivery contract.** That list drives a guard requiring everything an HTML file references to be **precached in `OFFLINE_URLS`** — the opposite of what this page must be. It got its own guard instead, which asserts the page references nothing at all: a strictly stronger property, and one that cannot be satisfied by adding entries to a precache list.
- **Precache the document.** `cache.addAll` is atomic and the offline set is the app's boot set. The policy is read online, usually before anything is installed; precaching it would spend an installed client's budget on bytes it never needs, and would put a second navigable HTML document in the worker's cache — the neighbourhood the poisoning defect lives in.
- **Defer the service-worker repair to P2** (E1 branch (b)). Defensible: the page is unlinked and nothing deploys before merge, so no client can reach it yet. Rejected because the defect would then ship on the same branch as its trigger and depend on a later packet remembering, and because the correspondence guard would have had to travel with it.
- **Keep the invariant leg as written** (E2 branch (b)). Only reachable by editing the document so it stops stating where it lives, which the packet forbids and which would make §1 and §10 read wrong.
- **A `location = /privacy.html { return 404; }` to suppress the twin.** A third location whose only purpose is to 404 a file the image ships, plus an entry in the drift guard's exempt list, to solve a duplicate that costs nothing.

### Effects

- **Added:** `app/privacy.html` (the document, 17 headings, no script, no link, inline style); `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md` enters the repository (it was untracked); two `location` blocks in `app/nginx.conf` and their mirror in `app/tests/server.js`; one `COPY` line; two entries in `NON_SHELL_PAGES`; `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` (35 static legs) and `app/tests/privacy-surface.spec.js` (6 runtime legs); three live-response legs and the `NON_SHELL_PAGES` correspondence guard in `app/tests/delivery-contract.spec.js`; one narrowing and one stricter leg in `app/tests/export-contour.spec.js`; two `testMatch` registrations; two paths in the hygiene hooks' exclude regexes; and this entry.
- **The declaration did NOT move.** `<meta name="theygrow-privacy-policy" content="none">` is untouched, no `href` anywhere names `/privacy`, and both facts are now asserted rather than merely true — a later packet that flips half the order reds. The flip is an owner act with its own RUNBOOK step.
- **Operability: none** (ADR-013 / contract §4.7). No new knob and no new signal. `CHANNEL_CONFIG.policyUrl` is read by the guards, parsed out of the knob source and never re-typed; `app/m/v7/channel/config.js` is not edited. **Net egress change: zero, and the page's own is zero** — it fetches nothing, and no GA4 event was added or removed.
- **No mount bump, no `CACHE_VERSION` bump.** `/m/v7/` is untouched, `OFFLINE_URLS` is unchanged, so no installed client's precache set moves; the worker changes by two array entries and a comment, which reaches clients on their next update the way any `sw.js` change does.
- **No baseline moved, and none could have:** this packet changes no shell markup, no CSS and no rendered surface. The 17 PNGs re-blessed at `f7ee031` stand, and the visual projects ran green in the container.
- **Two things the owner should know.** `app/transfer.html` is shipped but is **not** in the hygiene hooks' exclude list, so the header's claim that "every shipped app/ file is excluded" is still one file short — P2 retires that page, which closes the gap by deletion; it is named here so the choice is deliberate either way. And the **gitleaks hook cannot vouch for new files** (finding (f)): the owner's e-mail was cleared by a direct `gitleaks detect --no-git` over both documents, **no leaks found**, not by the green hook line.
- **A falsifiable prediction, and the numbers it must return.** On the next CI run of this branch: `parity` **green at 1455 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed** in the pinned container, and `quality` green with `pre-commit run --all-files` reporting no file modified — in particular the policy document coming out of the run byte-identical, its two hard line breaks intact, which is the whole point of decision (j) and the one thing that would silently regress. Per project, all measured locally on 2026-08-22: `contract` **1273** (1224 before — the 49 added are 35 in `privacy-page.spec.js`, 13 in `delivery-contract.spec.js` (three live responses, the new mirror pairing and nine correspondence legs) and one in `native-shell.spec.js`, which generates a byte-identity leg per shipped file and so grew by itself), `behavior` **99** (93 before — six runtime legs), `dom-desktop` **14**, `dom-mobile` **17**, `native` **38** and the two visual projects **20**, unchanged. If instead `parity` reds on `mount-reference`, the cause is a mount-shaped token in a new test file rather than anything about the page — it happened once during this packet and was fixed by asserting the absence of `/m/` rather than of a versionless mount token.

## PPR-DL-002 — PPR-P2 `consent-transfer-platform`: `/m/v8/` asks before it measures, retires a mechanism nobody calls, and stops offering a package the visitor cannot install

- **Date.** 2026-08-23
- **Type.** Packet — PPR-P2, the second rung of the milestone «Privacy policy and first L3 release», on branch `feat/privacy-policy-and-consent` (from `main` @ `cccff4b`, after `PPR-DL-001` @ `8dc41fc`).
- **Scope.** **In:** the copy-forward mount bump `/m/v7/` → `/m/v8/` with `CACHE_VERSION` v17 → v18; the web channel's analytics-consent gate — nothing fetched from `googletagmanager.com` and no GA4 configuration before an explicit yes, a banner offering two actions of equal weight, and withdrawal through a «Cookie» control in the footer; the retirement of the browser-to-native history transfer in both languages and on both sides of the ship list; and the platform-aware download offer (debt 21). **Out, by the ladder:** the declaration flip `theygrow-privacy-policy` `none` → `published`, and the milestone docs tail — `execution-map`, `INVARIANTS`, `RUNBOOK` (P3); every deploy, promotion, release and tag (owner-run); retiring `/m/v1/`–`/m/v7/` (owner-level); any new GA4 event or dimension, and analytics on the native channel.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. The web channel fetched the tag before anyone was asked, on every load.** `app/index.html:90-95` created the loader element in the head for every non-native visitor and `:114-117` ran `gtag('js')` / `gtag('config')` while the document was still parsing. The events could have been stopped without stopping that, and it would have changed nothing that matters: the request itself carries the visitor's address, which is the argument `L1-P4` used for the native channel and the same one that applies here.
- **b. The policy already promises the mechanism, in words that are the owner's and final.** `app/privacy.html:203` (= `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md:96`): «Аналитика работает только после вашего явного согласия на cookie. До согласия теги Google Analytics не загружаются. Настройка использует **базовый режим согласия**. В баннере отказ доступен одним действием наравне с согласием. Отозвать согласие можно в любое время по ссылке «Cookie» в подвале сайта». Every clause of that names an implementation choice, and «базовый режим» rules one out by name — see decision (b).
- **c. The transfer had no product caller and could not gain one.** `store/boot.js` re-exported six names and nothing in the shipped tree called any of them; `surfaces/import.js` went with the offer at L3-P2 (`FIU-DL-002`). What remained executed was its own tests — `FIU-DL-002` debt 18 said so and left the call to the owner, who made it on 2026-08-22.
- **d. The download offer was blind to the platform.** `shouldOfferApk(releaseState, native)` branched on the delivery channel and on the declaration, and on nothing else, so an iPhone or a desktop visitor was offered an Android package and then read four paragraphs about it. There was **no user-agent or platform read anywhere in this repository** before this packet — `grep -rn userAgent` over the whole tree returned nothing.
- **e. The `[hidden]` cascade defect was armed and waiting on the exact element this packet had to hide.** `a.modal-button { display: inline-block }` outranks the browser's `[hidden] { display: none }`, so `#installDownloadLink` marked `hidden` would have stayed on screen. The stylesheet already names this class of defect twice, at `.header-action[hidden]` and `.header-help[hidden]`; this is its fourth instance and the first where it bit in the same packet that created it.
- **f. Two guards were about to be measured on the wrong subject, and only one of them was foreseen.** `export-contour.spec.js` scanned the **whole shell** for an id matching `/consent|accept/` under a message about the policy link (foreseen; escalation E1). `signal-payload.spec.js` checked **every shipped generation's** emitters against the **running** generation's taxonomy (not foreseen) — which held only while the taxonomy could grow and never shrink, and went red on `/m/v4/surfaces/import.js` for a declaration that was correct when those bytes were published.

### The decisions

- **a. THE SHELL DEFINES HOW ANALYTICS STARTS; THE MOUNT DECIDES WHETHER.** `window.theygrowAnalytics.{enable,disable}` is defined in the head and called from nowhere in it. The only caller is `/m/v8/surfaces/consent.js`, and only when the visitor's stored answer is exactly `CONSENT_CONFIG.stateGranted`. The analytics vocabulary — the measurement id, the loader URL, `GA_DEBUG`, `trackEvent` — stays where it has always been, in the shell: moving it into a generation whose bytes are never rewritten would buy nothing and would put a third-party address in an immutable file. What moved is the decision. The seam between the two is **one declared name**, `CONSENT_CONFIG.shellBridge`, so a static leg can pair the mount's caller with the shell's definition and neither can be renamed alone. Cost, stated: analytics now initialises after module boot rather than at head-parse time. The loader is `async`, the page view still fires, and nothing depends on the ordering.
- **b. BASIC CONSENT MODE, AND DELIBERATELY NO `gtag('consent', 'default', …)`.** Advanced mode loads the tag first and asks it to behave; the policy says «До согласия теги Google Analytics не загружаются», and shipping advanced mode would make the owner's own sentence false. `consent-gate.spec.js` reds if such a call appears.
- **c. THREE STATES, TWO TOKENS, AND FAIL-CLOSED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** `granted` and `denied` are declared in `consent/config.js` with `changed_in` provenance; **undecided is the absence of the key or anything else at all**. Anything unrecognised loads nothing *and* asks again — asking is not a harm and loading is. A third explicit `undecided` token was rejected: two ways to spell one state.
- **d. THE KEY LIVES IN `core/storage.js` AND THE TOKENS IN `consent/config.js`, AND THAT SPLIT IS THE POINT.** Key identity is `core/storage.js`'s declared job for all seven keys this app touches; a second declaration beside the knob would be a second thing to drift. The state vocabulary is what the gate reasons about and belongs with the other knobs. `consent-gate.spec.js` pairs the two files, and reds if either names the other's half. The key is `analytics_consent`, flat, on the `onboarding_dismissed` precedent: it is neither profile data nor a filter, it is showcase state about the visitor's own choice, and it never touches the journal or its schema.
- **e. THE BANNER HAS NO ✕, AND THAT IS HOW «CLOSING IT IS NOT CONSENT» BECOMES A PROPERTY RATHER THAN A PROMISE.** Its only exits are the two answers, both `<button>`, both carrying one class, so «Включить» and «Не включать» cannot drift apart in size, weight, colour, padding or decoration — there is nowhere for them to drift to. The executing leg reads both back through `getComputedStyle` and requires nine properties equal, and requires the banner to hold exactly two controls. Price: an undecided visitor sees the question until they answer it. Bought back by the footer control, which makes the answer cost one click to change.
- **f. THE «Cookie» CONTROL IS THE THIRD CHILD OF `footer.control-footer`, NOT A SECOND `<footer>`.** Two body-level footers are two `contentinfo` landmarks. It gets `flex: 0 0 auto` and its own class — the positional `footer button:nth-child(3)` form is **not** reinstated, for the reason the stylesheet's own comment gives at the place that rule was deleted (`LSC-DL-003` (s)). Measured in the pinned container: `footer-height.spec.js` green, no control clipped, the footer height unchanged across filter states.
- **g. THE BANNER SITS UNDER EVERY MODAL, AND THAT WAS FOUND BY A RUN RATHER THAN FORESEEN.** `.app-banner` declares `z-index: 9999`, which suits a banner arriving alone on an event. This one arrives on the **first visit**, which is exactly when the intro window is open, and on a phone that window fills the screen: the banner covered its «Закрыть» button and `behavior.spec.js`'s *the intro closes for good* failed with `cookieDeclineBtn … intercepts pointer events`. **A parent on a first install could not have closed the intro.** `.cookie-banner` is `z-index: 90` — above the page and the footer, below all four modal layers — which also puts the two questions in the right order for free: what the app is, then whether to count visits.
- **h. WITHDRAWAL IS HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT DO.** A `<script>` the document has already fetched cannot be un-fetched and removing the element would not unload it. What can be done is what Google documents: `disable()` sets `ga-disable-<id>` and clears the shell's own flag, so nothing further is sent; on the next load the gate never creates the tag at all. Both halves are executed — the switch is read back after the click, and the reloaded page is checked for the tag element.
- **i. THE PLATFORM BRANCH IS INSIDE THE WINDOW, NOT ON THE HEADER CONTROL.** `#apkBtn` still opens the pre-install window wherever the declaration says published: that window explains what the app is and where the family's data lives, which is worth reading on any device. What is withheld is the **offer** — `#installDownloadLink` — and the same slot then carries the sentence the orchestrator fixed. Rejected: hiding `#apkBtn` on non-Android, which would leave a desktop visitor never learning the app exists, the opposite of what the sentence asks them to do. **Residual, named rather than smoothed over:** the header control is still labelled «Скачать APK» to a desktop visitor, one click before the honest sentence. Relabelling it is owner copy and would move `header.html` and `header.png` across three projects; it is left for the owner to decide.
- **j. PLATFORM DETECTION IS A HEURISTIC WITH A DECLARED FAILURE DIRECTION.** One exported pure function, `isAndroidPlatform(nav)` in `surfaces/channel.js`, matching `CHANNEL_CONFIG.androidPlatformToken` — the declared `navigator.userAgentData.platform` first, the user-agent string only where nothing is declared. **Everything unreadable returns false, and false is the sentence, never the offer:** no navigator, no string, an empty string, a non-string, an empty declared platform. Executed on both sources and on seven unreadable shapes. The declaration gate stays in front: an undeclared release is offered to nobody, whatever they are holding.
- **k. THE TRANSFER IS RETIRED IN ONE MOTION, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS OF THE SHIP LIST, BECAUSE HALF OF IT WOULD BE WORSE THAN NONE.** `cache.addAll` is atomic: a stale `OFFLINE_URLS` entry does not degrade quietly, it fails the install outright and leaves the client on the old worker. So the page, its four modules, the app-side drain, the `COPY` line, five precache entries, the `NON_SHELL_PAGES` entry, four delivery hints, the Android plugin, its `theygrow://transfer` intent-filter, its registration and the `Intent` plumbing in `MainActivity` all go together. `/m/v8/` is the first generation **smaller** than the one before it: a copy-forward that omits a file deletes it without touching a frozen byte, and `/m/v4/`–`/m/v7/` keep their copies untouched.
- **l. WHICH TRANSFER TESTS DIED AND WHICH SURVIVED UNDER A NEW SUBJECT.** Died with the mechanism, because in each the transfer **is** the subject: `handoff-source`, `handoff-transfer`, `transfer-drain-unit`, `transfer-format`, `transfer-seam`. Adapting one to assert the hole would be a test passing for a reason other than the one it names. Survived, retargeted: `storage-seam` and `delivery-contract` (one shell fewer in `SHIPPED_HTML`; the seam and the drift contract unchanged), `store-unit` (`COPIED_DIRS`), `embedded-js-parse` (two line-pinned allowances, which reded on the shift and were re-read rather than trusted), `signal-payload`. **The one property `handoff-transfer.spec.js` carried that was not about the transfer** — a separately-shipped page must not overwrite the app shell's offline copy — already had a second executor built to its shape at PPR-P1, and survives in `privacy-surface.spec.js`, which is now the only executor of it for any page.
- **m. `import-legacy.spec.js`'s RETARGETED LEG CHANGED SUBJECT, AND THE NAME CHANGED WITH IT.** At L3-P2 it moved off `surfaces/import.js` onto the handoff page — the legacy source's one remaining **read-only** consumer. There is no third address of that kind: the only consumer left is `core/repo-local.js`, which is the web channel's repository and writes the profiles key by design. Repointing the old assertion there would have asserted a property that file deliberately does not have. So the property is restated on the surviving fact: the legacy source has **exactly one** consumer in the shipped mount, it is the declared repository, and a second one appearing anywhere in the mount reds — checked across the whole mount rather than in one file, with the door and the repository both asserted non-empty first.
- **n. `history.handoff` IS REMOVED FROM THE TAXONOMY, AND SO ARE THE CODES ONLY IT DECLARED.** A kind flagged `emittedNow: false` is a kind waiting for its emitter; the handoff's cannot come back, because the mechanism it described does not exist. A declaration for a thing that does not exist is a false statement in a machine-readable surface. Gone with it: the `transport` and `refusal` field lists (declared for that kind and no other), and the three `outcome` codes `handed_off` / `refused` / `no_transfer` — which matters because that list is **shared**, so an unused code in it stays admissible in every kind that survives. `history.import` **stays** declared-not-emitted: importing a history is not the transfer, and the legacy path is still shipped.
- **o. `signal-payload.spec.js` NOW READS EACH MODULE AGAINST ITS OWN GENERATION'S TAXONOMY — the same lesson `export-contour.spec.js` learned at DIA-P2.** A frozen generation is not a second declaration and not a vote on the current one. The scan still walks every shipped `.js`, which is right; what changed is which taxonomy each is measured against. Without this, no signal kind could ever be removed, because a frozen generation would veto it forever.
- **p. `DeviceLogTest`'s TRANSFER LEG IS DELETED, NOT RETARGETED — escalation E2, branch (b), and the reason is measured.** Branch (a) was to move the property onto `ExportSinkPlugin`'s own tag. That plugin declares `@CapacitorPlugin(name = "TheyGrowExport")` and **no log tag at all**: it contains zero `android.util.Log` calls and zero `Logger` calls. Asserting the absence of lines under a tag nothing ever writes is a vacuous leg, which is the defect class this repository names, so the honest move is the narrowing rather than the appearance of coverage. **P3 must amend `DIA-P5-INV-001`'s Scope**: it loses the only leg that exercised a **plugin-argument** path, and keeps the bridge-config leg, the APK's-own-asset leg and the family-text probes. `SignalConsoleClient`'s `TheyGrowSignal` is the opposite property — a tag that must write — and cannot stand in.
- **q. THE `/consent|accept/` SCAN IS NARROWED TO THE INTRO WINDOW, AND PAID FOR — escalation E1, branch (a).** Its subject was and remains **policy acceptance**; its scan was shell-wide, which was free while the shell held no consent control of any kind. It happens that this packet's controls are named after their surface (`#cookieBanner`, `#cookieEnableBtn`, `#cookieDeclineBtn`, `#cookieSettingsBtn`) and would have slipped through the old pattern untouched — which is exactly why it is narrowed rather than left standing: a guard that passes because nobody happened to use a word has stopped meaning what its message says, and the next packet naming a control `#analyticsConsentBtn` would have gone red for a reason unrelated to the policy. The narrowing is bought back with something **stricter** on the narrowed scope: the policy link is gated on the **declaration alone** — `shouldOfferPolicy` takes one argument, and `surfaces/channel.js` may not read `readAnalyticsConsent`, `localStorage` or `consentState`. Nothing stored, consented to or remembered stands between a parent and the document. The old wide scan never asserted that.
- **r. `app/privacy.html` GETS NO FOOTER AND NO «Cookie» CONTROL, AND §5 STAYS TRUE.** The document carries no `<script>` and no `<a>` by design (`PPR-DL-001` (d), (g)), both asserted. A control there would need a script; a link there would need an `<a>`; either falsifies a property this milestone has already paid for. §5 says the withdrawal lives «в подвале сайта» — in the **site's** footer — and after this packet it does. **The residual is real and is stated rather than smoothed over:** a visitor who arrives on `/privacy` from a Play listing has no in-page path back to the showcase. Nothing on that page loads analytics at all, so nothing is collected while they are there. Giving them that path is an editorial pass over the document — the same pass `PPR-DL-001` (g) already defers for the four third-party links — and not a code change.
- **s. THE SEEDED FIXTURE STATES NOW CARRY `granted`, AND WITHOUT THAT THE SUITE WOULD HAVE GONE GREEN ABOUT NOTHING.** Fourteen `trackEvent` call sites are asserted through `window.dataLayer` across this suite. The gate makes `trackEvent` a no-op for anyone who has not consented, so a fixture with no answer stored would have silently emptied every one of those assertions. `STATES.firstRun` deliberately carries no answer — that is what a first visit is — and the consent spec seeds its own states either way.
- **t. THE MOUNT'S OWN PROSE STOPS NAMING THE GENERATION, WHERE IT NAMES A SIBLING.** Eight comments in `app/index.html` markup said `m/v7/surfaces/channel.js` and the like; two of them sit inside `<header>` and therefore inside a DOM baseline, so every bump moved `header.html` in three projects forever. They now name the sibling (`surfaces/channel.js`) and the class is gone. Comments that genuinely describe the **generation** — the delivery-hint block, the entry block, `sw.js`'s `changed_in` lines — keep naming it.

### Alternatives considered and rejected

- **Read the consent key in the head script and gate the injection there.** Workable, and it costs a second `DECLARED_SHELL_ACCESSES` entry beside `ga_debug` plus a third copy of the key name. Rejected for (a): the decision belongs in one module, and the shell should not grow a second storage door for it.
- **Advanced consent mode (`gtag('consent','default',{analytics_storage:'denied'})`).** Rejected on (b): it loads the tag before the answer, and the shipped policy says it does not.
- **A ✕ on the banner meaning «no change».** A third exit whose meaning has to be explained, on a surface whose whole property is that the two answers are the only ways out.
- **A second `<footer>` for the site.** Two `contentinfo` landmarks; rejected on (f).
- **Raising the intro window above the banner instead of lowering the banner.** Same pixels, wrong direction: it would leave the banner competing with every future modal rather than settling the layer once.
- **Hiding `#apkBtn` on non-Android.** Rejected on (i): the desktop visitor would never learn the app exists.
- **Retargeting `DeviceLogTest`'s transfer leg onto the export plugin's tag.** Rejected on (p), measured: that plugin writes no log lines at all, so the leg would assert an absence nothing could ever violate.
- **Keeping `history.handoff` declared-not-emitted.** Rejected on (n): the flag means "the emitter is gone", not "the mechanism is gone", and the shared `outcome` list would have kept three dead codes admissible everywhere.
- **Naming the consent controls so the old wide scan passes.** Rejected on (q) — it is what the ids happen to do, and relying on it would be the guard passing for the wrong reason.

### Effects

- **Added:** `app/m/v8/**` (52 files — `/m/v7/`'s 55 minus the four `transfer/` modules and `store/transfer.js`, plus `consent/config.js` and `surfaces/consent.js`); the cookie banner, the footer «Cookie» control and `#installPlatformNote` in `app/index.html`; `.cookie-banner`, `.cookie-banner-actions`, `.cookie-banner-btn`, `.footer-legal-btn`, `.modal-platform-note` and `a.modal-button[hidden]` in the mount stylesheet; `CONSENT_CONFIG` (three knobs) and `CHANNEL_CONFIG.androidPlatformToken`, all `changed_in: PPR-DL-002`; `readAnalyticsConsent` / `writeAnalyticsConsent` and one key in `core/storage.js`; `isAndroidPlatform` and `shouldOfferDownloadLink` in `surfaces/channel.js`; `app/tests/consent-gate.spec.js` (15 static and off-device legs) and `app/tests/consent-surface.spec.js` (12 executing legs); six executing platform legs in `channel-composition.spec.js`; two `testMatch` registrations; and this entry.
- **Removed:** `app/transfer.html`; `app/m/v8/transfer/**` and `store/transfer.js` (by omission in the copy-forward — no frozen byte moved); six re-exports from `store/boot.js`; five `OFFLINE_URLS` entries, one `NON_SHELL_PAGES` entry, four delivery hints and one `COPY` line; the `history.handoff` kind, the `transport` and `refusal` code lists and three `outcome` codes; `HistoryTransferPlugin.java` (734 lines) and `HistoryTransferTest.java` (1672 lines); the `theygrow://transfer` intent-filter, `onNewIntent`, `stageHandoff` and the `Intent` import from `MainActivity`; one leg and one helper from `DeviceLogTest`; and five specs with their two `testMatch` registrations.
- **Operability.** Four new knobs, one new config surface — `app/m/v8/consent/config.js` (`stateGranted`, `stateDenied`, `shellBridge`) and `CHANNEL_CONFIG.androidPlatformToken`, each with `changed_in: PPR-DL-002`. It takes the place `transfer/config.js` vacated, so the mount still ships four device-local config surfaces: `store/`, `export/`, `channel/`, `consent/`. **No new signals this packet**, and one signal kind removed (n). **Net egress change: strictly negative on the web channel** — nothing is fetched from `googletagmanager.com` until a visitor says yes, where it was fetched on every load — and **zero on the native channel**, behind two independent guards, one in `surfaces/consent.js` and one in the shell's own `enable()`, the second of which is executed by calling it directly.
- **Baselines moved, and the two kinds are handled differently.** DOM (text, deterministic markup, re-blessed here after reading the diff): `dom-desktop/header.html` and `dom-mobile/header.html` — exactly two comment lines each, from (t) — and `dom-desktop/control-footer.html` and `dom-mobile/control-footer.html` — the new control and its comment, with `hidden` gone, which is the reveal working. **Visual PNGs are owner-run in the pinned container and are NOT re-blessed here: 16 of the 20 are red.** Every changed region was measured rather than assumed, by decoding each `-diff.png` and taking the bounding box of the marked pixels: on desktop every one is rows **760–790 of 800**, on mobile rows **712–737 of 760** — the footer band, and nothing else on any page. The four modal shots move because a `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` overlay lets the footer show through, not because a modal changed. Green: `visual-desktop/header.png`, `visual-mobile/header.png`, `visual-mobile/create-profile-modal`, `visual-mobile/skill-modal`.
- **A falsifiable prediction, and the numbers it must return.** On the next CI run of this branch: `parity` **green at 1398 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed** on the five non-visual projects, and **red on the two visual projects at 16 of 20** until the owner re-blesses them in the container. `quality` green with `pre-commit run --all-files` reporting no file modified. Per project, all measured locally on 2026-08-23 against a baseline measured the same day from a clean `git archive` of `8dc41fc` (not quoted from a prior entry): `contract` **1224** (1273 listed before, 1224 now, and the −49 is fully accounted: `native-shell` **+51** — one byte-identity leg per shipped file: `/m/v8/` adds 52 and `transfer.html` removes 1 — `consent-gate` **+15**, `show-rule-coverage` **+1**; against `embedded-js-parse` **−50**, `delivery-contract` **−20**, `transfer-format` **−16**, `transfer-seam` **−9**, `transfer-drain-unit` **−8**, `handoff-source` **−6**, `storage-seam` **−4**, `undeclared-reference` **−3**); `behavior` **111** (99 before: `consent-surface` +12, `channel-composition` +6, `handoff-transfer` −6); `dom-desktop` **14** and `dom-mobile` **16**, both unchanged; `native` **33**, unchanged. The four Python suites are **257 passed** across `schema`, `export` and `release`, unchanged. **The instrumented suite is 33 tests, 0 failures, 1 m 16 s on the local emulator** (42 before — `HistoryTransferTest`'s 8 legs and `DeviceLogTest`'s 1, exactly), run against a **re-synced** APK web root: the first run of it in this packet was against a stale `assets/public/` that still carried `/m/v7/` and `transfer.html`, and it passed, which is precisely the green-about-the-wrong-bytes this repository names. **A local green is not a dispatch**: `android-instrumented` runs on `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch`, and nothing here has been observed on CI.
- **What P3 inherits, named here rather than left to be found.** (i) `PPR-P2-INV-001` — *no request reaches an analytics origin and no GA4 configuration runs until the visitor has explicitly consented; withdrawal returns them to a state where nothing further is sent* — enforced by `app/tests/consent-surface.spec.js` on the `behavior` project on every push. (ii) `PPR-P2-INV-002` — *the download is offered only to a visitor whose platform can act on it, and an unreadable platform is offered nothing* — enforced by `channel-composition.spec.js` and `consent-gate.spec.js`. (iii) `DIA-P1-INV-001` and `DIA-P1-INV-002` must be **retired**: their enforcing artifacts are deleted here, and an invariant with no enforcer is what `AGENTS.md` §10 forbids. (iv) `DIA-P5-INV-001`'s Scope must be amended per (p). (v) `DIA-P2-INV-002`'s Scope must name the platform branch. (vi) `PPR-P1-INV-001` is still owed from `PPR-DL-001` (d). (vii) **`docs/RUNBOOK.md` § "The browser-to-native history transfer — DIA-P1 (owner-run)" (`:802-886`), and the transfer sentences at `:724`, `:772` and `:1053-1062`, describe a mechanism that no longer exists.** That is an owner-facing procedure, which is why it is named prominently rather than as a quiet bullet. No exposure window opens by deferring it: nothing deploys before merge (ADR-020) and P3 lands on this branch first.

## PPR-DL-003 — PPR-P3 `declaration-flip-and-docs-tail`: the token that turns the link on, and the documentation the two packets before it deferred

- **Date.** 2026-08-23
- **Type.** Packet — PPR-P3, the closing rung of the milestone «Privacy policy and first L3 release», on branch `feat/privacy-policy-and-consent` (from `main` @ `cccff4b`, after `PPR-DL-001` @ `8dc41fc` and `PPR-DL-002` @ `88cc42a`). A close-out: it opens no invariant of its own beyond the three the earlier packets reserved, and enforces nothing new (`AGENTS.md` §10).
- **Scope.** **In:** the declaration flip `theygrow-privacy-policy` `none` → `published`, with the effective-date re-check `PPR-DL-001` (f) makes mandatory and the two test amendments the flip entails; the `docs/INVARIANTS.md` reconciliation this milestone owes — three entries written, three amended, two retired, ten CI-observation fields discharged; the `docs/RUNBOOK.md` tail — the retired transfer everywhere an owner would meet it, the `/privacy` promotion smoke, § Privacy policy read as done, the baseline note re-aimed at this milestone; `docs/execution-map.md`; and this entry. **Out, by the ladder:** every deploy, promotion, release, tag and Play Console action (owner-run); any change to `app/m/v8/**`; retiring `/m/v1/`–`/m/v7/` (owner-level); the «Скачать APK» label; the editorial pass over the owner's document; the PR text.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. The flip was not a one-token change, and the repository said so in advance.** `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` carried a leg written at PPR-P1 to red on exactly this edit — *"the policy declaration was flipped — that is an owner act with its own RUNBOOK step, and it belongs to a later packet"*. It is a tripwire aimed at this packet and doing its job; inverting it is the packet arriving, not the packet dodging a guard.
- **b. And a second leg would have gone quiet instead of red, which is worse.** `app/tests/channel-composition.spec.js`'s withheld-state leg opened with `test.skip(DECLARED_POLICY_STATE === POLICY_PUBLISHED_VALUE, 'this build declares the policy published, so the withheld state cannot be observed here')`. On the day the shipped token became `published`, the executing half of `FIU-P3-INV-002` that matters most — *nothing offers a policy link while the shell declares none* — would have stopped running, silently, inside a green suite. Two standing sentences would have been falsified by that and neither would have reddened: the block's own *"BOTH LEGS EXECUTE"*, and `INVARIANTS.md`'s **Soundness** claim that a fail-open `shouldOfferPolicy` reds "the withheld-state page leg".
- **c. The effective date had already slipped when the packet opened.** `PPR-DL-001` (f) fixed it at `22.08.2026` and required P3 to re-check it immediately before the flip. Nothing has deployed and nothing can before merge (ADR-020), so the earliest day the document becomes readable is the day this packet lands, 2026-08-23. The slip is one day and the rule fires on any slip.
- **d. Run 32535042631 exists, is green, and is not in this repository.** Ten `Observed.` fields have read **Not yet observed on CI** since L3. The discharging run is `workflow_dispatch` on `b882238` (the FIU-P5 commit, an ancestor of HEAD): `quality`, `eval`, `parity` and `android-instrumented` all green — sixteen steps in the instrumented job, including *Validate the print layer against PDF/A-2b* and *Instrumented store tests (emulator)* — and `android` **skipped**, which `ci.yml:254` does on every dispatch. Nothing in the repository records it: `grep` finds the number nowhere, and `ci-artifacts/` is gitignored and holds a **different** run whose report shows 16 tests and one failure. The evidence chain is therefore the run's own record read through `gh`, plus the repository's own answer to which enforcer runs in which job.
- **e. `docs/RUNBOOK.md` claimed a retirement notice that did not exist.** § Closing a milestone step 10 said of the transfer section that "its steps 3-7 cannot be performed any more and it says so at its head". That head note belongs to a **different** section — *The write path and the legacy import — L1-P4* — and *The browser-to-native history transfer — DIA-P1* carried no head note at all: seventy-nine lines of imperative owner procedure with nothing at the top to say the mechanism beneath it had been deleted. Its step 3 tells the owner that the transfer offer must appear and to **stop** if it does not; the Android-shell smoke, forty lines earlier, tells the same owner that **there must be no offer to move anything from a browser, at any point**.
- **f. And the transfer was named in more places than the handoff listed.** `PPR-DL-002` (vii) named `:802-886`, `:724`, `:772` and `:1053-1062`. The sweep also found the first-install warning conditioned on a path that can no longer exist (`:427`), the web-channel note's ADR-048 §5 condition (`:714`), a logcat caveat justified by a deleted test (`:971`), and — the strongest surviving instruction, missed by the list — the diary smoke ordered *after* the transfer smoke "because the transfer is what puts a profile there" (`:888`), which is the ordering step 10 had already withdrawn at L3-P4.
- **g. One live smoke step addressed the wrong mount generation.** § Promotion + rollback step 3 curls `/m/v7/app.css`. `/m/v8/` has been the running generation since PPR-P2, and `/m/v7/` is still served because frozen generations stay — so that check passes against bytes no client is being given, which is worse than failing. The same line was corrected once already, at L3-P1, for the same reason.

### The decisions

- **a. THE FLIP CARRIES ITS TWO TEST AMENDMENTS, AS ENTAILMENT AND NOT AS SCOPE.** Finding (a) reds; finding (b) goes quiet. A flip that lands the branch red is not the declared change, and a flip that retires a runtime claim while the sentence asserting it stays in `INVARIANTS.md` is the vacuous-guard failure this repository has already paid for four times (`AGENTS.md` §11). `privacy-page.spec.js`'s block turns over to the post-flip state — the declaration must read exactly the published token, read out of the knob source rather than re-typed — and its two siblings stand unchanged, because the shell still links the address nowhere in markup and the knob still names the address the page answers.
- **b. THE WITHHELD LEG IS RE-ARMED RATHER THAN THE INVARIANT WEAKENED.** Both branches now declare their own state before boot, symmetrically, each asserting the mutation took. The alternative — accept the skip and amend `INVARIANTS.md`'s Soundness sentence to admit the lost leg — was rejected: it trades an executing guard for a weaker sentence, and the guard costs four lines. **Re-measured after the flip rather than asserted:** `return true;` in place of the token comparison reds *while the shell declares nothing, no policy link is offered* with `unexpected value "visible"` on `#introPolicyLink`, past its mutation-took assertion. Run and reverted.
- **c. WHAT THE SELF-SKIP GAVE AWAY FOR FREE IS KEPT AS AN ASSERTION.** The skip had one virtue: whichever way the shell shipped, one leg was driving the shipped state. A third leg now says that outright — the declared token must be one of the two the branches execute — so a third value appearing in the shell (a typo, a future `withdrawn`) is a red rather than two legs quietly testing states no build has.
- **d. THE EFFECTIVE DATE MOVES TO `23.08.2026`, IN ALL FOUR PLACES, AND THE RESIDUAL IS THE OWNER'S.** The rule `PPR-DL-001` (f) states is the day the document becomes readable; that is the day this lands, at the earliest. Leaving `22.08.2026` was rejected on the ground the rule itself gives — a policy whose stated effective date precedes the day it became readable was never in force when it said it was. **What this packet cannot close is the day the owner actually promotes.** If that is later than 2026-08-23 the literal is wrong again, and the fix is the same four-token edit. It is therefore no longer buried in this log: § Privacy policy gains a numbered step naming all four locations by path, and the four are `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md:5` and `:145`, `app/privacy.html:103` and `:263`.
- **e. `app/privacy.html`'s HEAD COMMENT IS CORRECTED, AND THAT IS OWN-DIFF FALLOUT RATHER THAN SCOPE.** It said the page was "ОПУБЛИКОВАНА, НО НЕ ОБЪЯВЛЕНА" and that the declaration "остаётся content=none". This packet's own edit is what makes those words false. Statement only: no other word of the page changes, and the withdrawal rule it ends on is kept and sharpened. `app/index.html`'s two comment blocks were re-read and deliberately **left alone** — both are phrased conditionally ("Пока объявления нет…") and stay true — which also keeps two DOM baselines from moving for prose.
- **f. THE ORDER IS SATISFIED STRUCTURALLY, NOT PROCEDURALLY, AND THAT IS WRITTEN DOWN WHERE THE OWNER READS IT.** «Document first, declaration second» guards against a declaration reaching a parent before its document. `/privacy` (PPR-P1) and the declaration (PPR-P3) ship in the **same image**: there is no moment in which one exists without the other, on either channel. § Privacy policy now says so, marks steps 1 and 2 done, and keeps step 5's ordering rule intact for the case it still governs — a future redaction, or a withdrawal, where the token goes back to `none` **first**.
- **g. THE `/privacy` SMOKE IS APPENDED TO STEP 3, NOT INSERTED AS A NEW ONE.** `PPR-DL-001` (k) says "adds to § Promotion + rollback step 3", and appending is also the only cheap reading: inserting would shift 3→8 and break eight textual cross-references (`:69`, `:71`, `:74`, `:135`, `:297`, `:348`, `:1041`, `:1046`, `:1049`), one of which — "step 4 decides" — names a **sub**-step and would have been renumbered wrongly by reflex. The four checks are `PPR-DL-001` (k)'s verbatim, and they sit before promotion because ADR-020 makes the tagged-revision smoke the last gate a parent is behind.
- **h. THE TRANSFER SECTION IS FENCED AND KEPT, NOT DELETED — AND EVERY STEP IS MARKED, NOT JUST THREE.** The file's own precedent is to keep records and mark them (`:635`, `:719-729`, `:762`, `:769`), and §802 holds two things recorded nowhere else: the **band invariant** at step 8, and the **open premise** at step 4.3 — that an installed WebAPK and an ordinary Chrome tab share one `localStorage` partition for an origin, almost certainly true, verified nowhere, and now never measurable by this mechanism. Unlike §717, where steps 1, 2 and 8 still work, **not one step here can be performed**, so the head note says that rather than naming a range. Deleting the section was rejected: it destroys the record and both findings.
- **i. ONE TENSE CORRECTION IN §802 IS A FINDING RATHER THAN TIDYING.** The section read "This transfer **is** the source, and the sequence below **is** the only place the whole path is ever exercised end to end." It never was. The mechanism was retired before any owner ran the sequence against a family's real history, so the L1-P4 importer has been complete, idempotent and **sourceless for its entire life** — and, since `HistoryTransferTest` went with the plugin, it now has no device-side executor at all. Both facts are written where they were implied.
- **j. THE TWO RETIREMENTS ARE RECORDED IN PLACE, WITH A HEADING SUFFIX, AND THIS ESTABLISHES THE CONVENTION.** No invariant has ever been removed from `docs/INVARIANTS.md` — `git log -p` over the file returns no deleted `### ` heading in its whole history — and there is no retirement idiom to follow. `DIA-P1-INV-001` and `DIA-P1-INV-002` keep their bodies byte-untouched, because between them they carry the `DIA-` namespace note that exists in exactly one other place and the leg-by-leg CI evidence for run 31956524510 including the two harness-fault dispatches before it. They gain ` — RETIRED (PPR-P3)` in the heading and a `Retired` bullet naming every deleted enforcer. **The suffix is the part that is a choice**: a bullet alone was rejected because an enforced-only file carrying a live-reading heading for an unenforced claim is precisely the wish-list drift `AGENTS.md` §10 exists to prevent, and a separate "Retired" section was rejected because it breaks the file's chronological order.
- **k. ALL TEN CI FIELDS ARE DISCHARGED, AND EACH ONE CARRIES ITS BOUND.** Coverage is establishable and was established rather than assumed: every enforcer the ten name runs in `quality`, `parity` or `android-instrumented` — **none** in the skipped `android` job, which holds *The signature comparator rejects a foreign certificate* and *Release packaging fails closed…* and enforces nothing in any of the ten — and every instrumented executor they name existed at `b882238` and is unchanged on this branch but for a comment-only line in `StoreEngineTest`. **The bound each field now states:** the tree that run executed is L3's, so what is discharged is each invariant as it landed; PPR-P2's copy-forward to `/m/v8/` is re-observed by this branch's own run, not by that one. The granularity available is job-and-step, not per-test, and the fields say so by naming the job and the step rather than a test count.
- **l. THE STALE MOUNT IN THE PROMOTION SMOKE IS FIXED IN THE FILE ALREADY OPEN.** Finding (g) is not this packet's subject, but it is a live owner instruction that would pass against the wrong bytes, in a section this packet is editing anyway, and it has now gone stale at three consecutive closes. `/m/v7/` → `/m/v8/`, and the line gains the instruction that would have prevented all three: **read the generation out of `app/index.html`, not out of that sentence.**
- **m. THE VISUAL BASELINES ARE NAMED AND LEFT.** Sixteen of the twenty PNGs are red from PPR-P2's footer control; the flip adds the policy link to `modal-onboarding`, which is already in that set, so the count stays sixteen. The projects are docker-backed and the daemon needs a real terminal with `sudo`, so re-blessing is owner-run — this packet re-blesses **no** PNG and does not call the suite green while they stand. All sixteen are named file by file in § Closing a milestone, together with the four that must come back green, so the owner's run can be checked against a list rather than eyeballed.

### Alternatives considered and rejected

- **Flip only, and amend `INVARIANTS.md`'s Soundness sentence to admit the lost withheld leg.** Cheaper by four lines, and it converts an executing guard into a paragraph. Rejected on `AGENTS.md` §11: the claim *nothing offers a policy link while the shell declares none* is a runtime claim, and after the skip nothing would have executed it.
- **Delete § "The browser-to-native history transfer".** The cleanest-looking option, and the one that loses the band invariant, the unverified storage-partition premise, and the fact that the sequence was never run. Rejected on the file's own precedent and on decision (h).
- **Rewrite §802's nine steps into a short past-tense paragraph.** Shorter, and it deletes exactly the detail a record exists for. Rejected: fencing converts instruction to record without destroying it.
- **Remove `DIA-P1-INV-001` / `-002` from `INVARIANTS.md` outright.** Defensible under an enforced-only bar, and it would have destroyed the only record of run 31956524510's legs and the `DIA-` namespace note. Rejected; the heading suffix answers the discoverability half at a fraction of the cost.
- **Insert the `/privacy` smoke as a new step 3.** Reads better in isolation, breaks eight cross-references, one of them ambiguously. Rejected — see decision (g).
- **Leave the ten fields alone because the repository holds no record of the run.** The strictest reading of the evidence bar, and it would have left ten fields permanently false: the run happened, and its own record plus the repository's job mapping is exactly the kind of evidence the bar asks for. Rejected, with the bound written into every field instead.
- **Update the execution map's ladder section as well as Current state.** The file's own rule governs Current state, and the ladder is narrative. Rejected as a rule — but its L3 line still read "Current, FIVE PACKETS LANDED", which the merge had falsified, so that one **statement** was corrected and nothing else in the section was touched.
