## PPR-DL-004 — PPR-P4 `privacy-redirect-absolute`: the canonical address was reachable at one spelling and not at the other, and nothing in the suite could tell

- **Date.** 2026-08-23
- **Type.** Packet — PPR-P4, a **repair** packet on branch `fix/privacy-redirect-absolute`, cut from `main` @ `e68dc2a`. The milestone «Privacy policy and first L3 release» is **merged** (PR #27) and **not promoted**: the tagged revision `sha-e68dc2a` sits at 0% traffic. The defect was found by the owner smoke that `PPR-DL-001` (k) put into `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Promotion + rollback step 3 — the one thing in this project that observes production's answer for `/privacy` — and it is the smoke doing exactly what it was written for.
- **Scope.** **In:** `absolute_redirect off;` in `app/nginx.conf`; the guard that closes the gap the defect came through, static over the config and executed against the mirror; the two step-3 smoke lines this measurement proved wrong, plus the follow-the-redirect line neither of them carried; the `PPR-P1-INV-001` amendment; one falsified status statement and one packet bullet in `docs/execution-map.md`; and this entry. **Out, by the ladder:** every deploy, promotion, tag, release and Play Console action (owner-run, ADR-020); `app/m/v8/**`; `app/tests/server.js`; every other `docs/RUNBOOK.md` section; the milestone's standing residuals.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. The measurement, owner-run against the tagged revision, and it is unambiguous.** `curl -sI "$TAG_URL/privacy/"` returned `HTTP/2 301` with `location: http://<the tagged revision's own host>:8080/privacy` — the header verbatim is in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, which is where live-infra identifiers live (`M1-P3-INV-002`). Two things are wrong in one header: the port is the container's `listen 8080`, which is not exposed, and the scheme is `http`, which is what nginx sees behind a proxy that terminates TLS in front of it. The address does not answer. RUNBOOK step 3 expected «`301` to `/privacy`» and would have accepted this, because it read the status and not the address.
- **b. The config says the right thing and nginx sends the wrong thing, and that is not a contradiction.** `app/nginx.conf:106-108` is the file's only `return 301`, and its argument is `/privacy`. nginx's header filter rewrites **any** `Location` beginning with `/` into `scheme://host[:port]` + URI unless `absolute_redirect` is off; the file set neither `absolute_redirect` nor `port_in_redirect`, and `listen 8080` at `:18` supplies the port. So the defect belongs to the file's *silence*, not to the redirect line — which is why fixing the line would have fixed one address and left the class open.
- **c. The mirror was never wrong, and that is precisely why nothing was red.** `app/tests/server.js:287-289` has answered `/privacy/` with a **relative** `Location: '/privacy'` since PPR-P1. Every leg that touched the route passed: the delivery-contract live leg asserted `location` was exactly `/privacy` and it was, of the mirror; `privacy-surface.spec.js`'s trailing-slash leg followed the redirect through Playwright, which resolves a relative and an absolute same-host `Location` identically and could not have distinguished them. **Nothing anywhere compared the mirror's `Location` with what nginx would emit.** A drift guard that pairs locations and headers is not a drift guard for redirect form, and this repository had been reading the first as the second.
- **d. `PPR-P1-INV-001` said, in writing, that the pairing covered this.** Its Scope named «the delivery drift guard plus the owner's `curl` smoke» as what pairs the mirror to production. Both halves were blind to the form: the guard did not look, and the smoke line accepted a `301` without reading it. The sentence was not vague, it was false, in the one respect that mattered.
- **e. And the second smoke line reported a false red on a clean page.** `curl -s "$TAG_URL/privacy" | grep -c '<script'` → `0` returned **1**. The only hit is `app/privacy.html:14`, inside the head comment that itself explains the page carries no script. The static guard strips comments before matching for exactly this reason (`app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js:54`); the smoke line, written from the same intent, did not. Verified on the shipped page while writing this: naive `grep -c` **1**, comment-stripped **0**.

### The decisions

- **a. `absolute_redirect off;` AT SERVER SCOPE, AND IT IS A CLASS SETTING RATHER THAN A PATCH.** It is the one directive that reaches the cause: with absolute redirects off nginx emits the `Location` it was given, verbatim. **What it does to any future `return 301` in this file, stated as contract:** `return 30x /path;` → `Location: /path`, origin-relative; `return 30x https://host/path;` → untouched, because it does not begin with `/`, so a deliberate cross-origin redirect still works; nginx's own directory redirects from `try_files … $uri/` and `index` → relative too. Server scope, not location scope, is the whole point — a location-scoped copy fixes one address and leaves the next one to repeat this. Not http scope either: there is one server block, and `A1-DL-008` records that an http-level directive is the kind the delivery drift guard cannot see.
- **b. `port_in_redirect` IS DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED.** It would remove `:8080` and leave `http://<host>/privacy` — the wrong scheme, an extra hop through Cloud Run's own `http`→`https` redirect, and a visitor a moment on plaintext. With no absolute URL composed at all there is nothing left for it to govern, so adding it would be a second knob that reads as if it were doing work. Written into the config comment so the omission is a decision on the page rather than a gap.
- **c. THE GUARD IS SPLIT, AND EACH HALF IS LABELLED AS WHAT IT IS (`AGENTS.md` §11).** The **executed** half is `the redirect names the address, not the container` in `delivery-contract.spec.js`: a real `GET /privacy/` with `maxRedirects: 0`, asserting the `Location` in three separate properties — no scheme, origin-relative, no port — so a red names the class instead of a string mismatch. The **static** half is the `redirects stay inside the origin — config shape (PPR-P4)` block, which **parses `app/nginx.conf` and proves what the committed config says**. It does not run nginx, does not parse the file the way nginx parses it, and observes no header. Running the real image in CI was considered and rejected: it is a packet of its own and it changes the suite's Docker posture, and this is a repair.
- **d. THE STATIC HALF ASSERTS THE CLASS, NOT THE ADDRESS.** Three legs, because one would have been a check on `/privacy/` wearing a class's clothes: the directive is present at **server** scope and outside every location; **nothing** switches it back on (a location that did would re-arm the defect for itself while the first leg stayed green); and every `return 30x` target in the file is either origin-relative or an absolute `https://` URL. A fourth leg is anti-vacuity — the class leg holds trivially over zero targets, which is how a parser that quietly stopped matching presents itself.
- **e. THE SCAN PROVES ITSELF IN ITS OWN RUN, ON INPUTS IT BUILDS.** A fifth leg runs each detector against configs written inside the test: the directive absent, the directive present only inside a `#` comment, the directive present but only inside a location, a location re-enabling it, an `http://` redirect target, and a file with no `server` block at all (the extractor **throws** rather than returning an empty string every membership test would pass against). No shipped file is mutated and nobody is trusted to put one back.
- **f. THE MIRROR IS NOT EDITED.** It already emits the right form; the defect was never in it. A cross-reference comment there was considered and rejected as widening the file list for no assertion — the pairing is stated in the test that makes it, where a reader of a red will actually meet it.
- **g. THE `<script>` SMOKE LINE IS CORRECTED, NOT THE PAGE.** The comment at `app/privacy.html:14` is the page explaining its own most important property; deleting it to satisfy a `grep` would trade a real explanation for a lazy check. `perl -0777 -pe 's/<!--.*?-->//gs'` strips comments in a form an owner can paste with no JS toolchain, and a `python3` equivalent is given inline rather than left to be invented under pressure. `sed` was rejected — it cannot match across lines without contortions, and a comment containing `>` defeats the single-line spellings.
- **h. THE TRAILING-SLASH LINE GAINS A SECOND LINE THAT FOLLOWS THE REDIRECT.** Asserting `location: /privacy` exactly is what sees the repair took; it is not what sees the address **land**. A `301` whose target is unreachable still prints `301`, which is the whole shape of this defect, so `curl -sIL` through to the `200 text/html` is now its own bullet. Reachability at this address is what ADR-050 §5 gates the closed test on, and it had never been checked end to end.
- **i. STEP 3 IS REPAIRED IN PLACE AND NOT RENUMBERED,** for the reason `PPR-DL-003` (g) recorded: eight textual cross-references depend on the numbering and one of them names a sub-step.
- **j. THE CANONICAL-ADDRESS PROPERTY BELONGS IN `PPR-P1-INV-001`, AND NO NEW INVARIANT IS OPENED.** It is the same subject — what the policy address serves and under which spellings — and that entry already named the pairing apparatus, wrongly. A second entry would split one property across two addresses of its own. So the Statement gains the trailing-slash clause, Enforced by gains the two legs with the executed/static split named, and the Scope sentence that was false is corrected in place rather than left standing under an amendment that admits it (`AGENTS.md` §11). `Landed in.` stays `PPR-P1`; the amendment cites the packet id, never a SHA.

### Alternatives rejected

- **`return 301 https://$host/privacy;`.** Fixes the header without the directive. Rejected — it hard-codes a scheme into a file that also serves plain `http` locally, and it fixes one line while leaving the next `return 301` to repeat the class.
- **`port_in_redirect off;` alone.** The narrower-looking knob. Rejected — see decision (b): it leaves the wrong scheme.
- **Delete the head comment from `app/privacy.html` so the naive `grep -c` returns 0.** Rejected — the check exists to protect the property the comment explains; silencing the explanation to satisfy the checker is the wrong half to change.
- **Run real nginx in CI and assert the header.** The only thing that would make this an executed claim end to end. Rejected as out of a repair packet's shape, and named here rather than buried so the option stays on the table with its cost visible.
- **Open a `PPR-P4-INV-001`.** Rejected — see decision (j).

### Effects

- **Changed, product delivery:** `app/nginx.conf` — one directive, `absolute_redirect off;`, at server scope, with the comment block that records the measurement, the class contract for future redirects, and why `port_in_redirect` is absent. No location block is rewritten. `envsubst` in `app/docker-entrypoint.sh:127` runs with a two-name allowlist, so the line passes the template render untouched; the directive has existed since nginx 1.11.8 against an `nginx:alpine` base, and an unknown directive would make nginx refuse to start — a failed 0%-traffic revision, not a silent wrong redirect.
- **Changed, tests:** `app/tests/delivery-contract.spec.js` — one new describe block (five legs, one of them self-proving), one new live-response leg, and the `= /privacy/` exemption comment extended to name the half it never covered. `app/tests/server.js` is **untouched**.
- **Changed, docs:** `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Promotion + rollback step 3 — two bullets repaired, one added, and the preamble now says why the lines themselves have to be right. `docs/INVARIANTS.md` — `PPR-P1-INV-001` amended in Statement, Enforced by and Scope, plus a dated amendment bullet carrying the measurement, the mechanism, both arm-checks and the local observation. `docs/execution-map.md` — the milestone status statement the merge falsified, and a `P4` bullet. And this entry.
- **Operability: none** (ADR-013 / contract §4.7). No new knob, no new signal, no new closed code — `absolute_redirect` is a delivery directive, not a `changed_in`-provenanced config surface. **Net egress change: zero**: one response header changes shape and no request is added anywhere. One side property, named but not claimed as tested: with the directive off, a relative `Location` arriving from the `/api` upstream would also pass through unrewritten instead of gaining `:8080`. `/api` issues no redirect today.
- **No mount bump, no `CACHE_VERSION` bump, no schema change, no new dependency, no baseline moved.** `app/m/v8/**` is untouched, and nothing this packet edits can move a DOM or visual baseline.
- **What is executed and what is only read, said once and plainly.** Executed: the mirror's `Location` form, over real HTTP, in `contract`; the five static legs as a scan of a text file; the self-proving legs against configs built in-run; both mutation arm-checks, run and reverted. Read: `app/nginx.conf` — a static scan proves what the config **says**. **Nothing in this repository runs the real nginx image**, which is the reason this defect could ship green and does not change with this packet. **The only executor of the production behaviour is the owner-run smoke** in `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Promotion + rollback step 3, against the next tagged revision.
- **The repair is therefore UNOBSERVED in production, and is recorded as such.** What is observed is local, on the host: `contract` **1230 passed** (1224 before) and `behavior` **112 passed** (unchanged — `privacy-surface.spec.js`'s trailing-slash leg lives there and follows the redirect through a real browser), with the two arm-checks reproducing the exact failures the legs are written for. Whether `/privacy/` now lands is a fact the next tagged-revision smoke establishes and nothing before it does.
- **What it hands on.** Everything `PPR-DL-003` handed on stands unchanged — the «Скачать APK» label, `/privacy` with no in-page path back to the showcase and its four third-party policies as `<code>`, `/privacy.html` as a second address by decision, the 16 visual PNGs the owner re-blesses in the container, the effective date against the day the owner actually promotes, and the counsel trigger on the policy's §2. One is added: **executing the real nginx image anywhere in this repository remains undone**, and the class of defect it would catch is now known to be real rather than hypothetical.

## CGR-DL-001 — CGR-P1 `graphify-adoption`: the graph tool's artifacts were half-ignored, its corpus was half history, and its rules had no home

- **Date.** 2026-08-24
- **Type.** Packet — `CGR-P1`, the whole of a one-packet tooling track, on a branch cut from `main` @ `1d8cf11`. Documentation and ignore rules only. Repo-side definition site for vault `ADR-051` (see vault: `04-decisions/adr-051-graphify-code-graph-adoption-in-code-repo.md`), and the packet that closes the two debts the 2026-08-24 annotation to vault `ADR-049` names against this repository.
- **Scope.** **In:** `.gitignore` (the graph-artifact block); `.graphifyignore` (new file); `CLAUDE.md` (new `## Code graph (Graphify)` section, plus the one bullet in `## Vault clone (read-only)` this falsifies); `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (new `## Agent tooling on this workstation`); `docs/execution-map.md` (the `CGR` track declaration); and this entry. **Out, by the ladder:** every product and runtime file (`app/**`, `api/**`, `native/**`, `scripts/**`); `AGENTS.md`; `docs/INVARIANTS.md`; `.claude/settings.json` and any agent-permission surface; the post-commit hook and the MCP server; building a graph over the vault clone; the docs corpus in the graph; the PAT renewal itself, which is an owner act.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. The `.gitignore` block was half a rule, and `git` says exactly which half.** `git check-ignore -v graphify-out/graph.json` returned `.gitignore:54:graph.json` — the bare names *did* cover nested paths. `git check-ignore -v graphify-out` returned **exit 1, no rule**. So the directory itself, `manifest.json`, `cache/`, `.graphify_analysis.json`, `.graphify_root` and (when it exists) `cost.json` were covered by nothing, and `git status --porcelain | wc -l` printed **1**: `?? graphify-out/`. This was a known-red state, not an undetected one.
- **b. The artifact is a directory of seven entries, not three files.** Measured on disk: `graph.json` (6.8 MB), `graph.html`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, `manifest.json`, `cache/`, `.graphify_analysis.json`, `.graphify_root` — ~11 MB. `GRAPH_REPORT.md` and `graph.html` are written by the **second** command (`cluster-only`); after a bare `extract` they are not on disk at all. The comment above the old rule described "the vault graph tooling", which is not what the tool is pointed at.
- **c. Half the graph was frozen history.** `graphify-out/manifest.json` lists **556** scanned files, of which **323 are `app/m/v1…v7`** (42/42/42/47/49/51/50 by generation); `graph.json` holds **5 324** nodes, of which **2 582 — 48.5% — carry a `v1…v7` `source_file`**. The live mount `app/m/v8` contributes 47 files and 397 nodes. A navigation question therefore had roughly even odds of landing in a generation nobody ships.
- **d. The staged Android web root contributes nothing, and it was assumed to contribute double.** `native/android/app/src/main/assets/public` is excluded by `native/android/.gitignore:101`; `git ls-files` tracks **0** files under it; it appears **0** times in `manifest.json` and **0** times as a node `source_file`. The exclusion it needed already existed, in another subtree's ignore file.
- **e. Only `.graphifyignore` could have removed the frozen generations, and the reason is in the tool's own source.** `graphify/detect.py:_is_scan_ignored()` states it directly — *"`explicit_patterns` contains only .graphifyignore/--exclude rules, which remain authoritative even for tracked files"* — i.e. a file that `.gitignore` drops is **kept anyway if git tracks it**. `app/m/v1…v7` are tracked (55 files under v7 alone). So no `.gitignore` line, however written, could ever have shrunk the corpus. The mechanism was verified three ways before use: the `--no-gitignore` help text (*"prioritizes .graphifyignore"*), the bundled README §"Ignoring files", and `detect.py`'s `_load_graphifyignore` / `_parse_gitignore_line` / `_is_ignored`.
- **f. The `[sql]` extra is load-bearing and silent when absent — and the number that advertised it was mostly duplication.** With `tree-sitter-sql` 0.3.11 installed, the pre-exclusion graph held **209** nodes across **9** `.sql` files. Eight of those nine files were the **same** `store/schema/001-core.sql`, once per module generation: 7 frozen copies × 26 nodes = 182, plus the live `app/m/v8` copy's 26, plus 1 from `scripts/dev/init-pgvector.sql`. Post-exclusion the graph holds **27** `.sql` nodes across **2** files, and the schema — the DDL, the append-only triggers, the views — is fully present. The extra is exactly as load-bearing as it was (without it the live schema parses to nothing, and nothing reports that it did); the breadth the raw count implied was never there.
- **g. The vault clone's read-only lock is one repo-local file, and the global config is what makes that true.** `credential.helper=store --file=/home/dev/.config/git/vault-ro-credentials` is set **locally** in the clone; the file is mode `0600`, one line, outside any repository. `git config --global --list` returns `user.name` and `user.email` **and nothing else** — no global helper, and no `~/.git-credentials`.
- **h. And `GIT_ASKPASS` is a writing account sitting behind that lock.** Measured in a `cursor-server` shell: `GIT_ASKPASS` is set to the editor's `askpass.sh`, which supplies the **account** credentials, with **write** rights. Git consults the local helper first and it wins, so the lock holds *while the token is valid*. The failure mode is that expiry is silent: `pull` keeps working through askpass and the lock is gone with no signal. None of this was written down anywhere in this repository.
- **i. The `CLAUDE.md` section PR #29 landed carries no Graphify rule.** `## Vault clone (read-only)` has pull-first, read-only, the copy ban, the detector and the git-role split; the only graph sentence in it named three files as the artifacts, which (b) falsifies. And PR #29 (`bc2cb42`) touched `.gitignore` and `CLAUDE.md` only — `git show --name-only` shows no `docs/decision-log.md`, so **the vault-clone rules landed with no ledger entry at all**. This entry is the first.

### The decisions

- **a. THE `.gitignore` RULE REPLACES THE THREE BARE NAMES, IT DOES NOT JOIN THEM.** One anchored, directory-only rule: `graphify-out/`. Extending instead of replacing was the cheaper diff and it was rejected: a bare `graph.json` matches that filename **anywhere in the tree**, and the day a real product file is called that, the rule masks it silently. The three names are gone from the rule lines; the comment names them only to say what the directory contains. The comment also carries the vault path once, in full, so a reader who has never seen the decision can find it.
- **b. THE EXCLUSION IS A FILE IN THE REPOSITORY, NOT A FLAG IN SOMEBODY'S SHELL.** `graphify extract` takes a repeatable `--exclude` (`cli.py:3029`) that feeds the same authoritative pattern set, so the flag would have worked. It was rejected because it lives in shell history: the next session would re-run the two documented commands and silently get the noisy corpus back. `.graphifyignore` is read from the repository root on every run, by the tool itself, with no operator memory involved.
- **c. SEVEN EXPLICIT LINES, NOT A `v[1-7]` GLOB.** The maintenance action when a generation freezes is already "add a line", so explicit lines make the file its own instruction. A character class would additionally have rested on matcher behaviour that was not verified, and an exclusion file is not the place to find out what a glob does.
- **d. THE STAGED-COPY LINE SHIPS, AND ITS COMMENT SAYS IT MEASURES ZERO.** Finding (d) means the line changes nothing about a standard run. It is written anyway for two reasons that are not rhetorical: the graph's corpus should not depend silently on `native/android/.gitignore` continuing to say what it says today, and `--no-gitignore` — a flag whose name reads as being about something else entirely — disables `.gitignore` while **keeping** `.graphifyignore` in force, which is exactly the moment the whole staged copy would otherwise arrive. The comment states the measured zero rather than a duplication the graph does not show; a comment in a file authored here is written from what was measured here.
- **e. THE RULES GET THEIR OWN `CLAUDE.md` SECTION, A SIBLING AND NEVER A CHILD.** `## Code graph (Graphify)` sits beside `## Vault clone (read-only)`, not inside it. The two govern different perimeters — one is a read-only cache of somebody else's canon, the other is a derived index of this repository — and merging them would have made the clone section the home of a rule that must never be applied to the clone. The section states the subject (this repository only), the two mandatory flags with their reasons, the manual run mode, the consumption surface, the three limits, the maintenance action, and the detector.
- **f. THE FALSIFIED BULLET IN THE CLONE SECTION IS CORRECTED IN PLACE, NOT LEFT UNDER THE NEW SECTION.** It named three files as the artifacts, which (b) disproves. It is now one sentence saying the code graph is outside that perimeter and pointing at the section that governs it. A file being edited does not get to keep a statement known to be false.
- **g. `graphify claude install` AND `graphify-mcp` ARE NAMED AS NOT-RUN, WITH THE REASON, RATHER THAN LEFT UNMENTIONED.** The installer edits this normative `CLAUDE.md`, creates a `.claude/settings.json` that does not exist here, and installs a `PreToolUse` hook — it changes the agent's permanent behaviour as a side effect of installing a utility. That layer changes by docs packet on the normal cycle, which is what this packet is. The MCP server adds a process and a tool surface with no measured need. Both are written down because the commands exist, are advertised in the tool's own help, and would otherwise look like an oversight to the next reader.
- **h. THE THREE LIMITS ARE WRITTEN AS CONDITIONS OF USE, AND THEY TERMINATE IN A RULE.** No literals in the graph; `explain` truncates at 20 connections; `query` ranking is noisy. Stated alone these read as grumbling, so the section ends them with the thing that changes behaviour: the graph is a navigator to anchors, not a replacement for reading, and **an answer resting entirely on the graph is reported as unconfirmed**.
- **i. THE DETECTOR PRINTS COUNTS, AND `--timing` IS IN THE RUN COMMAND TO MAKE THE MODE CHECK PRINTABLE.** `git status --porcelain | wc -l`, `git check-ignore -v graphify-out`, and the clone's `| wc -l` — each yields a number, because an absence of output is not evidence of a clean tree. The mode half is `graphify-out/cost.json` absent **and** `[graphify timing] semantic extract: 0.0s` on stderr; measured in `cli.py:493`/`3045`, that line is printed **only under `--timing`**, so without the flag the check quietly degrades to its weaker half. The flag is therefore part of the documented command rather than an optional nicety.
- **j. `docs/RUNBOOK.md` GETS A NEW TOP-LEVEL SECTION, NOT A SUBSECTION OF `## Local dev`.** `## Local dev` is how to run *this product*; `## Live-infra divergence` is production identifiers. A workstation's agent tooling is neither, and burying the vault clone's operational reality under "local dev" would have hidden the one thing in it that fails silently. It is placed **before** `## Live-infra divergence` so that section stays terminal.
- **k. THE RUNBOOK RECORDS THE CREDENTIAL FILE'S PATH AND MODE AND NOTHING ELSE, AND SAYS SO.** The token value is not in this repository in any form, and the sentence that records the path also records that prohibition, so the next editor does not read the path as an invitation. The `GIT_ASKPASS` trap is written as the silent-failure mode it is — pull keeps working, the lock is gone, nothing prints — with the environment it was measured in named (`cursor-server`) and the explicit caveat that a hand-opened terminal may differ. The renewal is referenced as vault: `05-inbox/owner-backlog.md` item 12 and **not restated**: its procedure and negative probe live there, and a second copy would drift.
- **l. NO `.claudeignore`, AND THE REFUSAL IS RECORDED BECAUSE THE TOOL ASKS FOR ONE.** The bundled README suggests it, with a real-sounding rationale (writes into the workspace invalidating the agent's prompt cache). The installed Claude Code binary contains **zero** occurrences of the string `claudeignore` — likewise `cursorignore` and `aiignore`. A file no reader reads is worse than no file: it looks like a control, and the next person to ask whether the graph is excluded would believe it is. The supported analogue, `permissions.deny: ["Read(./graphify-out/**)"]` in `.claude/settings.json`, is rejected on decision (g)'s own reasoning — that file does not exist here, and creating it by hand for an unmeasured benefit is the same change with better manners. The rule instead lives in `CLAUDE.md` in the form the agent actually reads: the graph is consulted through `query` / `explain` / `path`, not by opening `graph.json`.
- **m. NO INVARIANT IS OPENED, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.** `docs/INVARIANTS.md` entries are properties something executes against. `graphify-out/` does not exist on a CI checkout, so there is nothing there for a runtime invariant to observe, and a static "the `.gitignore` rule exists" invariant would restate a one-line file. The obligation lives where it can actually be discharged: `CLAUDE.md` `## Code graph (Graphify)`, as a detector run by the session that ran the tool, printing counts.
- **n. A FRESH `CGR` NAMESPACE, DECLARED WHERE EVERY OTHER PREFIX IS DECLARED.** Filing a workstation-tooling packet under `PPR` would have put it inside a merged product milestone. `GWN`, `SLA`, `VDK`, `ICON` and `XPT` all opened fresh namespaces for standalone tracks and all declared them in `docs/execution-map.md`; without that declaration `CGR-DL-001` would be the only id in this ledger with no home.

### Alternatives rejected

- **Extend the `.gitignore` block instead of replacing it.** Smaller diff, keeps the masking hazard forever. See decision (a).
- **`--exclude` flags on the run command instead of `.graphifyignore`.** Works; lives outside the repository. See decision (b).
- **A `.gitignore` rule for `app/m/v1…v7`.** Cannot work at all — the files are tracked, and the tool preserves tracked files against `.gitignore`. See finding (e). It would also have hidden the frozen generations from **git**, which is the opposite of what anyone wants.
- **Run `graphify claude install` and keep whatever it writes.** The advertised path, and the fastest one. Rejected: it edits the normative contract file and installs a hook as a side effect of installing a utility.
- **Start `graphify-mcp`.** Rejected — a process and a tool surface with no measured need.
- **`graphify hook install` (post-commit regeneration).** Rejected for now: it bakes an interpreter path into this repository's hooks and needs reinstalling on upgrade. Incremental extraction makes the manual mode cheap enough that the machinery is not yet earned.
- **Add `.claudeignore`.** Rejected on measurement. See decision (l).
- **Put the Graphify rules inside `## Vault clone (read-only)`.** Rejected — see decision (e); it would have housed a rule inside the section it must never apply to.

### Effects

- **Changed, ignore rules:** `.gitignore` — the six-line ADR-049 block replaced by one `graphify-out/` rule with a comment naming the tool, the directory's contents, the vault decision by path, and why replacement beat extension. `.graphifyignore` — **new**, 34 lines: seven frozen generations, the staged Android web root, and the comment explaining why this file rather than a `.gitignore` line.
- **Changed, contract:** `CLAUDE.md` — new `## Code graph (Graphify)` between `## Vault clone (read-only)` and `## Packet discipline`, and one bullet inside the clone section rewritten from a falsified artifact list into a pointer.
- **Changed, docs:** `docs/RUNBOOK.md` — new `## Agent tooling on this workstation` with two subsections, placed before `## Live-infra divergence`. `docs/execution-map.md` — the `CGR` track and its `P1` bullet. And this entry.
- **Operability: none** (`ADR-013` / contract §4.7). No knob, no signal, no closed code. **Net egress change: zero, and measured rather than argued:** the run mode is `--code-only`, this environment holds no LLM key, `graphify-out/cost.json` is not created, and the reversal condition — a key appearing here re-opens the run-mode decision — is written into `CLAUDE.md` rather than left as an understanding.
- **No product or runtime file is touched, no dependency enters the repository** (the tool is a per-machine `uv tool` install that nothing in `pyproject.toml` or CI references), **no mount bump, no `CACHE_VERSION` bump, no schema change, no baseline moved.**
- **What is executed and what is only read, said plainly** (`AGENTS.md` §11). **Executed:** the three acceptance checks (`git status --porcelain | wc -l`, `git check-ignore -v graphify-out`, `git diff --stat`); a full regeneration of the graph under the new `.graphifyignore`, with the corpus re-counted from the regenerated `manifest.json` and `graph.json`; the mode check on that run; the clone's cleanliness before and after; and `pre-commit run --all-files`. **Read, not executed:** the tool's source in `detect.py` / `cli.py`, which is where the tracked-file exemption, the incremental prune and the `--timing` gating come from — those are static evidence about the tool, and the regeneration in this packet is what turns the corpus claim into an executed one.
- **The regeneration's own output, since the prune was an assumption before it was run.** `graphify extract . --code-only --timing` reported `323 excluded` and `Pruned 2582 node(s) from 316 deleted or excluded source file(s)` — the two numbers finding (c) predicted, to the node. **`--force` was not needed**; the incremental path evicted the excluded nodes by itself, which is what `cli.py`'s `_stale_graph_sources` claimed it would do. The graph went 5 324 → **2 742** nodes and 13 650 → **6 038** edges; `app/m/v8` still holds its 397, the staged Android copy still holds 0, and `[graphify timing] semantic extract: 0.0s` printed with no `cost.json` written. One incidental warning, unrelated to this packet and pre-existing: `pyproject.toml` produced zero nodes and is absent from the graph (the tool's `#1666`).
- **What it hands on.** Three things. **First**, the graph's own limits are now conditions of use rather than folklore, and the "answer built entirely on the graph is unconfirmed" rule has no enforcement beyond the agent reading it. **Second**, the vault clone's read-only lock has a **dated silent-failure mode**: at PAT expiry (≈2026-11-22, owner action, vault backlog item 12) `pull` keeps working through `GIT_ASKPASS` and the lock disappears with nothing printed — the RUNBOOK now says so, but saying so is not a detector, and the only real one is the owner-run negative probe. **Third**, `OQ#1` of the adoption decision is untouched: whether this repository's 61 documentation files belong in the graph is undecided, and the semantic pass that would put them there is the one thing that would change the egress answer above.

## UIP-DL-001 — UIP-P1 `analytics-retirement-and-mount-v9`: the measurement leaves the showcase, the surface built to ask about it leaves with it, and a fixture stops hiding a caching bound

- **Date.** 2026-08-26
- **Type.** Packet — `UIP-P1`, the first rung of the milestone «UI polish of the showcase and app», on branch `feat/ui-polish`, cut from `main` @ `7f1a183`. Product behaviour: a mount generation, a shell change, and the test surface that follows them. **Namespace, declared in `docs/execution-map.md` on the standing precedent for a new track (`CGR-DL-001` (n)):** decisions take `UIP-DL-{NNN}`, invariants `UIP-P{k}-INV-{NNN}`.
- **Scope.** **In:** the copy-forward `app/m/v8/` → `app/m/v9/` with the consent modules dropped and thirteen `trackEvent()` call sites removed; `CACHE_VERSION` `v18` → `v19`; the shell's whole analytics block, the cookie banner and the «Cookie» footer control; the suite that assumed analytics existed; a new two-tier static guard and a new executing guard; `.graphifyignore` (freezing `/m/v8/`); the two native test files the change forces; `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, `docs/execution-map.md` and this entry. **Out, by the ladder:** the privacy-policy document's revision to v1.1 (UIP-P2, and see (j)); header/intro polish (P3); first-entry UX (P4); the launcher icon (P5); retiring `/m/v1/`–`/m/v8/` (owner-level); every deploy, promotion and Play Console action; the GA4 property itself and its retained data, which are Google-side and outside this repository's reach.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. `trackEvent` was never a module — it was a bare global, and thirteen shipped call sites depended on it.** `grep -rn 'import.*trackEvent\|function trackEvent' app/m/v8/` returns nothing: the helper was declared in `app/index.html`'s inline `<head>` block and reached by every surface as an undeclared global. Deleting the block without deleting the callers would have shipped a `ReferenceError` on the first tick, filter toggle, accordion toggle, modal open, activities open or profile create. The handoff named the loader and the seam; the callers came with them by construction, not by scope widening.
- **b. The consent surface was four files, not two.** The handoff named `consent/config.js` and `surfaces/consent.js`, and both were where it said. It did not name `core/storage.js`, which owned the `analytics_consent` key and its two accessors and states in its own header that key identity lives there and nowhere else; nor `app.css`, which carried `.cookie-banner`, `.cookie-banner-actions`, `.cookie-banner-btn(:hover)` and `.footer-legal-btn(:hover)`. A stylesheet that still dresses a deleted surface is how the surface comes back (`FIU-P3-INV-003`'s subject, one milestone earlier).
- **c. `consent-gate.spec.js` was two unrelated files sharing a name.** Its first three describes were the consent gate; its fourth (`:293-359`) was the APK platform probe, which `PPR-P2-INV-002` names in its **Enforced by** field and which has nothing to do with consent. Deleting the file wholesale would have dropped half a live invariant.
- **d. The suite's dependence on analytics ran well past the four spec files the handoff listed.** `app/tests/support/seed.js` declared the storage key, seeded `analytics_consent: 'granted'` into three of four states, routed the three analytics hosts to an empty stub, and exported `gaEvents()`; `behavior.spec.js` consumed it in three assertions; `storage-seam.spec.js` declared `ga_debug` as a shell storage exception and reds on a declared door that no longer exists; `export-contour.spec.js` carried a consent-control scan narrowed for PPR-P2 and a reader list naming two consent functions; `signal-payload.spec.js`, `ship-list.js`, `prev-generation.js`, `privacy-page.spec.js` and `privacy-surface.spec.js` each described the shim in prose that this diff falsifies.
- **e. `APP_VERSION` had exactly one consumer, and it was the event payload.** `export-contour.spec.js` paired the shell's literal against `EXPORT_CONFIG.appVersion` under the name *the app version in the config surface matches the one the shell reports*. With the shim gone the shell reports nothing, and the pairing would have proved that a dead literal still says `1.0.0`.
- **f. The footer's right edge was never held by the «Cookie» control, and the CSS says which rule held it.** `#activitiesBtn { margin-left: auto }` predates PPR-P2 — it stands unchanged in the frozen `app/m/v7/app.css:855-856`, under a comment recording that a positional rule had already cost this footer 605 px once. PPR-P2 added `.footer-legal-btn` with a **second** `margin-left: auto`, and flexbox distributes free space equally among auto margins. Neither rule reads wrongly on its own; nothing in either file says the two now share the gap.
- **g. Two native test files name what the change moves.** `StoreEngineTest.java:565` quoted `app/m/v8/store/bridge.js`, and `EMV-P5-INV-001` reds on a stale mount address under `native/`. `WebViewStorageTest.java` asserted `typeof window.trackEvent === "function"` as anti-vacuity for the native branch — correct while the branch made the helper a no-op, and false the moment the helper was deleted.
- **h. `.graphifyignore` carries a standing instruction in capitals** — `WHEN A NEW GENERATION GOES LIVE, ADD THE ONE IT REPLACES HERE` — and `CLAUDE.md` § Code graph makes freezing a generation a one-line obligation.
- **i. AND THE ONE THING NO ARTEFACT SAID, WHICH THIS PACKET FOUND BY BREAKING IT.** `app/tests/upgrade-path.spec.js` leg 2 — *a client that never touches the banner gets the current mount on the next open* — passed for a reason unrelated to the product. `support/seed.js` registered a `page.route()` to stub the analytics hosts, and enabling routing in Playwright **disables the browser HTTP cache for the whole context**. The stub was written for hermeticity; the cache bypass was an undeclared side effect the leg depended on. Removing the stub with the surface it stubbed turned the leg red with the staged shell in the document. Measured, not inferred: with the mirror's shell header changed to `no-store` the leg goes green again, and a pure copy-forward bump with no analytics removal also passes — so the cause is the fixture, not the mount.
- **j. The published policy describes a control this packet deletes.** `app/privacy.html` §5 and `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md` promise withdrawal «по ссылке «Cookie» в подвале сайта». UIP-P2 revises the document; nothing deploys before merge (`ADR-020`).

### The decisions

- **k. THE CALLERS GO WITH THE SEAM, AND THAT IS ENTAILMENT RATHER THAN SCOPE.** All thirteen `trackEvent()` call sites and their `// Google Analytics event` markers are removed from `/m/v9/`. Rejected: keeping a no-op `trackEvent` stub in the shell so the mount could be copied forward untouched — it leaves the analytics vocabulary in the live tree, makes the new guard's second tier unenforceable where it matters most, and contradicts "the repo ships zero analytics" in the only sense a reader would check.
- **l. TWO REMOVALS BROKE THE PRODUCT AND THE EXECUTING LEGS CAUGHT BOTH — and the two are load-bearing in different degrees, which is worth stating exactly rather than rounding together.** `tier1Count` in `activities.js` was declared under a GA comment and is **read by product logic**: it decides whether the activities window shows its top note. `relation` in `skill-modal.js` is weaker and is described weakly: nothing reads its value, but it assembles the third argument of `openSkillModal(skill, true, `${relation}_chip`)`, so deleting it threw a `ReferenceError` at the call. That third argument is the `source` parameter this same packet marks unread (`void source`) and keeps for exported-arity reasons (see the rejected alternative below), so `relation` stays for the same reason `source` does, not because the product consumes it. Both were restored with comments saying which case they are. They were found by `behavior.spec.js` failing on a `ReferenceError` surfaced through the fixture's `pageerror` listener, which is exactly the executor this packet's plan named for the claim "the app still boots and works on `/m/v9/`". A static scan would have shipped both.
- **m. `consent-gate.spec.js` IS SPLIT AND THE SURVIVOR IS RENAMED `download-offer.spec.js`.** The four platform legs and their byte-verified import harness move across unchanged; the anti-vacuity leg that required `GA_MEASUREMENT_ID` in the shell is re-anchored on the imported functions, the declared token, and the token actually appearing in the user-agent string the legs probe with. `PPR-P2-INV-002`'s **Enforced by** is amended in the same packet. Rejected: keeping the old name — this field names the path, and a file named for a retired subject is how the next reader is misled.
- **n. `APP_VERSION` AND `UI_LOCALE` ARE DELETED AND THE DRIFT LEG IS RETIRED WITH THEM.** `EXPORT_CONFIG.appVersion` becomes the single home; the leg is replaced by one that asserts the version is declared once and that the shell has **not** grown a second copy — so if a copy ever comes back, the drift gate it needs comes back with it. The property "two copies agree" did not go unenforced; it ceased to exist.
- **o. THE FOOTER GETS NO NEW CSS, AND THE RESTORATION IS MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED.** Deleting `.footer-legal-btn` returns the free space to the auto margin that predates it. No positional rule is reintroduced — `footer button:nth-child(3)` would re-arm the same trap for the next button (`LSC-DL-003` (s)) — and the `.control-footer` container is untouched. Because (f) is invisible in the CSS, the claim is carried by an **executing** leg in `behavior.spec.js` that measures the button's bounding box against the footer's content box. Its mutation is recorded: adding a second auto-margined control reds it with *«Подходящие активности» is 284.5 px short of the footer content edge*, which also puts a number on what the «Cookie» button had been doing.
- **p. THE NEW GUARD IS TWO-TIERED, AND THE FROZEN GENERATIONS ARE EXCLUDED BY NAME WITH THE REASON IN THE FILE.** Tier 1 — origins, loader URL, `ga-disable-`, measurement-id pattern — covers every shipped text file, frozen generations included, and is provable over them as they stand: no mount generation has ever contained one. Tier 2 — the vocabulary — covers everything **live**: every shipped text file that is not a frozen generation, which is the shell, `app/sw.js`, `app/offline.html` and the running mount. Rejected: one flat list over everything, which would be red forever against immutable bytes; and scoping the guard to the shell and the mount alone, which is what the first draft did and which left the service worker uncovered — see (x). The stripper tracks string and template quotes rather than pattern-matching comments, for the reason (x) records.
- **q. "EVERY CHANNEL" IS A COMPOSITION AND IS PINNED AS ONE.** The scan's subject is `app/Dockerfile`'s COPY list; `native/www/` is a byte copy of that list under `LSC-P1-INV-002`. A leg asserts that premise so the composition cannot break silently and leave a web-only claim wearing a two-channel name. Rejected: a second token scan over the staged tree, which would duplicate a property already asserted by content hash.
- **r. THE TWO ORPHANED `localStorage` KEYS ARE LEFT IN PLACE.** `analytics_consent` and `ga_debug` stop being written and are not cleared. Adding a `removeItem` would be a write the storage seam must declare and a deletion in a visitor's own browser — the conservative branch of an escalation-list shape, so the conservative branch is taken and the residual is named instead: a returning visitor keeps a stale value recording an answer the product no longer honours in either direction. Neither is family data (`AGENTS.md` §4 untouched). `DECLARED_SHELL_ACCESSES` in `storage-seam.spec.js` is now **empty for the first time since A1-P4**, and because an empty list makes its mirror leg a loop over nothing, that leg gains a branch that asserts the stronger property the empty list actually means — that no shipped shell reaches Web Storage by a literal key at all. A bare `toEqual([])` on the list was written first and rejected on review: it would red on a legitimately-declared future exception **before** the loop could ever check it, leaving the loop dead in both states.
- **s. `export-contour.spec.js`'s CONSENT SCAN IS WIDENED BACK TO SHELL-WIDE, NOT MERELY STRIPPED OF DEAD IDS.** PPR-P2 narrowed it to the intro window and named the price in its own comment: the analytics controls were named after their surface and would have slipped the wide pattern, so the wide form was passing because nobody happened to use a word. The object of the narrowing is gone, so the narrowing goes with it — and the stricter property PPR-P2 bought on the narrow scope (the link gated on the declaration alone) is **kept**, not traded back. Of the three-name reader list, only `localStorage` survives: it is the general form, and the other two named functions that no longer exist anywhere.
- **t. THE UPGRADE-PATH LEG IS REPAIRED BY MAKING ITS DEPENDENCE EXPLICIT, NOT BY RESTORING THE BYPASS.** Leg 2 now clears the browser HTTP cache through CDP, immediately before the navigation, under a comment that states what the fixture was hiding and what the real bound is. Rejected: re-registering a pass-through route to get the side effect back — it would restore the green and the concealment together. **The bound itself is a finding and is recorded as one:** the shell is served `public, max-age=3600, must-revalidate`, network-first means `fetch()`, and `fetch()` reads the HTTP cache — so an installed client that reopens the app **within the hour** gets its own cached shell however new the waiting worker is. The property is true after that hour, or after the client accepts the banner (leg 1), and not before. Nothing in this packet changes that behaviour; what changes is that it is now written down.
- **u. TWO NATIVE TEST FILES ARE AMENDED, AND NO PRODUCTION NATIVE SOURCE IS TOUCHED.** `StoreEngineTest.java`'s mount address moves to `v9` (forced by the copy-forward, `EMV-P5-INV-001`), and `WebViewStorageTest.java`'s anti-vacuity probe is **inverted** — `typeof window.trackEvent` must now be `"undefined"`, with a second probe requiring the same of `dataLayer`. Strictly stronger; the anti-vacuity work moves to the `IS_NATIVE_SHELL` probe already standing above it. `grep` over `native/android/app/src/main/**` for `gtag|analytics|consent|dataLayer` returns zero, before and after.
- **v. `embedded-js-parse.spec.js`'s SKIP TABLE IS RE-READ, NOT RE-TRUSTED.** Editing `WebViewStorageTest.java` shifted three declared skip lines by 29; the table asserts its own line numbers precisely so a drifting entry reds. Each of the three was located and re-read before its number was changed.
- **w. THREE HEADER COMMENTS THAT CITE THE REVERSED DECISION ARE CORRECTED, AND THE DOM BASELINE MOVE IS ACCEPTED AS THE PRICE.** `app/index.html` explained the absence of telemetry on `#aboutBtn`, `#diaryBtn` and `#apkBtn` by «решение владельца 2026-08-16, гейт D» — the decision that kept GA4 until authentication at L4, and the one this packet exists because the vault reversed. Leaving them would have left a false attribution in the file this packet edits most. `dom-parity.spec.js` captures the header **including comments**, so correcting them moves `dom-desktop/header.html` and `dom-mobile/header.html`; the replacements were shortened for that reason, and the diff is comments only — no element, attribute or text node — which is why the two `header.png` shots stay in the green set.
- **x. TWO DEFECTS IN THE NEW GUARD WERE FOUND BY ADVERSARIAL REVIEW AFTER IT WAS FIRST WRITTEN AND GREEN, AND BOTH ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED.** A guard that has been wrong once is worth more with its history attached than without it. **(1) The comment stripper failed OPEN — the same class `LSC-DL-004` cost this repository once.** Its first form ran three `.replace()` passes with the block-comment pass before the line-comment pass, so a `/*` inside a `//` line opened a pseudo block comment running to the next real `*/`. `surfaces/diary.js:40` ends a sentence with `…только core/*.`, and **18 files of the live mount lost real text, 296 characters of it in `diary.js` alone, including `function el()` and the module's imports** — a region in which any forbidden token would have been invisible while every leg reported green. Folding the passes into one left-to-right alternation fixes that case and leaves a second standing (a `/*` inside a STRING, which is the shape of the loader URL itself), so the stripper is now a character scanner that tracks quotes, with `the stripper removes comments and nothing else` as its detector. **(2) Tier 2 did not cover the service worker.** The live scope was written as "the shell or the mount prefix", silently excluding `app/sw.js` and `app/offline.html` — live, editable, browser-executed, the first of them running on every navigation of an installed client. Both holes are now mutation-proven shut. **Four smaller repairs came from the same review and are named so the list is complete:** the extension filter gained a declared binary set and a leg that reds on any shipped file type it neither reads nor declares (silent truncation reads as full coverage); the leg proving the stripper strips analytics prose was **derived** from whatever files carry such prose rather than naming `/m/v8/surfaces/consent.js` by path, which `mount-reference.spec.js` correctly red as a test-side reference to a generation nothing runs; the replacement `APP_VERSION` leg lost an assertion that could never fail (`[^']+` already guarantees a non-empty capture) and its second-copy guard was widened past the single `const` spelling; and `analytics-egress.spec.js` gained the interaction leg its own header had promised — it claimed to be able to catch "a beacon fired from a handler" while every leg only navigated, so the leg now drives every surface that used to emit and asserts the network log is still empty afterwards.

### Alternatives rejected

- **Leaving `/m/v8/` in place and editing it.** Refused by `ADR-024` / `A1-DL-004`: bytes at a published mount URL are never rewritten, and a `CACHE_VERSION` bump alone does not deliver changed bytes inside the 30-day immutable window.
- **Keeping the consent surface and defaulting it to "denied".** That is a switched-off mechanism, not a removed one; it keeps the loader, the seam, the storage key and the banner in the tree, and leaves `PDR-019`'s deviation alive with a different default. The vault annotation is a reversal, not a change of default.
- **A single flat forbidden-token list over the whole repository.** It reds on `data/mvp_masterplan.md`, a superseded historical artifact that ships on no channel, and on the frozen generations' immutable `trackEvent()` calls. Scanning the ship list is the honest subject.
- **Deleting `consent-gate.spec.js` outright.** Drops half of `PPR-P2-INV-002`.
- **Removing the now-unread `source` and `action` parameters of `openSkillModal` / `closeSkillModal`.** Both functions are re-exported through `app.js`'s parity seam, so their arity is observable from outside; changing an exported signature in a packet about analytics would be changing the wrong subject. They are marked as unread in place instead, and are a P3 candidate.

### Effects

- **Added:** `app/m/v9/**` (50 files — `/m/v8/`'s 52 minus `consent/config.js` and `surfaces/consent.js`); `app/tests/analytics-absence.spec.js` (**17** legs, `contract`); `app/tests/analytics-egress.spec.js` (**8** legs, `behavior`); `app/tests/download-offer.spec.js` (5 legs, `contract` — 4 carried across plus a re-anchored anti-vacuity leg); a two-leg footer-geometry describe in `behavior.spec.js`; `app/m/v8/` in `.graphifyignore`; `UIP-P1-INV-001`; and this entry.
- **Removed:** the shell's whole `<!-- Google tag (gtag.js) -->` block except `window.IS_NATIVE_SHELL`, which is lifted into a `<script>` of its own — and which **no mount module reads**: the mount answers the channel question itself from `window.Capacitor`, and the flag's readers are four specs; the cookie banner and the «Cookie» footer control; 13 `trackEvent()` call sites across 7 surfaces; `consent/config.js` and `surfaces/consent.js`; the storage key and its two accessors; six CSS rules and their section; `app/tests/consent-surface.spec.js` (12 legs) and the consent half of `consent-gate.spec.js` (11 legs); `gaEvents()`, the analytics-host route stub and three seeded `granted` values in `support/seed.js`; three `gaEvents` assertions in `behavior.spec.js`; the `ga_debug` declaration in `storage-seam.spec.js`; the `APP_VERSION` drift leg.
- **Operability.** **No new knobs and no new signals this packet.** The mount goes from four device-local config surfaces to **three** — `store/`, `export/`, `channel/` — as `consent/config.js` and its three knobs (`stateGranted`, `stateDenied`, `shellBridge`, all `changed_in: PPR-DL-002`) retire. **Fourteen GA4 event kinds disappear, named so the loss is checkable:** `skill_complete`, `skill_view`, `skill_modal_close`, `graph_navigate`, `activity_skill_open`, `activities_open`, `category_toggle`, `onboarding_shown`, `onboarding_dismissed`, `profile_click`, `profile_create`, `filter_zpd_toggle`, `zpd_empty_state_shown`, `app_debug_ping`. Seams removed with them: `window.theygrowAnalytics`, `trackEvent`, `window.dataLayer`, `gtag`, `window['ga-disable-<id>']`, the `?dbg=1|0` / `ga_debug` switch, `GA_MEASUREMENT_ID`, `UI_LOCALE`. The device-local signal surface (`core/signals.js`, `emitSignal`, sink = device console) is untouched and never routed into analytics. **Net egress change: strictly negative on the web channel, zero on the native channel. No new egress of any kind.**
- **Measured, on the host, 2026-08-26, and stated per project so a CI run can be checked against it rather than eyeballed.** `contract` **1267**, `behavior` **110**, `dom-desktop` **14**, `dom-mobile` **16** (+1 skipped), `native` **35** (+5 skipped) — **1442 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed** across the five non-visual projects, after the two DOM baselines were re-blessed. The four Python suites **257 passed**, unchanged: this packet touches no Python, which is also why `pre-commit run --files <the new and renamed paths>` reports `ruff`, `ruff-format` and `mypy` as *(no files to check)* — **no new runtime import enters the repository, so no `additional_dependencies` stub is owed**. `pre-commit run --all-files` green, with no file modified by a hook. The 6 skips are pre-existing and are the same 6 the previous milestone predicted.
- **Baselines.** **Four DOM baselines moved, in two pairs, and no others.** `dom-desktop/control-footer.html` and `dom-mobile/control-footer.html` lost the PPR-P2 comment block and the `#cookieSettingsBtn` button. `dom-desktop/header.html` and `dom-mobile/header.html` moved for **comments only** — three header comments attributed the absence of telemetry on those controls to the very owner decision this packet acts on the reversal of, and were corrected in the same pass (decision (w)); no element, attribute or text node changed, which is why the two `header.png` shots stay in the green set. The `native` project shares `dom-mobile`'s snapshot path, so six failing tests moved four files. Each move was read as a diff before it was blessed. **The 20 visual PNGs are owner-run and are NOT re-blessed here**; `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Closing a milestone step 4 carries the expectation and, deliberately, no predicted pixel bands — PPR's numbers describe a different change and guessing UIP's would be inventing evidence.
- **What it hands on.** **First and most prominent, because only the owner can close it: a revision carrying UIP-P1 without UIP-P2 must not be promoted.** After this packet the shipped `app/privacy.html` §5 promises a «Cookie» control that no longer exists. The exposure window opens at **promotion**, not at merge — `ADR-020` keeps anything from deploying before merge, so nothing is exposed while both packets sit on this branch. `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Promotion + rollback now carries that as a numbered pre-promotion condition. **Second, the caching bound in (t)** — real, previously unstated, and unchanged by this packet. **Third, an installed client whose cached shell predates this packet still holds the loader in its own bytes** until its next navigation replaces the shell; no test here can see a real device's cache age, and § Promotion + rollback step 5's installed-client check is what observes it. **Fourth, `PPR-P2-INV-001` is retired unobserved on CI** — the field it carried can no longer be discharged. **Fifth, two unread parameters** (`openSkillModal(…, source)`, `closeSkillModal(action)`) are marked in place and left for P3. **Sixth, the GA4 property itself** — its existence, its retained data and its disposition — is Google-side, untouched, and nothing in this repository can reach it.
