## UIP-DL-002 — UIP-P2 `privacy-policy-v1-1`: the document catches up with the product, and the four things that had to move with it

- **Date.** 2026-08-26
- **Type.** Packet — `UIP-P2`, the second rung of the milestone «UI polish of the showcase and app», on branch `feat/ui-polish`, cut from `main` @ `7f1a183`, following `UIP-P1` @ `35be8f9`. The owner's published document, the delivery rule for its address, and the guards behind both. Repo-side effect of vault `PDR-035`'s 2026-08-25 annotation and `ADR-043`'s reversal of the same date; `PDR-019`'s accepted deviation ends here for the second and last time, by removal of its object rather than by consent.
- **Scope.** **In:** `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md` (new); `app/privacy.html` (the conversion, the links, the head comment); `app/nginx.conf` (one `location`); `app/tests/server.js` (its mirror); `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js`, `app/tests/privacy-surface.spec.js`, `app/tests/delivery-contract.spec.js`; one comment sentence each in `app/tests/export-contour.spec.js` and `app/playwright.config.js`; `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/execution-map.md` and this entry. **Out, by the ladder:** header/intro polish (P3); first-entry UX (P4); the launcher icon (P5); retiring `/m/v1/`–`/m/v8/` (owner-level); every deploy, promotion and Play Console action, including the Data safety form; the GA4 property itself; and §2's controller identity, which is being corrected on a parallel track and whose names and addresses this packet does not touch.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. The falsified statements were eight, not one, and only three of them were in §5.** Enumerated off the shipped page rather than off the section headings: the Краткая сводка bullet («GA4 работает лишь после явного согласия на cookie»); §2's contact-purpose list, which named «cookie» among the things to write in about; §5's three analytics paragraphs — the purpose and consent-mode paragraph, the retention-and-third-party paragraph, and the cookie-choice scoping paragraph; §9's `| Данные GA4 | 14 месяцев |` row; and the two edition literals in the header block. The handoff named «плюс GA4 (or equivalent) in §1»; §1 carries no analytics sentence at all — its structural claim is «Политика разделяет три ситуации», which stays true — and the equivalent is the Краткая сводка bullet, which is where the two-contour split is actually worded.
- **b. Deleting §5's paragraph 4 would have deleted two live third-party references with it.** «Информацию Google о конфиденциальности можно прочитать по адресу …, а информацию Cloudflare — по адресу …» sits inside the GA4 retention paragraph, but the processors it names are the **hosting** ones from paragraph 1 (Google Cloud in the EU region, Cloudflare in front), which the removal does not touch. §7 also names both in its provider set. A clean paragraph deletion would have left §7 pointing at a §5 that no longer disclosed them.
- **c. The page's own head comment asserted the property this packet reverses**, in capitals — «НЕТ ни одного `<a>`. Все адреса в тексте показаны как `<code>`, ровно так же, как они набраны в источнике» — and named `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md` as its source. Both sentences are false after this diff.
- **d. The change-history parser was pinned to the literal `1.0` and would have gone green against the wrong row.** `privacy-page.spec.js:71` read the effective date out of `/\|\s*1\.0\s*\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|/`. On a v1.1 document that regex keeps matching — the historical row is still there — so the guard would have paired the page against the **superseded** edition's date while the current one went unchecked. It was correct exactly once, for the only edition that had ever existed. This is entailment for any v1.1, on either fork of the file question.
- **e. `docs/RUNBOOK.md` addressed two of the four date literals by line numbers that were already wrong.** Step 6 named `app/privacy.html:103` and `:263`; PPR-P3 had added four comment lines and the real positions were `:107` and `:267`. The Markdown's `:5` and `:145` were still right. An owner following that step on promotion day would have opened the file at a paragraph of body text.
- **f. `/privacy.html` answered `200` with the document, and nothing said which address was canonical.** The file ships to the web root under its own name (`app/Dockerfile:41`), so `try_files $uri` in `location /` served it directly. The `= /privacy/` block four lines above already had the shape of the fix.
- **g. The step-0 promotion condition instructed its own deletion.** `docs/RUNBOOK.md:68-69`: «Delete this step when UIP-P2 has landed and the document says what the product does.»
- **h. Debts 29, 30 and 34 could not be read from this machine.** The bridge lives in the vault; the on-disk clone's body dates from 2026-08-21 (L2's close) and its numbered rollup stops at 13, so those debts belong to a rebuild later than anything here. No vault document was read for this packet — the session ran no `git`, so no pull, and `CLAUDE.md` forbids reading that cache un-pulled. The three debts are taken from the handoff verbatim and are recorded as such.

### The decisions

- **i. A NEW FILE, `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md`; v1.0 STAYS BYTE-UNTOUCHED.** The version is in the filename by this repository's own convention (`kb-v{N}.json`, `m/v{N}/`, and the document itself), and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` already excluded the **version-agnostic** prefix `docs/privacy-policy-v` from the whitespace hooks — the hygiene config was written expecting more editions, and v1.1's Markdown hard line breaks came through the gate untouched because of it. Rejected: bumping the edition inside the existing file, on the ground that the filename would then state a version its content contradicts.
- **j. THE PUBLISHED PAGE IS STILL ONE PAGE AT ONE ADDRESS, AND SUPERSEDED EDITIONS ARE NOT REPUBLISHED.** §10 of the document promises «Действующая редакция всегда размещена по адресу …/privacy», and `app/nginx.conf` deliberately serves it `max-age=3600, must-revalidate` and never `immutable` for exactly this reason (`PPR-DL-001`). Publishing v1.0 as a second page would be a new public surface with a new promise attached to it. Rejected also: a «superseded» banner prepended to v1.0 on the `data/mvp_masterplan.md` precedent (`M1-DL-001`) — that is retroactive editing of a published edition, and what it would buy is bought instead by a guard (decision (n)) that pins the conversion to the newest edition on disk.
- **k. §5 IS REWRITTEN TO THREE PARAGRAPHS AND SAYS THE POSITIVE THING, NOT ONLY THE ABSENCE.** Paragraph 1 keeps the hosting disclosure and **absorbs** the Google and Cloudflare policy references that decision (b) found stranded. Paragraph 2 keeps the access logs. Paragraph 3 is new: «Аналитики нет ни на сайте, ни в приложении… Поэтому согласие на аналитические cookie не запрашивается, и баннера согласия на сайте нет.» That is the sentence the handoff asked for — neither channel carries analytics — and it is backed by `UIP-P1-INV-001` in both its static and executing halves rather than asserted. **What §5 deliberately does NOT say: anything about cookies in general.** Cloudflare may set operational cookies of its own on this zone; this repository cannot observe that, and a sentence about it would be a claim the product cannot back. The document never enumerated cookies, and after this revision it does not mention them except to say that consent to *analytics* cookies is not asked for. **This was raised as an escalation and resolved by the orchestrator on 2026-08-26 in favour of silence, on the record that v1.0 was already silent on operational cookies and that removing analytics removes the only context in which they appeared. It is an orchestrator call, not an owner decision, and the owner can override it: taking the other branch costs one paragraph and a change-history row.**
- **l. §2 LOSES ONE WORD AND NOTHING ELSE.** «Используйте этот адрес для вопросов о сайте, cookie, закрытом тестировании…» is falsified by the removal, and it is in a file this packet already opens, so it is corrected here rather than left standing. **The controller's name, e-mail and the postal-address sentence are untouched** — that section is a parallel track's subject, and this edit is deliberately word-level so the two do not collide.
- **m. THE PAGE GETS LINKS, AND THE ENFORCED PROPERTY BECOMES A COMPOSITION RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE.** Two `/` back-links (before `<h1>` and after the closing `<hr>`, relative so both channels stay byte-identical and no second absolute address enters the document), and every EXTERNAL address becomes an `<a>` carrying `rel="noopener noreferrer"` with the URL still as its visible text. **The sweep is the class, not the four the debt names:** the Israeli supervisory authority's address in §8 is the same defect in the same file, and a reader who needs to file a complaint is the last one to strand with an unclickable URL. **The two SELF addresses stay `<code>`,** which is the half of PPR-P1's rule that was load-bearing: it keeps `export-contour.spec.js`'s «quotes `policyUrl`, never links it» true and the `FIU-P3-INV-002` amendment narrow. Rejected: `target="_blank"` without `rel` — the referrer would tell Google, Cloudflare, GitHub or a supervisory authority that this reader was on the privacy policy, which is a small disclosure and the one this document is least entitled to make. **The Markdown keeps backticked URLs:** the source is the owner's text, the page is its presentation, and linking changes no word a reader sees.
- **n. DEBT 34 IS ANSWERED BY A GUARD, NOT BY A COLLAPSE, AND THAT IS A CONSTRAINT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE.** There is nowhere for a single date literal to live: the web path is buildless by contract and `PPR-DL-001` (a) refused a renderer **by name** for the one page whose whole value is that it runs none. A committed dev-time generator on the `stage-webdir.js` precedent was rejected as a new build surface far outside this packet and as the thing the hand-conversion-plus-pairing design deliberately chose against. What is bought instead is that the four literals become a **derived** set — `UIP-P2-INV-001` — and that `docs/RUNBOOK.md` step 6 addresses them by content anchor rather than by the line numbers decision (e) found stale.
- **o. DEBT 30 IS FIXED BY A `301`, NOT BY `rel="canonical"`.** It removes the second address rather than annotating it, it reuses the shape of the `= /privacy/` block four lines above including the `absolute_redirect off` repair that already cost this project a production defect (`PPR-DL-004`), and it puts no third absolute-address literal into a document that ships byte-identically to both channels. `try_files /privacy.html =404` in the `= /privacy` block is a **filesystem** lookup and is not re-matched against locations, so the document keeps being served — asserted from outside by a leg of its own rather than by citing nginx documentation. **Both `NON_SHELL_PAGES` entries stay:** the worker compares `url.pathname` and sees the `/privacy.html` navigation before any redirect is followed, and the Capacitor channel has no nginx and still serves the file under its own name. `rel="canonical"` was kept as the documented fallback in case the bidirectional `NON_SHELL_PAGES` guard forbade a redirecting shipped page; it did not, and the fallback was not needed.
- **p. STEP 0 IS AMENDED RATHER THAN DELETED, WHICH OVERRIDES ITS OWN WRITTEN INSTRUCTION (decision (g)).** What the condition is about is that the code removal and the policy revision reach a parent in the **same** promotion; that stays true for every promotion while this milestone is open, and a tripwire deleted the moment it first goes green is removed at exactly the point it becomes cheap to keep. It is retired at milestone close, with the milestone it belongs to. The `PPR-DL-003` (g) note on why it is numbered `0` is kept: steps 1–5 are cross-referenced by number elsewhere in the file.
- **q. THE EFFECTIVE DATE IS `26.08.2026`, THE DAY THIS PACKET LANDED, AND THE RESIDUAL IS THE OWNER'S — AGAIN.** The rule is `PPR-DL-001` (f): the date is the day the document becomes readable, which is this day at the earliest. **What this packet cannot close is the day the owner actually promotes.** If that is later, the literal is wrong again and the fix is the same four-token edit — now guarded, so a partial edit is red, and now addressed by content anchor in § Privacy policy step 6 rather than by stale line numbers.
- **r. THE INVARIANT AMENDMENT IS BY REFERENCE, LEAVING `PPR-P1-INV-001`'s BODY BYTE-UNTOUCHED.** The plan had said the Scope sentence naming `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md` would be edited in place. It is not: this log's standing convention is that the original record stays as written and a dated amendment bullet carries the correction, and the Scope sentence was **true of PPR-P1**. Editing it would rewrite what that packet asserted.

### Alternatives rejected

- **A second published page for edition 1.0** — see (j). A new public surface, and a second address for a document whose §10 promises one.
- **A client-side Markdown renderer, so one file could be the single source** — refused by name at `PPR-DL-001` (a) and refused again here: it needs a `<script>` on the one page whose value is that it runs none.
- **Leaving §2's «cookie» for a later packet** because the section is on a parallel track — rejected: a known-false statement in a file already being edited does not survive the pass, and the edit is word-level and touches no identity field.
- **Linking only the four third-party policies the debt names** — rejected under (m): the debt names a class.
- **Deleting step 0 as it instructed** — see (p).

### Effects

- **Added:** `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md` (the current edition); one `location` block in `app/nginx.conf` and its mirror branch in `app/tests/server.js`; **17 test legs** — 10 in `privacy-page.spec.js` (7 allowlist including one self-proving, 5 edition-pairing, minus the 2 the old date leg and the `<a` token leg carried), 3 in `privacy-surface.spec.js`, 4 in `delivery-contract.spec.js` (2 live, 2 config-shape); `UIP-P2-INV-001`; and this entry.
- **Removed:** three §5 paragraphs, one §9 table row, one Краткая сводка clause and one word in §2, in both files; the `'<a '` entry from `privacy-page.spec.js`'s forbidden-token list, replaced by the allowlist describe; the `1.0`-pinned `effectiveDates()` helper.
- **Changed, the owner's document:** the edition block (`1.0` → `1.1`, `23.08.2026` → `26.08.2026`) and the change-history table, which now carries both rows. `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md` is **not** changed, at all.
- **Operability: none** (`ADR-013` / contract §4.7). No knob, no signal, no `changed_in` provenance, no config surface added or removed; `CHANNEL_CONFIG` is untouched and `policyUrl` still names `/privacy`, which the redirect makes the only answering spelling. **Net egress: unchanged, and the one change that could be misread as egress is named so it can be checked** — turning a `<code>` URL into an `<a>` starts no request, the visitor chooses to navigate, and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` keeps the referrer from reaching the third party. The detector is `privacy-surface.spec.js`'s existing leg, which records the network log for the navigation and asserts zero third-party requests; it stayed green with the links in place.
- **A guard hole was found in this packet's own work, by mutation, and closed.** Deleting `location = /privacy.html` from `app/nginx.conf` left `delivery-contract.spec.js` **entirely green — 361 passed, 0 failed** — because `app/tests/server.js` mirrors the redirect, every live leg runs against the mirror, and the drift guard asks only whether nginx grew a location the mirror LACKS, never the reverse. That is `PPR-DL-004`'s failure class one layer over: the mirror is never wrong, so the mirror cannot witness what the shipped config says. A config-shape leg was added naming **both** non-canonical spellings by location, with its own armed-parser leg; the mutation then reds naming the location, and deleting `= /privacy/` instead reds naming that one.
- **Measured, on the host, 2026-08-26, per project so a CI run can be checked against it rather than eyeballed.** `contract` **1281** (1267 at UIP-P1), `behavior` **113** (110), `dom-desktop` **14**, `dom-mobile` **16** (+1 skipped), `native` **35** (+5 skipped) — **1459 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed** across the five non-visual projects, via `PARITY_NO_DOCKER=1 scripts/parity-suite.sh`. `pre-commit run --all-files` green with no file modified by a hook, and `pre-commit run --files` over the new and changed paths reports `ruff`, `ruff-format` and `mypy` as *(no files to check)* — **no runtime import enters the repository, so no `additional_dependencies` stub is owed** (contract §4.8). The 6 skips are pre-existing and are the same 6 UIP-P1 recorded.
- **Baselines.** **None moved, and that is the expectation this packet stated in advance rather than a relief afterwards:** no DOM baseline contains the policy page, and the shell is untouched. `dom-desktop`, `dom-mobile` and `native` are green on the committed baselines. The 20 visual PNGs remain owner-run and are not re-blessed here.
- **What it hands on.** **First, and only the owner can close it: the effective date is `26.08.2026`, and if the promotion is later than that day the literal is wrong.** The fix is the four-token edit at `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Privacy policy step 6, which now names the four by content anchor and warns that the `1.0` history row is frozen and does not move with the date. *(**Closed at UIP-P6.** The promotion is later than that day, so the literal was wrong; the four-token edit ran and the date is `27.08.2026`. See `UIP-DL-006`. The decision at (q) above is left as written — it records what this packet decided, and predicted this correction in its own words.)* **Second, the pre-promotion condition is satisfied but the step stays** (decision (p)): both greps read `0`, and the step is retired at milestone close, not here. **Third, production nginx is unobserved.** The suite drives `app/tests/server.js`; what the shipped container does with `location = /privacy.html` is the owner's `curl` smoke against the tagged revision, and § Promotion + rollback step 3 now has a second address to check. **Fourth, the cookie question is an orchestrator call, not an owner decision** (decision (k)) and is overridable at the cost of one paragraph. **Fifth, whether edition 1.0 was ever read by a parent is not a repository fact** — the PPR milestone is merged and **not promoted**, so the change history records 1.0 and its stated effective date and claims nothing about a window of force. **Sixth, `native/android/app/src/main/assets/public/**` is stale** — pre-PPR-P3 text, `/m/v8/`, `content="none"`, the previous controller name and the `22.08.2026` date. It is git-ignored `cap sync` output regenerated at APK build time; the next release build is what refreshes it, and nothing in this packet touches it.

## UIP-DL-003 — UIP-P3 `header-and-intro`: the top of the page stops saying things twice, and the intro window stops arriving uninvited

- **Date.** 2026-08-26
- **Type.** Packet — `UIP-P3`, the third rung of the milestone «UI polish of the showcase and app», on branch `feat/ui-polish`, cut from `main` @ `7f1a183`, following `UIP-P1` @ `35be8f9` and `UIP-P2` @ `2b16a3a`. Product behaviour on both channels: the shell, the running mount `/m/v9/` edited **in place**, and the test surface that follows them. This is the milestone's actual subject — P1 and P2 cleared analytics and the policy document out of the way of it.
- **Scope.** **In:** `app/index.html`; `app/m/v9/` — `app.css`, `app.js`, `surfaces/onboarding.js`, `core/storage.js`, one comment in `surfaces/channel.js`; `app/tests/` — `support/seed.js`, `behavior.spec.js`, `channel-composition.spec.js`, `export-contour.spec.js`, `delivery-contract.spec.js`, `upgrade-path.spec.js`, one comment block in `analytics-egress.spec.js`; four DOM baselines; `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (one smoke literal), `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/execution-map.md`, this entry. **Out:** no mount generation (`/m/v9/` is unpublished on this branch — `ADR-020`), no `CACHE_VERSION` bump (v19 stands, one bump per milestone), no frozen generation, nothing under `native/` except the git-ignored staging re-run, no knob, no signal, no egress.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. The owner's six items are stated in product terms; four of the six map onto elements whose current shape argues against the change, and each argument is a recorded decision rather than an accident.** The header subtitle and the intro window really do say the same thing twice. The «?» control, the «Скачать APK» label, the page band above the table and the first-run auto-open are each the product of a named packet with a written reason — `L3-P3` for the first two and the auto-open's «closes for good» semantics, `DIA-P2` for the band. None of them can be removed as tidying; each is a reversal and is logged as one below.
- **b. The band above the table is web-only, and the intro window is not.** `#webChannelNote` ships `hidden` and is revealed by `surfaces/channel.js` on `!native` alone, because inside the app the device store is the source of truth and «the only copy is in this browser» is false. The intro window's markup is one set of bytes for both channels. So "carry the sentence into the window" is only truthful as an **element** move; folding the words into a shared paragraph would ship a false statement to the APK.
- **c. The intro window does not already say it.** Its first paragraph says personal data stays on this device and is sent nowhere. That is where the data lives; it is not that there is no second copy of it. Item 1's «carry the sentence there if the window does not already say it» resolves to: carry it.
- **d. `onboarding_dismissed` has exactly one reader, and item 6 deletes it.** `checkAndShowOnboarding()` was the only caller of `readOnboardingDismissed()`; `closeOnboardingModal()` wrote the key on all three doors. Removing the auto-open leaves a key written into every parent's browser on every close and read by nobody.
- **e. The tab title is checked in exactly one place, and it is a hand-written literal in a procedure.** `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Promotion + rollback step 3 greps `<title>Child Dev Tracker</title>` against the tagged revision. The same step already carries a warning to read the mount generation out of `app/index.html` rather than out of its own sentence — because that literal went stale at `/m/v6/`, `/m/v7/`, `/m/v8/` and `/m/v9/`. Item 5 puts a second literal into the same shape.
- **f. The label debt is written down as a debt, with an owner.** `PPR-P2-INV-002`'s Scope ends by saying it asserts "nothing about the control's LABEL, which still reads «Скачать APK» on a desktop where nothing is downloadable and is carried as debt rather than fixed here." Item 4 is the closure of exactly that sentence.
- **g. The upgrade-path fixture stages a pair no real client can hold, and this packet is what made that visible.** `support/prev-generation.js` derives the "previous generation" by repointing the CURRENT shell one mount back, and says so on the record — it is "the WEAKER of the two things … no longer the historical bytes". The current shell defines no `trackEvent`; frozen `/m/v8/` still calls it from `openOnboardingModal()`. That pair only executes if the intro opens, which the seeded fixture prevented by carrying `onboarding_dismissed`. Removing the key from the seeds made two `upgrade-path` legs red with `ReferenceError: trackEvent is not defined`. **It is not a product defect:** a real client on `/m/v8/` holds the shell that shipped with it, gtag shim included, and takes `/m/v9/` the moment it takes the new shell.

### The decisions

- **h. THE SENTENCE MOVES AS AN ELEMENT, KEEPING ITS ID, ITS `hidden` AND ITS ONE-LINE REVEAL.** `<p id="webChannelNote">` is cut from between `</header>` and the table and pasted into `.onboarding-modal-body`, directly after the paragraph about where data lives. `surfaces/channel.js` is **byte-unchanged** apart from its comment: same id, same `hidden = native`. The id is kept deliberately — it names the channel whose statement this is, not the place it sits. The `channel-note` class goes, with its rule: it drew a full-width band, and inside the window it is a paragraph among paragraphs. Follows (b) and (c). *Rejected:* re-wording the fact into the shared prose — it would be false inside the APK.
- **i. AND THE PRICE IS NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED: a web visitor now meets «there is no backup copy of this» only if they press the header control, where before they met it without opening anything — which is precisely the reason `DIA-P2` put it above the table.** Items 1 and 6 together do this; the orchestrator confirmed branch A (move it entirely) on 2026-08-26 after the plan costed the alternative. The alternative, if it is ever wanted back, is one `<p>`, one rule and one leg: a short line above the table with the full text in the window.
- **j. THE «i» REPLACES THE «?», AND NOTHING ELSE ABOUT THAT CONTROL MOVES.** Two `<path>` elements inside the same `<circle r="9">`. Id, class, `title`/`aria-label` «О приложении», the handler, the window and the policy link inside it are untouched. The sign was wrong for what is behind it: a question mark offers help with a difficulty, and what the button opens is an account of the product and a document about data — information, not assistance.
- **k. THE HEADER CONTROL FOR THE APP LOSES ITS VISIBLE LABEL AND STOPS PROMISING A DOWNLOAD — AND THIS REVERSES `L3-P3`, WHOSE ARGUMENT WAS MEASURED.** That packet deliberately kept `#apkBtn`'s label visible at the mobile viewport, against the rule its two neighbours follow, with two measurements in the stylesheet — the labelled button ends at 348 of 360 at the narrow width and at 400 of 412 at the wide one — and the reason «значок телефона со стрелкой сам по себе не называет ничего»: a parent arriving at the showcase saw a grey tile where an app was being offered. **The owner reversed it on 2026-08-25.** The `<span class="header-action-label">` and both `#apkBtn` exceptions in `app.css` are deleted, and the control becomes an icon like the archive and the diary. **What the reversal costs is exactly what L3-P3 measured** — a sighted parent on a phone now reads no name on that control — and what it buys is that the control stops naming an action it does not perform. The accessible name never depended on the span and is unchanged in kind: `title`/`aria-label` become «Приложение для Android», closing the debt at (f). The guard forbids the regression in its general form — the name may not match `/скачать/i` — because the defect was the promise of a download, not one particular wording.
- **l. THE AUTO-OPEN GOES, AND THE WHOLE `onboarding_dismissed` PATH GOES WITH IT, NOT JUST THE READ.** `checkAndShowOnboarding()` is deleted from `surfaces/onboarding.js` and from `app.js`'s `init()`; the key, `readOnboardingDismissed()` and `writeOnboardingDismissed()` leave `core/storage.js`. Keeping the writer would mean writing a value into a parent's browser that nothing will ever read. Follows (d). **Values already stored are left exactly where they are** — the `UIP-DL-001` precedent for `ga_debug` and `iosInstallDismissed`, for the same reason both times: clearing is also a write, and there is no reason for it. `core/storage.js`'s orphan-key paragraph gains a third name.
- **m. THE REACHABILITY OBLIGATION BECOMES A NAMED INVARIANT, `UIP-P3-INV-001`, RATHER THAN A LEG INSIDE SOMEONE ELSE'S.** Once the window no longer comes to the parent, the control is the only path to both texts inside it — the policy link, one of its exactly two carriers (`PDR-035`, annotation 2026-08-21), and the sentence from (h). The invariant has two halves, deliberately separately armed: nothing opens the window by itself, and the control is **offered** on a first run and really opens it. Both mutations were run and reverted, and their dispositions differ — 6 failed / 1 passed against a restored auto-open, 5 failed / 2 passed against an unwired control — which is what makes the pair evidence rather than decoration. *Rejected:* one leg asserting «the control works», which would answer «withheld» and «inert» with the same red and name neither.
- **n. THE TAB TITLE GETS A GUARD, NOT ONLY A CORRECTED GREP (`UIP-P3-INV-002`).** `app/tests/delivery-contract.spec.js` reads the shell's `<title>` (comment-stripped, so this packet's own explanation of the rename cannot be mistaken for the title) and the literal the RUNBOOK's smoke actually greps, and requires them equal, with an anti-vacuity leg because two null matches would make the pairing green about nothing. The value is deliberately **not** pinned: renaming the product is a product decision; renaming it in one of two places is the defect. Follows (e). *Rejected:* correcting the RUNBOOK and stopping there — that is the state that produced four stale mount references, and the failure it yields here is a false RED at promotion, on the one procedure whose job is to say whether the revision is sound.
- **o. THE UPGRADE-PATH FIXTURE CARRIES THE PREVIOUS GENERATION'S STORAGE VOCABULARY, AS A LITERAL, IN ITS OWN FILE.** `installPreviousGeneration()` seeds `onboarding_dismissed: 'true'` alongside `STATES.seeded`. The key is dead in `/m/v9/` and alive in the frozen `/m/v8/` this fixture stages, and a frozen mount cannot be edited (`A1-DL-004`). It is a literal rather than an import precisely because the constant it would import no longer exists — the current mount is right not to have it. Follows (g). *Rejected:* `allowConsoleErrors` on those two legs, which would mask exactly the class of signal that check exists to catch.
- **p. `/m/v9/` IS EDITED IN PLACE AND `CACHE_VERSION` STAYS `v19`.** `ADR-020` holds every push at 0% traffic and this branch is unmerged, so the generation has never been published and `A1-DL-004`'s immutability has no client to protect yet. One generation and one bump per milestone. The shell is `max-age=3600, must-revalidate` behind a network-first worker, so the title and the header changes reach an installed client on its next navigation without a second bump.

### Alternatives rejected

- **A short line above the table plus the full text in the window** — see (i). Available at one `<p>`, one rule and one leg if the owner wants the cost back.
- **Re-wording the only-copy fact into the intro's shared prose** — see (h). It would ship a false sentence to the APK.
- **Restyling `#apkBtn` to the `.header-help` circle** as the "plain" reading of item 4 — rejected: the install offer is still the web channel's one main action, which is the role `.header-action` encodes, and `FIU-P3-INV-001`'s anti-vacuity leg needs a hidden element carrying `header-action` in each composition — on the native branch `#apkBtn` is the only one.
- **Keeping `writeOnboardingDismissed()` against a future packet's needs** — see (l). Speculative, and `core/storage.js` would have to document a door with nothing behind it.
- **Clearing the orphaned key from visitors' browsers** — rejected on the `UIP-DL-001` precedent.
- **Deleting `STATES.firstRun` now that it equals `STATES.empty`** — rejected: each name states the question its callers ask, and collapsing them would rewrite a dozen unrelated call sites to say less.

### Effects

- **Changed, the product:** `app/index.html` (title; subtitle removed; `#aboutBtn` glyph; `#apkBtn` name and label span; `#webChannelNote` relocated into the intro window; five comment blocks rewritten where this packet falsified them). `app/m/v9/app.css` — `.header-subtitle` (base + the `≤767` override), `.channel-note` and the two `#apkBtn` mobile exceptions deleted; the profile-chip comment corrected, its rules untouched. `app/m/v9/app.js`, `surfaces/onboarding.js`, `core/storage.js` — the auto-open and the storage key. `app/m/v9/surfaces/channel.js` — comment only.
- **Added:** `UIP-P3-INV-001`, `UIP-P3-INV-002`, and this entry. **Amended:** `FIU-P3-INV-002` (its Reachability bullet described a mechanism that no longer exists), `DIA-P2-INV-002` (a static leg it names by title was renamed and its rule changed), `PPR-P2-INV-002` (its Scope's label debt is closed). **Retired:** nothing.
- **Test surface:** `behavior` **116** (113 at UIP-P2) — the intro block went from four legs to seven; `native` **38** (35), the same three legs again on the second channel; `contract` **1283** (1281) — the two title-pairing legs.
- **Operability: none** (`ADR-013` / contract §4.7). No knob, no signal, no `changed_in` provenance, no config surface added or removed; `CHANNEL_CONFIG` untouched. **The intro surface gained no emitters** — it lost them at UIP-P1, and the retired auto-open is removed silently, with nothing marking that it did not happen. **Net egress: unchanged, none added.**
- **Measured, on the host, 2026-08-26, per project so a CI run can be checked against it rather than eyeballed.** `contract` **1283** (1281 at UIP-P2), `behavior` **116** (113), `dom-desktop` **14**, `dom-mobile` **16** (+1 skipped), `native` **38** (35; +5 skipped — the `native` project runs `behavior.spec.js`, so the intro block's three new legs land there too) — **1467 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed** (1459) across the five non-visual projects, via `PARITY_NO_DOCKER=1 scripts/parity-suite.sh`. The 6 skips are the same 6 UIP-P1 and UIP-P2 recorded. `pre-commit run --all-files` green with no file modified by a hook; `pre-commit run --files` over the changed paths reports `ruff`, `ruff-format` and `mypy` as *(no files to check)* — **no runtime import enters the repository, so no `additional_dependencies` stub is owed** (contract §4.8).
- **Baselines.** **Four moved, and the diff of each was read before it was re-blessed:** `dom-desktop/header.html`, `dom-mobile/header.html`, `dom-desktop/modal-onboarding.html`, `dom-mobile/modal-onboarding.html` — the `native` project shares the `dom-mobile` files, which is why six legs reported the four. The header diff is exactly the glyph paths, the `#apkBtn` name, the removed label span, the removed subtitle and the rewritten comments; the modal diff is the arrived paragraph and two rewritten comments. Nothing else moved, which is what the plan predicted in advance. **The ~12 visual PNGs are NOT re-blessed here and remain owner-run:** they are container-only and Docker on this host needs an owner-started daemon.
- **What it hands on.** **First, the visual baselines.** `header.png`, `shell-seeded.png`, `shell-no-profile.png`, `shell-zpd-filtered.png`, `shell-zpd-empty-state.png` and `modal-onboarding.png` at both viewports are expected to move; `control-footer`, `modal-skill`, `modal-activities` and `modal-create-profile` are expected NOT to, and if they do that is a finding rather than a re-bless. **Second, the promotion smoke's title line is now paired to the shell** — if the product is ever renamed again, both places move together or `contract` reds. **Third, the cost at (i) is a product consequence no test can hold:** whether a parent who never presses «i» ever reads either text inside the window is not a repository fact. **Fourth, `native/android/app/src/main/assets/public/**` is still stale** — git-ignored `cap sync` output refreshed at the next APK build, unchanged since `UIP-DL-002` recorded it.

## UIP-DL-004 — UIP-P4 `first-entry-after-profile`: creating a child continues into the first entry, and the door closes without writing anything

- **Date.** 2026-08-26
- **Type.** Packet — `UIP-P4`, the fourth rung of the milestone «UI polish of the showcase and app», on branch `feat/ui-polish`, cut from `main` @ `7f1a183`, following `UIP-P1` @ `35be8f9`, `UIP-P2` @ `2b16a3a` and `UIP-P3` @ `50a4f55`. Product behaviour on the channel that has a store: the running mount `/m/v9/` edited **in place**, comments in the shell, and the test surface that follows them. **This is the one item in the milestone about the app's FLOW rather than its surface** — the owner found it while testing on a device (decision 2026-08-25, item 8).
- **Scope.** **In:** `app/m/v9/surfaces/diary.js`, `app/m/v9/surfaces/profile.js`, `app/m/v9/app.js`; `app/index.html` (two comment blocks, no markup); `app/tests/` — `support/page-bridge.js`, `diary-save.spec.js`, one leg of `behavior.spec.js`; `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, `docs/execution-map.md`, this entry. **Out:** no mount generation (`/m/v9/` is unpublished on this branch — `ADR-020`), no `CACHE_VERSION` bump (v19 stands, one bump per milestone), no frozen generation, no markup change, no baseline, no storage key, no knob, no signal, no egress; the launcher icon (P5), retiring `/m/v1/`–`/m/v8/`, anything Play-console or Google-side, the privacy policy, and the wider RUNBOOK editorial tail.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. The symptom is a missing step, not a broken one.** Every piece already exists: the create-profile window, the diary window, its compose form, and a save path whose invariants landed at `DIA-P3`. What is missing is the sentence between them — a parent who has just said who their child is has to find «Дневник» in the header, meet an empty list, and press «Новая запись» there. Three actions, none of them offered, for the thing they just asked for.
- **b. A profile is created through FOUR doors and ONE handler.** The dropdown item, the boot-time `offerProfileIfNone()` (`FIU-P2-INV-001`), the diary's own «Создать профиль» when there is no subject, and a skill tick with no child all submit `#createProfileForm`. Anything attached to that handler is attached to all four, which is what makes «after creating a profile» implementable without a flag.
- **c. The create handler does not await its own work.** `createNewProfile(name, birthdate)` was called unawaited and the window closed after it. Nothing depended on the order, because nothing happened afterwards. Something does now.
- **d. The compose form is a PANE, not a window.** `#diaryForm` and `#diaryListPane` live inside one `#diaryModal`, switched by `hidden` — there has never been a stack of windows in this shell, and `FIU-P2-INV-001` (b) records what happens to anyone who tries: every `.modal` shares one `z-index`, so DOM order decides, and `#createProfileModal` precedes `#diaryModal`.
- **e. The subject of an entry is late-bound.** `saveEntry` computes `author()` at SAVE time, not at open time. This was assumed to be the other way round when the packet was planned, and the assumption was corrected by a mutation rather than by reading — see (l).
- **f. `whyNotWritable()` already answers the question this flow has to ask.** It is the predicate that withholds «Новая запись» when there is no store or no child, and it is the reason the diary refuses to hand a parent a form that is certain to refuse (`ADR-015`, `ADR-046` §1).

### The decisions

- **g. THE FIRST ENTRY IS THE DIARY'S OWN FORM, IN THE DIARY'S OWN WINDOW.** `offerFirstEntry()` reveals `#diaryModal` and calls the same `showForm()` the ordinary door calls; «Сохранить» from it is the same `saveEntry`, the same `createRecord`, the same refusals. *Rejected:* a dedicated first-entry window — a second compose surface is a second write path in everything but name, and `DIA-P3-INV-001`/`-002` would have to be re-proved against it.
- **h. THE OFFER FIRES ON EVERY CREATION, THROUGH EVERY DOOR, FOR EVERY CHILD.** The owner said «after creating a profile» without qualifying it, and a first-time-only variant needs a remembered flag — a key in a parent's browser, in the milestone that has been retiring them (`UIP-DL-001`). The cost is named rather than discovered: a parent who ticked a skill with no child, or who is adding a sibling, meets an entry form they did not ask for and closes it in one press. *Rejected:* branching on which door was used, which needs a pending-intent variable and four call sites kept honest for a UX preference.
- **i. THE OFFER IS WITHHELD EXACTLY WHERE THE SAVE WOULD REFUSE — AND THE HANDOFF'S PREMISE ABOUT THIS WAS IMPRECISE, WHICH THE ORCHESTRATOR CONFIRMED ON 2026-08-26.** The handoff said the flow is shared across channels because the mount is shared. The mount is shared and this code is channel-blind — it asks `whyNotWritable()`, never `window.Capacitor` — but the **diary is a native-only surface**, and `whyNotWritable()` is true on the web **by construction**: `store/bridge.js` is inert in a browser (`LSC-P1-INV-001`), so there is no store to write into. **No channel branch is introduced and none may be added later**: the asymmetry a parent sees is the pre-existing honest-degradation decision that already hides «Новая запись» on the web, not a second behaviour for a second channel. Recorded here so the next reader does not re-open it. Enforced as `UIP-P4-INV-001` half (c).
- **j. «ЗАКРЫТЬ» CLOSES THE WINDOW, AND THE CONTROL SAYS SO.** The form's secondary control has two meanings, and `showForm()` sets its label on **every** open, so the label cannot drift from the behaviour: «Отмена» when the form was reached from the list, «Закрыть» when the form arrived by itself. *Rejected:* leaving «Отмена» and returning to the list pane — the list pane was never rendered in this flow, so the parent would meet a nearly blank panel, and «Отмена» a minute after «Создать» reads as cancelling the creation, which is precisely the misreading the owner's item 3 names. *Rejected:* a second button in the markup — a new hidden element to sweep, and a markup delta this packet does not need.
- **k. NOTHING ELSE ABOUT THE SAVE PATH MOVES.** An empty save keeps the refusal it already had — named, before the store, with the text left in the field — rather than gaining a disabled button, which states no reason and cannot tell «no text» from «no day». After a successful save the parent lands on the list with their entry first, because the list is the confirmation (`DIA-DL-005` (g)) and this door does not get a second one.
- **l. AN ORDERING CLAIM WAS WRITTEN, MEASURED, AND FOUND WRONG IN THE PLAN — AND THE CODE COMMENT NOW SAYS WHAT THE MUTATION SHOWED.** The plan said the offer must follow `await switchProfile(...)` or the first entry about the new child would be attributed to the previous one, and named the two-children leg as the executor. Moving the call earlier reds **four** legs and leaves that one **green**: attribution is late-bound at save time (e), so an early open still writes to whoever is current when «Сохранить» is pressed. What an early call really destroys is the fresh-install case — there is no current child yet, `whyNotWritable()` answers «no subject», and the parent who just created their first child is offered nothing at all. The order stands; the reason for it is now stated correctly in `surfaces/profile.js` and in the leg's own header.
- **m. THE IMPORT EDGE IS INVERTED, NOT ADDED.** `surfaces/diary.js` already imports `surfaces/profile.js` for `openCreateProfileModal`, so `profile.js` receives `offerFirstEntry` **injected from `app.js`**, exactly as it receives the table rebuild. *Rejected:* importing the diary from the profile surface, which closes a real cycle rather than a hypothetical one.
- **n. THE TEST SEAM LEARNS CHILD CREATION, AND STAYS FAIL-CLOSED.** `support/page-bridge.js` gains the three statements `appendChild` sends (the `child` row, `ENTRY_SQL`, `DETAIL_SQL.child_attribute`), a reader for a named constant living inside a frozen map, and **child-keyed** areas and records, so a two-children leg cannot pass by reading one shared pile. Everything it already promised holds: exact equality, statements read out of the shipped modules rather than retyped, and a throw with the statement's own text on anything unknown. **It models no SQL and no view** — that a child comes back out of a real journal is `DiaryEntryTest`, and `FIU-P2-INV-001`'s Scope already says so. **A slot error in that work was caught by the suite rather than by reading:** the search statement binds the MATCH expression first, so its child sits in slot 3 and not slot 2 — nine `diary-search` legs said so, and the seam now names the difference where it is made.
- **o. `/m/v9/` IS EDITED IN PLACE AND `CACHE_VERSION` STAYS `v19`.** `ADR-020` holds every push at 0% and this branch is unmerged, so the generation has never been published and `ADR-024` / `A1-DL-004` immutability has no client to protect. One generation and one bump per milestone; the `UIP-DL-003` (p) precedent.

### Debt this packet names and does not close

- **CREATION HAS NO REFUSAL SURFACE, AND IT IS THE ONLY WRITE IN THIS APP THAT HAS NONE.** *(Class: missing refusal surface. Owner: this milestone's close-out.)* A mark that cannot be recorded opens `#storeUnavailableModal`; a diary entry that cannot be written has four sets of strings and keeps the parent's text. A **profile** that cannot be created has nothing: `createProfile()` returns `null` on the `unavailable` backend and `createNewProfile()` returns early, while `appendChild` throwing gives an unhandled rejection — in both cases the create window has already closed and the parent is told nothing at all. It predates this packet: `FIU-P2-INV-001` withholds the boot-time offer on that backend for exactly this reason, but the dropdown door does not, and neither does the tick door. **This packet does not widen it and fails closed over it** — no profile means `whyNotWritable()` answers «no subject», so no form is offered on top of a creation that did not happen — and it does not fix it, because a refusal surface is a change shape this packet did not declare. It is written here rather than in a report so that it survives into the milestone close-out.

### Alternatives rejected

- **A dedicated first-entry window** — see (g).
- **A stored «has been offered» flag, so the form appears only for the first child** — see (h); this milestone retires keys rather than adding them.
- **Firing the offer on both channels literally, as the handoff's wording suggested** — see (i). It would make a parent write about their child into a form certain to refuse on save, and lose the text.
- **Keeping «Отмена» and returning to the list pane** — see (j).
- **Disabling «Сохранить» while the field is empty** — see (k).
- **Asserting the two-children leg into catching the ordering mutation** — rejected: the property it would have to catch does not exist (e), and a leg written to red on a mutation it cannot really observe is decoration. The disposition is recorded instead, in `UIP-P4-INV-001` and at (l).

### Effects

- **Changed, the product:** `app/m/v9/surfaces/diary.js` — `offerFirstEntry()` (new export), a `standalone` mode on `showForm()`, the mode-aware secondary control, the mode reset in `closeDiaryModal()`. `app/m/v9/surfaces/profile.js` — a second injected hook, called after `switchProfile()` resolves; the create window now closes **before** the create starts, so «exactly one window» is a property of statement order. `app/m/v9/app.js` — the injection and the GRAPH SHAPE paragraph. `app/index.html` — **comments only**; no markup byte moved, which is why no DOM or visual baseline is touched.
- **Added:** `UIP-P4-INV-001`, and this entry. **Amended:** `DIA-P3-INV-003` (the window has a second opener, gated on the same store condition) and `FIU-P2-INV-001` (its path continues past the create window; its own leg gained the negative arm). **Retired:** nothing.
- **Test surface:** `behavior` **121** (116 at UIP-P3) — five legs, four of them about the flow and one an arm; `contract` **1284** (1283) — the show-rule coverage guard generates a case per `classList.add('show')` call site and this packet adds one, `#diaryModal (surfaces/diary.js:448)`; `native` **38** and the two DOM projects unchanged.
- **Operability: none** (`ADR-013` / contract §4.7). No knob, no signal, no `changed_in` provenance, no config surface added or removed. The existing `diary.write` / `write.refused` signals fire exactly as before, because the save path is the same handler; the new door adds no emitter, and its withheld branch is **deliberately silent** — nothing was refused, because nothing was offered. **Net egress: unchanged, none added.**
- **Measured, on the host, 2026-08-26, per project so a CI run can be checked against it rather than eyeballed.** `contract` **1284** (1283 at UIP-P3), `behavior` **121** (116), `dom-desktop` **14**, `dom-mobile` **16** (+1 skipped), `native` **38** (+5 skipped) — **1473 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed** across the five non-visual projects, via `PARITY_NO_DOCKER=1 scripts/parity-suite.sh`. The 6 skips are the same 6 UIP-P1, UIP-P2 and UIP-P3 recorded. `pre-commit run --all-files` green with no file modified by a hook; `pre-commit run --files` over the changed paths reports `ruff`, `ruff-format` and `mypy` as *(no files to check)* — **no runtime import enters the repository, so no `additional_dependencies` stub is owed** (contract §4.8).
- **Baselines: none moved, as predicted in advance.** No markup and no CSS changed, and no DOM or visual baseline captures `#diaryModal`. The ~12 visual PNGs are **not** re-blessed here and remain owner-run (container-only; Docker on this host needs an owner-started daemon).
- **Side-find, in a file this packet edits:** `docs/execution-map.md` still carried `- **P3** — header / intro polish. **Open.**` beneath P3's own landed entry — the placeholder that packet rewrote above and left behind below. Corrected here, statement-level.
- **What it hands on.** **First, the device.** No off-device test can see this flow meet a real SQLCipher store; the owner's diary smoke in `docs/RUNBOOK.md` gained the step that does, and the two statements this packet falsified in that document («The window opens on the list», «Create a profile, reopen…») are corrected in place. **Second, the debt above** — creation still cannot say no. **Third, `native/android/app/src/main/assets/public/**` is still stale** — git-ignored `cap sync` output refreshed at the next APK build, unchanged since `UIP-DL-002` recorded it.

## UIP-DL-005 — UIP-P5 `app-launcher-icon`: the app on the phone stops wearing the toolchain's face

- **Date.** 2026-08-27
- **Type.** Packet — `UIP-P5`, the fifth and last rung of the milestone «UI polish of the showcase and app», on branch `feat/ui-polish`, cut from `main` @ `7f1a183`, following `UIP-P1` @ `35be8f9`, `UIP-P2` @ `2b16a3a`, `UIP-P3` @ `50a4f55` and `UIP-P4` @ `81944bb`. Native resources and a committed derivation tool: **no product code, no mount, no shipped web byte.** The owner's item, found on a device (decision 2026-08-25, item 9).
- **Scope.** **In:** `native/tools/gen-launcher-icons.py` (new); the fifteen bitmaps under `native/android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-{mdpi,hdpi,xhdpi,xxhdpi,xxxhdpi}/`; the deletion of `native/android/app/src/main/res/drawable/ic_launcher_background.xml` and `.../drawable-v24/ic_launcher_foreground.xml`; `app/tests/native-shell.spec.js`; `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md`, `docs/execution-map.md`, this entry. **Out:** the splash (`drawable*/splash.png`, eleven files, untouched — the lockup on the splash is the owner's 2026-07-26 decision); the app label (already «TheyGrow»); the whole web channel (`app/manifest.json`, `app/icons/`, the favicon set, `app/sw.js` — **not one byte under `app/` changes except the test**); the Play Console store-listing icon (a console artefact, `ADR-050`); `AndroidManifest.xml`, both `mipmap-anydpi-v26` XMLs and `values/ic_launcher_background.xml`, each already correct and left **byte-untouched**; no mount generation, no `CACHE_VERSION` bump, no ship-list entry, no baseline, no storage key, no knob, no signal, no egress.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. All three forms were the template's, and had been since L1-P1.** `npx cap add android` wrote fifteen bitmaps — legacy square, legacy round, adaptive foreground, five densities each — and none was ever replaced. They are the Capacitor mark: a blue "X" on a faint grid. The owner described what his phone shows; the tree agrees with him in every bucket. Verified by eye at `mipmap-xxxhdpi/ic_launcher.png` and `.../ic_launcher_foreground.png`, and by digest against the fifteen now pinned as `CAPACITOR_PLACEHOLDER` in `app/tests/native-shell.spec.js`.
- **b. What was already right, and stays byte-untouched.** `AndroidManifest.xml` names `@mipmap/ic_launcher` and `@mipmap/ic_launcher_round`; both `mipmap-anydpi-v26` XMLs are present and identical, naming `@mipmap/ic_launcher_foreground` over `@color/ic_launcher_background`; that colour is `#FFFFFF`; `values/strings.xml` says «TheyGrow» twice. The wiring was never the defect — the pictures were.
- **c. Two template resources were in the tree that nothing referenced.** `drawable/ic_launcher_background.xml` (the Android-Studio teal grid) and `drawable-v24/ic_launcher_foreground.xml` (its gradient vector). The adaptive icons resolve `@color/` and `@mipmap/`, never `@drawable/`, so both compiled into every APK for four milestones while answering nothing. A tree-wide grep for `ic_launcher` outside `build/`, `node_modules/` and `assets/public/` returns seven lines, and neither file appears among them.
- **d. `minSdkVersion = 24`**, so the legacy pair is a live fallback on API 24–25 and not a relic — the reason all three forms are regenerated rather than only the adaptive one.
- **e. The master is real and is what its name says.** `app/icons/icon-master-1024.png`, 1024×1024 8-bit RGBA, sha256 `46d27cf42368cf5934ae1e998b902ce7bda327b80f9555b2bcbac332a6bd3bcd`, the logo on full transparency, **carrying no wordmark** — the lockup lives in the separate `splash-logo-name-1024.png`. That absence is what makes this packet a scaling problem rather than a design one.
- **f. The image toolchain on this host was measured before anything was planned around it.** No ImageMagick (`convert`, `magick`, `identify` all absent), no `sharp`/`jimp`/`canvas` in `native/node_modules`. `/usr/bin/python3` has **Pillow 10.2.0**. A plan assuming an uninstalled tool is a plan that cannot run.

### The decisions

- **g. THE GEOMETRY, RECORDED IN FULL SO A FUTURE MASTER SWAP DOES NOT LOSE IT.** The master's content (alpha > 8) measures **553 × 737 px** inside its 1024 canvas, centred to within half a pixel on both axes, with bounding box `(235,143)–(787,879)` and a **minimal enclosing circle about the canvas centre of diameter 0.8803 of the canvas**. An adaptive foreground shows at most its central **72 of 108 dp (0.6667)** — every mask, circle or squircle or teardrop, is inscribed there — and Android's documented safe zone is a **66 dp circle (0.6111)**. Mapped 1:1 the logo's circle is 0.8803 against a 0.6667 window, so a full-bleed foreground **clips**: the orange swoosh's tip at `(771,143)` and the purple figure's foot both fall outside. The chosen scale is therefore **0.6111 / 0.8803 = 0.6942**, the safe-circle fit. **The 72 dp window fit (0.7574) was rejected** for two reasons stated together: it puts the logo's extreme point exactly on the mask edge of a circular launcher, where any OEM mask a shade tighter than stock cuts it, and it leaves nothing at all for the parallax a launcher applies while the home screen scrolls. **The cost is named:** 30.6 % smaller in linear terms than a full-bleed map — but inside the circle a parent actually sees, the logo still fills **66/72 = 91.7 %** of the diameter, so it reads large rather than timid. *Measured after generation, at all five densities:* content circle **0.6103–0.6138** of the foreground canvas (the spread is resize rounding and LANCZOS fringe, not drift), and **zero content lost** under the 72 dp inscribed circle at every density.
- **h. THE FRACTION IS MEASURED AT RUN TIME, THE MASTER IS PINNED BY DIGEST.** `gen-launcher-icons.py` re-derives `content_dia_frac` from the master on every run, so a corrected logo reflows by itself; `MASTER_SHA256` is pinned there **and** in the guard, so it cannot arrive quietly. *Rejected:* hard-coding 0.8803, which turns a corrected master into a silently mis-scaled icon.
- **i. THE BACKGROUND LAYER STAYS `#FFFFFF`, AND ITS FILE IS NOT TOUCHED.** The master's implied ground is white, the shipped web icon set is on white, and `A0-DL-001` already set `background_color` → `#FFFFFF` for this brand. *Rejected:* a brand-purple or gradient background layer — it needs a colour decision nobody has taken and would fight the logo's own purple at exactly the place the mask crops.
- **j. THE LEGACY PAIR IS SHAPED AND SIZED FROM THE ADAPTIVE GEOMETRY.** Legacy bitmaps are drawn **unmasked**, so the shape is baked: an opaque white plate, rounded-square at radius 0.20 of the canvas for `ic_launcher.png` and a full circle for `ic_launcher_round.png`, with the logo at `SAFE / VISIBLE = 0.9167` of the canvas so API 24–25 sees optically what API 26+ sees after masking. Masks are drawn at 4× and downsampled, so the edge is clean at 48 px. *Rejected:* full-bleed square legacy icons, which read as a different, larger, unshaped icon beside the adaptive one; and raising `minSdk` to 26 to delete them, which is not a side effect an icon packet gets to have.
- **k. PYTHON + PILLOW, COMMITTED AS A TOOL, NOT A DEPENDENCY.** `native/tools/gen-launcher-icons.py` sits beside `stage-webdir.js` because it is native-side hand-authored tooling; it is **under `native/`, never under `app/`**, so no generated intermediate can reach the web ship list. It is developer-run: no `package.json` entry, no `pyproject.toml` entry, nothing at build or run time invokes it, and the web channel stays buildless. *Rejected:* a Node generator to match the directory's language — it would put an image dependency into `native/package.json` for one occasional command.
- **l. REPRODUCIBILITY IS CLAIMED AS PIXEL IDENTITY, AND BYTE IDENTITY IS SCOPED TO A TOOLCHAIN.** PNG encoding depends on the Pillow/zlib pair, so `--check` compares **pixels** and the CI guard compares **bytes**; the pair used is recorded (CPython `/usr/bin/python3`, Pillow 10.2.0, 2026-08-27) and the fifteen digests are in (r) below. A green `--check` with a red guard means a Pillow difference, not an icon difference — said in `docs/RUNBOOK.md` so nobody has to rediscover it. *Rejected:* claiming byte-for-byte across machines, a promise the format cannot keep.
- **m. THE TWO DEAD TEMPLATE VECTORS ARE DELETED, AND A GUARD KEEPS THEM DELETED.** The scope item names a class — "no placeholder asset remains in the tree" — and these are members of it, found in the directory already open. The guard asserts the general property (*no `ic_launcher*` resource that nothing references*) rather than these two filenames, so it catches the next one too. Safety was verified before deleting, and again by a real compile afterwards: `aapt2` tolerates a colour and a drawable sharing a name, and `:app:assembleDebug` is green.
- **n. THE CI ENFORCER IS BYTES, DIMENSIONS, REFERENCES AND PROVENANCE; THE PIXEL RE-DERIVATION IS A COMMAND.** `app/tests/native-shell.spec.js` links no image library on purpose — the `contract` project installs nothing beyond Playwright, and adding Pillow to that container for one asset check is a cost with no second use. `UIP-P5-INV-001` is therefore worded to exactly what runs on every push, and names `--check` as the part that is not. **An invariant left without an enforcer is a defect; an invariant that claims more than its enforcer proves is the same defect wearing a badge.**
- **o. THE TWO CHANNELS' ICONS DIVERGE ON PURPOSE, AND THE 2026-07-26 DECISION IS NOT OVERTURNED.** **Confirmed by the orchestrator at go-ahead:** the divergence stands — the native launcher carries the emblem (owner item 9) while the web/PWA install icon keeps the lockup; the 2026-07-26 decision is **not** reversed, its subject narrows to the web channel, and the orchestrator records that narrowing in the vault at milestone close. A handset carrying both the browser shortcut and the APK shows two different icons, and that is the intended state.

### Debt this packet names and does not close

These three are **side-finds, not scope**, and they are logged here rather than only reported so they survive into the milestone close-out.

- **(a) The web channel's `maskable` icons are byte-identical to its plain ones.** `app/icons/maskable-192-v2.png` == `icon-logo-192-v2.png` (sha256 `ec3520a5…`) and `maskable-512-v2.png` == `icon-logo-512-v2.png` (`ef24dadb…`), while `app/manifest.json` declares the pairs under `purpose: "maskable"` and `purpose: "any"` respectively. So the maskable set has no maskable treatment and the plain set is padded like one. Measured: their content circle is **0.6201** of the canvas — inside the 0.6667 visible window, so a circular mask does **not** clip them, but outside the 0.6111 safe circle, so a stricter OEM mask grazes the lockup. Low severity, real, and web-channel — out of scope here by the packet's own boundary.
- **(b) `app/icons/icon-master-1024.png` (276 KB) is inside `app/Dockerfile`'s COPY list.** The brand master is therefore served by the web channel and packaged into the APK although nothing references it — 276 KB of dead weight in both channels. Confirmed from a second direction by mutation (4) in `UIP-P5-INV-001`, where flipping a byte of it reddened `LSC-P1-INV-002`'s byte-identity leg as well as this packet's provenance leg.
- **(c) `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `android`-job comment repeats the stale toolchain claim** corrected in `docs/RUNBOOK.md` by this packet — it says the development machine has no Android SDK, no Gradle and Node 18, where it now has build-tools 35.0.0/36.0.0, OpenJDK 21.0.11 and Node v22.23.2. Left alone deliberately: that file is outside this packet's allowlist and is the gate of record.

### Alternatives rejected

- **Deriving from `app/icons/icon-logo-512-v2.png`** — rejected: it is the lockup, at half the resolution, and re-deriving from a derivative loses what the master still has.
- **A one-off generation with no committed tool** — rejected by the scope, and rightly: the fifteen files would then be unreproducible bytes whose only provenance is a session transcript.
- **Pinning only the placeholder digests, not the expected ones** — rejected: it proves the icons are not the template's without proving they are the product's.
- **Wiring `--check` into CI** — rejected at (n).

### Effects

- **Changed, the native resources:** fifteen bitmaps regenerated under `mipmap-{mdpi,hdpi,xhdpi,xxhdpi,xxxhdpi}/`; two unreferenced template vectors deleted (`drawable-v24/` goes with the second). **Added:** `native/tools/gen-launcher-icons.py`, `UIP-P5-INV-001`, and this entry. **Amended:** nothing. **Retired:** nothing.
- **Not changed, and the list is the point:** no file under `app/` except `tests/native-shell.spec.js`; `AndroidManifest.xml`, both adaptive XMLs, `values/ic_launcher_background.xml`, `values/strings.xml`, `values/styles.xml` and all eleven `splash.png` byte-untouched; no mount, no `CACHE_VERSION`, no ship-list entry, no baseline.
- **Operability: none** (`ADR-013` / contract §4.7). No knob, no signal, no `changed_in` provenance, no config surface added or removed, and nothing this packet touches is reachable at run time by a parent. **Net egress: unchanged, none added** — the generator makes no network call and is not invoked by either channel.
- **No runtime dependency enters the repository** (contract §4.8). Pillow is a workstation tool in the class of the Android SDK; it appears in no `package.json` and no `pyproject.toml`. `pre-commit run --files` over the changed paths reports `ruff`, `ruff-format` and `mypy` as *(no files to check)* for the JS, PNG and Markdown, and the one new `.py` file is linted and type-checked by them with **no `additional_dependencies` stub owed** — `PIL` is imported by a tool that CI never executes and mypy never follows into.
- **Measured, on the host, 2026-08-27, per project so a CI run can be checked against it.** `contract` **1290** (1284 at UIP-P4 — the six new legs), `behavior` **121**, `dom-desktop` **14**, `dom-mobile` **16** (+1 skipped), `native` **38** (+5 skipped) — **1479 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed** across the five non-visual projects, via `PARITY_NO_DOCKER=1 scripts/parity-suite.sh`. The 6 skips are the same 6 the four preceding packets recorded. Generator: `--check` green on fifteen files, `--check --arm` red as designed.
- **The compile leg ran, and it is the only executing evidence in this packet.** `npm run sync && ./gradlew assembleDebug` on the host → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 17s**, `:app:processDebugResources` included, which is `aapt2` over the new `res/` tree and over the two deletions. `aapt2 dump badging` reports `application-icon-{120,160,240,320,480,640,65534}` all resolving to `res/mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml` with `label='TheyGrow'`; `unzip -l` shows the five densities of each of the three names plus both adaptive XMLs, and **no** `drawable*/ic_launcher*` at all.
- **A predicted limit did not hold, and the correction is in our favour.** The plan said APK-internal PNG bytes could not be compared to the tree because AGP may "crunch" them. They were compared: all fifteen extracted from `app-debug.apk` are **byte-identical** to the committed files. So for the **debug** build the packaged icon is provably the committed icon. The caveat survives only for the **release** build, which was not run here.
- **Baselines: none moved, as predicted in advance.** No shipped web byte changed. The ~12 visual PNGs are **not** re-blessed and remain owner-run (container-only; Docker on this host needs an owner-started daemon).
- **The fifteen digests, so a regeneration is checkable against a written record and not only against the test.**
