## UIP-DL-006 — UIP-P6 `policy-effective-date`: the date the policy names becomes the day it reaches a reader

- **Date.** 2026-08-27
- **Type.** Packet — `UIP-P6`, a repair rung of the milestone «UI polish of the showcase and app», added **after** the milestone's own PR merged. `UIP-P1`–`UIP-P5` are on `main` @ `2163ed3` (PR #32), so this packet cannot land on `feat/ui-polish`; it takes a branch of its own cut from that commit, and the branch and the checkpoint are the owner's (`CLAUDE.md`, No autonomous git). **Four date literals and one sentence of procedure: no product code, no mount, no shipped behaviour.**
- **Scope.** **In:** `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md` (header block, top change-history row); `app/privacy.html` (the same two places); `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Privacy policy step 6, its closing sentence only; `docs/execution-map.md`; this entry, and the one-clause correction to `UIP-DL-005`'s hand-on note. **Out:** the edition itself — **this is not v1.2** (d); the frozen `1.0` row in either file and `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md` entire; every word of the policy that is not the date; `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` (e); `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (f); no mount generation, no `CACHE_VERSION` bump, no shell change, no ship-list entry, no baseline, no storage key, no knob, no signal, no egress.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. The date said `26.08.2026`, in exactly four places, and nowhere else.** `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md:5` (header) and `:140` (the `1.1` history row); `app/privacy.html:137` (header block) and `:292` (the `1.1` history row). Enumerated **before** any of them was touched, because a partial edit is this packet's whole failure mode. A tracked-file sweep for the literal returned eight hits in four files: those four, `docs/RUNBOOK.md:405`, and three narrative lines inside `UIP-DL-002`. `app/m/v9/channel/config.js` carries only `policyUrl` and no date; `native/www/privacy.html` and `native/android/app/src/main/assets/public/privacy.html` are git-ignored staging copies, byte-identical to `app/privacy.html`, and are re-derived rather than edited.
- **b. `26.08.2026` was the day `UIP-P2` landed, and `UIP-DL-002` (q) said so and named this residual by name:** "What this packet cannot close is the day the owner actually promotes. If that is later, the literal is wrong again and the fix is the same four-token edit." That entry is a correct record of what P2 decided and is **not** amended here; the residual it named is what this packet closes.
- **c. Edition 1.1 has had no reader.** Nothing reaches a parent before merge and manual promotion (`ADR-020`), and no promotion has happened since the edition was written. So the stated date is not a date that was ever in force and is now being revised — it is a date being **set correctly before publication**.

### The decisions

- **d. THE DATE BECOMES `27.08.2026`, THE DAY OF PROMOTION, AND THIS IS NOT A NEW EDITION.** The rule is `PPR-DL-001` (f): the date is the day the document becomes readable. Vault `ADR-043`'s 2026-08-25 annotation puts the code removal and the policy revision in **one** promotion, and that promotion is the day this date names. The edition stays **1.1**, gains **no** change-history row, and the filename does not move. §10 of the document promises a new edition «при изменении описанной здесь обработки данных» — the processing described has not changed by one word, and the four literals are the same four `UIP-P2` wrote. *Rejected:* publishing `v1.2` with an "effective date corrected" row (see Alternatives).
- **e. THE GUARD IS NOT EDITED, AND THAT IS THE MEASURE OF `UIP-P2`'S WORK.** `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` hard-codes **no date**: `editionHeader()` reads the version and the date out of the Markdown header and every leg derives from them. Its one hand-kept literal is `EDITION = '1.1'`, which does not move because the edition does not move. A date bump touches four content locations and **zero** test locations. Writing the new date into the spec as a second check would re-create, inside the guard, the four-hand-kept-literals defect the guard exists to prevent.
- **f. `UIP-P2-INV-001` IS NOT AMENDED.** Its Statement stays exactly true, and its Scope already assigns this judgement away from itself: it "says nothing about whether the stated effective date is the day the document actually became readable, which is a wall-clock judgement no test can make and which `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Privacy policy step 6 assigns to the owner." This packet **is** that judgement being made, in the place the invariant points at. An invariant that needed rewording every time the surface it governs moved correctly would be describing an instance rather than a property.
- **g. RUNBOOK STEP 6'S TEACHING SENTENCE IS CORRECTED IN THE SAME PACKET, BECAUSE IT IS THE SENTENCE THAT PRODUCED THE DEFECT.** The step's headline already read "Re-check the effective date against the day you actually promote"; its closing sentence then recorded, as the worked example a reader copies, "UIP-P2 set edition 1.1 to `26.08.2026`, the day it landed". A procedure whose example contradicts its own rule teaches the example. It now states which reasoning was wrong and why, names the day of promotion as the date the step is about, and says that a merged-but-unpromoted revision is corrected in place rather than superseded. The four content anchors and the frozen-row rule below them were already correct and are untouched.
- **h. THE FROZEN `1.0` ROW DOES NOT MOVE, IN EITHER FILE.** Editing a superseded edition's row would rewrite history to make a later promotion look tidy. The row-for-row leg reds on it in both files, and mutation (2) in the Effects below is the arming of a neighbouring leg on the same table.
- **i. THE PACKET WRITES ITS OWN RECORD.** Every UIP packet carries a `UIP-DL-{NNN}` entry and an execution-map bullet; a repair packet with neither would be the odd one, and `docs/execution-map.md` is *the state* (`AGENTS.md` §6), which stops being true the moment a sixth packet lands under a fifth that says the list is closed. **The scope fork was raised in the plan's Escalations and answered at go-ahead:** the handoff's "everything else is out of scope" meant product surfaces, not the packet's own bookkeeping; the orchestrator recorded that imprecision as its own.

### Alternatives rejected

- **Publish edition `1.2` with a row reading "effective date corrected"** — rejected at (d): it would announce a revision to a reader who never saw the thing revised, and spend a public version number on a date that was never in force. `PDR-035`'s 2026-08-25 annotation freezes the **previous** edition in the history; 1.1 is not previous to anything.
- **Amend `UIP-DL-002` to say the date is now `27.08.2026`** — rejected at (b): nothing there is false. It records what P2 decided and predicted this correction in its own words; a decision log that is edited to match later state stops being a log.
- **Pin the new date in `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` as a belt-and-braces literal** — rejected at (e).
- **Leave step 6 alone and change only the date** — rejected at (g). The next promotion would read the same worked example.
- **Defer this entry and the execution-map bullet to the milestone close-out** — rejected at (i), on the answer given at go-ahead.

### Effects

- **Changed, the owner's document:** the effective date `26.08.2026` → `27.08.2026` in four places — the header block and the top change-history row of `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md`, and the same two in `app/privacy.html`. **Not one other byte of either file**, and the Markdown hard line breaks at lines 3–4 survive the edit (both paths are excluded from the rewriting hygiene hooks by `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and the edit did not touch line ends either). **Changed, the procedure:** one sentence of `docs/RUNBOOK.md` step 6. **Added:** this entry, a `P6` bullet in `docs/execution-map.md`. **Amended:** `UIP-DL-005`'s hand-on note, one clause — it said P5 was the milestone's last packet. **Retired:** nothing. **Not changed:** `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md`, the `1.0` row in both current files, `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js`, `docs/INVARIANTS.md`.
- **Operability: none** (`ADR-013` / contract §4.7). No knob, no signal, no config surface added or removed, no `changed_in` provenance. **Net egress: unchanged, none added** — no code runs and no request is made that did not exist before.
- **The evidence is static, and is named as static** (`AGENTS.md` §11). `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` boots nothing: it reads two files off disk and compares strings, exactly as `UIP-P2-INV-001` already declares. **There are no runtime claims in this packet** — a date literal is a property of the tree. `app/tests/privacy-surface.spec.js` does execute a browser at the address and deliberately makes no claim about the edition, so it discharges nothing here.
- **Armed before it was trusted — two mutations, run and reverted, both landing exactly where predicted.** (1) Moving **only** `app/privacy.html`'s header date: **2 failed / 43 passed** — *the edition is resolved, and the page states the same one* and *the effective date is stated exactly twice in the page*. (2) Moving **only** the Markdown's top history row: **2 failed / 43 passed** — *the newest history row IS the current edition* and *the change history is the same table in both files, row for row*. Between them the two arm all four of the derived set's corners; no prediction needed correcting.
- **Measured, on the host, 2026-08-27:** `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` **45 passed** before the edits, **45 passed** after them, via `PARITY_NO_DOCKER=1 scripts/parity-suite.sh --project=contract`, which stages `native/www/` first — required here, because `app/privacy.html` is in the ship list and a stale staging would red `LSC-P1-INV-002` on the wrong cause.
- **What it hands on, and it is the owner's:** **the promotion actually happening on 2026-08-27.** Nothing in this repository can compare the date to the wall clock — `UIP-P2-INV-001`'s Scope says so, and step 6 is where the judgement is made. If the promotion slips, the literal is wrong again and the remedy is this same four-token edit; the step now teaches the rule rather than the wrong example. **And the APK's bundled copy** of `privacy.html` keeps the old date until the next release build (`ADR-020`) — very likely unread either way, since the in-app link resolves `CHANNEL_CONFIG.policyUrl`, an absolute web address, so a parent on a phone reads the web copy.

## UIP-DL-007 — UIP-P7 `policy-control-naming`: the published policy stops naming a control by the sign painted on it

- **Date.** 2026-08-28
- **Type.** Packet — `UIP-P7`, a second repair rung of the milestone «UI polish of the showcase and app», added after `UIP-P6` merged. `main` is at `948e677` (PR #33). **This is the first packet of the milestone that edits a document with READERS:** `UIP-P6` set edition 1.1's effective date to `27.08.2026` and the owner promoted on that day, so the text this packet changes has been live for a day. The branch and the checkpoint are the owner's (`CLAUDE.md`, No autonomous git).
- **Scope.** **In:** `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md` (§1, two sentences); `app/privacy.html` (the same two sentences, plus a note in the head comment); `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` (one new describe block — a scope extension, escalated and granted, see (h)); `docs/execution-map.md`; this entry. **Out:** the edition, its version, its effective date and its change history — **this is not v1.2** (c); `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md` entire and the frozen `1.0` row in either current file; §10's promise itself; the controller identity in §2 (parallel track); `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (g); `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (i); every product and runtime file; no mount generation, no `CACHE_VERSION` bump, no ship-list entry, no baseline, no storage key, no knob, no signal, no egress.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. Two sentences of §1 named the header control «?», and the control has not carried that sign since `UIP-P3`.** `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md:21` («…за кнопкой «?» в шапке приложения и на сайте») and `:27` («…остаётся доступной через кнопку «?» в шапке»), with their twins at `app/privacy.html:156` and `:162`. `UIP-DL-003` (j) records what actually changed: two `<path>` elements inside the same `<circle r="9">`, with id, class, `title`/`aria-label` «О приложении», the handler, the window and the policy link inside it untouched. **The document described the one part of the control that moved.**
- **b. A tracked-tree sweep for the literal was run before anything was touched**, because a partial edit across the paired files is this packet's whole failure mode. It returned the four in-scope hits above and eleven out of scope: `app/index.html:242` and the two `header.html` DOM baselines (the comment that *explains* the change — correct usage); `docs/RUNBOOK.md:372`, `:374`, `:758`, `:761` (i); `app/m/v9/app.css:170` and `app/m/v9/surfaces/profile.js:165` (i); `docs/INVARIANTS.md:561`, `docs/decision-log.md` and `docs/execution-map.md` (historical narration, correct); `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md:21`, `:27` (a superseded edition, frozen); **and six more in `app/m/v7/` and `app/m/v8/`** — frozen generations, immutable by `ADR-024`, which the plan had not enumerated and which are named here so the next sweep does not re-derive them.

### The decisions

- **c. THE CORRECTION LANDS IN PLACE INSIDE EDITION 1.1 — NO VERSION, NO DATE, NO HISTORY ROW.** Owner gate decision **2026-08-27**, option 1 of three. The ground is on record and is §10's own wording: a new edition is promised when the **DATA PROCESSING** described changes. Naming a UI control describes the interface, and no processing changed by one word. This is the **first** in-place correction of a shipped edition in this repository, so it is stated as a precedent rather than left to be reconstructed from a diff — and the same statement is written into `app/privacy.html`'s head comment (f), because the person who needs the warning is reading the file.
- **d. THE NEW WORDING NAMES THE CONTROL, NOT ITS SIGN, AND THE NAME IS THE ONE THE PRODUCT OWNS.** «за кнопкой **«О приложении»** в шапке приложения» and «через кнопку **«О приложении»** в шапке» — one token replaced per sentence, nothing else in either sentence moved. «О приложении» is the control's `title` and `aria-label`, and `UIP-DL-003` (j) records that the name was chosen **deliberately wider than today's contents** («Имя у кнопки нарочно шире её сегодняшнего содержимого: «О приложении», а не «Инструкция»») precisely so that a change behind the button does not change the button. The glyph was the volatile half and has already moved once; the name is the half the product committed to keeping. *Rejected:* a functional paraphrase with no quotation («за кнопкой сведений о приложении») — glyph-independent but anchored to nothing checkable, and a parent scanning the header has no string to match. *Rejected:* naming the shape («круглая кнопка») — a second visual property, i.e. the same defect with a different sign.
- **e. ONE TOKEN PER SENTENCE, ON A LIVE PUBLIC DOCUMENT.** No softening, no additions, no new claims: what the sweep proved false is the name of the control and nothing else in those two sentences. The full word-diff of both files is four tokens.
- **f. A NOTE GOES INTO `app/privacy.html`'S HEAD COMMENT.** That comment already says a shipped edition is never rewritten retroactively (of 1.0) and that this file invents nothing (of the conversion). Both stay true — but standing alone they invite the next reader to infer a rule this packet has just made false for 1.1. The note is two sentences, records the gate decision and its ground, and is stripped by `PAGE_CODE` before any assertion, so it moves no guard and no reader of the document sees it. **It is an addition beyond the literal change shape, was flagged as such in the plan, and the owner kept it at go-ahead.**
- **g. `UIP-P2-INV-001` IS NOT AMENDED.** Its Statement is about the edition, its effective date and the heading-for-heading conversion; none of the three moves here. What this packet adds to the guard file is a **new** property with its own subject (h), not a widening of that one.
- **h. THE COUPLING IS MADE DERIVED RATHER THAN REMEMBERED, AND THAT WAS A SCOPE EXTENSION THE OWNER GRANTED.** As planned, the packet's durability claim — *the next glyph change must not falsify the document again* — rested on the accessible name staying «О приложении», a commitment recorded in a decision-log entry and enforced by nothing. **This milestone has been bitten by exactly that shape twice**: the date literal at `UIP-P6`, this control's name here. So `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` gains one describe block, `the document names the header control by its name, not its glyph (UIP-P7)`, which reads `#aboutBtn`'s `aria-label` **out of the shell's own markup** and requires both policy files to quote that exact string — the same "derived set rather than four things to remember" move `UIP-P2` made for the four date literals. *Escalated as E3 because it exceeds the declared file allowlist, and granted at go-ahead in those terms.*
- **i. THE FOUR OTHER FALSE STATEMENTS THE SWEEP FOUND ARE RECORDED AS DEBT, NOT FIXED HERE.** `docs/RUNBOOK.md` names the retired glyph three times — `:372` and `:374` (§ Privacy policy step 4: «press the round **«?»** in the header», ««?» is the only way back into that window») and `:761` (on-device smoke, "since PPR-P3") — and **`:758` is doubly stale and cannot pass as written**: the "since L3-P3" bullet instructs the owner to verify the greeting «closes **FOR GOOD**» after a ✕ and does not reappear on relaunch, but `UIP-P3` removed the auto-open entirely, so there is no auto-open to suppress and an owner running that step today would read the result as a regression. Two product comments carry the same residue, `app/m/v9/app.css:170` and `app/m/v9/surfaces/profile.js:165`. All six are out of scope by the packet boundary — the handoff admits RUNBOOK only for a sentence *this* packet falsifies, and `UIP-P3` falsified these — and are named by line so the follow-up does not re-find them.
- **j. `native/android/app/src/main/assets/public/**` IS STALE AGAIN, AND `UIP-DL-005`'S RETIRED NOTE IS TRUE ONCE MORE.** That entry recorded the staleness as closed — «`npm run sync` ran in this packet's compile leg and refreshed it» — and `UIP-P6` then edited `app/privacy.html` without re-running `cap sync`, so the bundled copy states `26.08.2026` in both places against the tracked `27.08.2026`, and now carries the old control name as well. Nothing to fix: it is git-ignored `cap sync` output refreshed at the next release build, and this packet's edit reaches it by the same route. Recorded so the milestone close does not carry a retired note that has come back.

### Escalated to the owner and NOT closed here

- **k. THE POLICY TELLS A PARENT THEY CAN DELETE A FAMILY RECORD IN THE APP. THEY CANNOT, AND THE DOCUMENT HAS BEEN PUBLIC SINCE 27.08.2026.** This is the sweep's serious finding and it is **open**, escalated as E1 and confirmed by the owner as branch (i) — a gate of its own, not a correction under this packet's "in place" precedent.
  - **What is claimed, in four places:** the summary's fifth bullet («Вы сами просматриваете, исправляете, экспортируете и **удаляете** семейные записи в приложении»); §3.4's action list («просмотр; изменение; экспорт; **удаление**»); §3.4 ¶4 twice («Для удаления **отдельной записи** используйте действие удаления в соответствующем разделе дневника», «Для удаления всех записей **удалите их в приложении** либо удалите приложение»); and §8 ¶1 («используйте функции приложения: … и **удаление**»). The sharpest is the third: it tells the parent which control to press.
  - **What is measured:** no delete affordance for an individual diary record — or for a child's profile — exists anywhere in the shipped shell. `app/m/v9/surfaces/diary.js:12` states it as a design decision with its reason: «ЧТО ЭТО ОКНО НЕ ДЕЛАЕТ. **Не удаляет записи.** Удаление стирает цитаты, скопированные из записи, и оставляет отметки с деградированным основанием (`ADR-015`) — поведение в схеме уже есть и уже проверено (`app/tests/schema/test_store_append_only.py`), но предупреждение, на которое родитель может опереться, требует отметок с цитатами, а они появляются на **L5**.» The schema-level behaviour exists and is tested; there is **no surface on top of it**. A tree-wide search for a delete control returns nothing.
  - **What is NOT wrong:** «удалите приложение» is true and is the only path that works; §2's statement that the developer cannot reach these records at all is true; §8's e-mail route is unaffected; and «изменение»/«исправляете» is true for records — diary text is edited by overwrite (`overwriteRecord`, `PDR-026` §4 rule 1) and a skill mark is corrected by a new statement on top (`PDR-025` §2). **Secondary observation, same subject:** the child's own fields, name and birthdate, both named in §3.1, have a create surface and a switch surface and **no edit surface**.
  - **The loss window is open now.** Exposure began at promotion on **27.08.2026**, and every day the live document stands is a day it overstates a right.
  - **Why it is not corrected here.** It is not a naming fix. Either the product grows a delete surface, or the document's description of erasure changes — and a changed description of erasure is arguably a change in the **processing** described, which is exactly what §10 promises a new edition for. That is the owner's call at the same gate that settled (c), and it is the first item the milestone close-out inherits.

### Alternatives rejected

- **Publish edition 1.2, or add a change-history row** — rejected at (c), on the owner's gate decision and §10's own wording.
- **Reword §1's last paragraph so it stops implying the intro window arrives by itself** — raised as **E2**, answered branch (i) at go-ahead: leave both sentences. «Ссылка на полный текст **показывается** в приветственном окне. **После начала работы с дневником** политика остаётся доступной…» is a residue of the once-only intro `UIP-P3` abolished, but neither clause is false — the document never promised the window appears unbidden — and on a promoted public document "not false" is the bar this packet was given.
- **Correct the four deletion sentences in this packet** — rejected at (k), branch (ii): it would decide §10's question by implication, silently widen a packet whose subject is one control's name, and ship rights-bearing wording drafted in an hour.
- **Ship the wording with no guard** — rejected at (h). That is the shape this milestone has already been bitten by twice.
- **Fix the RUNBOOK's four statements here** — rejected at (i), on the packet boundary. Named as debt instead.

### Effects

## UIP-DL-008 — UIP-P8 `policy-v1-2-erasure`: edition 1.2 says what the app can actually erase

- **Date.** 2026-08-28
- **Type.** Packet — `UIP-P8`, the third repair rung of the milestone «UI polish of the showcase and app», added after `UIP-P7` merged. `main` is at `85f1e00` (PR #34) and is **PROMOTED**. This packet takes the open item `UIP-P7` handed on: `UIP-DL-007` (k), the four places where the live document tells a parent they can delete a family record in the app. The branch and the checkpoint are the owner's (`CLAUDE.md`, No autonomous git).
- **Scope.** **In:** `docs/privacy-policy-v1.2.md` (**new** — the current edition); `app/privacy.html` (the conversion: the edition block, a new history row, nine places of body text, and the head comment); `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` (the `EDITION` constant, one comment sentence, and one new describe block — a scope extension, escalated as **E1** and granted at go-ahead, see (g)); `app/playwright.config.js` (one comment sentence); `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Privacy policy steps 1 and 6, and only the statements **this** packet falsifies (h); `docs/execution-map.md`; this entry. **Out:** `docs/privacy-policy-v1.0.md` and `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md` entire — **both frozen** (c); §8's GDPR rights paragraphs, byte-untouched and deliberately so (e); §2's controller identity (parallel track); `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (i); the four `docs/RUNBOOK.md` glyph statements and two product comments `UIP-DL-007` (i) recorded as debt; **every product and runtime file** — no delete surface and no edit surface were built, and building one is a product packet the owner has not scheduled; no mount generation, no `CACHE_VERSION` bump, no ship-list entry, no baseline, no storage key, no knob, no signal, no egress.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. THE DEFECT, RE-MEASURED FROM THE CODE RATHER THAN INHERITED FROM THE FINDING.** `UIP-DL-007` (k) named four places; the measurement was redone at `85f1e00` against the shipped mount `/m/v9/` (`app/index.html:108`, `:132`, `:145-181`), and `native/www/` is byte-identical to `app/`, so every anchor holds on both channels.
  - **Delete of a record: does not exist, anywhere.** `app/m/v9/surfaces/diary.js:12` states the deferral and its reason — «ЧТО ЭТО ОКНО НЕ ДЕЛАЕТ. **Не удаляет записи.** … требует отметок с цитатами, а они появляются на **L5**» — and the store layer says the same thing one level down, `app/m/v9/store/records.js:32-38`: «**No delete** … Shipping an exported `deleteRecord()` nothing calls would be dead code carrying a destructive cascade.» The full `<button>`/`<form>` inventory of `app/index.html` (26 controls, `:191-798`) contains no delete control of any kind, and there is no bulk-delete, reset or "clear all" affordance: a sweep of `app/index.html` + `app/m/v9` for `Удалить|Стереть|Очистить|Сбросить|clearAll|resetData|wipe` returns one user-visible string, `app/index.html:651`, which is prose about **uninstalling**. The `record` table is deliberately outside the eight append-only triggers (`store/schema/001-core.sql:212-223`), so the DB *can* delete a row — **nothing in the shipped JS ever issues it.**
  - **Delete of a child profile: does not exist.** `core/repo-local.js` has four writers (`:102`, `:107`, `:119`, `:131`) and `profiles.push(child)` at `:138` is the only mutation of the array's membership — no `splice`, no filter-out anywhere in the mount. On the device a child is identity-only and its attributes are an append-only journal (`001-core.sql:41-45`, `:218-219`); there is no `DELETE FROM child`.
  - **Edit of a record: EXISTS, and the document was right about it.** A per-entry **«Изменить»** button, `app/m/v9/surfaces/diary.js:99-105`; handler `:625-641` («Правка — это **ПЕРЕЗАПИСЬ** той же строки… `PDR-026` §4, правило 1»); the save branches on `editingRecordId` into `overwriteRecord({recordId, body, eventDateLocal})` (`:570-577`), so **both** the text and the event date are editable. A skill mark is not overwritten — un-ticking appends a revocation (`store/repo-journal.js:47-52`) — which is still a change the parent makes, on a date, and the document now says so in those terms.
  - **Edit of the child's own fields: does not exist**, and this is the secondary finding `UIP-DL-007` (k) recorded. Create surface `app/index.html:427-443` → `surfaces/profile.js:228-243` → `core/state.js:296`; switch surface `surfaces/profile.js:79`, `:93-100`. `createProfile` has exactly two call sites (its declaration and the create form) and `appendChild()` two (creation, and the one-time legacy migration `store/import-legacy.js:100`). No `editProfileModal`, no `renameProfile`, no second form. The schema **anticipates** correction — `child_attribute` is append-only and resolved by `v_child_attribute_current` (`001-core.sql:182-188`, `:306-307`) — but nothing in the UI ever appends a second `name` or `birthdate` attribute. **Name and birthdate are write-once.**
  - **What is TRUE and had to survive:** uninstalling erases the local database (SQLCipher `theygrow`, encrypted from creation, key in `EncryptedSharedPreferences` behind an AndroidKeyStore MasterKey — `store/store.js:7-12`, `:197-208`, `store/config.js:24-26`; Android backup off; both die with the package, and `app/index.html:651` already tells the parent so); export exists and is the way to keep what matters first (`exportBtn` revealed only in the Capacitor shell, `surfaces/channel.js:148-149`, producing one unencrypted ZIP of TXT + JSON index + PDF/A-2b through Android's `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT`, with no network leg); and the developer holds no copy and cannot reach these records.
- **b. TWO SWEEPS WERE RUN BEFORE ANYTHING WAS TOUCHED, because a partial edit across the paired files is this packet's whole failure mode.** **Sweep 1, the claim class** («a statement telling a parent the app offers a self-service action it does not»): **12 lines examined per file** — 11 by token (`удал|исправляете|исправлении|изменение`) plus **one found by hand that carries no shared token**, §8 ¶4's «выполните нужное действие в приложении» (`:122` / `:272`). Disposition: **8 changed, 1 added, 3 examined and left** — §3.4 ¶1 (`:74`), every clause of which is true; §8 ¶2 (`:118`), the GDPR rights, out by (e); and the history table's own «Изменение» column header (`:138`). A tree-wide pass over `app/index.html`, `app/m/v9/**` and `docs/RUNBOOK.md` returned **five** further hits, all of them comments or true prose, and **no other surface in the repository promises a parent a deletion**. **Sweep 2, the current-edition filename**: 26 matching lines, of which **6 are live references that this packet falsifies** and moved — `app/playwright.config.js:179`, `app/privacy.html:38`, `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js:6`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md:352`, `:387`, `:388` — plus two more locations that are the same fact under another spelling, `const EDITION` (`privacy-page.spec.js:68`) and step 1's frozen-editions enumeration (`RUNBOOK:356`). The remaining 20 stay: `docs/RUNBOOK.md:60` (narrates what `UIP-P2` did, and still true), seven lines of this log, two of `docs/execution-map.md` and two of `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (historical narration, correct), and `native/android/app/src/main/assets/public/privacy.html` (git-ignored `cap sync` output). **Post-edit, both sweeps were re-run:** zero occurrences of any retired claim shape in either current file, and the only surviving `privacy-policy-v1.1` references in `app/` and the RUNBOOK are the three that name it deliberately as **history**.

### The decisions

- **c. A NEW EDITION, 1.2, AND 1.1 FREEZES THE MOMENT IT IS WRITTEN.** Owner gate decision **2026-08-27**, option 2 of three. The ground is §10's own wording: a new edition is published when the **DATA PROCESSING** described changes, and a changed description of erasure is exactly that. This is the deliberate contrast with `UIP-P7`, settled at the same gate: naming a UI control describes the interface and was corrected **in place**; describing what can and cannot be erased describes the processing and takes a version, a date and a history row. File layout repeats the 1.0 → 1.1 step (`UIP-DL-002` (i)): a new `docs/privacy-policy-v1.2.md`, with 1.0 and 1.1 left byte-untouched as history. `.pre-commit-config.yaml:110`/`:112` already exclude the **version-agnostic** prefix `docs/privacy-policy-v` from the rewriting hooks, so the Markdown hard line breaks at lines 3–4 came through the gate without a new exclusion.
- **d. NINE PLACES, NOT FOUR — THE ITEM NAMES THE CLASS.** The handoff's four are the *items*; the class is what sweep 1 measured, and it has nine members. Beyond the four: §2 ¶3 («запросы о просмотре, исправлении, экспорте и **удалении** … выполняются вами в самом приложении»), §3.4 ¶2's retention sentence («до **их удаления вами в приложении** или до удаления приложения»), §9's retention row («До **удаления пользователем в приложении**…»), and §8 ¶4's pointer. Leaving them would have published an edition whose §3.4 says a per-record deletion is impossible and whose §9 says it is how retention ends — a document at war with itself, which is worse than the one it replaces. **Confirmed by the owner at go-ahead in those terms.**
- **e. §8's RIGHTS PARAGRAPHS ARE BYTE-UNTOUCHED, AND THAT IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF OF NOT OVERCORRECTING.** «Вы вправе запросить доступ к данным, их исправление или удаление, ограничение обработки, возражение против обработки и переносимость…» and the supervisory-authority paragraph are **verified byte-identical** between 1.1 and 1.2. Those rights run against the **developer**, who holds tester-side data and no family records at all; nothing measured at (a) touches them. What changed in §8 is ¶1's list of app functions and ¶4's pointer. **The narrowing is about which SELF-SERVICE actions the app offers, not about rights** — and the other direction was watched just as closely: every place that now says the app cannot delete one record also says, in the same breath, how a parent **can** erase everything, so the edition cannot be read as "your family data is unerasable". It is erasable, completely, by uninstalling, and that path is stated in the summary, in §3.4 twice and in §8.
- **f. THE EFFECTIVE DATE IS `28.08.2026`, THE DAY OF PROMOTION, SET BEFORE PUBLICATION.** Owner's literal, named at go-ahead. Same rule as `UIP-P6`: the date a policy states is the day it becomes readable (`PPR-DL-001` (f)), which is the day of **promotion** (`ADR-020`), and it is set in advance rather than revised after. Four literals carry it — the header block and the top history row of `docs/privacy-policy-v1.2.md`, and the same two in `app/privacy.html` — as one derived set that `UIP-P2-INV-001` holds together. **If the promotion slips to another day, all four move together BEFORE promoting**, by `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Privacy policy step 6, which is where that wall-clock judgement lives and which no test can make.
- **g. THE CLAIM IS COUPLED TO THE CODE THAT WOULD FALSIFY IT, AND THAT WAS A SCOPE EXTENSION THE OWNER GRANTED (E1, branch (i)).** The new wording's durability rested on *the app offers no per-record deletion, and if it ever does, this document moves with it* — a promise in a decision-log entry with no executor. **This milestone has been bitten by that exact shape three times**: the date literal at `UIP-P6`, the control name at `UIP-P7`, and this erasure claim, which is the one that reached readers. So `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` gains one describe block, *the document says what the app can erase, and the code is what says it (UIP-P8)*, five legs. It reads the mount's store door (`m/v9/store/boot.js`'s `export { … }` block, derived through the existing `currentMount()`) and its web-channel twin (`m/v9/core/repo-local.js`'s exported functions), requires that **neither** carries an erasure operation — matched by vocabulary, `delete|remove|erase|purge|wipe|destroy|drop|clear|forget`, not by two spellings — requires both paired files to carry the same erasure and child-field sentences **derived by stem rather than pinned as literals**, forbids the seven retired claim shapes in either file, and proves every parser and the detector in-run on fragments it builds itself. *Rejected:* scanning the markup for "a delete button" — a negative over a shape nobody has yet chosen, green for any spelling not guessed. *Rejected:* pinning the new sentences as literals — it would force a test edit on every legitimate reword, which is the tax `UIP-P7` deliberately refused.
- **h. `docs/RUNBOOK.md` IS EDITED, AND ONLY WHERE THIS PACKET MAKES IT FALSE.** `UIP-P7` (i) drew that line and this packet keeps it. Falsified **by this diff**: step 1's «the CURRENT edition — `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md` since UIP-P2 —», step 1's enumeration of frozen superseded editions (1.1 has now joined 1.0, so the sentence was about to be incomplete on the one procedure that must not be), and step 6's two bullets addressing the source document by path — which would otherwise send the owner to edit a **superseded** file at the exact moment they are promoting the new one. Step 6's worked-example sentence gains one clause recording 1.2's date and the slip rule, on the `UIP-P6` precedent. **Not touched:** `:60`, which narrates what `UIP-P2` did and is still true, and the four glyph statements at `:372`, `:374`, `:758`, `:761` — `UIP-P3` falsified those, not this packet, and `:758` still **cannot pass as written**.
- **i. `docs/INVARIANTS.md` IS NOT AMENDED — third packet running, and stated as a decision rather than left as an omission.** `UIP-P2-INV-001` names no edition filename: it asserts the page converts the **newest** edition present in `docs/`, which is exactly the property that made this bump a one-constant change on the test side. Its Scope already assigns the wall-clock date judgement to the RUNBOOK. `PPR-P1-INV-001`'s 2026-08-26 amendment does name `docs/privacy-policy-v1.1.md`, but it states the rule generically — «The Scope's source-document sentence **moves with the edition**» — and this log's standing convention (`UIP-DL-002` (r)) is that a dated amendment stays as written. The block at (g) adds a **new** property with its own subject, not a widening of `UIP-P2-INV-001`, and follows `UIP-P7` (h) in taking no invariant entry of its own.

### Escalated to the owner and NOT closed here

- **j. THE GOOGLE PLAY DATA SAFETY DECLARATION MAY NOW DISAGREE WITH THE DOCUMENT, AND ONLY THE OWNER CAN SEE IT.** That form carries its own answer to «users can request that data be deleted», it lives in the Play Console, and it is invisible to this repository: no test here can read it and no packet here can move it. If it currently declares an in-app deletion path, it and edition 1.2 are in conflict **from the moment 1.2 is promoted**. Recorded by the orchestrator as an owner-run check at promotion, in the same sitting as `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Privacy policy step 6. **This packet does not close it.**

### Alternatives rejected

- **Correct edition 1.1 in place, on the `UIP-P7` precedent** — rejected at (c), on the owner's gate decision and §10's own wording. `UIP-P7`'s precedent is about an *interface description*; this is a *processing description*, and the two branches are now written side by side in `app/privacy.html`'s head comment so the distinction is not reconstructed from a diff.

- **Correct only the four places the finding named** — rejected at (d).
- **Narrow §8's GDPR rights to match** — rejected at (e). It would answer a UI measurement with a legal one, about a party that never held the data.
- **Ship the new wording with no guard** — rejected at (g). Mutation (2) below is the measurement that makes that a finding rather than an opinion.

- **The evidence is static, and is named as static** (`AGENTS.md` §11). `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` boots nothing, the new block included: it reads four files off disk — the two policy files, the shell, and the two mount modules — and compares strings. **There are no runtime claims in this packet.** The behaviour statements at (a) are **readings of the source**, and are reported as readings; what a browser meets at the address is `app/tests/privacy-surface.spec.js` (`PPR-P1-INV-001`), which makes no claim this edition changes and was run to show the reworded page still renders and still links only the allowlist.
- **Armed before it was trusted — four mutations, run and reverted, and TWO of them corrected the plan's own prediction.** **(1) `EDITION` left at `1.1` with `docs/privacy-policy-v1.2.md` on disk: 6 failed / 49 passed.** The plan predicted **one** red, *the conversion tracks the newest edition on disk*. The finding is that `EDITION` is not one leg's input but the **selector for the entire paired source**, so a half-applied bump also reds *the edition is resolved…*, *the change history…row for row*, *the effective date is stated exactly twice*, and **both** new `UIP-P8` legs — the latter because the pairing then reads the superseded Markdown, which still carries the retired claims. A half-done edition bump is not a quiet green anywhere. **(2) §3.4 ¶4 reverted to its 1.1 wording in `app/privacy.html` alone, Markdown left at 1.2: 2 failed / 53 passed** — and the 53 include **all 50 pre-existing legs**, every heading leg, the edition block, the history table and the `UIP-P7` control-name coupling among them. That is the measurement E1 was granted for, shown: without the new block this revert is **fully green**, and the two legs that catch it are *both files state the absence, in the same words* and *neither file still carries the claim edition 1.1 shipped*. **(3) `deleteRecord` added to `m/v9/store/boot.js`'s door: 2 failed / 53 passed.** Predicted one leg — *neither the store door nor the web repository offers a way to erase one record or one child* — observed two, the second being the arm leg, which re-asserts the real door as part of proving the detector. That is by design and is recorded so the count is not read as noise. **(4) The frozen `1.1` history row edited in the Markdown alone: 1 failed / 54 passed**, *the change history is the same table in both files, row for row* — exactly as predicted, and it is what makes "1.1 is frozen" a fact rather than a promise. All four reverted; every mutated file is byte-identical to its pre-mutation state, verified by checksum.
- **One divergence inside this packet's own guard, found by the first green run and repaired before it shipped.** The sentence extractor pulled the **change-history row for 1.2** into the prose pairing — the row states the same change in the same words, and its Markdown `| version | date |` cells are spelled `<td>` in the page, so the leg compared two spellings of one row. The extractor now skips Markdown table rows, with the reason written where it is skipped: the history table is already paired **cell for cell** by `UIP-P2-INV-001`, and what this block derives is the document's **prose** promise. The arm leg gained a case for it, so the exclusion is proven rather than asserted.
- **Measured, on the host, 2026-08-28:** `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js` **50 passed** before (the count `UIP-DL-007` recorded) and **55 passed** after — the five added legs and no other movement. `contract` **1295 → 1300 passed**; `behavior` **121 passed**, unmoved. Via `PARITY_NO_DOCKER=1 scripts/parity-suite.sh`, which stages `native/www/` first — required here, because `app/privacy.html` is in the ship list and a stale staging would red `LSC-P1-INV-002` on the wrong cause.
- **What it hands on.** **First, and it is the owner's: (j)** — the Play Console Data safety declaration, open, and due at promotion. **Second, the loss window (`UIP-DL-007` (k)) closes at PROMOTION, not at merge** (`ADR-020`): every day between now and then, the live document still overstates a right. **Third, `docs/RUNBOOK.md` has no step for publishing an edition** — step 6 covers the date and nothing covers "when you publish edition N+1, these current-edition references move with it". This packet moved them by hand and (b) enumerates them; turning that list into a numbered step is a docs packet for the milestone close. **Fourth, the debts `UIP-P7` left are untouched and still true:** the four glyph statements at `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (`:758` still cannot pass), the two product comments, and the stale `cap sync` copy under `native/android/`, which this edition reaches by the same route at the next release build. **Fifth, a side-find of (a) that is nobody's defect yet:** in a browser the shell holds the child's name, birthdate and ticked skills in `localStorage` (`core/storage.js:34-42`), the document's erasure sentences are scoped to the Android app its header declares, and §3.2's «только на устройстве» covers the browser case — so nothing is false, but the web channel has no erasure sentence of its own.

## NAV-DL-001 — NAV-P1 `header-menu`: the app's header becomes one menu, the showcase keeps one control, and the tenth mount generation carries both

- **Date.** 2026-08-29
- **Type.** Packet — `NAV-P1`, the opening packet of the milestone «navigation and menu» (`NAV`), the first packet after the `UIP` milestone closed. `main` is at `73115a2` (PR #35) and is **PROMOTED** on both channels. Branch `feat/nav-menu`, cut from that commit; the checkpoint and the PR are the owner's (`CLAUDE.md`, No autonomous git). **Id split, on the standing precedent for a new track** (`GWN`, `SLA`, `VDK`, `ICON`, `XPT`, `CGR`, `UIP`): decisions take `NAV-DL-{NNN}` and invariants `NAV-P{k}-INV-{NNN}`, declared in `docs/execution-map.md` because a prefix with no declaration there is an id with no home (`CGR-DL-001` (n)).
- **Scope.** **In:** `app/m/v10/**` (**new** — the tenth generation, copy-forward of `/m/v9/`), and inside it `surfaces/menu.js` (new), `surfaces/channel.js`, `app.css`, `app.js`, `surfaces/onboarding.js`, `surfaces/profile.js`; `app/index.html` (the menu markup, `#exportBtn` re-parented, the glyph's frame, and every `/m/v10/` reference); `app/sw.js` (`OFFLINE_URLS` and `CACHE_VERSION` v19 → v20); `app/tests/channel-composition.spec.js` (one helper, three repaired legs, one new block); `app/tests/behavior.spec.js` (one comment); `app/tests/support/prev-generation.js` and `app/tests/upgrade-path.spec.js` (the generation-pair comments the bump checklist names by file); `native/android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/theygrow/StoreEngineTest.java` (one javadoc mount address, which `EMV-P5-INV-001` reds on); nineteen baselines; `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (debt 49 and the current-generation statements); `docs/INVARIANTS.md`; `docs/execution-map.md`; this entry. **Out:** `app/m/v1`–`v9` entire — **frozen, byte-untouched** (b); the «Обновление» item and every line of network code, which is `NAV-P2` with policy edition v1.3 (vault `ADR-052` §1); the hardware back button, modal back arrows and every close cross, which is `NAV-P3`; the APK window's copy and the no-profile «Подходящие активности», which is `NAV-P4`; `#diaryBtn`, which stays a direct header control (f); `app/Dockerfile`, `app/nginx.conf`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (the bump needs none of them); `app/privacy.html` and every policy edition — **no rename, so no edition** (e); no storage key, no knob, no signal, no egress.

### What the artefacts establish, before anything was decided

- **a. THE HEADER ROW HAD FIVE CONTROLS AND A ROLE PROBLEM, NOT A CROWDING PROBLEM.** `app/index.html`'s `.header-right` carried `#profileButton`, `#aboutBtn`, `#exportBtn`, `#diaryBtn` and `#apkBtn`, of which `surfaces/channel.js` revealed a different subset per channel. The row is where the app's whole vocabulary of actions lives, and vault `PDR-034` §1 says that vocabulary grows on the **native** channel and does not on the **web** one, which is a showcase. A row is the wrong container for a list that grows on one side only.
- **b. THE MOUNT WAS PUBLISHED, AND THAT DECIDED THE PACKET'S SHAPE BEFORE ANY DESIGN DID.** `/m/v9/` has been live since the `UIP` merge, `docs/RUNBOOK.md:435` triggers a bump on **any** byte change under a published generation — "a one-character CSS fix included" — and a menu is not achievable without new CSS and new JS. The handoff asked for no new generation unless the packet could not land otherwise; it could not, and this is recorded as the reason rather than as a preference (g).
- **c. THE GLYPH DREW TWO CIRCLES, IN TWO FILES.** `.header-help` set `border: 1px solid var(--primary-purple)` with `border-radius: 50%` (`app/m/v9/app.css:183-184`) and the SVG inside it drew its own `<circle r="9">` (`app/index.html:268`). Neither file is wrong on its own; together they render a ring inside a ring, which the conventional info pictogram does not have. Verified by reading the blessed baseline `app/tests/__baselines__/visual-desktop/header.png`, not by reading the rules.
- **d. THE POLICY NAMES THIS CONTROL, AND THE VAULT HAD ALREADY SETTLED WHICH KIND OF CHANGE COSTS AN EDITION.** Vault `PDR-035`'s annotation **2026-08-27** draws the line by subject rather than by diff size: a description of the **interface** is corrected in place, a description of the **processing** takes a new edition. It also names the form that closes the class — the document quotes the control's `title`/`aria-label`, not the sign painted on it — and says the coupling is made checkable. `app/tests/privacy-page.spec.js:475-499` is that coupling, and it reads `#aboutBtn`'s `aria-label` out of the shell.

### The decisions

- **e. THE NAMES DO NOT MOVE, ON EITHER CHANNEL, AND THAT IS WHY THIS PACKET NEEDS NO EDITION.** The handoff described the menu rows as «Информация» and «Сохранение архива»; the shipped strings stay **«О приложении»** and **«Сохранить архив»**. The first because renaming it is exactly the change (d) says costs an edition, and the constraint was explicit; the second because «Сохранение архива» exists nowhere in this repository and `app/tests/export-contour.spec.js:483-497` pins the name in three places at once. Redrawing the glyph and re-parenting a button are interface changes and cost nothing. `docs/privacy-policy-v1.2.md` is not opened.
- **f. TWO ROWS, AND THE THIRD IS REFUSED RATHER THAN LEFT ROOM FOR.** «Обновление» belongs to `NAV-P2` together with the first network call this channel makes; a placeholder row would be a control that promises something nothing does. The panel is sized to two rows, the markup says so in a comment, and *pressing it opens exactly two named rows, and no third* reds on a third arriving early. **`#diaryBtn` stays a direct header control and is not folded in** — owner decision on this packet's escalation (a), branch A, with the destination named: `NAV-P3` replaces it with a left swipe from the skills view and removes the button there, so moving it into the menu now would move it twice.
- **g. `/m/v10/` AND `CACHE_VERSION` v20 LAND HERE, ONCE FOR THE WHOLE MILESTONE.** Owner decision on escalation (b). `NAV-P1` is the first mount-touching packet of `NAV`, so this is the milestone's single copy-forward and `NAV-P2`–`P4` edit `/m/v10/` in place — the `UIP-P1` → `UIP-P3`/`P4` shape. The alternative, editing `/m/v9/` now and copying forward later, was rejected because it parks modified bytes of a published immutable-cached generation on the branch, which is the defect vault `ADR-024` exists to prevent. The full checklist of `docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Module mount was run, including the two hand steps no guard covers: `changed_in:` lines were **excluded** from the substitution (`app/sw.js:68` and `:78` still describe the v18 → v19 bump and still say `/m/v9/`, correctly), and the generation-pair prose in `support/prev-generation.js` and `upgrade-path.spec.js` was re-read and corrected.
- **h. THE CHANNEL SPLIT USES THE EXISTING SEAM, AND ADDS ITS FIRST *MUTUAL* PAIR.** `surfaces/channel.js` gains two lines — `headerMenu.hidden = !native` and `aboutButton.hidden = native` — and that second one is the first branch in the file written **without** a negation. Its question is different from its neighbours': they ask whether a channel can perform an action, this asks where a channel's entry to one shared window lives. `archiveButton.hidden = !native` is **kept** although the panel around it is already hidden on the web: hidden inside hidden is a default refusal at the item itself, and removing it would make the archive's absence a consequence of somebody else's decision about menus.
- **i. THE MENU'S BEHAVIOUR IS A SURFACE, NOT A CHANNEL FACT.** `surfaces/menu.js` is new and follows the split `channel.js` states in prose: the seam decides whether the menu is **offered**, the surface decides what it **does**. It closes on a choice through **one delegated listener on the panel**, so «Сохранить архив» closes the menu without this module naming it — `surfaces/export.js` keeps its listener untouched, which is what makes the relocation a relocation.
- **j. A DISCLOSURE PATTERN, NOT `role="menu"`.** `#menuBtn` carries `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the panel is a plain container of plain buttons. `role="menu"` promises arrow-key navigation and a single Tab stop, and honouring that promise means focus-management code no surface in this repository has. What is declared is what is executed. Escape closes **and returns focus to the toggle**, because otherwise closing from the keyboard loses the reader's place while closing with the mouse does not.
- **k. THE RING COMES OFF THE BUTTON, NOT THE CIRCLE OFF THE ICON.** Removing the SVG's circle would leave a bare "i" inside a 44px ring — one circle, but not the pictogram. `border: none` leaves the icon's own circle as the only one; `border-radius: 50%` stays so the hover halo is round; the 44px box is untouched, so the circle left the eye and not the finger. The glyph goes 22px → 24px, matching its neighbours now that no frame surrounds it, and 20px → 22px on the narrow layout, where the neighbours keep a filled pill to carry the eye and this control does not.
- **l. DEBT 49 IS REWRITTEN TO WHAT THE PRODUCT DOES AFTER THIS PACKET, NOT TO WHAT IT DID BEFORE IT.** The owner runs `docs/RUNBOOK.md` after the merge, so repairing the four «?» statements to the `UIP-P3` state would have made them stale on arrival. The privacy-policy step now names the control **by name** and lists the per-channel door; the on-device smoke drops the «close it with ✕ and see whether it stays closed» premise entirely, because `UIP-P3` removed the auto-open it was about, and gains a menu check. Also corrected, in the same file and for the same reason: the four statements that named `/m/v9/` as the **running** generation. Historical statements naming past generations were left alone.
- **m. DEBT 50, EXACTLY THE TWO COMMENTS THE PACKET NAMED.** `app.css:170` («Круг с «?»») and `surfaces/profile.js:165` («открывается по «?» в шапке»), both corrected in `/m/v10/` and both now naming the control rather than its sign — the same form (d) settled for the document. No wider sweep was run. **Two further comments were corrected because this packet made them false**, which is a different rule (`AGENTS.md` §11's neighbourhood, and the standing "no false statement survives an edit pass"): `surfaces/onboarding.js`'s «у него ровно один вход — кнопка «i»», and `app/index.html`'s two header comment blocks.

### Escalated to the owner and NOT closed here

- **n. NOTHING REMAINS OPEN FROM THIS PACKET'S OWN ESCALATIONS** — both were answered at go-ahead and are recorded at (f) and (g) as decisions rather than as questions. **What is open and is the owner's** is listed under Effects: the `.graphifyignore` line, the promotion, and the release build.

### Alternatives rejected

- **A second channel mechanism for the menu — rejected at (h).** The handoff forbade it and the seam fits: the question "does this channel offer this" is the one `wireChannel()` already answers.
- **Relocating `#aboutBtn` itself into the panel at runtime — rejected at (h).** One element instead of two, but it moves DOM nodes and swaps classes after boot, and the codebase's own rule is one local variable per id precisely to keep that kind of indirection out.
- **Rewriting `#exportBtn` as a purpose-built menu row — rejected at (e)/(i).** Its `id`, `class`, `hidden`, the three-place name and the `<span class="header-action-label">` are each pinned by a guard, one of them as another test's anti-vacuity witness. Re-parenting it changes none of them.
- **`role="menu"` with roving focus — rejected at (j).**
- **Editing `/m/v9/` in place and copying forward in a later NAV packet — rejected at (g).**
- **Folding `#diaryBtn` into the menu now — rejected at (f)**, by owner decision, with `NAV-P3`'s swipe named as its actual destination.

### Effects

- **Added:** `app/m/v10/**` (**51** files: 45 byte-identical copies of `/m/v9/`'s 50, five carried forward and edited — `app.css`, `app.js`, `surfaces/channel.js`, `surfaces/onboarding.js`, `surfaces/profile.js` — and one new, `surfaces/menu.js`; `diff -rq app/m/v9 app/m/v10` names exactly those six and nothing else); the `#headerMenu` block in `app/index.html`; the `.header-menu*` rules in the mount's `app.css`; the ten-leg `NAV-P1-INV-001` block in `app/tests/channel-composition.spec.js`; `NAV-P1-INV-001` in `docs/INVARIANTS.md`.
- **Changed, the product:** `#exportBtn` re-parented into the panel (markup byte-identical, indentation aside); `.header-help` loses its border and gains two pixels of glyph; `surfaces/channel.js` gains two branches; `app.js` gains one import and one call; four comment blocks corrected. **Changed, delivery:** every `/m/v10/` reference in the shell and the worker, one added `modulepreload` hint and one added `OFFLINE_URLS` entry (the hint count series in the shell moves 41 → 42), `CACHE_VERSION` v19 → v20 with its own `changed_in:` paragraph. **Changed, the guards:** one helper and three repaired legs in `channel-composition.spec.js`, one comment in `behavior.spec.js`, two generation-pair comments, one javadoc mount address. **Changed, the docs:** four `docs/RUNBOOK.md` glyph statements, four `/m/v9/` current-generation statements, and `docs/execution-map.md`. **Retired:** nothing. **Not changed:** `app/m/v1`–`v9`, `app/Dockerfile`, `app/nginx.conf`, `app/privacy.html`, every policy edition, every store and export module, `#diaryBtn`, every close cross.
- **Operability: none this packet** (`ADR-013` / contract §4.7). No `theygrow_api.parameters` knob — the menu introduces no qualitative value, and `app/m/v10/channel/config.js` is a byte copy with no key added; the typed-config home is `/api`, outside this front-only perimeter (`VDK-DL-001` / `A1-DL-004` precedent). No `theygrow_api.signals` taxonomy entry, no `emitted_now` change, **and deliberately no counter of menu openings**: there is no analytics on either channel since `UIP-P1`, and the absence of a signal here is a decision, written into `surfaces/menu.js` where a future reader will look for it. **Net egress: unchanged, none added** — no request is made that was not made before, which is also why vault `ADR-052`'s subject is `NAV-P2` and not this packet. The one provenance line written is `CACHE_VERSION`'s.
- **The evidence is a mixture, and each half is named** (`AGENTS.md` §11). **Executing:** the ten `NAV-P1-INV-001` legs and the three repaired ones load a real page in a real browser and press real controls, with `window.IS_NATIVE_SHELL` asserted first so the native block cannot silently test the web branch; `mount-derivation.spec.js` fetches what `/m/v10/` computes for its own assets, on both delivery surfaces; `upgrade-path.spec.js` installs the staged `/m/v9/` client and drives it onto `/m/v10/`, on both legs; the visual baselines are a rendered comparison. **Static, and preferred where it fits:** the ship-list agreement in four directions, `.show`-rule coverage, the mount-reference sweep, `#exportBtn`'s structure and name triple, and the `UIP-P7` policy coupling.
- **Armed before it was trusted — three mutations, run and reverted, and the third measured a hole instead of confirming a guess.** **(1) The `#menuBtn` click handler removed: 8 failed / 123 passed** — the five native menu legs and the three pre-existing legs that now reach their subject through the menu, and nothing else. **(2) `.header-menu[hidden] { display: none }` deleted: 2 caused failures / 128 passed** — the `[hidden]` sweep reds naming `headerMenu` by id, and the web-composition leg reds. **(3) `#menuAboutBtn`'s `aria-label` changed to «Информация»: 2 caused failures / 124 passed** — and **the whole `contract` project stayed 1361 passed, the `UIP-P7` policy↔name coupling included**, because that guard reads `#aboutBtn` and the drift is on the other entry. That is the precise hole the two comparison legs close, and it is now a measurement rather than an argument. **Six reds across runs (2) and (3) were `ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED` and every one of them passes in isolation with the mutation still applied**; they are reported as the environment flake they are and excluded from the counts, not folded into them.
- **Measured, in the pinned Playwright container, 2026-08-29:** the full suite **1580 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed** after re-blessing. `behavior` **118 → 131 passed** (the thirteen added and repaired legs are the difference), `contract` **1361 passed**. **Nineteen baselines moved and are enumerated in the execution report**; each was re-blessed only after its diff was read, and the header's own diff was read as an image on both sides.
- **What it hands on.** **First, the `.graphifyignore` line, and it is the owner's at PROMOTION rather than at merge:** the file freezes `app/m/v1…v7`, `v8` was never added when `/m/v9/` went live, and `/m/v9/` needs adding when `/m/v10/` is promoted — the rule keys on the generation going live (`docs/RUNBOOK.md` § *Corpus exclusions*), so doing it here would be a claim about a deploy that has not happened. **Second, promotion step 5 is not optional this time** (`docs/RUNBOOK.md` § Promotion + rollback): a mount bump is exactly the case it exists for, and no test can see which generation a live client holds. **Third, the APK:** the app channel gets nothing until a release build is produced and installed by hand (`ADR-020`, `ADR-047`), so the menu reaches a phone later than it reaches the web. **Fourth, `NAV-P2` inherits a menu built to receive it** — vault `ADR-052` §1 puts «Обновление» in exactly this list, and §1.5 leaves that row's behaviour in a Play copy to the packet rather than to the decision. **Fifth, a side-find that is nobody's defect:** `scripts/parity-suite.sh` on this workstation produced six `ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED` reds across two parallel runs, all of which pass in isolation; it is a WSL networking artefact under load, not a suite defect, and it is recorded so the next session does not read a stray red as a regression.
